Pair resolution permits only: anchors agree (`steady`); authority selects target whose exact previous digest is old bootstrap anchor (`checkpoint_pending`); or no authority and a valid parent initialisation anchor plus its matching `bootstrap_prepared` phase chain selects prepared target (`preauthority_prepared`). A lagging bootstrap anchor is repaired only from valid authority reference; anchor ahead, wrong previous digest, wrong initialisation-intent digest, wrong credential-owner fingerprint, or unreferenced target is invalid.

Bootstrap object and import ticket are each at most 64 KiB. Store retains current, previous rollback dependency, and active-transition object only; complete stable control directory, including one temporary, key, anchor, verifier key, reset intent, and import ticket, is capped at 4 MiB. Reference-aware GC runs only after matching composite authority/history anchor or completed reset is durable. Capacity +1 refuses before bootstrap/authority/manager mutation.

Initialisation creates store only through parent transaction above. Listener, manager, service label, or config adoption publishes inert prepared bootstrap object, then matching composite authority while lifecycle and authority locks remain held; authority anchor selects both. Bootstrap-anchor checkpoint follows commit and is idempotent. Crash before authority anchor leaves prior pair effective plus inert object; crash after authority anchor leaves new pair effective and exact checkpoint repair. No unmatched bootstrap selector can disable prior runtime. Quarantine reset uses only bootstrap object selected by valid terminal authority, preserves bootstrap and authority keys plus named config object into staged replacement, and reconstructs exactly sealed tuple. Missing, corrupt, unpinned, or nonterminal bootstrap identity refuses automated reset; V1 never guesses reconstruction fields from corrupt authority.

Primary/candidate role is verified from bootstrap identity plus signed authority, or declared only by an exclusive initialisation command authorised to create that role. Before state access, lexical dispatch assigns exactly one closed request class: `role_neutral_read|primary_semantic_read|candidate_only|ordinary_mutation|parent_transaction_recovery|operator_operation_recovery`. `parent_transaction_recovery` contains only `candidate prepare`, `authority initialise prepare|status|handoff|activate|abort`, `authority import-legacy prepare|status|handoff|activate|abort`, `recovery authority inspect|quarantine-reset`, `recovery initialise status|resume|abort`, and `recovery transition status|resolve|restore|resume`. `operator_operation_recovery` contains only `operation status|recover`; another spelling can never acquire either exceptional class. Read-only dispatch uses non-mutating `InspectInstance` and retained ancestors; it never creates lifecycle/key/root state or refuses fact collection merely because a fact is absent, malformed, or incompatible. Role-neutral inspection (`status`, `info`, `health`, `doctor`, `logs`, `client-bearer-barrier status`, and `config path|show|validate|diff`) reports the securely selected sealed role when one exists and otherwise the exact absent, legacy, invalid, or unavailable matrix state below. Primary-semantic reads (service, rescue, feature/settings/Codex/policy, and other primary-only surfaces) require an inspected primary except for the matrix's inspection-only legacy/default service-status cells. Candidate `status`, `candidate receipt show`, and root-form `validate-http` require an inspected candidate. Role-polymorphic validation follows its explicit contract: installed-client validation targets candidate or primary as specified, production profile targets candidate, and real-client proof targets primary. Commands still return collected facts when role enforcement fails. Every primary data-plane operation and ordinary primary mutator uses fail-closed `EnforcePrimary` before authority. Candidate start/stop, candidate artifact switch, candidate barrier refresh, root-form HTTP validation, candidate installed/production/release validation, and terminal candidate removal instead use the closed `EnforceCandidateRun` gate below and can never fall through to `EnforcePrimary`; first candidate preparation remains authorised only by the parent initialisation transaction. The other exceptions are first `InitialisePrimary`, `client-bearer-barrier stage` through `EnforceClientBearerBarrierStage`, the exact pre-authority legacy lifecycle surface authorised by `EnforceLegacyLifecycle`, and the two store-authority matrices below; no exception confers authority outside its closed command set. Missing floor outside the fresh transaction is incompatible. Mutators upgrade selector to `ProxyInstanceContext` only after secure final-root acquisition and exclusive initialisation or verified existing bootstrap plus authority. Context contains verified role, immutable `proxy_instance_id`, retained state-root capability, canonical listener, service label, sealed normal-config capability/fingerprint, compatibility-store capability/access mode, and every runtime path. Manager manifests seal control-directory identity, resolved state root, external compatibility paths, and config-home identity so launcher, supervisor, worker, and CLI cannot resolve different homes.

`InspectInstanceResultV1` is the closed non-authoritative inspection result `{selector_kind:"default_primary|explicit",topology:"absent|legacy_primary_live|legacy_primary_stopped|primary|candidate|partial_invalid|unavailable",sealed_role:null|"primary"|"candidate",role_source:"none|legacy_attestation|bootstrap_authority",instance_fact_status:"known|absent|invalid|unavailable|permission_denied"}`. Topology `primary|candidate` requires the matching non-null sealed role and `bootstrap_authority`; both legacy topologies require null sealed role and `legacy_attestation`; every other topology requires null sealed role and `none`. Legacy attestation authorises only the inspection and legacy-service cells below, never `EnforcePrimary`. `legacy_primary_live` requires the complete live correlation/challenge; `legacy_primary_stopped` requires one exact supported stopped configuration plus the complete absence proof below. `instance_fact_status` is `absent` only for `absent`, `invalid` only for `partial_invalid`, `unavailable|permission_denied` only for `unavailable`, and otherwise `known`. Inspection applies this exhaustive topology-by-request matrix before any role-specific collector or mutator gate:

| Securely inspected topology | Role-neutral reads | Primary-semantic reads | Candidate-only reads | Mutation authority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Absent reserved default-primary root | collect with `instance` absent and no inferred sealed role; each leaf uses its closed absent/down mapping | `service status` may collect stopped/absent facts and returns `down`/2; every other primary-semantic leaf returns `instance_uninitialised`/3 with initialise remediation | `instance_uninitialised`/3 | only `InitialisePrimary` |
| Absent explicit non-default root | collect with `instance` absent and no inferred role; each leaf uses its closed absent/down mapping | `instance_uninitialised`/3 | `instance_uninitialised`/3 | candidate preparation only when its separate parent-creation gate proves every candidate precondition; otherwise none |
| Exact live attested legacy topology at reserved default root | collect as `legacy_primary_live`; reconciled status is `legacy`/1 | only `service status` may collect and return `legacy`/1; every other primary-semantic leaf returns `instance_uninitialised`/3 with import remediation | `instance_mismatch`/3 | only the exact `EnforceLegacyLifecycle` cell or legacy import |
| Exact stopped configured legacy topology at reserved default root | collect as `legacy_primary_stopped`; reconciled status is `down`/2 with stopped manager facts | only `service status` may collect and return `down`/2; every other primary-semantic leaf returns `instance_uninitialised`/3 with import remediation | `instance_mismatch`/3 | only the exact stopped `EnforceLegacyLifecycle` cell or legacy import |
| Valid sealed primary | collect with sealed primary role | allowed; leaf oracle decides exit | `instance_mismatch`/3 | `EnforcePrimary` only |
| Valid sealed candidate | collect with sealed candidate role | `instance_mismatch`/3 | allowed only for the leaf's closed candidate state; leaf oracle decides exit | `EnforceCandidateRun` only |
| Partial, malformed, mixed-role, multiply selected, or cryptographically invalid state | collect independent safe facts with `instance` invalid | `authority_invalid` or exact ownership/generation conflict, exit 3 | same conflict, exit 3 | none |
| Ancestor/root/authority inspection unavailable or permission denied | collect every independent safe fact with matching unavailable status | `indeterminate`/4 | `indeterminate`/4 | none |

Role enforcement never suppresses already collected safe facts. A role-neutral leaf's existing read-side oracle remains authoritative after the matrix admits collection: `info` may therefore return 0 with unavailable facts, while status, health, doctor, logs, and config retain their exact command-specific exits. No matrix cell creates a directory, lifecycle inode, key, anchor, configuration, journal, manager action, provider request, or process.

`parent_transaction_recovery` is a topology-matrix exception resolved from the retained parent and authenticated store state, never from an inferred role or a malformed canonical tree. Its exhaustive store-authority matrix is:

| Retained parent/store state | Read/status authority | Mutation authority |
|---|---|---|
| No lifecycle/key, initialisation anchor, bootstrap authority, coordinator anchor, or legacy-lifecycle anchor | `recovery authority inspect`, `recovery initialise status`, and `recovery transition status` collect absence and return their closed idle/inspection result; an explicit well-formed selector misses with `requested_object_absent`/3 | only the topology row's exact creation leaf: reserved-default `authority initialise prepare`, explicit non-default `candidate prepare`, or attested live/stopped legacy `authority import-legacy prepare`; no recovery mutation |
| One valid selected initialisation chain or legacy-import ticket/chain | both initialisation status spellings may inspect, but command ownership and selector routing follow the anchored phase exactly | only the phase-owned `recovery initialise resume|abort`, `authority initialise handoff|activate|abort`, or `authority import-legacy handoff|activate|abort`; the selected parent chain/ticket is authority even while the canonical root is absent, staged, partial, or inhibited |
| No selected initialisation; one valid structured bootstrap/authority plus matching active coordinator child, or one valid pre-authority legacy-lifecycle anchor | `recovery transition status` and `recovery authority inspect` may inspect the exact selected chain | only exact `recovery transition resolve|restore` for that coordinator/child or legacy-lifecycle chain, plus `recovery transition resume` solely for a structured listener-release child selected at `barrier_waiting`, subject to its existing action/proof table; no ordinary primary or candidate mutation is admitted through this row |
| Authority unreadable, but a valid bootstrap pins the coordinator verifier and the exact reset prerequisites | `recovery authority inspect` reports the unreadable authority and independently verified reset facts | only `recovery authority quarantine-reset` through the closed unreadable-authority/reset-supersession path; no transition or initialisation command may borrow this authority |
| Parent identity, lifecycle/key, initialisation anchor, bootstrap verifier, coordinator, selected child, or cross-store relation is malformed, conflicting, multiply selected, permission-denied, or unavailable for the requested proof | every safe independent collector still runs and returns the exact conflict/indeterminate fact | none; mutation is conflict/3 or indeterminate/4 and creates no object or external action |

The parent-store classifier first proves the retained parent identity and opens existing entries no-follow; it never creates a lifecycle inode or key for a status/inspect leaf. A valid selected parent transaction is therefore recoverable even when ordinary `InspectInstance` reports `absent` or `partial_invalid`, while an absent or malformed parent transaction never turns that topology into initialisation authority. Preparation still must satisfy its topology creation cell, and every later phase must satisfy both this store matrix and the command-ownership paragraph above.

`operator_operation_recovery` is the other topology-matrix exception and is resolved only from the reserved default-primary locator, any already existing securely retained state-root capability, and authenticated `operator-control` state. Its exhaustive topology/store matrix is:

| Default-primary topology/operator store | `operation status` authority | `operation recover` authority |
|---|---|---|
| Absent or exact live/stopped legacy topology, with no authenticated `operator-control` store | no selector returns `idle`/0; a full selector returns `requested_object_absent`/3; no path, key, anchor, or object is created | full selector returns `requested_object_absent`/3 with zero mutation |
| Valid sealed primary and absent store | the same idle-or-selector-miss result without creating the store | selector miss/3 with zero mutation |
| Valid sealed primary and one valid authenticated store, plus one live authenticated owner-control connection to the current supervisor whose instance, root, operation-store, caller-capability, authority generation, and listener-generation mutation-key relation match the selected chain | inspect only the exact active chain or retained terminal receipt selected by the leaf rules | mutate only the selected operation chain through the closed `ControlRecover` phase table; the connection's current authenticated `runtime_instance_id` may differ from the originating runtime after a supervisor/service restart and is a recovery-observation fact, never an equality predicate against persisted operation identity; no ordinary command or provider effect is authorised anew |
| Valid sealed primary and one valid authenticated store, plus a live authenticated current-supervisor owner-control connection whose instance/root/store relation matches but whose caller-capability, authority-generation, current-runtime attestation, or listener-generation mutation-key relation conflicts with the selected chain | inspect only the exact active chain or retained terminal receipt selected by the leaf rules | create no recovery request, control frame, successor, receipt, or acknowledgement; preserve every safely authenticated operation fact and return `recovery_control=conflicted`, state `conflicted`, exit 3, null remediation, and exactly `ownership_conflict` for caller-capability mismatch, `generation_conflict` for authority/listener mismatch, or `runtime_identity_mismatch` for current-runtime attestation mismatch |
| Valid sealed primary and one valid authenticated store whose retained bootstrap identity byte-matches the store's immutable instance/root binding, but no live authenticated matching owner-control connection is reachable, including an absent, stopped, inhibited, or unreachable otherwise valid primary | inspect only the exact active chain or retained terminal receipt selected by the leaf rules | return a retained terminal receipt directly; an active chain creates no recovery request, control frame, successor, receipt, or acknowledgement, preserves its safely authenticated result facts, and returns `recovery_control=unavailable`, forces envelope state `indeterminate`, `operator_operation_indeterminate`/4, with exact `cq proxy service start --manager launchagent` remediation |
| Valid sealed candidate, or an authenticated store whose immutable instance/root binding names another instance or role | `instance_mismatch`/3 | `instance_mismatch`/3 with zero mutation |
| Malformed, partially selected, multiply selected, MAC-invalid, generation-conflicting, or replaced store/root relation | `conflicted`/3 | `conflicted`/3 with zero mutation |
| Required root/store identity or bytes unavailable or permission denied | `indeterminate`/4 after every safe independent fact | `indeterminate`/4 with zero mutation |

The operator-store classifier opens only already existing ancestors and entries no-follow, requires full operation IDs before state access, and never creates a root, key, anchor, object, receipt, runtime, or control connection for status. Status is an authenticated same-descriptor local store/receipt read and never sends an owner-control frame. Recovery may create only the next immutable successor or terminal receipt reserved by the already selected operation and may send only the operation-addressed reconciliation frames below. That mutation authority exists only through a matching live authenticated owner-control connection; its current runtime identity proves the current connection but need not equal an originating runtime identity after restart, while its listener generation must still satisfy the selected operation's mutation-key/journal relation. A live authenticated connection with any closed relation mismatch is conflict/3 and is never treated as service unavailability; only absence, stopped/inhibited state, or unreachable matching control selects the no-live indeterminate/4 branch and service-start remediation. Stopped/inhibited service state or a byte-matching retained bootstrap/store relation alone permits status and direct retained-receipt projection, never active-chain recovery. It cannot borrow `EnforcePrimary`, parent-transaction, legacy, candidate, initialisation, or creation authority.

Managed arguments, launchd plist, signed authority, control handshake, and runtime identity bind same state-root digest and service label. Except for the fixed lifecycle/initialisation/operation/legacy/quarantine/controller stores explicitly enumerated at the retained parent, every root-owned authoritative/private writable coordinator, continuity, routing, readiness, diagnostic, log, cache, canary, primer, registry, socket, and temporary path derives beneath root. Only registered compatibility projections and the exact parent stores may write externally. Candidate startup requires unique root, label, explicit listener, and securely copied `--source-config` snapshot; reload reads only sealed candidate copy. Candidate compatibility is check-only against primary floor and read/write only against candidate-local floor. Candidate launcher, supervisor, worker, and installed-client processes receive neither a provider credential descriptor nor reusable provider credential bytes and have no provider-origin network authority; only the distinct trusted controller-owned provider broker may consume an explicitly authorised read-only credential input and open an exact broker-authorised provider transport. Candidate processes cannot open any primary mutable path, parent controller store, broker journal, or external projection sink; only the distinct controller process owns those parent-store authorities.

`proxy.json.port` is consumed directly only by the frozen pre-authority foreground runner and is imported into structured state only by explicit primary initialisation/import. Thereafter bootstrap identity and signed authority own listener and normal-config path, and the frozen runner refuses with exact `service start --manager launchagent` remediation. Before structured authority, `start --port` is only the legacy runtime override for the foreground source; it never seeds or retargets structured authority. Disagreement after import directs the operator to transactional listener migration. No implicit port/config retargeting occurs.

`CredentialOwnerCommitStoreV1` is a distinct durable owner store beneath `credential-owner/`; operator-control objects and process memory are transport, never its recovery authority. `credential-owner/key` is exactly 32 OS-CSPRNG bytes in one owner-only `0600`, single-link regular file created, file-synced, directory-synced, and reopened through the retained root before the first credential-owner reservation. Let `credential_owner_key_fingerprint=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/credential-owner/root-key/fingerprint/v1\0") || uint32be(32) || K_co_root))`; it is a public identity commitment, never a key derivation input or substitute for reopening the key. The persistent `mutation.lock` serialises exactly one active credential-effect chain across foreground commands, restored refresh jobs, the proxy worker, and recovery. Let `K_co_root` be the exact key bytes, `K_credential_owner_commit=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_co_root,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/credential-owner/commit/key/v1"),L=32)`, `K_co_anchor=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_co_root,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/credential-owner/anchor/key/v1"),L=32)`, `K_co_receipt=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_co_root,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/credential-owner/receipt/key/v1"),L=32)`, `K_co_reservation_absence=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_co_root,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/credential-owner/reservation-absence/key/v1"),L=32)`, and `K_co_refresh_capacity=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_co_root,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/credential-owner/refresh-capacity/key/v1"),L=32)`. For a complete `CredentialOwnerCommitV1` with `mac` omitted canonical bytes `J`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_credential_owner_commit,ASCII("cq/credential-owner/commit/mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(J)) || J))`; `credential_owner_commit_object_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/credential-owner/commit/object/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))` over complete MACed canonical bytes `C`. These formulas, the purpose strings, empty HKDF salt, key length, lowercase hex, and recursive `CanonicalJSONV1` are invariant.

`CredentialOwnerCommitAnchorV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,commit_id,head_sequence,head_object_digest,credential_generation,mac}` is closed. `NormalCredentialParentTerminalV1={schema_version:1,kind:"normal_credential_parent_terminal_v1",operation_id,commit_id,caller_request_authority_digest,provider:"claude|codex",terminal_kind:"retained_provider_rejection|dispatch_terminal",retained_provider_rejection_digest:null|string,dispatch_terminal_digest:null|string,credential_terminal_object_digest,authority_generation,routing_generation,credential_generation,sequence,previous_object_digest,mac}` is the normal-worker request-authority terminal selected after the credential terminal; exactly the digest named by `terminal_kind` is non-null, and the other is null. `CredentialOwnerParentCompletionV1` is the closed tagged union with common fields `{schema_version:1,kind:"operator_control_acknowledged|normal_request_terminal",operation_id,commit_id,credential_terminal_object_digest,parent_terminal_object_digest,parent_store_identity_digest,credential_generation}`. Its `operator_control_acknowledged` member is a closed nested union on `completion_scope:"outer_result|refresh_credential_mutation_child"` and always adds `operator_control_request_digest`. `outer_result` adds exactly `{selected_terminal_operation_object_digest,selected_acknowledged_operation_object_digest,acknowledgement_context_digest}` and null child fields; the acknowledged successor must be the immediate selected successor of the named terminal object and byte-match its rendered-and-flushed acknowledgement context. `refresh_credential_mutation_child` adds exactly `{credential_child_id,credential_child_ordinal,planned_slot_ordinal,source_kind,writer_reachability_entry_digest,selected_credential_parent_terminal_object_digest,credential_child_context_digest,oauth_child_id:null|string,oauth_child_ordinal:null|integer,oauth_child_object_digest:null|string}` and null outer-result fields. The selected object is the exact reopened `RefreshCredentialMutationChildV1` `credential_parent_terminal` head named by the selected outer operation, binds this credential terminal/commit/generation and signed writer row, and the context digest binds the outer request, actual and planned ordinals, source kind, provider, safe mutation outcome, and OAuth relation when present without claiming human rendering. OAuth fields are all non-null only for `source_kind="oauth_reauth"` and otherwise all null. Its `normal_request_terminal` member adds exactly `{caller_request_authority_digest,normal_parent_terminal_object_digest}`; both terminal digest fields equal the same reopened `NormalCredentialParentTerminalV1`, which byte-matches the caller, commit, credential terminal, generations, and selected retained-rejection or dispatch terminal. Cross-scope/variant members, a parent selected before the credential terminal, or a parent from another store/operation fail closed. For complete union bytes `P`, `credential_owner_parent_completion_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/credential-owner/parent-completion/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`. `CredentialOwnerCommitReceiptV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,commit_id,terminal_object_digest,terminal_outcome:"committed|not_committed|indeterminate",credential_generation,selector_provenance_bundle_digest:null|string,writer_reachability_entry_digest:null|string,reserved_child_terminal_digest:null|string,parent_completion:CredentialOwnerParentCompletionV1,parent_completion_digest,receipt_generation,mac}` is closed and embeds the exact complete union whose recomputed digest equals `parent_completion_digest`. Anchor and receipt MACs use the corresponding purpose key and the same framed-HMAC construction with domains `cq/credential-owner/anchor/mac/v1\0` and `cq/credential-owner/receipt/mac/v1\0`; their complete-object digests use framed SHA-256 domains `cq/credential-owner/anchor/v1\0` and `cq/credential-owner/receipt/v1\0`. Commit objects are exactly `objects/<32-lower-hex-commit-id>.<canonical-non-negative-decimal-sequence>.json`; object temporaries are `objects/.<commit-id>.<sequence>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`. The single anchor is exactly `anchor`, with temporary `.anchor.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`; receipts are exactly `receipts/<commit-id>.json`, with temporary `receipts/.<commit-id>.receipt.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`. Every final and temporary is owner-only `0600`, regular, single-link, no-follow, and contained by a retained parent; unknown members, alternate suffixes, duplicate sequence, a gap, a nonzero first sequence, or a predecessor/anchor/operation/generation mismatch fail closed.

Structured-refresh ownership adds one acyclic parent reference. `CredentialOwnerCommitV1` has additional members `refresh_mutation_reservation_digest:null|string` and `refresh_capacity_lease_consumption_digest:null|string` immediately before `source_id`; `CredentialOwnerCommitReceiptV1` has the same members immediately before `parent_completion`; and the `refresh_credential_mutation_child` member of `CredentialOwnerParentCompletionV1` additionally requires both. All six values are non-null and pairwise equal by member only for a structured-refresh mutation; every outer-result and normal-request operation requires null. The reservation digest names the complete authenticated reopened `RefreshCredentialMutationChildV1` `mutation_reserved` object selected by the current outer-operation anchor before credential-owner sequence zero, and the lease digest names the immediate selected `CredentialOwnerRefreshCapacityLeaseV1` consumption successor for that reservation. Commit sequence zero byte-matches the reserved object's operation, plan, child/actual/planned ordinals, commit ID, provider, source kind, closed source-row reference, signed source-action map entry and writer row, OAuth relation, exact intent-action digest, typed target-selector digest, and capacity lease/counters. The receipt and parent completion repeat both digests, and the selected `credential_parent_terminal` successor proves descent from that reservation and consumption. A digest-only, unselected, stale, foreign-operation, foreign-plan, foreign-lease, foreign-slot, foreign-commit, map-drifted, action-drifted, selector-drifted, already-abandoned, or counter-reused reservation rejects before credential-owner anchor publication or effect.

For a structured-refresh mutation, parent selection precedes credential-owner reservation. Worker constructs the complete `RefreshCredentialMutationReservationCoreV1`, publishes and reopens its `mutation_reserved` child, publishes and reopens the immediate outer-operation child-head successor, and compare-and-swaps/reopens the unchanged outer anchor. Only that selected relation permits credential owner to take `mutation.lock`, reserve capacity, or publish sequence zero. If no credential-owner anchor or object for the reserved commit ID exists, recovery may either resume that byte-identical reservation or select its `abandoned_pre_effect` terminal disposition after a same-descriptor complete absence proof; it cannot reclassify inventory, select another slot/action/target, or reuse either ordinal. Once any matching credential-owner object or anchor exists, abandonment is forbidden and recovery follows only that exact owner chain.

`CredentialOwnerReservationAbsenceProofV1={schema_version:1,kind:"credential_owner_reservation_absence_proof_v1",operation_id,operator_control_request_digest,refresh_credential_mutation_plan_digest,refresh_capacity_lease_object_digest,refresh_mutation_reservation_digest,credential_child_id,credential_child_ordinal,planned_slot_ordinal,credential_commit_id,source_row_ref_digest,writer_reachability_entry_digest,credential_mutation_intent_action_digest,credential_mutation_target_selector_digest,mutation_lock_identity_digest,credential_owner_store_identity_digest,selected_outer_operation_object_digest,selected_outer_anchor_digest,credential_store_enumeration_digest,matching_anchor_count:0,matching_object_count:0,matching_receipt_count:0,matching_temporary_count:0,matching_action_attempt_count:0,observed_tick_ns,nonce,mac}` is closed. While holding the same reopened `mutation.lock`, the credential owner enumerates the retained credential-store descriptor, canonicalises every regular-leaf basename/identity/content digest in lexical byte order into `credential_store_enumeration_digest`, and proves that no leaf, selected anchor, receipt, publication temporary, capacity-consumption mismatch, or attempt-bearing action object matches the exact reserved commit. A proof is at most 16,384 bytes. It is written through sole grammar `absence-proofs/.<operation_id>.<credential_child_id>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`, file-synced, no-replace renamed to `absence-proofs/<credential_owner_reservation_absence_proof_digest>.json`, directory-synced, and same-descriptor reopened byte-, MAC-, digest-, lease-, reservation-, outer-anchor-, lock-, and enumeration-identically. A same-count assertion, digest without complete proof, proof observed outside the held lock, proof for a stale outer head, or any nonzero matching count is never absence authority.

Before either plan is published, the worker constructs both plans in memory, takes and reopens `mutation.lock`, proves the complete current store has all 64 OAuth-result object slots plus their sole publication temporary, one receipt slot plus one 32-object/four-temporary action-chain reserve, and the exact expanded cap below, and publishes sequence zero with state `selected`, zero consumption, null last/terminal fields. The one live receipt/action-chain reserve is reusable only after the preceding committed child's bound/clear/GC barrier; each abandoned proof consumes one of the fixed 256 proof finals permanently until outer receipt. No counter can be inferred from outer heads or repaired, skipped, or decremented.

For canonical lease bytes `L0` with `mac` omitted, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_co_refresh_capacity,ASCII("cq/credential-owner/refresh-capacity/mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(L0)) || L0))`; for complete bytes `L`, `credential_owner_refresh_capacity_lease_object_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/credential-owner/refresh-capacity/v1\0") || uint32be(len(L)) || L))`. Lease objects are at most 16,384 bytes and use `refresh-capacity/objects/<operation_id>.<canonical-sequence>.<digest>.json` plus random-exclusive `refresh-capacity/objects/.<operation_id>.<sequence>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`; `refresh-capacity/anchor` and `.anchor.<32-lower-hex>.tmp` are closed MACed `{schema_version:1,operation_id,sequence,lease_object_digest,mac}` selection. Object and anchor publication uses file sync, no-replace object rename, directory sync, exact-prior anchor CAS, directory sync, and same-descriptor reopen. At most one live lease anchor exists. After every mutation/OAuth child is terminal and no credential anchor or attempt remains, one `terminal_released` successor binds the selected outer terminal-capacity head before the lease anchor is cleared; only then may the outer operation acknowledge. A lease selected before any matching outer plan exists is recoverable only by holding `mutation.lock`, proving the operator store contains no selected plan, mutation reservation, OAuth child, result head, or terminal receipt for the bound operation/plan, selecting `orphan_abandoned`, clearing the lease anchor, and syncing both directories. A foreign plan, counter jump, early release, unselected lease object, missing predecessor, or live orphan ambiguity blocks every credential effect and new refresh admission.

The shared lock linearisation is exact. Reservation-child and outer-head publication completes and releases the operator-store exclusion before any waiter takes `mutation.lock`; thereafter the only nested order is `mutation.lock -> credential refresh-capacity anchor exclusion -> operator-operation store exclusion`, and no path waits for `mutation.lock` while retaining either later exclusion. An abandoning path retains `mutation.lock` while it performs the final same-descriptor enumeration; publishes, exact-prior-anchor-CAS-selects, syncs, and reopens the immediate lease-consumption successor binding the reservation and incremented counter; publishes and reopens the absence proof bound to that selected successor; publishes and reopens the embedded abandoned child; publishes and reopens the matching outer-head successor; and CAS-selects, syncs, and reopens the outer anchor. It releases the lock only after those selections agree in that order. A committing owner retains the same lock, reopens the selected lease, reservation child, outer head and anchor, and revalidates immediately before publishing credential-owner sequence zero that no matching proof or `abandoned_pre_effect` successor exists. Whichever path first obtains the lock may select its complete edge; after lease-consumption plus proof/outer selection, sequence zero rejects, and after sequence-zero/credential-anchor selection, absence and abandonment reject. Crash recovery reacquires the lock and resumes only the first missing edge in `lease-consumption successor -> absence proof -> abandoned child -> outer-head successor -> outer-anchor CAS`; it never treats a predicted or orphan lease object, orphan proof, or orphan outer child as selected authority.

Before the first external effect, the credential owner reserves the complete bounded action, publishes sequence zero containing the selected `refresh_mutation_reservation_digest` when applicable to a random-exclusive temporary, file-syncs, no-replace renames, directory-syncs, reopens byte-identically, then compare-and-swaps and reopens the authenticated anchor. Each successor is exactly `sequence+1`, binds the previous complete object digest, repeats object durability, and CAS-replaces the unchanged anchor; only the reopened anchor selects an object. An orphan not selected by the anchor is never authority. Cross-store completion is strictly `mutation_reserved -> credential-owner reservation -> credential terminal -> credential parent terminal -> credential receipt -> credential receipt bound -> credential-anchor clear -> child terminal` for structured refresh and retains the existing suffix beginning at credential terminal for every other scope. Terminal publication first durably selects and reopens the credential terminal object and proves the action-specific credential generation plus any reserved child terminal while its anchor pins every predecessor. Ordinary operator control renders and flushes the safe outer result and selects one acknowledged successor; every structured-refresh persistent mutation instead selects the matching `RefreshCredentialMutationChildV1` `credential_parent_terminal` object and outer-operation child-head successor before the receipt, and normal request authority selects one `NormalCredentialParentTerminalV1` before response release. The credential owner reopens that exact parent store, outer anchor, selected reservation/parent object, predecessor relation, MAC, digest, plan slot, source kind, closed source-row reference, signed writer row, intent action, and typed target selector, publishes and reopens one receipt embedding the matching reservation digest and parent-completion union, and performs no parent or credential effect while either store is ambiguous. A refresh mutation child then selects and reopens its immediate `credential_receipt_bound` object plus outer child-head successor containing the reservation, receipt, and parent-completion digests; a normal parent selects its immediate `credential_receipt_bound` successor; an outer-result operator parent publishes its terminal receipt with the live receipt digest. Only after that scope-exact parent binding is reopened may the credential owner clear and directory-sync its anchor and release the predecessor, parent-terminal, selector, writer-row, reservation, and reserved-child pins. A bound refresh mutation child may then advance to committed `terminal` and the next contiguous actual ordinal; no next persistent mutation, provider effect, response, or outer acknowledgement is legal earlier. A crash before or after reserved-child publication, child reopen, outer-successor publication, outer-anchor CAS, credential sequence zero, credential-anchor CAS, any action phase, parent terminal, receipt, bound successor, anchor clear, GC, or child terminal resumes only the first missing edge from both reopened stores. It never fabricates an acknowledgement, treats response delivery as an operator acknowledgement, skips or reuses a planned slot, substitutes an action/selector/source row, sends a response before the normal binding, or clears either side early. Loss before a credential effect may terminalise `not_committed` only through the selected reservation/owner absence relation; loss after any attempt uses only the already selected action-specific recovery and never replays an external effect.

Without a selected refresh-capacity lease, the store admits exactly one key, one persistent lock, one anchor, at most 32 selected commit objects, at most 16 terminal receipts, and at most four publication temporaries: 55 regular files total and at most 4,194,304 bytes. A selected structured-refresh lease expands that same store by at most 256 absence-proof finals, one absence-proof temporary, 258 lease-chain objects, one lease-object temporary, one lease anchor, and one lease-anchor temporary: exactly `55 + 256 + 1 + 258 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 573` regular files. The expanded byte cap is exactly `4,194,304 + (256 * 16,384) + 16,384 + (258 * 16,384) + 16,384 + 4,096 + 4,096 = 12,656,640`. A commit object is at most 98,304 bytes, an ordinary credential anchor at most 4,096 bytes, a receipt at most 16,384 bytes, and each proof or lease object at most 16,384 bytes. Every exact base or leased maximum succeeds; file, category, object, receipt, proof, lease, temporary, per-object byte, or aggregate byte `+1` refuses before plan publication, reservation, or external effect. Under `mutation.lock`, receipt generation is zero only when no valid retained receipt exists and otherwise is the greatest retained `receipt_generation+1`; the unsigned 64-bit addition is checked and exhaustion refuses before lease selection or reservation. Collection orders candidates by `(receipt_generation,commit_id)`. A selected refresh `credential_receipt_bound` mutation-child head is the durable parent binding: after its outer successor, credential-anchor clear, and directory sync, its credential receipt digest becomes a non-resolving authenticated completion commitment and the live receipt/action/provenance-bundle/object chain is unpinned and may be collected before the next mutation. The outer terminal receipt later derives its digest array from those selected bound heads, not from reconstructed or still-live credential receipts. Thus at most one of the 256 sequential refresh-mutation receipts is newly pinned at once; the capacity lease reserves one receipt slot plus the full one-chain successor/temporary budget before plan publication, and sixteen otherwise pinned receipts refuse lease selection before any plan or mutation effect. Abandonment proofs and the selected lease chain remain pinned until the terminal outer object binds their complete digest projections; after terminal receipt publication they are removed in proof-ordinal then lease-sequence order, each parent directory is synced, and neither removal is evidence that a credential or OAuth effect may be replayed. Collection otherwise removes only the oldest parent-completed, unreferenced receipt and its now-unreferenced action, provenance bundle, and objects after proving no anchor, unresolved operator mutation child, normal request terminal/binding, manifest child, generation publication, or release receipt refers to either side and after syncing every unlink. Recovery reopens the root key, proves `credential_owner_key_fingerprint` equal to the bootstrap, composite authority, `ProxyInstanceContext`, launcher handoff, boot acknowledgement, and current release/store-open binding, then reopens the lock, credential and lease anchors, complete predecessor and lease chains, receipt/proof sets, signed writer row, selector bundle, generation and parent-operation references and verifies every MAC/digest/cap/counter and same-descriptor identity before resuming only the selected phase. Missing, unreadable, replaced, malformed, invalid, or fingerprint-mismatched `key` while any anchor, object, receipt, proof, lease, temporary, bootstrap, authority, runtime, or release reference exists is `credential_owner_store_unavailable`: V1 never regenerates a key, guesses an outcome, or performs an effect. A provably empty store may receive its first key only through the initialisation/activation key-publication transaction below before normal readiness; every other key-loss case requires explicit destructive reinitialisation outside V1.

Credential-owner key identity propagation is closed. The terminal-initialisation schemas above have one additional member `credential_owner_key_fingerprint:null|string` immediately before `created_at`: it is non-null in `FreshPrimaryInitialisationTerminalReceiptV1` and `LegacyImportInitialisationTerminalReceiptV1`, equals the selected key-preparation phase, bootstrap, every intervening primary authority generation, and final same-descriptor key reopen, and is null in `CandidateInitialisationTerminalReceiptV1`; in `InitialisationAbortTerminalReceiptV1` it is non-null exactly when a fresh-primary or legacy-import chain reached `credential_owner_key_prepared`, whose abort receipt and quarantine identity set then pin the inert key/root until terminal cleanup, while candidate requires null. Every immutable primary composite authority object and its anchor add non-null `credential_owner_key_fingerprint` beside the authority-key fingerprint; it is immutable, equals the selected bootstrap, and candidate authority/anchor require null. Primary `ProxyInstanceContext` adds a retained no-follow credential-owner key capability, its file-identity digest, and this fingerprint; candidate context has no capability and null fingerprint. Construction upgrades to that context only after same-descriptor reopening the key and checking bytes, owner, mode, link count, identity, fingerprint, bootstrap, and authority equality. Every credential-owner store open consumes that retained capability or a private-bootstrap-derived child capability for the same open file and repeats equality before reading an anchor/object/receipt or taking `mutation.lock`; path-only reopen and fingerprint-only trust are forbidden.

Runtime and release propagation is equally closed. `RuntimeLauncherHandoffV1` adds non-null `credential_owner_key_fingerprint` immediately before `created_at`; every primary `RuntimeBootAckV1` adds the same non-null member immediately before `acknowledged_at`, while candidate boot acknowledgements require null. The primary launcher can copy it only from the same reopened bootstrap/authority tuple, and the supervisor private-bootstrap grant to the worker binds both the fingerprint and the same-key file capability; supervisor and worker independently reopen and verify the key before publishing `worker.credential_owner_store` or any normal readiness acknowledgement. The following instance-scoped release objects add non-null `credential_owner_key_fingerprint` covered by their existing MAC/signature/digest: `PrimaryStagedReleaseOperationV1`, `PrimaryStagedReleaseOperationReceiptV1`, `ImportFinalisationReferenceManifestV1`, `PrimaryBundleRehearsalReceiptV1`, `ImportFinalisationReceiptV1`, `ImportFinalisationCompletionReceiptV1`, and every primary `authority-history.anchor` checkpoint. Each equals the selected bootstrap, current authority, every embedded primary boot acknowledgement and `worker.credential_owner_store` marker, and the same-descriptor store-open proof; finalisation and staged promotion revalidate all equal immediately before semantic-release or terminal-authority CAS. Candidate preflight/floor-validation and build-global `ReleaseArtifactSetV1`/construction reports contain no live instance key fingerprint: their `worker.credential_owner_store` marker instead binds the fixed key-policy/store-schema digest and candidate's null-key/read-only result. A non-null candidate key, a key value in any release object, a target/floor fingerprint mismatch, or a missing/stale primary fingerprint refuses before handoff, admission, rehearsal receipt, promotion, finalisation, history checkpoint, or store access.

Resolution first groups sinks by stable retained target identity `(device,inode(parent),basename)`; path-string equality is never authority. One generation performs at most one publication transaction per group. Different renderer kinds targeting one identity are invalid except the two Claude capability sinks. That permitted pair renders one canonical `{timestamp:<Unix-second int64>,models:[...]}` object: contributions are processed in table order, empty IDs reject, later contribution replaces the same byte-exact ID, and final exact `{id,max_input_tokens,max_tokens}` entries sort by descending UTF-8 ID byte length then ascending ID bytes. `claude_config_capabilities_v1` contributes complete synthetic catalogue; `claude_home_capabilities_v1` contributes complete registry Anthropic projection. When targets differ each receives only its own contribution. This rule prevents either complete-object writer from erasing the other at default shared target.

`claude_code_options_v1` admits absent file or one JSON object of at most 1 MiB, preserves every unrelated top-level member and every user/malformed option byte-semantically after canonical re-encoding, removes only entries matched by prior CQ fingerprint set or exact CQ marker, appends current managed entries, and replaces only two CQ ownership members. `codex_models_cache_v1` admits absent file or one JSON object of at most 16 MiB, preserves recognised `etag`, preserves `client_version` when current projection supplies none, replaces `models` and `fetched_at`, and rejects malformed recognised fields; unrecognised top-level fields remain byte-semantically present after canonical re-encoding. Complete Claude capability targets do not merge prior contents.

Authority stores group membership, sink IDs, retained parent identity, basename, source-generation digests, and keyed target/content fingerprints, never public raw path. Worker renders immutable root-local objects from one frozen registry/catalogue snapshot and operation clock. Supervisor-owned `ExternalProjectionPublisher` accepts only renderer ID plus preopened directory capability. It verifies owner/mode/link/ACL/mount/identity, reads absent-or-current target through retained parent with sink bound, records identity/digest, writes a random-exclusive `0600` temporary, file-syncs, reopens target immediately before commit, and compares same identity/digest or continued absence. Match permits no-replace/atomic rename and directory sync; mismatch discards temporary and rerenders from newly read preserved fields, at most twice. Second conflict returns `projection_concurrent_writer`, performs no target replacement, and degrades every member sink. Group success publishes one shared output digest/generation while retaining per-sink state. Crash before rename preserves old target; after rename recovery accepts only exact output digest. Final same-UID post-check writer race remains stated residual. Candidate owns no publisher and writes renderer outputs only below candidate root. Model overlay remains a registered external input opened read-only by runtime; only the closed operator command path below may mutate it.

Resolver matrix evaluates sinks independently. `claude_code_options_v1` and `claude_home_capabilities_v1` require captured home. `claude_config_capabilities_v1` uses nonempty `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` resolved once against captured CWD without home, otherwise requires home. `codex_models_cache_v1` uses nonempty `CODEX_HOME` resolved once against captured CWD without home, otherwise requires home. Home-resolution failure degrades only dependent sinks. Each sink state is exactly `effective|degraded|unavailable`; `info` and `doctor` expose sink ID, state, target-group digest, last safe error code, and generation only—never target path/content. `external_projection_v1` acknowledgement requires all six direct marker children from the exhaustive feature table plus the complete transitive `RequiredMarkerChildren(normal_claude_v1)` and `RequiredMarkerChildren(normal_codex_v1)` unions, including duplicate-target, merge-preservation, CAS-conflict, candidate-write-negative, Codex route/origin, and both provider differential cases. Missing/unavailable sink makes projection feature degraded but does not fail provider data plane; invalid capability, unsupported target collision, preservation failure, candidate external write, or either missing/inhibited provider dependency makes marker invalid and blocks activation.

Primary import captures one immutable `LegacyResolutionContextV1` before opening any source: exact relevant environment values, `UserHomeDir` result, `UserCacheDir` result, `Getwd` result, and keyed environment/result digest. `H`, `V`, and CWD are results, never assumed strings. `D` and `Q` are byte-exact outputs of actual `LegacyConfigDir()` and `cache.DefaultDir()`; `M` is byte-exact output of `modelregistry.OverlayPath`, requiring `H` only when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is empty. `C` is continuity directory selected by same-FD parsed legacy config. Each resolver first records raw baseline path. Relative raw path is sealed once against retained captured CWD; absolute raw path does not require CWD. Failed CWD capture makes only relative-path sources unavailable. Failed home capture makes every H-dependent source unavailable; failed `UserCacheDir` makes installed-validation namespace unavailable. Import cannot prove absence beneath unavailable mandatory root, so prepare blocks with exact safe resolver error rather than substituting empty home, `.`, another cache root, or later process environment. Resolver parity tests invoke actual baseline functions for every environment/home/cache/CWD branch and require identical raw path/error before sealing.

`SensitiveRetentionControllerV1` is an owner-scoped scheduler independent of the proxy supervisor, worker, foreground process, capture-enabled state, and instance desired mode. `claude_cq_keyring_v1` uses compile-time adapter `cq_native_keyring_v1` for exact service/account selectors committed from either an existing manifest row or the authenticated operation's planned new account; it launches no helper and exposes native Get/Set/Delete status classes to the credential owner without persisting their values. Account is the exact non-empty `AccountUUID`, and service is exactly `cq-claude-` plus the first eight lower-case hexadecimal characters of `SHA256(AccountUUID)`. `existing_manifest` binds that UUID and the zero-based ordinal of the first matching row under manifest order, exactly matching the baseline replacement loop even when later duplicate-UUID rows exist. `planned_new_account` is legal only when a fresh same-descriptor manifest observation proves no matching UUID row and the authenticated operation commits the same UUID before the native effect; this is the baseline first-login and missing-row path, not authority to select an arbitrary account. Existing-versus-new classification compares the complete UUID, never the eight-character service suffix: distinct UUIDs with the same `Hash8` service remain distinct `(service,account)` selectors. Upsert exactly preserves baseline `StoreCQAccount`: first issue one `Set`; on success issue no delete or retry; on any non-success issue one best-effort `Delete` of the same selector and then one retry `Set`, with the retry result determining baseline success. The ignored baseline delete result remains non-controlling but is recorded for recovery. The following manifest `replace`, including update of exactly that first matching row or append of the exact planned row, remains a distinct ordered child and is never inferred from keyring success. A crash or manifest-write failure after keyring success preserves the committed upsert and resumes or classifies only that already planned manifest child; it never repeats the upsert or silently treats the orphaned native item as manifest authority. The mapping authority is the following seven-row literal table and has no extension point. This table amends each named store's native publication grammar with every displayed destination-local namespace and no alias. Rows 1 and 5–7 retain the imported-receipt, manifest, receipt, and tombstone namespaces required by their native phase machines rather than collapsing the store to two names. Each immutable object, manifest, receipt, or tombstone uses its store's existing complete-object digest and object-first file-sync/no-replace/destination-directory-sync/reopen protocol; each selector uses that store's existing exact-prior or authenticated-absence CAS, file sync, directory sync, and reopen protocol. A `pre` namespace can be reached while constructing the already-reopened inert child relation and therefore requires an empty matching-entry-set observation in the proof. A `later` namespace is registered and bounded by its native store but is not required absent by this pre-authority proof; its residue is reconciled only by that store's native later-phase recovery and never counts as selection of the current child. Row 2 derives `intent_authority_generation` from the coordinator intent, reconstructs the complete proposed composite-authority successor from the reopened current authority plus the exact row-two child intent, recomputes its native digest, and constructs both the generation-prefixed final basename and object temporary beneath `R`; supplied generation, digest, control-directory locator, or digest-only basename rejects. Any implementation or recovery path using a temporary outside the complete row registry cannot produce this proof.

A row mismatch, caller-supplied alternate store or locator, scalar lock identity, reordered/incomplete lock vector, wrong lock mode, path reopen, unbounded glob, nonempty proof-required namespace, extra or omitted proof-required namespace, a `later` namespace inserted into the proof, alternate quarantine discriminator, non-one start, gap, reused ordinal, wrong terminal value, observation before the final directory sync, or over-cap `Q` is not evidence.

`OperationCoordinatorPreAuthorityAbortProofV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,domain,coordinator_intent_digest,coordinator_anchor_digest,coordinator_intent_object_identity_digest,child_kind,child_intent_digest,child_intent_object_identity_digest:null|string,intent_authority_generation,reopened_authority_generation,reopened_authority_object_digest,reopened_active_initialisation_ref:null,reopened_active_operation_ref:null,reopened_active_initialisation_abort:null,child_selection_absence_proof:OperationCoordinatorChildSelectionAbsenceProofV1,child_selection_absence_proof_digest,checkpoint:"before_authority_selection"}` is closed.
