The sole abort successor is an immediate phase-`terminal` object with the intent as predecessor, next sequence, selected-authority fields null, `terminal_outcome:"aborted"`, `terminal_proof_digest=pre_authority_abort_proof_digest`, the complete proof embedded byte-identically, and null reset supersession. It never selects or terminalises the child. Before that terminal object is selected, recovery must reobserve the same exhaustive store/lock/locator set and reproduce the deterministic contiguous observation ordinals and byte-identical canonical proof bytes; after selection it copies only the reopened signed terminal object's embedded proof into the deterministic receipt. Receipt recovery and lookup reopen the terminal chain and receipt, recompute both nested digests, and verify the receipt signature without re-observing a mutable child store; the durable receipt is the historical zero-action authority and pins the inert child intent until publication completes. A null intent generation, unreadable-authority reset, reset-supersession intent, changed authority generation/object, selected child, any non-null authority reference including `active_initialisation_abort`, later coordinator phase, missing locator or observation, temporary-inventory drift, noncanonical observation ordinal, or any observed post-authority action forbids abort and permits only the already-defined exact recovery path.

`OperationCoordinatorTerminalReceiptV1={schema_version:1,receipt_kind:"ordinary_terminal|reset_supersession",operation_id,domain,child_kind,child_intent_digest,coordinator_object_digest,coordinator_sequence,coordinator_chain:[{sequence,object_digest}],ordinary_terminal:null|{terminal_outcome,terminal_proof_digest,pre_authority_abort_proof:null|OperationCoordinatorPreAuthorityAbortProofV1,selected_authority_generation,selected_authority_object_digest,reset_supersession,displaced_receipt_digest},reset_supersession:null|{selecting_reset_operation_id,selecting_reset_intent_digest,unreadable_authority_proof_digest,displaced_terminal_outcome:"superseded_authority_unreadable"},signature}` is closed. The chain is nonempty, strictly contiguous from sequence zero, contains each selected coordinator object exactly once, and ends at `coordinator_sequence`/`coordinator_object_digest`. `ordinary_terminal` requires that payload non-null and `reset_supersession` null; its common identity, complete chain, terminal fields, selected-authority nullability, proof digest, and pre-authority-abort-proof nullability/bytes must equal the reopened terminal coordinator object. The embedded proof is non-null exactly for the typed `aborted` edge and its independently recomputed digest equals `terminal_proof_digest`; every mapped child-terminal outcome requires it null. Within that payload, `reset_supersession` and `displaced_receipt_digest` are either both null or both non-null; the non-null form is legal only for `domain:"authority_reset"`, repeats the terminal object's exact reset-supersession value, and reopens the named receipt as `receipt_kind:"reset_supersession"`. `reset_supersession` requires the other payload null, common identity and chain equal the displaced unfinished operation through the object named by the selecting reset intent, the selecting fields and unreadable-authority proof equal that intent's exact `reset_supersession`, and no selected-authority or success interpretation. Unknown fields, mixed payloads, a terminal receipt for an unmapped row, or any field inferred rather than reopened reject.

Receipt addressing and authentication are exact. `operation_key=lowerhex(SHA256(ASCII("cq-operation-coordinator-operation-key-v1\0") || CanonicalJSONV1({schema_version:1,operation_id})))`; the only final name is `receipts/<operation_key>.json`. For `R0=CanonicalJSONV1(receipt excluding signature)`, `receipt_digest=lowerhex(SHA256(ASCII("cq-operation-coordinator-terminal-receipt-v1\0") || uint32be(len(R0)) || R0))` remains the separate domain-separated receipt identity, while `signature=Ed25519.Sign(signing.key,R0)` follows the global canonical-signature rule. Every coordinator-receipt reference, including `displaced_receipt_digest` and any child-terminal, history, external-reference, or recovery authority, is exactly that 64-lower-case-hex string; raw 32-byte, base64, upper-case hexadecimal, omitted-frame, wrong-frame, or differently framed values reject. Signing the receipt digest, signing `ASCII("cq-operation-coordinator-terminal-receipt-signature-v1\0") || receipt_digest`, or treating either form as an alternate verification input rejects. A receipt MAC is forbidden because the bootstrap-pinned public verifier is the recovery verifier. Publication creates `receipts/.tmp-<operation_key>-<128-bit-lowerhex>` with create-new/no-follow and mode `0600`, writes the one canonical byte string, file-syncs, installs the final name no-replace, syncs `receipts/`, reopens the final regular file no-follow, and requires byte-identical canonical bytes, operation key, digest, signature, owner, mode, link count, and stable identity before treating it as durable. An already-present final file is idempotent only when every reopened byte and identity predicate matches; otherwise it is `generation_conflict`. Temporary cleanup is directory-synced and never makes a missing final receipt durable.

Capacity admission counts complete file content, not directory metadata, and treats every declared object/query/envelope number as an upper bound rather than a promise that a closed schema can be padded to equality. `signing.key` and `verifier` are each exactly 32 bytes; anchor and every receipt are at most 65,536 bytes; every coordinator object is at most 524,288 bytes. An ordinary chain has at most one object for each of `intent|authority_selected|child_active|terminal`. Reset supersession may retain at most the displaced three-object nonterminal prefix followed by the reset's four objects, so seven active objects is the closed maximum. With sixteen ordinary terminal receipts, one reset-supersession receipt, one immutable-content-temporary reservation of 524,288 bytes, and one anchor-temporary reservation of 65,536 bytes, the structural ceiling is `1+1+1+7+16+1+2 = 29` files and the conservative byte reserve is `32+32+65,536+(7*524,288)+(17*65,536)+524,288+65,536 = 5,439,552`, within the independent 8,388,608-byte ceiling; the conservative receipt reserve is `17*65,536 = 1,114,112` bytes. The matching-entry-set query input is at most 8,192 bytes and consumes no leaf or store byte. The largest derived child-selection proof is row 1 or 5 with two lock rows, one selector observation, and two temporary-namespace observations carrying two context-bound empty matching-entry-set digests; the complete later-phase registry is verifier-derived through `derived_store_binding_digest` and is not duplicated as proof observations. Its canonical `Q` is at most 24,576 bytes and its enclosing `P` is at most 32,768 bytes. For `R=CanonicalJSONV1(the complete signed ordinary-terminal receipt containing P)`, the receipt envelope is exactly `len(R)-len(P)` and is at most 32,768 bytes. The arithmetic reserve `32,768+32,768 = 65,536` is conservative nested capacity, not a claim that both closed encodings can attain their bounds simultaneously; actual complete `R` is always measured and is final authority. The same measured `P` must fit the 524,288-byte terminal coordinator-object upper bound without another file or temporary. Checked-in maximum-cardinality fixtures use the longest independently legal value for every closed member, record `len(Q)`, `len(P)`, `len(R)`, each envelope difference, every complete file length, the receipt subtotal, and the aggregate, and assert the actual measurements stay within their respective upper bounds with no padding or equality fiction. Bounded readers reject a raw matching-entry-set input, child-selection proof, pre-authority proof, receipt, coordinator object, key-bootstrap state, or recovery-authority query at the first byte above its complete-input bound before semantic parsing or mutation; after canonical parsing, envelope subtraction rejects the first byte above an envelope bound. A thirtieth file, eighth active object, seventeenth ordinary receipt, second reset-supersession receipt, third coordinator-store temporary, extra mapping/lock/proof-required-namespace observation, wrong row-specific observation count, conservative reservation above 5,439,552 bytes, or aggregate above 8 MiB refuses before child intent or external action. Native child-store later-phase temporary capacity remains governed by its row's independent cap and does not consume coordinator-store leaves. Ordinary admission reserves all seven object positions, both reset-related receipt positions, and both coordinator-store temporaries before publishing its child intent.

Lookup derives only the operation-keyed final name, reopens and fully verifies the receipt, requires its embedded operation ID byte-equal to the request, and returns its closed outcome without reopening or repeating child/authority action. After an ordinary receipt is durable and the anchor is retired, object GC derives the finite deletion set only from its authenticated `coordinator_chain`, reopens and verifies each exact content-addressed object before unlink, removes in reverse sequence with `objects/` sync after each boundary, and treats absence as progress only for a listed digest. Crash recovery before final receipt durability reconstructs and republishes only the deterministic receipt from the still-selected terminal object; after receipt durability it performs only missing anchor/object retirements. For reset supersession, the anchor CAS first selects the reset intent, then recovery publishes/verifies the deterministic displaced-operation receipt before any reset child action; a crash on either side of that publication never resumes the displaced child. The later reset terminal receipt pins that displaced receipt digest. Only the reset terminal receipt, old-tree absence/tombstone proof, and zero retained displaced-child references permit collection of the supersession receipt; deletion and directory sync are resumable, and until complete its sole reserved slot blocks another operation that could require supersession.

The table plus the common typed pre-authority abort edge immediately below is the compile-time-total coordinator relation; no domain, child kind, selection rule, or terminal mapping exists outside that closed relation:

| Coordinator domain | Exact selected child | Authority selection | Child terminal → coordinator terminal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feature_activation` | `feature_activation`: `FeatureActivationIntentV1` | ordinary `active_operation_ref` CAS | `target_effective` → `target_effective`; `aborted_before_floor` → `aborted`; `rollback_inhibited` → `rollback_inhibited` |
| `authority_transition` | `authority_journal`: precomputed transition-journal intent | ordinary CAS, with subordinate token/lifecycle children named by the journal | `target_effective` → `target_effective`; `prior_restored` → `prior_restored` |
| `lifecycle_action` | `lifecycle_action`: standalone `LifecycleActionV1` | ordinary CAS | `target_effective` → `target_effective`; `prior_restored` → `prior_restored` |
| `staged_release` | `staged_release`: `PrimaryStagedReleaseOperationV1` | ordinary CAS; no release/floor/artifact selection | `terminal` with `staged` → `target_effective`; `terminal` with `cleared` → `cleared`; pre-selector `terminal` with `prior_restored` → `prior_restored` |
| `import_finalisation` | `import_finalisation`: `ImportFinalisationStateV1` | ordinary start CAS; finalisation-only terminal authority clears the reference after cleanup and before the child's terminal-generation policy acknowledgement/history/completion chain | child `terminal` with `released`, exact terminal-generation acknowledgement/history/completion proof → `target_effective` |
| `candidate_removal` | `quarantine_candidate_remove`: coordinator-owned `QuarantineLedgerV1` | ordinary CAS before any move or direct-leaf unlink | `tombstone` with exact removed-tree, direct-leaf absence, and no-job/process/listener proof → `removed` |
| `authority_reset` | `quarantine_authority_reset`: coordinator-owned `QuarantineLedgerV1` | ordinary CAS, or exact unreadable-authority/reset-supersession path | `tombstone` with exact inhibited replacement and old-tree absence proof → `quarantine_finalised` |

Every table row additionally permits exactly one coordinator-only pre-authority edge from its selected phase-`intent` object to `terminal`/`aborted` with the complete `OperationCoordinatorPreAuthorityAbortProofV1`; this edge has no child terminal object and is never inferred from a child outcome. Every other terminal coordinator object names the exact child terminal object and its domain-specific proof digest. A terminal value paired with any other row, a child terminal not listed in its row, an `aborted` value carrying neither the feature child's exact `aborted_before_floor` terminal nor the typed coordinator proof, or any typed proof attached to a mapped child-terminal outcome rejects. Initialisation abort is deliberately absent because its MACed initialisation ledger variant is pre-authority and never consumes the coordinator.

Start ordering is exact. Writer first publishes and syncs an immutable unselected child-intent object or a precomputable authority-journal intent projection. It then publishes coordinator intent referencing that digest and replaces/syncs coordinator anchor. One composite-authority CAS sets `active_operation_ref={operation_id,domain,coordinator_intent_digest,intent_authority_generation}` and, for an embedded authority transition, selects the matching journal intent in the same generation. Only after coordinator, authority reference, and child intent agree may a child anchor advance or any floor, artifact, manager, process, listener, token, quarantine, or evidence-release action occur. Child-only residue is inert. For each of the seven table rows, coordinator-active/authority-idle may only finish the exact CAS or take the typed pre-authority abort edge after reopening every fact required by its zero-action proof; no other abort is supported. Authority-active/child-anchor-lag may only checkpoint the named child. Any other mismatch is `generation_conflict` and permits only matching recovery.

`authority_reset` has one closed exception when the selected authority is unreadable and therefore cannot perform the ordinary CAS. A valid bootstrap object must pin the coordinator verifier and exact logical identity; the exclusive parent lifecycle lock, an inert signed reset-ledger intent, and a signed reset coordinator intent then jointly select only the reset while the data plane remains fail-closed. If the coordinator is idle, that reset intent has null `reset_supersession`, null selected-authority fields, sequence zero, and null previous digest. If a valid coordinator anchor instead selects an unfinished operation, the new reset intent must carry `reset_supersession={displaced_operation_id,displaced_domain,displaced_coordinator_object_digest,displaced_child_kind,displaced_child_intent_digest,unreadable_authority_proof_digest,displaced_terminal_outcome:"superseded_authority_unreadable"}`, set `intent_authority_generation` and selected-authority fields null, name the displaced object as `previous_object_digest`, and increment its sequence exactly once. One signed coordinator-anchor CAS from that exact displaced object to the reset intent is the supersession linearisation point: it terminally freezes the displaced child/reference, selects the reset child, and permits only the named reset to continue. The displaced object, child, unreadable-authority proof, and compact supersession receipt remain pinned through reset terminalisation and are never resumed, cleared, or interpreted as target/restoration success. A malformed or unverifiable coordinator cannot be superseded. If authority is readable, ordinary CAS/recovery ordering is mandatory and supersession is forbidden. The staged replacement's first inhibited authority selects the reset intent through the same `active_operation_ref`; terminal ordering is ordinary from that generation onward, and the reset terminal proof retains the supersession receipt when present. Missing bootstrap, verifier mismatch, an authority-readable mismatch, or any coordinator other than the idle or exactly superseded state forbids reset.

The inert child intent cannot contain its coordinator-object digest because that coordinator object names the child digest. Instead it binds operation ID, domain, and expected intent authority generation; the coordinator object selects its exact content digest; after the authority reference selects the coordinator, the child publishes and anchors one successor that names the coordinator intent digest before any action. Feature activation, lifecycle action, staged release, and import finalisation use that two-object selection rule. Local-token cutover is subordinate to its `config_adopt|listener_migration|legacy_import` authority-transition operation and shares that operation ID/reference; it never claims a second coordinator slot. Manager/listener work recorded in both authority journal and `LifecycleActionStore` uses one subordinate lifecycle child whose selected intent/attempt digests are named by the parent journal. A child cannot terminalise or act for another operation. The typed pre-authority abort is the sole terminal-ordering exception: after the proof is constructed and reopened, the writer publishes and exact-prior-CAS-selects its signed terminal coordinator object, publishes the deterministic ordinary-terminal receipt containing the same proof, and retires the coordinator anchor without selecting the authority or child; recovery from any boundary may only complete that same object/CAS/receipt/retirement suffix. For every ordinary table row except `import_finalisation`, the exact child terminal state and corresponding composite terminal authority commit first; authority clears `active_operation_ref` only in that mapped terminal generation; coordinator then selects its signed terminal object and publishes/syncs the operation-keyed compact terminal receipt. The `import_finalisation` row is governed only by its table-specific ordering: cleanup completes, terminal authority clears the reference, that terminal generation obtains its policy acknowledgement/history/completion proof, the child terminalises, and only then may the coordinator select its terminal object and publish the receipt. After the applicable receipt is durable, the writer reopens that receipt plus the exact terminal anchor/object through retained descriptors, requires their chain head, bytes, digests, signatures, identities, operation, phase, and sequence to agree, unlinks only that stable `anchor`, syncs the operations directory, and same-descriptor proves anchor absence; replacement or mismatch is `generation_conflict`. Only that retirement makes the coordinator idle and permits another ordinary sequence-zero intent. A crash before receipt resumes the selected terminal object, while a crash after receipt but before anchor retirement performs only that verified unlink/absence suffix; explicit lookup resolves the receipt and never repeats child or authority action. `rollback_inhibited` uses an inhibited terminal authority rather than an active one, but otherwise follows the ordinary order and its restricted remediation below. Crash in either direction recovers from exact cross-references and fresh topology, never repeats external action. Candidate removal is the authority-ref clearing exception because it intentionally moves/deletes the authority tree: parent coordinator terminalises only from the signed pre-move authority reference plus exact terminal absence/quarantine proof. Unreadable-authority reset supersession is the sole nonterminal coordinator-anchor exception and follows its exact reset intent/receipt rules above. Every mutator checks coordinator anchor and both authority active-reference fields before work; no second domain proceeds while any reference is active or mismatched.

`QuarantineLedgerV1` is a closed parent-scoped discriminated store at `<parent>/.cq-instance-<basename>.quarantine/{anchor,objects/,manifests/,tombstones/}`. Common entry fields bind operation ID, exact original and random quarantine sibling identities, retained device/inode/tree digest, `deletion_manifest_digest`, byte/entry/depth counts, `direct_leaf_actions:[{ordinal,phase:"pending|removing|removed",attempt_id,absence_proof_digest}]`, phase `intent_unselected|intent|moved|terminal_topology|purge_committed|tombstone`, tree-purge deletion-attempt ID, sequence, previous-object digest, and outcome. Direct-leaf actions are nonempty only for coordinator-owned `candidate_remove`, equal the manifest ordinals, and advance at most one target per successor: a present target is `pending` with both nullable fields null, then `removing` first fixes a fresh non-null attempt ID before unlink, then `removed` preserves it and adds exact absence proof; a target already absent in the inert snapshot starts `removed` with null attempt and the manifest's non-null pre-existing absence proof. Every other kind requires the empty array. The `owner_kind:"initialisation"` variant permits only `kind:"initialisation_abort"`, requires `{initialisation_intent_digest,abort_from_phase_digest,selecting_initialisation_phase_digest}`, forbids every coordinator field and signature, and authenticates each selected object, anchor, and tombstone with a distinct HMAC domain derived from `initialise.key`; the selecting-phase field is null only in inert `intent_unselected`, then becomes exact and immutable. The `owner_kind:"coordinator"` variant permits only `kind:"candidate_remove|authority_reset"`, requires `{coordinator_intent_digest,coordinator_domain}`, forbids initialisation-selection fields and MAC, and signs each object, anchor, and tombstone with the coordinator key; coordinator digest is null only in inert `intent_unselected`, then becomes exact and immutable after ordinary authority selection or the reset exception. Cross-kind chains, integrity algorithms, selectors, and tombstones reject. Every newly selected ledger intent requires an absent ledger anchor, sequence zero, and null previous digest; a retained tombstone is archive evidence, never a cross-operation predecessor.

The deletion registry is one immutable `QuarantineDeletionManifestV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,owner_kind,roots:[{root_ordinal,original_identity_digest,quarantine_identity_digest}],entries:[{ordinal,root_ordinal,parent_ordinal,basename_b64url,kind:"directory|regular|symlink|other_leaf",device,inode,mode,size,content_digest}],direct_leaf_targets:[{ordinal,parent_identity_digest,basename_b64url,kind:"regular|socket",expected_identity_digest,preexisting_absence_proof_digest}],entry_count,direct_leaf_count,max_depth,canonical_entry_bytes}`. Roots are ordered by ordinal and exactly match the ledger tree identities. Entries are preorder, ordinal-contiguous and duplicate-free; `parent_ordinal` names an earlier directory entry in the same root or is null only for an immediate child of its root. `basename_b64url` is the canonical unpadded base64url encoding of 1–255 raw basename bytes and decoded bytes may contain neither NUL nor slash nor equal `.` or `..`. Sibling decoded basenames are unique. `content_digest` is non-null exactly for regular tree files; size is exact for every tree leaf and zero for directories. Direct targets are ordinal-contiguous, duplicate-free, outside every quarantined root, and nonempty only for `candidate_remove`, where they contain exactly the candidate service plist, controller plist, and controller socket in that order. Each direct target records exactly one of a present expected identity or a same-descriptor pre-existing absence proof; its retained parent identity and basename are the sole deletion locator. Every complete tree entry or direct target is at most 1,024 bytes, depth is at most 16, and traversal may open a tree child only by its registered parent ordinal and decoded basename. For `M=CanonicalJSONV1(manifest)`, `deletion_manifest_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/quarantine-deletion-manifest/v1\0") || uint32be(len(M)) || M))`. Writer streams each retained tree once, securely inspects every direct target from its retained parent descriptor, rejects identity/type/count/byte/depth/encoding drift, publishes and syncs the content-addressed manifest by no-replace rename, and only then may publish the inert ledger intent that names it. Collision is acceptable only for byte-identical canonical content.

Limits are shared across both variants and aggregated across all live manifests: four live quarantine trees, three direct leaf targets per candidate-removal manifest, 512 MiB/tree, 1 GiB tree bytes, 32,768 combined tree entries/direct targets, depth 16, 34 MiB complete canonical manifest bytes, one parent-wide active purge, sixteen compact tombstones, and 36 MiB total ledger metadata including manifests and two temporaries. Each manifest is at most 34 MiB and the exact aggregate entry/direct-target/canonical-byte counters plus every direct-action successor are reserved before intent selection, rename, or unlink; an exact cap succeeds and any count, entry-size, manifest-size, tree-size, or metadata `+1` refuses before authority, tree, leaf, or ledger mutation. Before each direct unlink the finaliser reopens the retained parent and exact target without following links, requires the selected `removing` attempt and expected identity, then unlinks only that basename, syncs its parent, proves absence, and commits `removed`; mismatch is indeterminate and never deletes a replacement. Only after every direct target is `removed` may candidate removal commit terminal topology. Once rollback is no longer legal and the owning transaction's exact terminal topology and receipt are durable, its original destructive confirmation authorises one tree-manifest-bounded purge; the finaliser revalidates the same owner variant, selector, manifest digest, root identities, and every opened registered entry identity, never follows symlinks, crosses mounts, opens an unregistered child, or deletes lifecycle/coordinator files. Crash resumes only the selected direct-leaf or tree-purge attempt from retained descriptors and entry-level absence facts. Tombstone retains owner kind, operation, tree and direct-leaf identities/digests, manifest digest, counts, final direct-action set digest, and outcome but no path or content, and uses the same MAC/signature authority as its chain. After tombstone, complete manifest-wide absence proof, and the owning initialisation or coordinator terminal receipt are durable, writer atomically unlinks and parent-syncs the ledger anchor; only that retirement makes the ledger idle. A crash before the owning receipt leaves the tombstone selected, while a crash after the receipt performs only anchor retirement. GC may then unlink and parent-sync the unreferenced manifest; it may remove only an unreferenced oldest tombstone beyond the newest fifteen after the matching receipt/history checkpoint is durable. Referenced or indeterminate quarantine state or manifest is never reclaimed and blocks new work rather than exceeding cap.

`CandidateValidationControllerStoreV1` is the parent-owned selection and recovery authority for one current candidate validation run plus the newest two retained terminal-run authority capsules and lives at `<parent>/.cq-instance-<basename>.candidate-controller/{mutation.lock,anchor,objects/,manifests/,authority-runs/,authority-references/,authority-index,receipts/,validation-evidence/,controller.plist,controller.sock}` outside the candidate root and process tree. Each current or retained run has exactly one descriptor-relative `authority-runs/<validation_run_id>/` directory; no manifest, capsule, or retained verification dependency may live in another run's directory. It exists only for candidate role. `mutation.lock` is an owner-only mode-0600 regular file created, file-synced, and parent-directory-synced under the exact lifecycle inode held exclusively before the first controller object; its device/inode identity is retained by the parent, copied into the sequence-zero controller intent/state and the initialisation phase that selects that intent, and never replaced while any controller state, capsule, receipt, evidence, retirement, removal, export, or import reference exists. Crash recovery accepts the file only when that durable identity and the retained parent/store identities all agree. `K_candidate_controller_store=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=initialise.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/candidate-validation-controller-store/v1"),L=32)` remains parent-only and derives distinct state-anchor, state-object, terminal-receipt, bootstrap-commitment, command-channel, authority-capsule, authority-index, external-reference-ledger, validation-evidence-retirement, and validation-evidence-retirement-receipt keys. The runtime-evidence selection key is exactly `K_candidate_runtime_evidence_selection=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_candidate_controller_store,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/candidate-runtime-evidence-selection/v1"),L=32)` and likewise remains parent-only. For run ID bytes `R=ASCII(validation_run_id)`, the only subkey delivered to the controller is `K_candidate_controller_channel=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_candidate_controller_store,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/candidate-validation-controller-command-channel/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R)) || R,L=32)`; the controller never receives `initialise.key`, a retained controller-store directory descriptor, or any state/anchor/receipt/capsule/retirement key. The controller LaunchAgent label is `dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy.candidate-controller.<suffix>`, where `suffix` is the first sixteen lower-case hexadecimal characters of `HMAC-SHA256(K_candidate_controller_store,ASCII("cq/candidate-controller-label/v1\0") || uint32be(len(CanonicalJSONV1({parent_identity_digest,basename,validation_run_id}))) || CanonicalJSONV1(...))`. Its exact complete owner-only plist names the accepted controller executable digest, launchd-owned `controller.sock` endpoint, validation run, candidate identity, runtime-envelope digest, candidate-prepared-core digest and object-identity digest, capability-manifest digest and object-identity digest, but no controller-store directory capability, credential, secret, or self-digest; the plist, job, process, and socket are distinct from the sealed candidate job and tree. For complete rendered plist bytes `P`, `controller_plist_content_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-validation-controller-plist/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))` is stored only in the inert controller intent. Before bootstrap and again before selecting Ready, the parent opens the plist without following links through the retained controller-store descriptor and requires its exact bytes, stable identity, and recomputed digest to equal that intent; recovery never regenerates or adopts different bytes.

`CandidatePreparedManifestCoreV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,validation_run_id,candidate_proxy_instance_id,parent_identity_digest,source_registry_revision,target_release_bundle_digest,target_release_set_digest,client_build,client_executable_digest,launcher_digest,supervisor_digest,worker_digest,profile_set_digest,primary_bootstrap_digest,primary_authority_digest,accepted_floor_digest,selected_config_object_digest,manager_definition_digest,listener_tuple_digest,candidate_root_plan_digest,declared_read_inputs:[{ordinal,source_kind:"credential_manifest|credential|target_release_bundle|installed_client|local_token_client_registry|launcher|supervisor|worker|candidate_policy",descriptor_kind:"regular|directory",source_id_digest,parent_identity_digest,basename_b64url,identity_digest,keyed_content_fingerprint,byte_count}],declared_read_input_count}` is the sole pre-input authority for candidate protected-static inputs and every registered retained read-only input required after prepare. Entries are ordinal-contiguous from one, sorted by `(source_kind,source_id_digest,identity_digest)`, duplicate-free by source ID and retained identity, and exact projections of `ExternalAuthoritySourceRegistryV1`; basename bytes, ownership, mode, link count, local-APFS mount, identity, content, parser, and byte bounds are revalidated on the same retained descriptors. The mandatory `--local-token-client-registry` contributes exactly one `local_token_client_registry` entry whose retained identity and keyed fingerprint equal the registered manifest source and whose parsed revision/client/request-sender/domain/transport projection equals candidate authority and barrier-bootstrap input; omission, substitution, or representation under another source kind refuses before input publication. `declared_read_input_count` equals the array length and is 1–46; the existing cap includes this mandatory row and does not expand the descriptor envelope. Raw token, bearer, credential bytes, signing key, controller key, later object digest, later filesystem identity, or unregistered source is forbidden. Complete `CanonicalJSONV1` bytes `M` are 1–65,536 bytes and round-trip byte-identically. `candidate_prepared_manifest_core_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-prepared-manifest-core/v1\0") || uint32be(len(M)) || M))`. Before capability-manifest, controller-runtime-envelope, initialisation-input, tree, authority, or intent publication, the parent writes and syncs `M` through a random-exclusive temporary, no-replace renames it to `manifests/prepared-<candidate_prepared_manifest_core_digest>.json`, syncs `manifests/`, and same-descriptor reopens exact canonical bytes; collision succeeds only on byte equality, and the reopened stable file identity produces `candidate_prepared_manifest_core_object_identity_digest`. The only legal prelaunch dependency order is prepared core -> capability manifest -> `CandidateValidationControllerRuntimeEnvelopeV1` -> `InitialisationInputManifestV1` -> inert controller intent. The controller-signed validation-case catalogue set, broker policy, candidate runtime resource envelope, and their source identities do not exist yet and are forbidden in every prelaunch object. Each persisted manifest binds the complete preceding digest/object-identity pair, the controller runtime envelope and input bind both manifest pairs, and no earlier object names a later digest or identity; omission, reversal, foreign pairing, regeneration, or adoption of different bytes refuses before candidate execution.

`CandidateValidationControllerRuntimeEnvelopeV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_validation_controller_runtime_envelope_v1",operation_id,validation_run_id,candidate_proxy_instance_id,candidate_prepared_manifest_core_digest,candidate_prepared_manifest_core_object_identity_digest,controller_capability_manifest_digest,controller_capability_manifest_object_identity_digest,process_birth_limit:1,exec_limit:1,wall_time_limit_seconds:1260,cpu_time_limit_seconds:180,address_space_limit_bytes:1073741824,resident_memory_limit_bytes:536870912,fd_limit:258,socket_limit:128,combined_output_limit_bytes:32768}` is the sole prelaunch resource envelope and is sealed into the plist and Ready receipt. It contains no controller public key or key ID, validation-case/catalogue, broker-policy, candidate-runtime-envelope, provider credential, or later source digest. For complete canonical bytes `E`, `controller_runtime_envelope_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-validation-controller-runtime-envelope/v1\0") || uint32be(len(E)) || E))`; the parent and controller recompute the same digest from the byte-identical embedded value. Its wall bound is the complete 300-second prepare bound plus the 960-second Begin-bound run. `CandidateValidationControllerCapabilityManifestV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,validation_run_id,candidate_proxy_instance_id,candidate_prepared_manifest_core_digest,candidate_prepared_manifest_core_object_identity_digest,controller_lifecycle_slot_plan_digest,descriptors:[{ordinal,kind:"lifecycle_shared_lock_slot_plan|candidate_validation_evidence|declared_read_input",access:"shared_lock|read_write|read_only",identity_digest,lifecycle_slot_index,lifecycle_slot_role,prepared_input_ordinal}],descriptor_count}` is closed, canonical, and fixed after the prepared core but before the resource envelope, input manifest, and inert controller intent; it deliberately omits every later digest and identity. Its complete `CanonicalJSONV1` encoding is 1–65,536 bytes, contains no duplicate member, and must round-trip byte-identically through the strict parser. Ordinals one through seventeen are an abstract slot plan for the retained lifecycle inode, not descriptions that exist before launch: slot index zero/role `controller`, followed by slot indices one through sixteen/role `runtime_holder`, where ordinal equals slot index plus one; each row's `identity_digest` is the same retained lifecycle-inode identity. Seventeen slots are the controller hold plus the sealed `CandidateRuntimeResourceEnvelopeV1` maximum of sixteen candidate process births. `controller_lifecycle_slot_plan_digest` is the framed digest of the complete ordered `{slot_index,slot_role,lifecycle_inode_identity_digest}` projection. It makes no prelaunch OFD-identity or kernel-nonce claim. Ordinal eighteen is exactly the controller-store `validation-evidence/` directory with `read_write`. Every remaining descriptor is the one-to-one ordinal-shifted projection of prepared-core input `n` at capability ordinal `n+18`, with `declared_read_input`, `read_only`, equal retained identity, and `prepared_input_ordinal=n`. Lifecycle-plan and evidence entries require null prepared-input ordinal; declared inputs forbid both lifecycle-slot fields. `descriptor_count=declared_read_input_count+18` and is exactly 19–64. Under the 258-FD controller envelope, 66 slots are reserved for transferred manifest capabilities—at most 64 prepared capabilities plus exactly two late release-input capabilities—128 for the existing socket cap, and 64 for stdio, command/launchd/process-observation, and all other non-manifest non-socket descriptors; no partition borrows from another, and the first prepared-manifest descriptor over 64, late-input descriptor over two, ancillary-data, or partition `+1` rejects before transfer or launch. No other kind/access/slot/projection pairing is legal. For complete canonical bytes `C`, `controller_capability_manifest_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-validation-controller-capability-manifest/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`. The parent streams `C` through the same random-exclusive/sync/no-replace/reopen protocol to `manifests/capability-<controller_capability_manifest_digest>.json`; an existing name succeeds only on exact byte equality, and the reopened stable identity produces `controller_capability_manifest_object_identity_digest`. Resource envelope, input, inert intent, plist, and prelaunch controller state bind both prepared-core and capability-manifest digest/object-identity pairs plus the slot-plan digest; only Ready and later state may additionally bind the post-open pool-attestation digest below. Recovery derives both manifest locators only from the retained controller-store descriptor plus their digests, reopens the two exact identities and bytes in dependency order, and never renders, substitutes, or regenerates either. The controller receives those persisted bytes and capabilities only through the authenticated one-shot `SCM_RIGHTS` transfer below; it may retain them, its owner-only IPC, exact launchd candidate submit/stop authority, and process-observation primitives, but receives no lifecycle-parent or controller-store directory descriptor and may not path-reopen a transferred capability. It has no primary mutable/control/listener authority, credential/keychain write, external network outside the closed `CandidateProviderEgressBrokerV1` official-origin role, arbitrary launchd, debug, child-exec, or parent store-key capability; no candidate role receives that broker network or vault authority. Kernel limits and an immutable sandbox profile restrict descriptor-relative operations to the manifest access modes at process creation. After process creation the controller generates its 32-byte Ed25519 seed inside locked, non-dumpable process-private memory; the seed is never inherited, persisted, sent, logged, or returned and is destroyed on exit. Missing enforcement, key-memory protection, prepared-core equality, canonical-byte equality, slot-plan cardinality/order, descriptor projection/count/partition bound, or first exact `+1` invalidates before further candidate work and transfers only sealed job/PID identities to parent cleanup.

`K_candidate_controller_authority_capsule=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_candidate_controller_store,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/candidate-validation-controller-authority-capsule/v1"),L=32)` and `K_candidate_controller_authority_index=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_candidate_controller_store,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/candidate-validation-controller-authority-index/v1"),L=32)` remain parent-only. Each terminal controller run is verified through one immutable parent-MACed `CandidateValidationControllerAuthorityCapsuleV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_validation_controller_authority_capsule_v1",validation_run_id,candidate_proxy_instance_id,controller_store_mutation_lock_identity_digest,candidate_prepared_manifest_core_digest,candidate_prepared_manifest_core_object_identity_digest,controller_capability_manifest_digest,controller_capability_manifest_object_identity_digest,candidate_release_input_manifest_digest:null|string,candidate_release_input_manifest_object_identity_digest:null|string,authority_support_objects:[{ordinal,role:"prepared_manifest|capability_manifest|release_input_manifest",content_digest,source_object_identity_digest,final_basename_b64url,snapshot_object_digest,snapshot_object_identity_digest}],controller_plist_canonical_bytes_b64url:null|string,controller_plist_content_digest,controller_plist_identity_digest:null|string,controller_service_label,controller_job_bootstrap_attempt_id:null|string,controller_job_identity_digest:null|string,controller_process_identity_digest:null|string,controller_socket_identity_digest:null|string,controller_ready_receipt_digest:null|string,controller_ready_receipt_object_identity_digest:null|string,controller_public_key:null|string,controller_key_id:null|string,terminal_controller_receipt_digest,terminal_controller_receipt_object_identity_digest,terminal_evidence_anchor_digest:null|string,terminal_evidence_anchor_identity_digest:null|string,admission_controller_anchor_digest,admission_anchor_descendant_chain_digest,created_from_terminal_state_digest,external_reference_producer_catalogue_digest,external_reference_binding_set_digest,mac}` with no other member. The release-input digest/identity pair is both null exactly when no late manifest was selected; the job-attempt/job-identity pair is both null exactly when the chain never reached `job_bootstrap_attempted`; the process/socket identities are both null exactly when it never reached `socket_published`; the Ready digest/identity, public-key/key-ID, and terminal-evidence-anchor digest/identity pairs are all null exactly when it never selected Ready/evidence; and the plist canonical-bytes/identity pair is both null exactly when it never reached `plist_published`. Support rows are ordinal-contiguous in the listed role order, contain the two mandatory manifests plus the release-input manifest exactly when selected, and identify byte-identical owner-only run-directory snapshots by their exact content-addressed basename, complete snapshot digest, and stable identity; when non-null, the strict base64url plist bytes decode to the complete rendered plist and recompute its content digest. ### `ProxyAuthorityStore`

One authority generation commits control, routing, executable, compatibility, and transition state together. Private tree is:

```text
<instance-state-root>/
  runtime.lock
  authority.key
  authority.lock
  authority.anchor
  authority-history.anchor
  authority-objects/<generation>-<sha256>.json
  control.sock
  launcher/cq-proxy-launcher
  artifacts/payloads/<sha256>/cq
  artifacts/manifests/<sha256>.json
```

`authority.key` is OS-CSPRNG 256-bit root secret. HKDF labels derive independent keys for object MAC, history-anchor MAC, compatibility-intent digest, live control, session HMAC, caller-credential fingerprint, and CQ-local-token fingerprint. Keys and tokens never appear in authority JSON. Compatibility record uses stable bootstrap Ed25519 signer, separate from `authority.key`, so candidate verification does not require primary root secret.

Each immutable authority object has bounded canonical JSON, `schema_version`, `authority_generation`, previous object digest, key fingerprint, operation-coordinator verifier fingerprint, `active_operation_ref`, `active_initialisation_ref`, `active_initialisation_abort`, candidate-only `candidate_validation_run_id` and `candidate_controller_intent_digest`, required features, listener/config/service identity, `normal_credential_origin_binding_set_digest`, desired traffic mode, rescue suspension, full routing-policy generation, exact artifact manifest, compatibility floor, and transition journal. The candidate fields are non-null exactly for candidate role, immutable for its lifetime, and must equal the candidate input/bootstrap and parent controller intent; primary forbids them. Object MAC covers every field except itself. `authority.anchor` is sole atomic commit point and contains schema, committed generation/object digest, key fingerprint, required-feature floor, and MAC. The three active-reference fields are a closed discriminated union: all are null in ordinary idle authority; at most one may be non-null; `active_operation_ref={operation_id,domain,coordinator_intent_digest,intent_authority_generation}` resolves through the retained parent coordinator, with `intent_authority_generation` null only for an unreadable-authority `authority_reset` intent carrying the exact reset exception and non-null otherwise; and `active_initialisation_ref={operation_id,initialisation_intent_digest,target_authority_generation}` may originate only on the first inhibited fresh-primary authority selected by the matching parent initialisation anchor; `active_initialisation_abort:null|{operation_id,initialisation_intent_digest,validation_run_id,external_reference_binding:CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1,quarantine_intent_digest,quarantine_identity_set_digest}` is non-null only on a candidate-authority successor selected after candidate `authority_committed` and abort-quarantine selection but before controller-anchor selection, directly carries the row-one binding, and inhibits every action except the exact quarantine/reference-retirement abort suffix. That initialisation reference must remain byte-identical on every successor generation in the same inhibited initialisation chain until the final active generation clears it, and no later or unrelated authority may introduce or adopt one. Missing, mismatched, dual, or concurrent references inhibit every mutation/data-plane publication except recovery of the exactly named transaction.

Commit protocol under retained `authority.lock`:

1. Verify current anchor and referenced object from retained descriptors.
2. Write one random-exclusive object temporary, sync it, rename to content-addressed final name, and sync object directory.
3. Write and sync random anchor temporary, atomically replace anchor, then sync root directory.
4. Only new anchor makes object effective. Orphan objects are ignored and may be garbage-collected after next clean start. Anchor never references an unsynced object.

This gives one cross-domain linearisation point and crash recovery at every write boundary. It detects missing, altered, replayed, or mismatched objects while current anchor survives. It does not claim protection against same-UID rollback of entire instance root, key, and anchor together; that actor is inside local-user trust boundary. Existing compatibility floor supplies an independent primary downgrade check, but not tamper-proof monotonic storage.

Primary `CompatibilityFloorStore` owns exact legacy-global paths above. `InspectPrimary` is dual-format and never creates/converts/refuses fact collection: positive decimal scalar `s` becomes compatible when `s <= compiled_epoch`, incompatible when higher; missing, malformed, bad signature/key/root/bootstrap-key/root mismatch, or unknown feature become typed facts. `EnforcePrimary` consumes same fact and refuses every data-plane/ordinary mutation unless compatible. For bounded duplicate-free structured record, `epoch <= compiled_epoch`, supported `required_features`, matching immutable tuple `(proxy_instance_id,state_root_digest,bootstrap_key_fingerprint,authority_key_fingerprint,verification_key_fingerprint)`, and valid Ed25519 signature are compatible. Primary obtains authority-key fingerprint from owner-only context; candidate verifies public tuple against sealed manifest and opens no primary secret. Only explicit primary initialisation, legacy import, or structured-to-structured feature activation writes primary floor.

Feature activation acquires stable lifecycle lock, retained `authority.lock`, then retained `compatibility_epoch.lock`, never reverse, re-reads coordinator/bootstrap/authority/floor, and holds them through floor file/parent sync and authority object/anchor/root sync. While committed floor receipt is unmatched by authority, every mutation except exact receipt resume or quarantine recovery refuses. `AdvancePrimary` CAS-converts missing, scalar, or prior JSON to `{schema_version,epoch,required_features,proxy_instance_id,state_root_digest,bootstrap_key_fingerprint,authority_key_fingerprint,verification_key_fingerprint,activation_receipt_id,target_intent_digest,signature}` with random-exclusive write, file sync, rename, and parent sync. Missing is accepted only during proven first primary initialisation. Scalar `s <= compiled_epoch` converts only inside ticketed initialisation/import, with target epoch at least `max(s,compiled_epoch)`; higher scalar refuses. `feature activate activate` accepts structured input only and otherwise returns `compatibility_incompatible` plus import remediation. Structured record may only increase epoch/feature set and preserve complete immutable tuple. `target_intent_digest` is independently precomputable keyed digest over length-prefixed operation ID, target authority generation, immutable tuple, and sorted union current+target features. It excludes mutable bootstrap generation/object, listener, manager, service label, config selection, target authority object, and floor-record digest. Matching authority object references exact committed floor digest, intent digest, and coordinator intent digest.

Before scalar conversion, immutable ticket binds signed `PreSchemaWriterCatalogueV1={schema_version:1,authority_baseline_commit,bootstrap_key_fingerprint,proxy_config_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest,legacy_atomic_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest,entries:[{executable_sha256,release_manifest_digest,writer_capability:"scalar_v1|structured_v1|none"}],allowed_importer_sha256,nonce,signature}` and signed `PreSchemaLaunchSourceCatalogueV1={schema_version:1,authority_baseline_commit,bootstrap_key_fingerprint,writer_catalogue_digest,home_identity_digest,entries:[{source_id:"cq_candidate_proxy_v1|cq_proxy_v1|cq_refresh_v1|homebrew_proxy_v1",acquisition_rule:"homebrew_services_info_v1|launchctl_user_job_and_plist_v1",domain,job_label,plist_presence:"present|absent",plist_path_identity_digest:null|string,plist_digest:null|string,program_arguments_digest:null|string,resolved_executable_sha256:null|string,writer_capability:"scalar_v1|structured_v1|none",loaded_state:"loaded|unloaded|not_applicable",spawn_policy_digest:null|string,stop_action:"brew_services_stop_cq|launchctl_bootout|none",pre_floor_restore_action:"brew_services_start_cq|launchctl_bootstrap|none",post_floor_disposition:"retire|restore_structured|none"}],nonce,signature}`. Both catalogues use sorted, duplicate-free entries and the bootstrap key signs `CanonicalJSONV1` with signature omitted. Both non-null reachability-catalogue digests are inside those signed bytes; the launch catalogue's `writer_catalogue_digest`, the import ticket, and every matching `WriterQuiescenceAttemptV1.writer_catalogue_digest` therefore bind them transitively. The launch catalogue contains exactly four rows, one for each listed source ID and no other ID. A present row requires every plist-derived digest and `loaded|unloaded`; an absent row alone uses null plist-derived fields, `not_applicable`, `none` writer capability, and `none` actions. Present action tuples are fixed: `homebrew_proxy_v1=(brew_services_stop_cq,brew_services_start_cq,retire)`, `cq_candidate_proxy_v1=(launchctl_bootout,launchctl_bootstrap,retire)`, `cq_proxy_v1=(launchctl_bootout,launchctl_bootstrap,retire)`, and `cq_refresh_v1=(launchctl_bootout,launchctl_bootstrap,restore_structured)`. The launch-source catalogue is exhaustive over managed sources, not just currently running processes. `homebrew_proxy_v1` is exact user-domain label `homebrew.mxcl.cq`, exact absolute `brew services info cq --json`, the securely retained sole selectable Homebrew plist from the lifecycle rules, `launchctl print gui/<effective-uid>/homebrew.mxcl.cq`, and agreeing argv/executable/process/listener facts; `cq_candidate_proxy_v1` is exact user-domain label `dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy.candidate`, securely retained `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy.candidate.plist`, `launchctl print gui/<effective-uid>/dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy.candidate`, exact argv `[resolved-cq-executable,"proxy","start","--port",<valid-non-primary-port>]`, and agreeing executable/process/listener facts; `cq_proxy_v1` is exact user-domain label `dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy`, securely retained `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy.plist`, `launchctl print gui/<effective-uid>/dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy`, and agreeing argv/executable/process/listener facts; `cq_refresh_v1` is exact user-domain label `dev.jacobcx.cq.refresh`, securely retained `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.jacobcx.cq.refresh.plist`, `launchctl print gui/<effective-uid>/dev.jacobcx.cq.refresh`, argv `[resolved-cq-executable,"refresh"]`, `RunAtLoad=true`, positive `StartInterval`, and stderr path `~/Library/Logs/cq/refresh.log`. Missing HOME, unsafe/unreadable plist ancestry, another selectable plist, label/argv/executable disagreement, unknown CQ launch source, or catalogue/source drift is `unclassified_cq_writer`; absence is authoritative only when the registered plist acquisition and user-domain `launchctl print` both prove no source for that exact ID. Catalogue names importer artifact, never prepare-process identity.

`LegacyAtomicWriterReachabilityCatalogueV1={schema_version:1,authority_baseline_commit,entries:[{entrypoint_id,entrypoint_symbol,implementation_symbol,call_chain_digest,source_id,writer_kind:"atomic_file|file_delete|file_move_no_replace|file_link_no_replace|socket_create|file_mode_change|lock_acquire|native_keychain_upsert|native_keychain_delete",final_grammar:null|string,temporary_grammar:null|string,transition_source_grammar:null|string,transition_destination_grammar:null|string,native_namespace:null|"claude_platform|claude_cq",operation_shape:null|"file_unlink|descriptor_unlink|rename_no_replace|secure_promote_no_replace|link_no_replace|unix_socket_create|chmod_0600|exclusive_lock_create_or_open|exclusive_lock_create_new|platform_update_or_add|cq_set_delete_retry_set|platform_repeated_service_delete|cq_manifest_selector_delete",failure_policy:null|"abort|continue",process_kind:"foreground_command|proxy_runtime"}],entry_set_digest}` is the closed source-derived catalogue for every registered pre-schema persistent leaf mutation, including a transition, cleanup, or lock edge that does not write JSON bytes. Every row names the exact fully qualified production `entrypoint_symbol` and the concrete production `implementation_symbol` that owns its terminal filesystem or native effect. `atomic_file` requires non-null final/temporary grammars and null transition/native/operation/policy fields; its call chain covers create, sync, replacement/no-replace rename, directory sync, and all temporary cleanup branches. `file_delete` requires one non-null final grammar, null temporary/transition/native fields, `file_unlink|descriptor_unlink`, and the caller-exact `abort|continue` policy. `file_move_no_replace|file_link_no_replace` require null final/temporary/native fields, non-null source and destination grammars, their exact move/link shape, and caller-exact policy. `socket_create|file_mode_change` require only a non-null transition destination grammar, respectively `unix_socket_create|chmod_0600`, and caller-exact policy. `lock_acquire` requires only a non-null transition destination grammar, caller-exact policy, and exactly `exclusive_lock_create_or_open` for an API that may open an existing leaf or `exclusive_lock_create_new` for a create-only API that uses `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` and never opens an existing leaf. The two lock shapes are distinct even when their destination basename grammar is equal. Native rows require null path grammars plus their exact namespace/operation pair and policy. No row may smuggle a second terminal effect or collapse two distinct callers, bindings, call sites, branches, source members, or failure policies.

The lexically sorted atomic-file rows retain complete coverage for Claude `BackfillCredentialsFile`, `WriteCredentialsFile`, and manifest save; Codex `atomicWrite`, registry write, `ManagedStore.durableReplace`, production system activator replacement, and removal journal; Gemini refresh; quota cache and burn-history stores; model-overlay save; both Claude capability projections, Claude Code options, and Codex model cache; compatibility epoch; canary state/key/stop request; proxy config; routing/readiness; every current continuity edge from `OpenCodexLeaseStore`, `commitRecordsLockedWithWriter`, V1/V2 archive/migration and `commitV2LockedWithPrecondition`, and `InitialiseCodexContinuityAuthority`; both primer edges; installed-validation request creation; credential-endpoint sidecar plus maintenance/rollback records; and every exact final, archive, staged-final, fixed/random, and whole-component temporary grammar registered above.

Non-atomic rows are equally exhaustive. Quota-cache deletion contains each of the six successful ordinary Claude/Codex login, switch, and remove dispatch branches through `invalidateProviderCache`, plus Claude and Codex explicit refresh through the `invalidateProviderCacheFn` production binding, ending at direct `os.Remove(Q/<provider>.json)` with `failure_policy=continue`; a shared function or implementation never collapses those eight entrypoint/callsite rows. Installed-validation rows cover every `request.lock` acquisition; request cleanup and claim cleanup through `SecureDirectory.Remove`; exact `request.json -> request.claimed` `RenameNoReplace`; and every claim/request/used promotion to `used-<digest>.json` or `cancelled-<digest>.json` through `SecurePromoteNoReplaceInDirectory` or `SecurePromoteNoReplaceInDirectoryChecked`, preserving each returned-error `abort` and ignored-cleanup `continue` branch. Continuity rows cover both staged key/journal secure promotions to canonical finals, and canary-stop rows cover the no-replace request-to-inflight move. Readiness rows cover every marker and poison removal through the retained `SecureDirectory.Remove`, including already-absent and cleanup policy branches. Credential-endpoint rows cover `.lock` acquisition; the exact absent-lock branch has its own foreground-command row from `internal/provider/codex.(*legacyCredentialMaintenanceNamespace).acquirePrepareLockAndProbe` through direct `internal/fsutil.AcquireNewExclusiveLockInDirectory`, the `internal/fsutil.NewExclusiveLocker` interface binding, and concrete `internal/fsutil.(*unixSecureDirectory).OpenNewExclusiveLock`, with the registered `.lock` destination grammar, `writer_kind=lock_acquire`, `operation_shape=exclusive_lock_create_new`, and `failure_policy=abort`. Existing-lock paths retain separate `exclusive_lock_create_or_open` rows and may never satisfy that create-new row. Credential-endpoint rows also cover `.cq-credential-<32-lower-hex>.sock` creation by `net.ListenUnix`; its exact `os.Chmod(...,0600)`; publication to `credential.sock` by `publishCredentialSocketNoReplaceAt -> unix.Linkat`; and every production-reachable socket, sidecar, maintenance, rollback, quarantine, and journal `unix.Unlinkat` or `unix.Linkat` edge in normal close/cleanup, owner maintenance, and reversible transition recovery. The generator enumerates each direct call and every interface or function-value binding; any registered final, temporary, lock, request, claim, marker, poison, socket, sidecar, journal, maintenance, rollback, or quarantine leaf with no matching mutation row is an error.

The native rows retain one row for every distinct production-reachable entrypoint-to-writer chain ending at `UpdateKeychainEntry` with `claude_platform|platform_update_or_add|continue`, `StoreCQAccount` with `claude_cq|cq_set_delete_retry_set|continue`, `RemovePlatformClaudeKeychainAccountsByEmail` with `claude_platform|platform_repeated_service_delete|abort`, or `RemoveCQClaudeAccountsByEmail` with `claude_cq|cq_manifest_selector_delete|continue`, including direct ordinary login, switch, removal, refresh/synchronisation, provider backfill/refresh, shared persistence, pending-removal recovery, and proxy-runtime reachability. Platform deletion preserves service order, numbered first-gap termination, every repeated same-service delete, and abort-on-delete-error; CQ deletion preserves every matching manifest-row selector in source order and ignored-error continuation before manifest replacement. Every row classifies each reachable caller as foreground command or proxy runtime; coalesced physical targets retain all logical writer rows.

The generator constructs closed `LegacyWriterCallChainV1={schema_version:1,entrypoint_symbol,implementation_symbol,edges:[{ordinal,caller_symbol,callee_binding_symbol:null|string,callee_symbol,source_path,byte_offset}]}` from the pinned source syntax and type graph. Edges are nonempty, ordinal-contiguous, repository-relative, begin in the named entrypoint, end at the concrete implementation, and include every direct call plus each function-variable or interface binding as a separate non-null `callee_binding_symbol`; a direct call uses null. For canonical bytes `C`, `call_chain_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/legacy-writer-call-chain/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`. Entries sort lexically by `(entrypoint_symbol,implementation_symbol,call_chain_digest,source_id,writer_kind,operation_shape,transition_source_grammar,transition_destination_grammar,failure_policy)`; `entrypoint_id` is the stable source-derived ID of that tuple and duplicates reject. For canonical row bytes `E`, `writer_reachability_entry_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/legacy-atomic-writer-reachability-entry/v1\0") || uint32be(len(E)) || E))`; this is the only value accepted by a credential mutation naming that row. For complete canonical catalogue bytes `A`, `legacy_atomic_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/legacy-atomic-writer-reachability-catalogue/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`. Import regenerates it at preparation, immediately before writer quiescence, after `writers_stopped`, and immediately before floor commit. A missing/extra/direct writer, transition, cleanup, lock, move, promote, link, socket, mode, unlink, native edge, changed caller/binding/callsite, alternate grammar, policy drift, uncatalogued process, or digest disagreement blocks before termination or floor mutation. Source-derived goldens regenerate both reachability catalogues and every complete call-chain object from baseline source and require byte-identical digests in the signed pre-schema catalogue, import ticket, every quiescence attempt, initialisation/finalisation manifests, signed construction-unit report sets, release artifact sets, and named floor-acceptance, candidate-preflight, floor-validation, primary-rehearsal, and release receipts.

At activation, before terminating anything, writer commits ticket-linked digest-chained `WriterQuiescenceAttemptV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,attempt_id,writer_catalogue_digest,launch_source_catalogue_digest,activation_pid,activation_start_token,activation_executable_sha256,launch_source_actions:[{source_id,prior_presence:"present|absent",prior_loaded_state:"loaded|unloaded|not_applicable",stop_attempt_id:null|string,stop_action:"brew_services_stop_cq|launchctl_bootout|none",stop_outcome:null|absent|not_required|stopped|indeterminate,restore_attempt_id:null|string,restore_action:"brew_services_start_cq|launchctl_bootstrap|none",restore_outcome:null|not_required|restored|retired|indeterminate}],legacy_crash_residue_action_digests:[string],burn_history_terminal_snapshot_digest:null|string,clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",boot_session_id,started_tick_ns,deadline_tick_ns,state:"intent|launch_sources_stopped|writers_stopped|crash_residue_removed|floor_committed|sources_finalised|terminal",previous_state_digest,mac}`. `launch_source_actions` contains the same four source IDs exactly once in lexical order. `legacy_crash_residue_action_digests` is the duplicate-free lexical list of every selected `LegacyCrashResidueActionV1` head and cannot change after `intent`; `burn_history_terminal_snapshot_digest` is null before `writers_stopped`, then fixes the post-quiescence absent-or-final secure-leaf observation and remains immutable. `crash_residue_removed` requires every listed action terminal, no newly appeared registered temporary, unchanged terminal burn-history snapshot, and the complete post-quiescence source topology proof. Every non-null stop, restoration, or residue-removal attempt ID and its exact command or basename is committed before invocation; null is legal only before that action or when its action is `none`. Homebrew mutation uses only the registered absolute `brew services stop|start cq` authority; CQ jobs use exact user-domain `launchctl bootout|bootstrap` against the retained plist. Fresh job/plist/process topology determines whether an attempted action happened; ambiguous issuance remains pending and is never replayed. Before the floor, failure restores exactly each prior loaded source once and proves prior unloaded/absent topology unchanged. After the floor, both legacy proxy sources and the fixed singleton candidate proxy source are retired in favour of selected socket-manager authority; a refresh source may be re-bootstrapped only when its revalidated executable is a `structured_v1` catalogue member and its exact prior state was loaded, otherwise it remains safely retired with visible status/doctor remediation. No scalar source is restarted after the floor.

Implementation symbols are operation-specific. Injected Codex managed/system/journal deletes end at the concrete production `fsutil.OSFileSystem.Remove`; `fsutil.FileSystem.Remove`, `FileSystemActivator.Remove`, and the closure installed by `NewCredentialCoordinator` remain explicit typed binding edges. Ordinary/refresh quota invalidation ends at direct `os.Remove`; retained-directory deletion ends at `internal/fsutil.(*unixSecureDirectory).Remove -> unix.Unlinkat`; direct credential-endpoint deletion ends at the containing production function's `unix.Unlinkat`; no-replace moves end at `internal/fsutil.(*unixSecureDirectory).RenameNoReplace`, with each `SecurePromoteNoReplaceInDirectory[Checked]` wrapper retained in its call chain; endpoint hard-link publication ends at `publishCredentialSocketNoReplaceAt -> unix.Linkat`; socket creation and mode rows end at `net.ListenUnix` and `os.Chmod`; create-or-open lock rows end at their concrete existing secure-lock acquisition implementation, while create-new rows end specifically at `internal/fsutil.(*unixSecureDirectory).OpenNewExclusiveLock` and retain both the `AcquireNewExclusiveLockInDirectory` caller and `NewExclusiveLocker` binding edge. Test-only `MemFS.Remove`, fake bindings, and test call sites are never admitted.

`WriterQuiescenceAttemptV1.writer_catalogue_digest` commits the signed `PreSchemaWriterCatalogueV1` whose `legacy_atomic_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest` equals the freshly regenerated expanded catalogue. `writers_stopped` is legal only after the launch catalogue and process graph prove every foreground/runtime process capable of any of the nine writer kinds absent or stopped, and after a same-descriptor rescan proves every registered source/transition namespace unchanged except a catalogued already-completed effect. Reappearance, an unclassified executable, a changed call-chain digest, any newly reachable leaf mutation, or substitution of `exclusive_lock_create_new` for `exclusive_lock_create_or_open` or vice versa returns to pre-quiescence classification and blocks residue removal and floor mutation; equal destination basenames never make those operation shapes equivalent. The same nested digest equality and lock-shape distinction are rechecked at source finalisation, activation, rollback rehearsal, and every release receipt named above.

Any `cq_refresh_v1` source restored after the floor executes only the structured `refresh` row of `RefreshCommandAuthorityCatalogueV1`; its launch-source identity supplies no legacy credential/cache authority, and owner-control unavailability produces zero local fallback.

Exact activation executable must equal allowed structured importer and be sole permitted non-scalar CQ process; only `scalar_v1` entries are terminated. Classification is exact digest membership; copied/renamed bytes remain same member. The baseline executable's ordinary `cq check` path is therefore a scalar writer process, including its quota-cache, credential-refresh, `gemini_credentials_tmp_v1`, and `burn_history_v1` effects, and receives no history-only exemption.

`ProxyConfigWriterReachabilityCatalogueV1={schema_version:1,authority_baseline_commit,implementation_id:"internal/proxy.saveConfig",entries:[{entrypoint_id,entrypoint_symbol,call_chain_digest,write_kind:"load_default_generation|explicit_save",process_kind:"foreground_command|proxy_runtime"}],entry_set_digest}` is the closed source-derived catalogue for every production path to the unexported fixed-temporary writer, and its digest is mandatory in `PreSchemaWriterCatalogueV1`. It contains exactly nineteen lexically sorted rows: `[codex_canary_start_load_default,models_local_refresh_load_default,models_try_proxy_refresh_load_default,models_use_proxy_load_default,proxy_codex_default_clear_load_default,proxy_codex_default_clear_save,proxy_codex_default_set_load_default,proxy_codex_default_set_save,proxy_codex_default_show_load_default,proxy_expired_pin_load_default,proxy_expired_pin_save,proxy_pin_clear_save,proxy_pin_load_default,proxy_pin_set_save,proxy_prime_load_default,proxy_prime_save,proxy_runtime_reload_load_default,proxy_start_load_default,proxy_status_load_default]`. Every `load_default_generation` row binds its exact production call site to `LoadConfig -> generateDefaultConfig -> saveConfig` when the final is absent; every `explicit_save` row binds its exact `SaveConfig -> saveConfig` call site. The runtime rows cover periodic reload and automatic expired-pin clearing, not only CLI dispatch. A source call-graph golden recomputes symbols, call sites, branches, and chain digests from baseline source; any missing/extra/renamed/rebound edge, direct `saveConfig` caller, or alternate fixed-temporary writer invalidates the signed writer catalogue. Every listed process is a scalar `proxy_config_v1` writer until quiesced. Structured inspection uses non-creating `InspectLegacyProxyConfigV1`, which returns absent/final/invalid facts through the retained parent and never calls `LoadConfig`, `generateDefaultConfig`, `SaveConfig`, or `saveConfig`; structured runtime reads only its selected immutable config object.

For complete canonical reachability-catalogue bytes `G`, `proxy_config_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/proxy-config-writer-reachability-catalogue/v1\0") || uint32be(len(G)) || G))`. Import preparation recomputes `G` from the exact `authority_baseline_commit`, requires byte-identical entry set and digest before signing `PreSchemaWriterCatalogueV1`, then reopens and recomputes both immediately before launch-source quiescence and immediately before floor commit. Omission, null, foreign catalogue/digest pairing, changed call edge, or any writer/launch/quiescence receipt whose transitive digest chain does not resolve to that same `G` refuses before process termination or floor mutation.

A second process using the allowed structured importer digest is forbidden by the sole-non-scalar rule. Same-UID CQ-signed/build-identified executable outside catalogue is `unclassified_cq_writer` and blocks conversion. One fixed 30-second forward subphase commits and issues bounded registered launch-source stops within 5s, TERM-waits scalar writers 5s, KILLs/reaps survivors 5s, proves exact importer plus zero scalar/other CQ processes and all registered launch sources unable to spawn for 5s, then within 5s revalidates final `D/proxy.json` and all three quota-cache final/temporary pairs, selects the burn-history terminal snapshot, completes every registered crash-residue action including `gemini_credentials_tmp_v1`, `proxy_config_tmp_v1`, and all three `quota_cache_<provider>_tmp_v1` actions, commits `crash_residue_removed`, commits floor, re-enumerates/rereads exact floor, and finalises source dispositions; final 5s is recovery reserve. State objects make boundaries resumable without repeating launch-source action, termination, residue removal, restoration, or floor publication. A recorded tick comparison is valid only when clock domain and boot-session identity match and current continuous time has not regressed. Boot mismatch/regression yields `timeout_pending`; recovery takes fresh topology proof and may terminalise the recorded outcome, but never infers elapsed time, repeats an action, or republishes floor from the stale deadline. Permission, timeout, either catalogue mismatch, unclassified writer/source, extra live process, spawn-capable source, config/quota-cache final/temporary drift, Gemini credential final/temporary drift, residue/snapshot drift, ambiguous restoration, or floor mismatch refuses or leaves conservatively advanced exact-receipt recovery. New supervisor continuously watches floor descriptor/format/digest and revalidates at ingress and immediately before `DispatchAdmitted`; change inhibits all data-plane admission. Other same-UID code deliberately launched after barrier remains inside stated trust boundary.

Initialisation/import and incremental activation use two-stage inhibited activation. Before primary floor mutation, exact parent-MACed `CandidateReleasePromotionReceiptV1`, whose recursively reopened inner `RollbackFloorValidationReceiptV1` proves target and independently known-good rollback release sets support requested union and pass candidate protocol/policy corpus. “Preactivation receipt” is only the CLI role of the outer promotion object; no separate `PreactivationReceiptV1` wire type or weaker projection exists. Floor advances and authority selects target with `feature_activation_state=activation_inhibited`; supervisor serves owner control/health while public data-plane admission remains closed. One single-use owner-MAC `PreactivationValidationPermit` exercises only exact marker fixtures over private validation channel; it cannot authenticate public traffic, arbitrary accounts, or user requests. Primary target then produces exact installed marker children and `RuntimePolicyAckV1`; final authority CAS changes state to `active`, then admission opens. Candidate receipts never substitute for primary markers; they authorise only inhibited selection.

Crash before floor commit leaves old floor/authority. Crash after floor commit or target selection leaves conservatively advanced non-serving authority; only the exact intent resumes or selects the retained compatible rollback set as one matched supervisor/worker pair, still inhibited. Marker failure never re-enables unsupported runtime. If that rollback pair boots and its exact topology/public-admission-closed proof is durable but activation still cannot obtain the required marker/policy proof, recovery commits an inhibited terminal authority with `feature_activation_state=rollback_inhibited`, clears only the matching operation reference, terminalises the feature child/coordinator with that same proof, and never publishes normal admission. Failure to prove even that inhibited rollback topology remains nonterminal matching recovery; it is not `rollback_inhibited`. Competing CAS, receipt mismatch, changed authority, or mixed target/rollback runtime refuses. Newly started pre-schema binary encounters JSON at existing path, fails scalar parse, and refuses; no claim covers pre-schema code already running before quiescence. Candidate can only verify public primary record; `AdvanceInstance` writes candidate-local floor and leaves primary bytes/existence equal.

V1 `FeatureID` is closed and monotonic:

| Feature | Dependencies | Gated surface |
|---|---|---|
| `capability_evidence_v1` | `normal_codex_v1`, `routing_policy_store_v1` | capability evidence mutation or probe write |
| `capability_routing_v1` | `capability_evidence_v1`, `session_pools_v1` | derived-pool mutation or binding |
| `caller_delegation_v1` | `normal_caller_auth_v1`, `normal_worker_protocol_v1`, `routing_policy_store_v1` | delegation grant/revoke and delegated dispatch |
| `external_projection_v1` | `normal_claude_v1`, `normal_codex_v1` | external compatibility projections |
| `instance_authority_v1` | none | composite primary authority |
