The dependency column is the canonical `FeatureDependencyAdjacencyV1`: each feature appears exactly once; `none` encodes the empty array; every other cell is a duplicate-free lexically sorted array of literal `FeatureID` values; and aliases, prose expansion, self-edges, cycles, unknown IDs, missing rows, and extra rows reject. Its canonical producer emits rows in lexical feature-ID order and dependency arrays in lexical order.

Authority/floor `required_features` is duplicate-free sorted active requirement set. Artifact manifest `supported_features` is duplicate-free sorted implementation capability set; `minimum_floor_features` is smallest set required merely to boot that artifact. Target role-set support is the intersection across launcher/supervisor/worker and target minimum is their union. A floor set contains supervisor/worker only: its effective support is their intersection with the already selected launcher's manifest support, and admission additionally requires the launcher's `launcher_abi_digest` to equal the floor set's signed `required_launcher_abi_digest`. Compatibility mode is legal only when current floor contains set minimum and the effective launcher/supervisor/worker combination supports every current requirement; inactive supported surfaces remain unreachable. Unknown value or absent/mismatched launcher ABI is incompatible.

`ProxyReleaseFeatureSetV1` is literal sorted set `[capability_evidence_v1,capability_routing_v1,caller_delegation_v1,external_projection_v1,instance_authority_v1,normal_caller_auth_v1,normal_claude_v1,normal_codex_v1,normal_gemini_v1,normal_worker_protocol_v1,operator_control_v1,rescue_relay_v1,routing_policy_store_v1,session_pools_v1,socket_supervisor_v1]`. Fresh primary initialisation and final release import require target/floor artifact `supported_features` supersets and target desired requirement equal this exact set; `minimum_floor_features` must remain compatible with preactivation floor. Final active authority/floor and primary installed marker set equal exact release set; subset/superset refuses. Compatibility-mode import leaves scalar/old feature set unchanged. Candidate validation advances only candidate-local floor.

`MarkerChildID` is the closed string enum containing exactly every backticked child below. `RequiredMarkerChildren` returns the duplicate-free lexical union of transitive dependencies plus literal IDs; no prose expansion, implicit base child, or extra row exists. The sole historical marker wire type is closed `InstalledMarkerV1={schema_version:1,kind:"installed_marker_v1",producer_schema:"installed_marker_producer_v1",marker_child_id:MarkerChildID,scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,installed_validation_run_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,launcher_artifact_digest,launcher_artifact_manifest_digest,supervisor_artifact_digest,supervisor_artifact_manifest_digest,worker_artifact_digest,worker_artifact_manifest_digest,client_build,client_executable_digest,fixture_digest,result_digest,result:"passed",observed_at,expires_at,integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}`. Candidate scope requires the non-null selected controller `validation_run_id`, `controller_signature`, and that controller's public key; primary requires null validation-run ID/public key and `owner_mac`. `installed_validation_run_id` is always non-null, `expires_at` is exactly 24 hours after `observed_at`, and every artifact, generation, fixture, and result member is a non-null byte-identical projection of that marker child's completed producer result. With `K_installed_marker=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/installed-marker/v1"),L=32)` and `M0=CanonicalJSONV1(marker with integrity omitted)`, candidate integrity is `Ed25519.Sign(controller_seed,ASCII("cq/installed-marker-signature/v1\0") || uint32be(len(M0)) || M0)` and primary integrity is `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_installed_marker,ASCII("cq/installed-marker-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(M0)) || M0))`. For complete integrity-protected canonical bytes `M`, `marker_object_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/installed-marker/v1\0") || uint32be(len(M)) || M))`. No unversioned marker, alternate producer schema, failed result, other key/domain, or independently shaped marker projection is valid.

Each scope's historical release markers live only at `runtime-evidence/installed-markers/objects/<marker_object_digest>.json`; registered publication temporaries are exactly `runtime-evidence/installed-markers/.installed-marker.<ordinal-1-through-4>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`. An object is at most 16,384 bytes. The candidate controller or primary installed-validation owner is the sole integrity issuer; the scope's existing trusted publisher bounded-streams the complete issuer-protected bytes to a random-exclusive registered temporary, file-syncs, no-replace-renames to the recomputed content address, directory-syncs, and same-descriptor reopens schema, integrity, filename, and bytes before a row may name it. An existing address succeeds only for byte-identical content. For candidate scope the controller sends complete signed `M`, stage ordinal, and target-store identity through the authenticated controller-parent channel. After exact publication the parent returns closed `CandidateInstalledMarkerPublicationAckV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_installed_marker_publication_ack_v1",validation_run_id,installed_validation_run_id,stage_ordinal,marker_child_id,marker_object_digest,reopened_object_identity_digest,mac}`, where `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_candidate_runtime_evidence_selection,ASCII("cq/candidate-installed-marker-publication-ack/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A0)) || A0))` for `A0=CanonicalJSONV1(ack with mac omitted)`. The controller verifies that deterministic acknowledgement against retained `M` before including the row; after object sync parent recovery reconstructs the byte-identical acknowledgement, while controller loss before closure selection leaves the marker inert for reference-aware cleanup. The parent never creates or alters signed marker bytes and the controller never receives the root descriptor. Recovery removes and syncs only a registered, same-operation, unreferenced temporary after writer-quiescence and identity proof; a complete object is adopted only after same-descriptor verification, while a collision, unknown basename, ambiguous sync, replaced identity, invalid integrity, or incomplete 90-object set inhibits the stage. The exact release feature set expands to 90 distinct `MarkerChildID` values. Candidate scope reserves its one current four-stage graph: exactly 360 immutable marker objects plus four temporaries, for 364 files and `364 * 16,384 = 5,963,776` bytes under 6 MiB. Primary scope simultaneously retains one prior pinned four-stage graph and reserves one complete next four-stage graph: exactly 720 objects plus four temporaries, for 724 files and `11,862,016` bytes under 12 MiB. The combined boundary is 1,088 files and `17,825,792` bytes, exactly 17 MiB. Candidate object 361, primary object 721, either scope's fifth temporary, a 16,385-byte object, or the first aggregate byte over its scope or combined cap refuses before producer work or stage mutation.

Candidate-scoped markers can satisfy only candidate preactivation/rehearsal evidence; primary activation/finalisation requires corresponding primary markers. A current runtime/policy source accepts a marker only while `observed_at <= now < expires_at`. A historical stage closure instead records immutable `captured_at` and accepts exactly `observed_at <= captured_at < expires_at`, irrespective of later wall time; recovery never regenerates either timestamp. The current policy acknowledgement, active producer, stage closure/proof, candidate stage selector, validation or rehearsal receipt, import-finalisation manifest, and last-final-release history recursively pin every reachable marker. Candidate admission reserves its complete current graph plus four publication temporaries before the first producer; primary next-graph admission reserves the prior pinned graph, complete next graph, and four temporaries. Pinned objects are never counted as replaceable headroom. GC, under the scope lifecycle/store lock, first reopens that complete reference graph, syncs the reference checkpoint, unlinks only unreferenced content addresses, and syncs the marker directory; candidate removal additionally waits for terminal receipt export/import and finalisation completion. A marker row, closure, or receipt is never retained after its referenced marker, and a pinned marker is never removed to admit new work.

Let `MarkerSetFingerprintInputV1={schema_version:1,kind:"marker_set_fingerprint_input_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",installed_validation_run_id,proxy_instance_id,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,required_features,marker_rows:[{marker_child_id:MarkerChildID,marker_object_digest}]}`. `marker_rows` is the non-empty duplicate-free list sorted by raw `MarkerChildID` bytes; its IDs equal `RequiredMarkerChildren(required_features)` exactly, with no missing or extra row. Every digest resolves from the scope-local historical marker store and byte-verifies an `InstalledMarkerV1` carrying that literal ID, scope, installed-validation run, proxy, runtime, authority/routing/listener generations, release set, and exact launcher/supervisor/worker/client artifact set shared by the installed terminal receipt. For canonical bytes `F=CanonicalJSONV1(MarkerSetFingerprintInputV1)`, the sole algorithm is unkeyed `marker_set_fingerprint=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/marker-set-fingerprint/v1\0") || uint32be(len(F)) || F))`. No HMAC/keyed, raw-marker-byte, reordered, digest-only, implicit-child, or extra-child variant is valid.

`worker.credential_owner_store` is the sole marker for the complete key-policy, fingerprint, retained-capability, store-open, parent-completion, receipt-generation, pin/GC, and crash-recovery contract above. Its primary producer result binds the non-null `credential_owner_key_fingerprint`, same-descriptor key/store identity, schema digest, and reopened empty-or-valid store proof; its candidate result binds the same policy/schema digest, null fingerprint, absent key/store write capability, and the candidate read-only refusal corpus. Another worker marker, a fingerprint without the store proof, or a candidate key cannot satisfy it.

Table is compile-time total over `FeatureID`; an exact adjacency-list golden plus feature, dependency, marker, and CU-manifest enumeration tests fail on reordered/unsorted/duplicate/aliased/cyclic/unknown dependency, or any missing/extra row or child.
`RequiredMarkerChildren(capability_evidence_v1)` therefore contains its four literal capability children plus the complete transitive marker children of `routing_policy_store_v1` and `normal_codex_v1`, including normal caller-auth, worker-protocol, socket-supervisor, and instance-authority children. `capability.model_probe` alone can never satisfy activation without that normal-Codex closure. `RequiredMarkerChildren(external_projection_v1)` contains its six literal projection children plus the complete transitive unions of both `normal_claude_v1` and `normal_codex_v1`; a Codex sink or registry projection can never activate from Claude-only route/origin/differential evidence. In the activation paragraph below, “one exact `PrimaryStagedReleaseV1`” means the target-kind selector selected by `release-staging/anchors/target.json`; the independently resolved rollback set must come from the rollback-floor-kind selector selected by `release-staging/anchors/rollback-floor.json`. Prepare requires equality among the target selector's accepted-floor set, validation receipt floor set/acceptance/ABI, rollback selector set/acceptance/ABI, and both release-build authorities before inert activation publication.
`RequiredMarkerChildren(operator_control_v1)` contains its seven literal control children plus the complete transitive marker unions of all three normal providers and `normal_worker_protocol_v1`, including `worker.credential_owner_store` and `worker.operator_control`; no structured command may dispatch merely because a provider data-plane marker exists. The adjacency golden enumerates all seven literal children, including `control.refresh_reauth`, and the complete 90-child transitive closure; six-child, old 89-child, or 88-child projections reject. `normal_gemini_v1` is deliberately not a public ingress feature: its complete marker set attests only authenticated operator-control discovery/refresh/quota work, the exact credential adapter/origins, and instance-local cache parity.

`FeatureActivationStore` lives at `feature-activation/{key,anchor,objects/,receipts/}` beneath instance root and is subordinate to `OperationCoordinatorStore`. `feature-activation.key` derives from `authority.key` with HKDF info `cq/feature-activation/v1`; immutable object cap is 1 MiB, history retains active plus last terminal, and complete directory including imported receipt plus two temporaries is capped at 8 MiB. Anchor is MACed `{schema_version,object_digest,operation_id,external_reference_binding:null|CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1,phase,sequence,mac}`. Its binding is non-null exactly for the candidate-consuming feature activation, equals every selected intent/successor and imported row-six binding byte-for-byte, and is null for every other activation. Object is `FeatureActivationIntentV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,coordinator_intent_digest,requested_feature,dependency_closure,prior_floor_digest,target_floor_digest,target_authority_generation,target_intent_digest,target_release_set_digest,rollback_release_set_digest,preactivation_receipt_digest,activation_receipt_id,external_reference_binding:null|CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1,phase:"prepared_unselected|prepared|floor_committed|authority_inhibited|markers_committed|authority_active|terminal",sequence,previous_object_digest,terminal_outcome:null|target_effective|rollback_inhibited|aborted_before_floor,terminal_authority_generation,terminal_proof_digest,mac}`. `coordinator_intent_digest` is null only in inert `prepared_unselected`, whose previous digest is null and which is never anchor-selected; every selected successor requires it. Terminal authority/proof fields are null before `terminal`; `target_effective` names the active authority/marker/policy proof, `aborted_before_floor` names the no-floor/no-action proof and has null terminal authority generation, and `rollback_inhibited` names the exact inhibited authority generation plus matched rollback supervisor/worker release-set, boot, listener-lineage, and public-admission-closed proof. Closure is sorted/duplicate-free; IDs pre-generated; every selected phase increments sequence and chains digest. The securely imported receipt and `prepared_unselected` object publish inertly first. Coordinator intent selects that object digest, composite `active_operation_ref` selects the coordinator, then a `prepared` successor binds both digests and advances the child anchor. Object publication and anchor replacement use file/directory sync before any floor, artifact, or manager action. Recovery resumes exact next phase; a different feature conflicts. Anchor clears only after terminal authority/history/coordinator checkpoint, while terminal object remains for idempotence. Capacity and unknown/multiple successor fail before action. CU-2 owns store/schema/crash matrix; owning feature CU supplies preactivation and marker oracles.

Feature activation is sole incremental post-authority feature producer and accepts only already structured authority/floor; `instance_authority_v1` is initialisation/import-only. `prepare` requires one exact `PrimaryStagedReleaseV1`, resolves its target set and selected `CandidateReleasePromotionReceiptV1` by the full CLI digest and recursively reopens its inner `RollbackFloorValidationReceiptV1`, copies that already verified outer receipt and pins its inner receipt into the activation store, independently resolves the retained rollback release set, requires the outer MAC/controller-terminal/accounting/End/confinement linkage plus the inner receipt's exact candidate run/signature/artifact/corpus linkage, computes closure, proves both sets support the complete union, and commits prepared child/coordinator/authority references. It never opens an external release or receipt path and performs no floor, artifact selection, manager, provider, credential, or public-runtime action. Status without ID follows sole-active coordinator rule; full operation ID reopens retained terminal receipt. `activate` requires exact operation ID and confirmation, revalidates every selected receipt/set/current generation, then follows inhibited floor/authority/primary-marker protocol. `abort` is legal only in prepared phase, terminalises `aborted_before_floor`, releases imported receipt references after history checkpoint, clears authority operation reference, and terminalises coordinator; at or after floor commit only exact activate/recovery is legal. Primary marker set is required before final active CAS, not before prepared/floor phases. Re-entry with same operation ID reuses IDs; another feature returns `generation_conflict`/3 and exact matching command. JSON always returns operation/receipt IDs after prepare intent; pre-intent failure returns nulls. Activation never deactivates. A terminal `rollback_inhibited` generation is a deliberately degraded, non-serving state with an idle coordinator: aside from exact state-preserving inspection/recovery or quarantine reset, the sole permitted semantic mutation is a new `feature activate prepare` for the same unsatisfied requested feature/dependency closure, using a new operation ID and freshly staged target/validation receipt against the already advanced structured floor. It may not reuse the failed receipt, operation, marker, policy acknowledgement, or runtime proof. Matching activation success replaces the inhibited state with active authority; another `rollback_inhibited` result remains eligible only for the same fresh remediation loop. Every other gated mutator requires complete active dependency set, non-inhibited feature state, and idle coordinator; missing/inhibited feature returns `feature_inactive`/3 with exact release-stage then feature-prepare remediation and performs no floor, authority, provider, credential, or network action. Reads remain non-mutating. Failed pre-intent work, probes, no-op mutations, and removal of last use never change set; committed set never shrinks. Rescue entry performs no compatibility work and remains available only after active `rescue_relay_v1`. Unknown ID, missing staged release/preactivation/marker/dependency, unsupported artifact, or scalar floor is `compatibility_incompatible`.

Each authority object is at most 16 MiB; routing document at most 8 MiB, 1,024 pools, 10,000 bindings, and 10,000 evidence records. Authority history retains current plus previous fifteen terminal semantic generations. Active operation may add at most twelve nonterminal plus one terminal object and publication may require two simultaneous temporary/orphan objects. Authority directory cap is 576 MiB: legal worst case is 31 objects ×16 MiB =496 MiB plus fixed 80 MiB anchors, receipts, directory metadata, and recovery reserve. Before intent, writer reserves complete worst-case remaining operation budget; insufficient capacity refuses before mutation. No pruning occurs during active transition. Storage pruning never creates semantic authority generation. Instead `authority-history.anchor` is the separately MACed closed storage-chain record `{schema_version,checkpoint_sequence,semantic_authority_generation,semantic_object_digest,previous_history_anchor_digest,pruned_through_generation,pruned_chain_digest,last_terminal_receipt,floor_receipt_digest,candidate_provider_broker_journal_identity_digest:null|string,candidate_provider_broker_journal_close_digest:null|string,candidate_provider_broker_journal_seal_digest:null|string,candidate_provider_broker_journal_digest:null|string,candidate_provider_broker_routing_authority_object_count:null|integer,candidate_provider_broker_routing_authority_store_byte_count:null|integer,candidate_provider_broker_routing_authority_set_digest:null|string,candidate_provider_validation_case_authority_catalogue_set_digest:null|string,candidate_provider_broker_dispatch_tuple_set_digest:null|string,candidate_synthetic_route_budget_consumption_count:null|integer,credential_echo_scan_evidence_count:null|integer,candidate_provider_credential_echo_scan_evidence_run_set_digest:null|string,candidate_provider_credential_echo_scan_evidence_object_count:null|integer,candidate_provider_credential_echo_scan_evidence_store_byte_count:null|integer,candidate_provider_credential_echo_scan_evidence_store_set_digest:null|string,credential_echo_scan_delivered_prefix_byte_count:null|integer,generated_control_observation_run_set_digest:null|string,credential_owner_key_fingerprint,external_reference_binding:null|CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1,candidate_controller_external_reference_binding_set_digest:null|string,mac}`. `credential_owner_key_fingerprint` is always non-null and obeys the primary equality rule below; the seventeen broker/generated-control members are all null before a checkpoint reaches a canonical candidate promotion/final release and all non-null with the exact sealed-run values at and after that boundary while the last-final-release reference remains. No partial tuple is legal. Under locks, with no active transition and after semantic revalidation, writer syncs/replaces history anchor, syncs root, then unlinks only unreferenced objects and syncs directory. Runtime acknowledgements bind semantic anchor only. Tests drive full max-size retained history through all thirteen operation commits plus temporaries and every complete fingerprint/broker-tuple nullability boundary.

The closed history-anchor member `candidate_controller_external_reference_binding_set_digest:null|string` is non-null exactly for a checkpoint whose `last_terminal_receipt` is a candidate-validated promotion/final release and equals the signed validation receipt, promotion terminal receipt, import-finalisation reference/evidence/completion receipts, and controller capsule/index binding set. The first such checkpoint carries the row-seven single-row `CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1`; after it has copied every retained root to canonical release/history authority, one synced successor preserves the binding-set digest as non-resolving audit provenance but removes that single-row binding and no longer recursively reaches the controller run. Only that successor plus its exact GC proof may produce row seven's released tombstone. Other checkpoints require the field null unless they preserve an existing last-final-release record byte-identically. The field, credential-owner fingerprint, complete broker tuple, and row binding are covered by the existing history MAC; omission, wrong nullability, or catalogue/run/row/reference/fingerprint mismatch blocks checkpoint and release.

Never-initialised means stable control dir and root were freshly created in one exclusive initialisation transaction and contain no unexplained residue. Any pre-existing partial/missing-anchor state is invalid, never default normal. Unknown schema/feature, bad MAC, lower generation, key replacement, or corrupt anchor fails closed. Quarantine reset holds exclusive stable lifecycle lock, verifies bootstrap identity and coordinator verifier, publishes the coordinator-owned reset-ledger intent binding exact old/quarantine/replacement identities plus a closed deletion manifest, and stages/syncs the complete replacement sibling, including preserved validated authority key when structured floor requires it. It then publishes the reset coordinator intent and selects both by ordinary authority CAS, by the idle unreadable-authority exception, or by the one signed coordinator supersession CAS when an authenticated unfinished coordinator chain would otherwise block reset. Only after that selected child/intent state may it perform the two no-replace renames with parent sync after each. Crash recovery under the same parent lock deterministically finishes replacement, restores original, or reports both intact; it never invents identity, resumes a superseded child, or deletes either tree. Once replacement authority is inhibited and rollback is no longer legal, the existing reset confirmation authorises exact ledger purge/finalisation of the old quarantine; a committed deletion-attempt ID, descriptor-relative purge, absence proof, and coordinator-signed tombstone make this resumable and bounded. Waiters cannot retain moved inner locks. Routing reset requires separate policy-loss acknowledgement.

Transition journal lives inside committed authority object:

```json
{
  "operation_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "kind": "rescue_enter|rescue_exit|config_adopt|config_setting|worker_switch|supervisor_switch|runtime_bundle_switch|legacy_import|listener_migration|launcher_upgrade",
  "intent_authority_generation": 9,
  "phase_sequence": 3,
  "phase": "intent|quiescing|manager_mutation|booting|verifying|restoring|terminal",
  "clock_domain": "mach_continuous_time_v1",
  "boot_session_id": "opaque",
  "attempt_started_tick_ns": 123,
  "attempt_deadline_tick_ns": 90000000123,
  "attempt_started_wall": "RFC3339-display-only",
  "restart_attempts": 0,
  "rollback_attempts": 0,
  "terminal_outcome": null,
  "terminal_proof_kind": null,
  "terminal_proof_digest": null,
  "details": {}
}
```

`details` is a closed discriminated union. Common fields above are forbidden inside it; every listed field is required and non-null unless marked nullable, and every unlisted field is forbidden:

| Kind | Exact `details` fields |
|---|---|

All digests are full lower-case fixed-length values in their registered domain; listeners/tuples have exact canonical JSON schemas; manager/source/phase enums are closed. For legacy import, the compatibility-proof digest equals the ticket/input member above. Before any external action, writer derives and durably commits `legacy_headroom_activation_revalidation_digest` from the fresh same-variant config/process/listener/projection-or-absence result; it remains null only before that revalidation, and every action-attempt field requires it non-null. Coupled local-token fields are all null when selected token is unchanged and all non-null otherwise; state/ack digest update with each cutover phase. The two rehearsal-failure fields are both non-null only for the controller/finaliser-authorised failed-target operation: the barrier digest binds scope/run or finalisation operation, target/rollback pair, attempt ID, and deliberately rejected boot token, while the reap proof binds that exact attempted target process group and its complete absence before rollback issue. They are both null for every initial, successful, ordinary-failure, or rescue switch. Wrong nullability, missing, unknown, or wrong-kind field rejects complete journal.

Every phase is a new composite authority generation carrying same operation ID, immutable intent generation, and increasing phase sequence. `terminal_outcome`, proof kind, and proof digest are null before terminal. Terminal phase permits exactly `target_effective|prior_restored`; proof kind/digest must establish corresponding fresh topology. A failed command that made no external or semantic change emits a failed CLI envelope without creating a terminal journal; any failure after committed action remains pending until target or prior topology is proven. Thus target and restoration remain distinguishable even with zero rollback attempts. Terminal receipt is `(operation_id,intent_authority_generation,phase_sequence,terminal_outcome,terminal_proof_kind,terminal_proof_digest,terminal_authority_generation)` and history anchor retains it. Next phase commits before irreversible manager action. Startup publishes generation-bound attempt identity before worker initialisation. `mach_continuous_time_v1` is boot-wide monotonic continuous time, not process-relative time; same boot/session/domain computes remaining deadline from persisted ticks. Wall time is display/correlation only. After reboot, boot-ID change, unsupported clock domain, tick regression, or clock ambiguity, committed attempt becomes `timeout_pending`: recovery takes fresh evidence and may accept proven terminal state, but never infers elapsed time, repeats manager/spawn attempt, or rolls back from time alone. Terminal object retains result; later unrelated semantic mutation clears active journal while history anchor retains terminal receipt.

`supervisor_switch` records role, target/rollback artifacts, manager binding, kickstart attempt, inherited listener, boot token, readiness acknowledgement, and at most one rollback. Before target kickstart or rollback, writer commits `verifying` or `restoring` generation with exact attempt ID and post-exec boot token. Started supervisor MAC-acknowledges `{operation_id,attempt_kind,kickstart_attempt_id,verifying_authority_generation,post_exec_boot_token,artifact_digest,manager_binding_digest,inherited_listener_tuple,process_identity_digest}`. Manager verifies acknowledgement and fresh topology, stores acknowledgement digest, then commits terminal `target_effective` or `prior_restored`. Only after observing terminal generation does supervisor publish ordinary runtime-generation acknowledgement. Crash after readiness acknowledgement but before terminal commit resolves from same acknowledgement/topology without repeating kickstart. `launcher_upgrade` uses same ordering plus mandatory client-stop proof and socket-ABI proof. `worker_switch` uses worker attempt acknowledgement without manager kickstart.

`runtime_bundle_switch` selects one matched supervisor/worker pair. Admission closes, the old worker stops and reaps, one authority generation names both target digests, and launchd starts the stable launcher on the retained socket. Every managed primary `initial|target|rollback|restart` boot uses one closed launcher protocol. Before reading control, root, authority, artifact-selection, or other instance-private state, the launcher opens the fixed lifecycle entry without following links through the retained exact parent, validates the selected device/inode, takes nonblocking `LOCK_SH` on a new open-file description, and keeps it locked. Only then may it revalidate the launchd event/listener and selected pair. Before `exec` it publishes and same-descriptor reopens one owner-MACed `RuntimeLauncherHandoffV1={schema_version:1,kind:"runtime_launcher_handoff_v1",operation_id,attempt_kind:"initial|target|rollback|restart",attempt_id,launcher_process_identity_digest,launcher_executable_digest,expected_supervisor_artifact_digest,expected_worker_artifact_digest,verifying_authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,manager_event_digest,manager_binding_digest,inherited_listener_tuple,post_exec_boot_token,lifecycle_lock_identity_digest,lifecycle_lock_descriptor_identity_digest,lifecycle_shared_lock_proof_digest,inherited_lifecycle_fd,exec_lineage_nonce,created_at,mac}`. Post-exec bootstrap has a closed two-step order and accepts no reopened lock substitute. Before any root read, the supervisor verifies only kernel/process facts available without trusting the handoff object: both inherited descriptors occupy their fixed unequal roles, the lifecycle `fstat` identity equals the manager-sealed lifecycle identity and still carries `LOCK_SH`, the listener is the sealed socket type/tuple, PID/start token and boot session are unchanged across `exec`, the executable is the expected supervisor, and the bounded role-manifest framing is well formed. Only after that verification may it read any other private state, adopt artifacts or listener admission, create a holder checkpoint, spawn a worker, publish acknowledgement, or serve. Failure closes the listener and private descriptors and exits without acknowledgement. The supervisor then retains the same locked open-file description for its complete lifetime; primary boot has no post-exec readiness issuer or supervisor-to-issuer lifecycle transfer.

Before spawning or granting root access to the selected worker, the supervisor securely reopens the lifecycle inode through a freshly retained exact parent, takes `LOCK_SH` on a new worker-only open-file description distinct from its inherited description, and transfers one duplicate over the authenticated private bootstrap. Candidate holder acquisition never reopens the lifecycle path. Controller exit closes the pool and follows cleanup-only invalidation; parent recovery never opens a replacement slot.

Every initial candidate/primary boot, every pair switch, and every admitted primary launchd replacement emits one closed `RuntimeBootAckV1={schema_version:1,kind:"runtime_boot_ack_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,operation_id,attempt_kind:"initial|target|rollback|restart",kickstart_attempt_id,restart_attempt_id,restart_attempt_digest,launcher_handoff_digest,launcher_process_identity_digest,launcher_exec_lineage_digest,candidate_launcher_exec_lineage:null|CandidateLauncherExecLineageV1,verifying_authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,post_exec_boot_token,release_artifact_set_digest,launcher_artifact_digest,launcher_artifact_manifest_digest,supervisor_artifact_digest,supervisor_artifact_manifest_digest,worker_artifact_digest,worker_artifact_manifest_digest,manager_binding_digest,inherited_listener_tuple,supervisor_process_identity_digest,worker_process_identity_digest,lifecycle_lock_identity_digest,lifecycle_lock_holders:[{role:"supervisor|worker",process_identity_digest,descriptor_identity_digest,shared_lock_proof_digest,lifecycle_slot_index,candidate_slot_allocation_digest}],launcher_abi_digest,private_abi_digest,supported_features_digest,acknowledged_at,integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}`. `lifecycle_lock_holders` has exactly two ordered rows, supervisor then worker, distinct descriptor identities, and no other role.
