After observed exec, only that same PID/start token and boot token running the expected supervisor with the inherited exact description may complete the signed lineage and acknowledgement. A pre/post-exec ambiguity remains pending and cannot resubmit, retransmit to a new process, burn the slot, or issue another manager action. Within one selected candidate slot allocation, a forbidden second transfer means any concurrent transfer or any different attempt, peer, descriptor nonce, slot index, identity, or open-file description. If the private connection dies before durable selection, recovery may reconnect only to the same live PID/start token and accept one retransmitted duplicate from the retained exact allocated description with the same operation/attempt/boot-token/descriptor nonce/slot and same-open-description proof. A later process attempt is not a retry of that transfer: only after resolving the prior allocation as `receiver_attested_live`, `receiver_retired`, or `burned` under that closed successor rule may it select and consume the next previously unused pool slot. A mismatch remains pending or follows the selected cleanup/rollback rule and never reopens or reuses a slot.

`RuntimePolicyAckV1` is the sole policy-acknowledgement wire type; the former unversioned seven-value tuple and any independently shaped stage projection are unknown schemas. It is closed `RuntimePolicyAckV1={schema_version:1,kind:"runtime_policy_ack_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,listener_generation,authority_generation,routing_generation,required_features,readiness_marker_set_fingerprint,effective_policy_digest,acknowledged_at,integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}`. `required_features` is sorted and duplicate-free. Candidate requires a non-null selected controller `validation_run_id`, `controller_signature`, that controller's public key, and Ed25519 integrity; primary requires null validation-run ID/public key, `owner_mac`, and the authority-derived key `K_runtime_policy_ack=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/runtime-policy-ack/v1"),L=32)`. For `P0=CanonicalJSONV1(ack with integrity omitted)`, candidate integrity is `Ed25519.Sign(controller_seed,ASCII("cq/runtime-policy-ack-signature/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P0)) || P0)` and primary integrity is `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_runtime_policy_ack,ASCII("cq/runtime-policy-ack-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P0)) || P0))`. For complete integrity-protected canonical bytes `P`, `runtime_policy_ack_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/runtime-policy-ack/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`. `acknowledged_at` is captured once before publication and never regenerated during adoption or recovery.

The exact current acknowledgement is selected at scope-local `readiness/runtime-policy-ack.json`; its sole registered temporary is `.runtime-policy-ack.<32-lower-hex>.tmp` in that directory. The supervisor and ready worker jointly attest the effective tuple, but only the owning candidate controller or primary authority issuer constructs and protects the canonical object. Under that owning transition, the issuer bounded-writes canonical `P` to an exclusive no-follow temporary, file-syncs, atomically replaces from the exact reopened prior bytes or proved absence, directory-syncs, then same-descriptor reopens and recomputes schema, integrity, and digest before any admission, stage source, receipt, or history may name it. Existing current bytes are idempotent only when byte-identical. Wrong scope/run/key/generation, an unknown field, malformed integrity, ambiguous replace, or current authority/history mismatch inhibits admission and every mutator. Recovery before replace removes only the registered same-operation temporary after identity and writer-quiescence proof; recovery after replace accepts only the byte-identical current object with its original `acknowledged_at`, and ambiguity before directory sync or same-descriptor reopen remains inhibited rather than regenerating time, integrity, or bytes. Each scope admits exactly current plus one temporary, each at most 65,536 bytes: two files and 131,072 bytes. A stage producer retains that reopened descriptor until the complete acknowledgement bytes are embedded in and protected by its durable stage closure; no later policy mutation may replace the current selection first. Thereafter the closure, not a digest-only readiness lookup, preserves the historical acknowledgement.

Stage validation is one closed stored object rather than projections asserted by the closure producer. The exhaustive terminal source types are:

- `InstalledValidationTerminalReceiptV1={schema_version:1,kind:"installed_validation_terminal_receipt_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,operation_id,installed_validation_run_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,required_features,corpus_revision,corpus_case_set_digest,corpus_execution_result_digest,transport_results:{http:"passed",compact:"passed",retained:"passed",websocket:"passed"},required_marker_children:[{marker_child_id:MarkerChildID,marker_object_digest}],marker_set_fingerprint,started_at,completed_at,outcome:"passed",integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}`;
- `ExplicitPoolValidationTerminalReceiptV1={schema_version:1,kind:"explicit_pool_validation_terminal_receipt_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,operation_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,pool_object_digest,binding_object_digest,delegation_object_digest,cases:[{case_kind:"positive"|"unavailable"|"excluded"|"zero_fallback",fixture_digest,result:"passed",upstream_attempt_count}],started_at,completed_at,outcome:"passed",integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}`;
- `CapabilityPoolValidationTerminalReceiptV1={schema_version:1,kind:"capability_pool_validation_terminal_receipt_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,operation_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,pool_object_digest,capability_predicate_set_digest,capability_evidence_set_digest,cases:[{case_kind:"positive"|"unavailable"|"excluded"|"zero_fallback",fixture_digest,result:"passed",upstream_attempt_count}],started_at,completed_at,outcome:"passed",integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}`; and
- `RuntimeTopologyObservationTerminalReceiptV1={schema_version:1,kind:"runtime_topology_observation_terminal_receipt_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,operation_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,listener_tuple_digest,supervisor_process_identity_digest,worker_process_identity_digest,runtime_holder_checkpoint_digest,public_admission_state:"inhibited",started_at,completed_at,outcome:"passed",integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}`.

These are the only members of `BundleStageTerminalSourceReceiptV1`. Candidate nullability/key rules are the selected controller rules used by `InstalledMarkerV1`; primary uses null validation-run ID/public key and owner MAC. With `K_bundle_stage_source=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-source/v1"),L=32)` and `T0=CanonicalJSONV1(receipt with integrity omitted)`, candidate integrity is `Ed25519.Sign(controller_seed,ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-source-receipt-signature/v1\0") || uint32be(len(T0)) || T0)` and primary integrity is `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_bundle_stage_source,ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-source-receipt-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(T0)) || T0))`. For complete protected canonical bytes `T`, `bundle_stage_source_receipt_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-source-receipt/v1\0") || uint32be(len(T)) || T))`.

Each source is selected by closed `BundleStageSourceSelectorV1={schema_version:1,kind:"bundle_stage_source_selector_v1",scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,source_kind:"installed|explicit_pool|capability_pool|topology",operation_id,receipt_digest,receipt_object_identity_digest,terminal_outcome:"passed",completed_at,selector_key_kind:"candidate_parent|primary_owner",candidate_controller_key_id,candidate_proposal_digest,candidate_evidence_bytes_digest,candidate_proposal_sequence,mac}`. Candidate selector MAC uses `K_candidate_runtime_evidence_selection`; primary uses `K_bundle_stage_source_selector=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_bundle_stage_source,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-source-selector/v1"),L=32)`. Candidate scope requires all four `candidate_*` members non-null and byte-exact projections of the verified `CandidateRuntimeEvidenceProposalV1`: controller key equals the selected controller key, proposal digest is its normative complete signed digest, evidence-bytes digest equals the reopened receipt bytes, and proposal sequence equals `(stage_ordinal-1)*4+source_ordinal`; the proposal must use `evidence_kind:"bundle_stage_source_receipt"`, the selector's run/source operation/receipt digest and object identity, `selection_kind:"bundle_stage_source_selector"`, and null predecessor. Primary scope requires all four `candidate_*` members null. In both cases `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K,ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-source-selector-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S0)) || S0))` for `S0=CanonicalJSONV1(selector with mac omitted)`, and complete bytes `S` have `bundle_stage_source_selector_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-source-selector/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S)) || S))`. Exact stores are scope-local `runtime-evidence/stage-sources/receipts/<source-kind>/<receipt-digest>.json` and `runtime-evidence/stage-sources/selectors/<source-kind>/<operation-id>.json`. The only receipt temporary is `runtime-evidence/stage-sources/receipts/.stage-source-receipt.<ordinal-1-through-4>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp` and the only selector temporary is the analogous `selectors/.stage-source-selector.<ordinal-1-through-4>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`; publication serialises the four source kinds within an ordinal, and at most one of each class may survive per stage ordinal, yielding the four-plus-four reserve below. Selector filename operation ID, source kind, embedded operation ID, receipt digest, reopened object identity, outcome, time, scope/run, candidate linkage/nullability, and MAC must all agree. Candidate source-receipt bytes use the existing signed-proposal/parent-publication channel before the parent selects them; primary source owners publish directly. The terminal receipt is synced and same-descriptor reopened before selector publication; the selector then uses file sync, exact-prior-or-absence CAS, directory sync, and same-descriptor reopen. No operation can select two terminal receipts of one source kind.

Each receipt is at most 65,536 bytes, selector at most 4,096 bytes. Candidate scope's one current four-stage graph retains exactly 16 receipts and 16 selectors and reserves four receipt plus four selector temporaries: exactly 40 files and `16*65,536 + 16*4,096 + 4*65,536 + 4*4,096 = 1,392,640` bytes under 2 MiB. Primary scope's prior pinned plus complete next graph retains 32 receipts and 32 selectors with the same eight-temporary reserve: exactly 72 files and `2,506,752` bytes under 3 MiB. Both scopes total 112 files and `3,899,392` bytes under 4 MiB. Candidate receipt or selector 17, primary receipt or selector 33, either scope's fifth temporary of either class, an oversized object, or the first aggregate byte over its scope or combined cap refuses before the source operation. Before any candidate source operation, admission reserves the complete current graph and all eight temporaries; before a primary next-graph source operation it reserves the complete prior-plus-next graph and all eight temporaries. Publication collision accepts only byte equality. Recovery adopts only a completely verified receipt followed by its exact selector, removes and syncs only registered unselected same-operation temporaries, and otherwise inhibits; it never regenerates source time, identity, receipt, or selector. A selected source remains pinned by its stage closure/proof, candidate selector, validation/rehearsal receipt, finalisation graph, and last-final-release history; pinned receipts/selectors are never counted as replaceable headroom, and reference-aware synced GC removes a receipt and selector together only after every such reference clears.

The nested closure objects are closed projections that carry their authority: `BundleStageInstalledEvidenceV1={schema_version:1,scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,source_receipt_digest,source_receipt_object_identity_digest,source_selector_digest,installed_validation_operation_id,installed_validation_run_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,required_features,corpus_revision,corpus_case_set_digest,corpus_execution_result_digest,transport_results:{http:"passed",compact:"passed",retained:"passed",websocket:"passed"},required_marker_children:[{marker_child_id:MarkerChildID,marker_object_digest}],marker_set_fingerprint,validated_at}`; `BundleStageExplicitPoolEvidenceV1={schema_version:1,scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,source_receipt_digest,source_receipt_object_identity_digest,source_selector_digest,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,operation_id,pool_object_digest,binding_object_digest,delegation_object_digest,cases:[{case_kind:"positive"|"unavailable"|"excluded"|"zero_fallback",fixture_digest,result:"passed",upstream_attempt_count}],completed_at}`; `BundleStageCapabilityPoolEvidenceV1={schema_version:1,scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,source_receipt_digest,source_receipt_object_identity_digest,source_selector_digest,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,authority_generation,routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,operation_id,pool_object_digest,capability_predicate_set_digest,capability_evidence_set_digest,cases:[{case_kind:"positive"|"unavailable"|"excluded"|"zero_fallback",fixture_digest,result:"passed",upstream_attempt_count}],completed_at}`; and `BundleStageTopologyEvidenceV1={schema_version:1,scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,source_receipt_digest,source_receipt_object_identity_digest,source_selector_digest,operation_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,listener_generation,authority_generation,routing_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,listener_tuple_digest,supervisor_process_identity_digest,worker_process_identity_digest,runtime_holder_checkpoint_digest,public_admission_state:"inhibited",observed_at}`. Installed marker rows are non-empty, duplicate-free, sorted by raw ID bytes, equal `RequiredMarkerChildren(required_features)` exactly, and resolve the historical store. Pool case lists have exactly the four displayed rows in that order, with attempt count one only for `positive` and zero otherwise. Topology resolves the same-descriptor selected holder checkpoint and its exact two live holders.

`BundleStageEvidenceClosureV1={schema_version:1,kind:"bundle_stage_evidence_closure_v1",ordinal,scope:"candidate|primary",validation_run_id,installed_validation_run_id,stage_kind:"candidate_target_before|candidate_floor|candidate_floor_restored|candidate_target_after|primary_target_before|primary_floor|primary_floor_restored|primary_target_after",operation_id,proxy_instance_id,runtime_instance_id,effective_authority_generation,effective_routing_generation,listener_generation,release_artifact_set_digest,required_features,marker_set_fingerprint,installed:BundleStageInstalledEvidenceV1,policy:RuntimePolicyAckV1,explicit_pool:BundleStageExplicitPoolEvidenceV1,capability_pool:BundleStageCapabilityPoolEvidenceV1,topology:BundleStageTopologyEvidenceV1,captured_at,integrity_kind:"owner_mac|controller_signature",issuer_public_key,integrity}` is closed. `required_features` is sorted, duplicate-free, and equals literal `ProxyReleaseFeatureSetV1`; `installed_validation_run_id` is always non-null and is independent of the outer candidate-controller run field.

| Closure field or relation | Candidate scope | Primary scope | Required equality/source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stage_kind`, `validation_run_id` | candidate stage literal; non-null selected controller run | primary stage literal; canonical null | stage proof, candidate controller/receipt, and every nested `validation_run_id` agree; primary nested run fields are null |
| `installed_validation_run_id` | non-null and equal to the selected candidate installed-validation operation run within that controller run | non-null primary installed-validation operation run, independent of null `validation_run_id` | `installed.installed_validation_run_id` and every required marker object's validation-run ID equal it |
| `proxy_instance_id` | selected candidate instance | ticketed primary instance | outer, installed, policy, both pool objects, topology, boot acknowledgement, and containing receipt agree |
| `runtime_instance_id` | selected candidate stage runtime | selected primary stage runtime | outer, all five nested objects, boot acknowledgement, holder checkpoint, and stage proof agree |
| effective authority/routing/listener generations | selected candidate effective tuple | selected primary effective tuple | outer tuple equals installed, policy, both pool objects, and topology; listener also equals boot/stage proof, while entry generations remain the separate earlier proof fields |
| `release_artifact_set_digest` | selected target/floor stage set | selected target/floor stage set | outer and every nested object equal the boot/stage proof and release graph |
| `required_features` | exact candidate receipt requirement | exact primary ticket/rehearsal requirement | outer, installed, policy, containing receipt, and literal release set agree; every required marker row is its exact transitive closure |
| `marker_set_fingerprint` | candidate installed-validation marker set selected during the controller run | primary installed-validation marker set | outer equals `installed.marker_set_fingerprint` and `policy.readiness_marker_set_fingerprint`; recomputation from exact `MarkerSetFingerprintInputV1` and the ordered marker rows must match |
| installed source | controller-selected `InstalledValidationTerminalReceiptV1` | history-selected `InstalledValidationTerminalReceiptV1` | selector is `source_kind=installed`; evidence source digest/identity/selector equal reopened bytes; `installed_validation_operation_id=operation_id`, `validated_at=completed_at`, and every remaining evidence field is byte-identical to the receipt |
| explicit-pool source | controller-selected `ExplicitPoolValidationTerminalReceiptV1` | history-selected `ExplicitPoolValidationTerminalReceiptV1` | selector is `source_kind=explicit_pool`; evidence source digest/identity/selector, `operation_id`, complete object digests/cases, and `completed_at` are byte-identical receipt projections |
| capability-pool source | controller-selected `CapabilityPoolValidationTerminalReceiptV1` | history-selected `CapabilityPoolValidationTerminalReceiptV1` | selector is `source_kind=capability_pool`; evidence source digest/identity/selector, `operation_id`, complete object digests/cases, and `completed_at` are byte-identical receipt projections |
| topology source | controller-selected `RuntimeTopologyObservationTerminalReceiptV1` | history-selected `RuntimeTopologyObservationTerminalReceiptV1` | selector is `source_kind=topology`; evidence source digest/identity/selector, `operation_id`, holder/process/listener facts, and `observed_at=completed_at` are byte-identical receipt projections |
| integrity | selected-controller signature/public key | authority-derived owner MAC with null issuer key | closure and embedded policy acknowledgement independently satisfy their exact scope integrity and nullability |

Each of the four source receipt operations is terminal `passed`; its `started_at` is no earlier than the stage entry terminal/boot acknowledgement and its `completed_at` is no later than closure capture. Its selector is durable after receipt sync and before capture, and its operation ID may differ from the outer stage operation only through the exact typed selector above. The four selected receipt/object identities are pairwise distinct across stages; a prior-stage selector or receipt cannot be reused. `captured_at` equals the maximum of the four receipt completion projections and `policy.acknowledged_at`. At capture the producer securely reopens each selector, then its named receipt and every marker through retained directory descriptors; it retains those exact open descriptions until the complete closure is published and same-descriptor verified. Replacement between selector, receipt, marker, or closure reopen; path-based reopen; nonterminal outcome; source outside the stage window; source/field substitution; and source GC all inhibit before proof construction.

With `C0=CanonicalJSONV1(closure with integrity omitted)`, candidate `integrity=Ed25519.Sign(controller_seed,ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-evidence-closure-signature/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C0)) || C0)`. Primary uses `K_bundle_stage_evidence=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-evidence/v1"),L=32)` and `integrity=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_bundle_stage_evidence,ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-evidence-closure-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C0)) || C0))`. For complete canonical bytes `C`, `bundle_stage_evidence_closure_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/bundle-stage-evidence-closure/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`. The owning candidate controller or selected primary stage operation is the sole producer: after reopening the four exact terminal receipt/selector pairs, the canonical readiness acknowledgement, and all 90 marker objects, it constructs, signs/MACs, content-addresses, publishes, syncs, same-descriptor reopens, and verifies the closure before constructing the corresponding `BundleStageProofV1`. Caller-supplied bytes, a history-only scalar projection, a digest-only source/policy/marker claim, a source that changes across reopen, cross-stage reuse, or construction after the proof is forbidden.

Candidate controller signatures and candidate-root writes are joined by one closed proposal/publication/selection protocol; neither party impersonates the other. Closed `CandidateRuntimeEvidenceProposalV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_runtime_evidence_proposal_v1",validation_run_id,controller_key_id,evidence_kind:"runtime_boot_ack|runtime_holder_checkpoint|bundle_stage_source_receipt|bundle_stage_evidence_closure|bundle_stage_proof",evidence_digest,evidence_bytes_digest,target_store_identity_digest,selection_kind:"holder_checkpoint_anchor|bundle_stage_source_selector|candidate_stage_evidence_anchor",selection_operation_id,expected_selection_predecessor_digest,sequence,created_at,signature}` is 1–4,096 canonical bytes. For canonical proposal bytes `Q0` with signature omitted, `signature=Ed25519.Sign(controller_seed,ASCII("cq/candidate-runtime-evidence-proposal-signature/v1\0") || uint32be(len(Q0)) || Q0)`; for complete signed canonical bytes `Q`, `candidate_runtime_evidence_proposal_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-runtime-evidence-proposal/v1\0") || uint32be(len(Q)) || Q))`. For complete canonical evidence bytes `X`, `evidence_bytes_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-runtime-evidence-bytes/v1\0") || uint32be(len(X)) || X))`; `evidence_digest` independently equals the evidence kind's normative framed digest. Boot acknowledgements, checkpoints, source receipts, and stage-evidence closures also carry their own selected-controller integrity. A candidate `BundleStageProofV1` is authenticated by the complete signed proposal that binds its exact bytes and digest; the parent never treats the otherwise unsigned stage object alone as controller evidence. Proposal and evidence bytes bind the same run/controller key/operation/attempt/runtime/holder, terminal source, or stage facts. Over the authenticated controller-parent channel, the controller sends complete `Q` and complete `X`, with evidence bounded to 65,536 bytes, and retains both until terminal acknowledgement. The parent retaining the candidate-root descriptor is the sole publisher: it verifies the selected controller key, proposal signature, canonical bytes, both framed digests, current run, exact store identity, legal selector, sequence, and selected predecessor, then bounded-streams `X` to a random-exclusive temporary, syncs, no-replace-renames, syncs the directory, and same-descriptor reopens exact bytes. Publication alone is inert. A `bundle_stage_source_receipt` proposal has `selection_kind=bundle_stage_source_selector`, null predecessor, `selection_operation_id` equal to the terminal receipt operation, and sequence `(stage_ordinal-1)*4+source_ordinal`, where source ordinals are exactly installed=1, explicit_pool=2, capability_pool=3, topology=4. After receipt reopen, the parent alone publishes the exact MACed candidate `BundleStageSourceSelectorV1`; no later source or closure proposal is accepted before the controller verifies its deterministic selection acknowledgement.

Candidate boot-ack and checkpoint proposals select together through the candidate rows of `RuntimeHolderCheckpointAnchorV1`. Candidate stage proposals select through the crash-linearised single-current-graph store `runtime-evidence/candidate-stage-evidence/{graphs/,candidate-stage-evidence.anchor}`. `CandidateStageGraphIDV1` is exactly 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters from an independent OS-CSPRNG 128-bit value. Closed `CandidateStageEvidenceGraphV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_stage_evidence_graph_v1",validation_run_id,controller_key_id,graph_id,graph_generation:0,sequence,previous_graph_object_digest,selected:[{ordinal,proposal:CandidateRuntimeEvidenceProposalV1,evidence_digest,evidence_bytes_digest,reopened_object_identity_digest}],mac}` has `sequence=length(selected)` in 1–8, strictly contiguous selection ordinals one through sequence, null predecessor only at sequence one, and otherwise the exact prior complete graph-object digest for the same ID, generation zero, and run. Every successor preserves all prior rows byte-identically and appends exactly one row whose embedded complete signed proposal has `selection_kind="candidate_stage_evidence_anchor"`, `selection_operation_id=graph_id`, equal ordinal/sequence/run/key/digests/object identity, and `expected_selection_predecessor_digest` equal the reopened predecessor or null at the first row. For stage ordinal `n` in one through four, selection ordinal `2n-1` is exactly its `bundle_stage_evidence_closure` proposal and selection ordinal `2n` is exactly its `bundle_stage_proof` proposal; the proof names the immediately preceding selected closure digest, and no later-stage row may appear until both rows for `n` are selected. For canonical graph-object bytes `G0` with MAC omitted, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_candidate_runtime_evidence_selection,ASCII("cq/candidate-stage-evidence-graph-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(G0)) || G0))`; the stored value is exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters. For complete MACed bytes `G`, `candidate_stage_evidence_graph_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-stage-evidence-graph/v1\0") || uint32be(len(G)) || G))`. A graph object is at most 65,536 bytes and lives content-addressed at `graphs/<candidate_stage_evidence_graph_digest>.json`; a proposal/evidence object remains inert until named by its same-descriptor reopened graph successor. A prepared candidate admits exactly this one graph ID and generation-zero chain for its one controller run; another ID, any nonzero generation, or row nine refuses before publication.

The sole parent selector is closed `CandidateStageEvidenceAnchorV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_stage_evidence_anchor_v1",validation_run_id,external_reference_binding:CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1,controller_key_id,sequence,previous_anchor_digest,current:{graph_id,graph_generation:0,sequence,graph_digest},mac}`. Anchor `sequence` begins at one and increments by one; `previous_anchor_digest` is null only for the first anchor and otherwise equals the reopened prior complete-anchor digest. `current` is always non-null and resolves the exact graph object whose run/key/ID/generation-zero/sequence/digest agree. Initial publication selects the first row of the run's sole graph as `current`; each later graph-row publication is inert until one anchor CAS advances that same current head to its immediately following successor. No retirement, rotation, promotion, prior/next pair, second graph ID, or generation increment exists inside a candidate run. For canonical anchor bytes `A0` with MAC omitted, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_candidate_runtime_evidence_selection,ASCII("cq/candidate-stage-evidence-anchor-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A0)) || A0))`; the stored value is exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters. For complete MACed bytes `A`, `candidate_stage_evidence_anchor_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-stage-evidence-anchor/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`. The anchor is at most 65,536 bytes and is published by file-sync, exact-prior compare-and-replace, directory-sync, and same-descriptor reopen; graph objects use bounded temporary publication, file sync, content-addressed no-replace rename, directory sync, and same-descriptor reopen. Recovery adopts only a byte-identical selected anchor or resumes this one graph against its exact selected predecessor with the same live controller; an unselected graph successor is inert, controller loss leaves it cleanup-only, and ambiguous selector sync, duplicate/different ID, nonzero generation, stale predecessor, a second graph, or a head naming a missing/nonmatching object inhibits. The complete row-eight current head and its predecessor chain remain pinned through validation-receipt signing, export retirement, canonical import verification, and every retained finalisation/final-release reference; candidate removal may retire them only after a byte-identical canonical imported receipt has durably preserved and verified the terminal selection below or after every successful validation/export reference has been abandoned. The graph-object publication followed by the current-head CAS is the sole candidate stage-evidence selection path: no stage receipt, CLI result, validation receipt, or next-stage action may name stage `n` until rows `2n-1` and `2n` are selected by `current`.

After any durable selector, the parent returns deterministic closed `CandidateRuntimeEvidenceSelectionV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_runtime_evidence_selection_v1",validation_run_id,external_reference_binding:CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1,controller_key_id,proposal_digest,evidence_kind,evidence_digest,evidence_bytes_digest,reopened_object_identity_digest,selection_kind,selector_digest,selector_sequence,stage_graph_id:null|string,stage_graph_generation:null|uint64,stage_graph_digest:null|string,stage_parent_anchor_digest:null|string,mac}`. Every member is a byte-identical projection of the selected holder-anchor row, the source selector's persisted `candidate_controller_key_id`, `candidate_proposal_digest`, `candidate_evidence_bytes_digest`, `candidate_proposal_sequence`, receipt digest and receipt object identity, or the embedded selected stage-graph proposal/row plus the parent anchor that selects that graph as `current`; all four `stage_*` fields are non-null exactly for stage evidence and otherwise null, every non-null `stage_graph_generation` is zero, and there is no time, nonce, or process-local member. A candidate source selector or stage selector missing any required projection is not a selector and cannot produce an acknowledgement. For canonical selection bytes `S0` with MAC omitted, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_candidate_runtime_evidence_selection,ASCII("cq/candidate-runtime-evidence-selection-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S0)) || S0))`; the stored value is exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters. For complete MACed bytes `S`, `candidate_runtime_evidence_selection_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-runtime-evidence-selection/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S)) || S))`. The controller re-verifies this acknowledgement against retained `Q` and `X` before a later source, closure, admission, terminal authority, stage completion, or sender-reference release. It never receives the candidate-root/store descriptor; the parent never creates or changes controller-signed bytes. Before object publication, recovery may request only exact-byte retransmission from the same live controller and proposal. An object published before selector sync remains inert and recovery may select only the same proposal against the unchanged predecessor or absent source selector. After selector sync, any parent recovery deterministically reconstructs the byte-identical selection acknowledgement from the reopened selector and selection key. Different bytes, key, graph ID/generation, predecessor, selector, source operation, or a dead/lost controller before selection leaves the object inert and follows run cleanup. Proposal and acknowledgement are bounded IPC frames, not store leaves.

For complete canonical boot-ack bytes `B` including integrity, `runtime_boot_ack_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/runtime-boot-ack/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))`; launcher-handoff and restart-attempt digests use the same construction over complete MACed bytes and domains `cq/runtime-launcher-handoff/v1\0` and `cq/runtime-restart-attempt/v1\0`. The primary boot-integrity issuer or owning primary stage/restart operation publishes and reopens its exact object; candidate boot acknowledgements, checkpoints, stage-source receipts, stage-evidence closures, and stage proofs use the proposal/publication/selection protocol above; the embedded candidate launcher lineage is part of the boot-ack bytes and needs no separate object. No journal, attempt, source, stage, receipt, or finalisation state may name an object before its corresponding durable selector. Exact objects live beneath the scope's own `runtime-evidence/boot-acks/<runtime_boot_ack_digest>.json`, `stage-evidence/<bundle_stage_evidence_closure_digest>.json`, `stage-proofs/<bundle_stage_proof_digest>.json`, primary-only `launcher-handoffs/<launcher_handoff_digest>.json`, primary-only `restart-attempts/<restart_attempt_digest>.json`, or candidate-only `candidate-stage-evidence/{graphs/<candidate_stage_evidence_graph_digest>.json,candidate-stage-evidence.anchor}`; candidate handoff/restart entries are forbidden. Historical marker and terminal-source objects/selectors live only in their separately capped `installed-markers` and `stage-sources` subtrees defined above and are not charged again to this base runtime-evidence envelope. Boot acknowledgements, stage-evidence closures, stage proofs, restart attempts, graph objects, parent anchor, and publication temporaries are at most 65,536 bytes each; launcher handoffs are at most 4,096 bytes. Primary admits at most 32 boot acknowledgements, eight stage-evidence closures, eight stage proofs, 32 launcher handoffs, 16 restart attempts, and four publication temporaries: exactly 100 regular files and `4,587,520` bytes under a 5-MiB aggregate cap. Candidate admits 32 boot acknowledgements, four stage-evidence closures, four stage proofs, eight immutable graph-successor objects, one parent anchor, four publication temporaries shared by evidence, graph, and anchor publication, and zero handoff/restart attempts: exactly 53 regular files and `53 * 65,536 = 3,473,408` bytes under a 4-MiB aggregate cap. Both base runtime-evidence stores total exactly 153 files and `4,587,520 + 3,473,408 = 8,060,928` bytes under 8 MiB; the first file or byte over either scope or combined cap refuses before producer work. Those four closure/proof pairs and eight graph-successor slots are exactly the current candidate run's one four-stage graph; admission reserves their separately capped marker/source children and every object/selector slot before the first stage producer action. Publication is bounded streaming to a random-exclusive temporary, file sync, content-addressed no-replace rename, parent sync, and same-descriptor canonical reopen; an existing digest succeeds only on exact byte equality. Active journals, current runtime and holder checkpoint, current policy acknowledgement, every source selector, the selected current stage-graph head, the parent anchor and every embedded signed proposal, open candidate run/receipt export, four-stage receipts, active import finalisation, current plus 15 authority-history generations, and the last final release pin their boot, handoff, restart, marker, source receipt/selector, closure, and stage-proof objects. GC removes only unreferenced objects after the owning history/receipt checkpoint and directory sync; a stage proof pins its exact closure and that closure pins all 90 markers plus four source receipt/selector pairs, the selected current graph head pins its complete predecessor chain and stage objects, and a graph/anchor/object unlink is directory-synced before its capacity may be reused. Journal `readiness_ack_digest`, launcher/restart references, and every stage/finalisation reference name these exact stored objects.

When explicitly invoked while rescue is effective, `runtime_bundle_switch` remains a matched-pair operation but never opens normal admission. The replacement supervisor inherits the listener in rescue, privately boots the exact paired worker only for the same ABI/feature/process proof, then stops and reaps it before terminal rescue acknowledgement. Success selects the matched pair while preserving the saved rescue intent/suspension; failure restores the prior matched pair or remains pending under the ordinary one-rollback switch protocol. A later, separate `rescue exit` is the only operation that may boot that selected worker for normal service.

Boot acknowledgement never claims feature readiness and does not open admission. Target pair remains `activation_inhibited` until exact primary installed validation creates marker set for that pair and current runtime publishes `RuntimePolicyAckV1`; only then terminal authority may open admission. No mixed pair admits traffic. Terminal proof binds both digests, constant socket lineage, boot acknowledgement, marker-set fingerprint, and policy acknowledgement. One rollback restores matched prior pair through same protocol. Candidate form is permitted only through controller-authenticated `candidate artifact switch` during open confinement run and binds validation-run digest in lifecycle action; generic service form rejects candidate role. Release rehearsal has four effective-runtime stages and three switch operations: initial target; successful target→floor target attempt; a deterministic floor→target target-attempt failure followed by the operation's sole rollback to a newly booted floor runtime; and a separate successful floor→target target attempt. The rehearsal-only failure barrier is legal only under the exact candidate validation controller or selected import-finalisation child while admission is inhibited and the real client is stopped. It commits the target attempt before action, forces a definite pre-readiness boot-token rejection, kills/reaps that exact failed target process group, and permits the already journalled floor rollback once; it is unavailable to generic service commands. Its terminal receipt is `prior_restored` and binds the failed target attempt plus floor rollback boot acknowledgement. Ambiguous failure remains pending and cannot count as the rollback stage. This four-stage chain tests both target success and actual prior restoration across every inter-role crash boundary.

Unfinished transition never silently blocks all future recovery. `recovery transition status` performs fresh read-only topology proof. `resolve`, `restore`, and the listener-release-only `resume` leaf require exact operation ID plus explicit confirmation. Resolve and restore use this closed table:

| Fresh evidence | Permitted recovery |
|---|---|
| target topology fully satisfies original terminal proof | `resolve --accept-current-target` commits terminal `target_effective`; no external action |
| prior topology fully satisfies original terminal proof | `restore --accept-current-prior` commits terminal `prior_restored`; no external action |
| target is definitely absent/failed, prior is absent, original target outcome is non-ambiguous, and journal proves no restoration was issued | `restore --attempt-prior` first commits one recovery-attempt ID, performs exact retained restoration once, then commits terminal only after proof |
| target outcome ambiguous, foreign/partial topology, missing retained artifact, or any prior recovery attempt uncertain | no action; remain `pending|timeout_pending` until operator establishes one exact supported topology |

The `staged_release` coordinator row deliberately narrows that generic table because its only external fact is one stage-kind anchor CAS. Before that CAS, when the selected child is still at `intent` and the exact prior anchor bytes or proved initial absence remain effective, only `restore --accept-current-prior` is legal: it performs no selector write, commits the child directly to terminal `prior_restored`, clears the matching authority operation reference, and maps the coordinator to `prior_restored`. `resolve` and `--attempt-prior` refuse on that side. Once fresh same-descriptor evidence proves the exact proposed anchor bytes effective, only `resolve --accept-current-target` is legal: it checkpoints `selector_committed` if needed and completes `staged` or `cleared`; `restore` and `--attempt-prior` refuse and may not undo the CAS. A missing, substituted, cross-kind, or neither-prior-nor-proposed anchor remains pending/indeterminate with no selector write. Terminal staged-release recovery is inspection-only and never repeats import, anchor CAS, clear, or GC.

`recovery transition resume` is a disjoint fourth recovery action, not another branch of the evidence table. It is admitted only when the full operation ID resolves one structured `LifecycleActionV1` listener-release child selected at `phase=barrier_waiting`, its coordinator and authority references still select that same child, and its trusted socket-hold/respawn-inhibition proof reopens current. The command requires both confirmations, the exact operation-bound current barrier selection, a fresh complete request-sender/domain/transport enumeration and `ClientStopProofV1`, zero permits/connections/admitted work, and unchanged manager/job/socket/listener/desired-target identity. It first selects and syncs a same-operation `barrier` successor with the fresh proof and the command's new recovery deadline; only then may the existing lifecycle state machine commit its first external action-attempt ID and continue the original target action. It creates no second coordinator or lifecycle intent, never accepts current target/prior as a substitute, never resumes a pre-authority legacy journal or another phase/kind, and never repeats an action already attempted. Conflict returns 3 with no external action; unavailable or ambiguous required proof returns 4; timeout or a safely durable unfinished suffix remains pending/1 with the inert trusted socket owner retained; exact terminal target proof returns 0. Re-entry reopens the same child and either continues its one committed attempt under ordinary ambiguity rules or returns its terminal result.

`--attempt-prior` is unavailable for any record whose prior/target local-token fingerprints differ; restoring credential authority requires a new forward cutover, never revival through generic recovery. For listener-releasing records it conditionally requires fresh `--confirm-client-stopped`, `ClientStopProofV1`, and the exact `ClientBearerBarrierV1` receipt over the complete current authoritatively enumerated set of sensitive request senders and transports, including senders incapable of `Authorization`, and binds those proofs to recovery-attempt ID. Missing barrier support or any unsupported/unregistered request sender or transport makes restoration refuse before action. `--accept-current-prior` remains proof-only and performs no token/listener action. Recovery never repeats original target action, never infers outcome from timeout, never changes listener/config/policy intent, and never clears journal without one proven terminal topology. Quarantine remains unavailable while transition is active.

Candidate launcher bootstrap uses the same fixed two-role exec ABI as primary. Before any candidate-root, artifact, credential, routing, or other private-state read, the inhibited launcher must possess exactly one launchd-provided listener at fixed `listener_fd` and the already selected supervisor lifecycle slot at fixed unequal `lifecycle_fd`; it verifies the listener's socket type, tuple, manager event, generation, descriptor identity, and live ownership, and verifies the lifecycle row against the selected allocation. Immediately before same-PID/start-token `exec`, it clears `FD_CLOEXEC` on exactly those two descriptors, closes every other inherited or private-state descriptor, and carries both unchanged into the selected supervisor. The complete `CandidateLauncherExecLineageV1` member list above is amended with mandatory `{listener_fd_role:"listener_fd",lifecycle_fd_role:"lifecycle_fd",inherited_listener_tuple,listener_descriptor_identity_digest,pre_exec_listener_proof_digest,post_exec_listener_proof_digest}`. The listener proofs bind the run, operation, attempt, boot token, manager event, listener generation, fixed descriptor number, socket type/tuple, kernel socket identity, launcher/supervisor PID and start token, boot session, and pre-/post-exec executable identities; both proofs establish the same live socket description across exec. The existing lifecycle proofs analogously bind fixed `lifecycle_fd` and the same selected locked slot. Post-exec, before the narrow bootstrap read or any other private-state access, the supervisor validates both unequal fixed roles, continuing listener and shared-lock facts, and equality of the embedded signed lineage and `RuntimeBootAckV1.inherited_listener_tuple`; it then restores `FD_CLOEXEC` on both. Missing, extra, swapped, reopened, duplicated, wrong-socket, wrong-slot, changed-tuple, CLOEXEC-retained, or lineage-mismatched roles produce no boot acknowledgement or holder checkpoint and enter controller cleanup-only recovery. Crash classification accepts a post-exec process only through both complete proof pairs; otherwise it proves pre-exec absence or remains pending and never fabricates a supervisor or reopens either descriptor.

### `RuntimeControlChannel`

Supervisor retains `<instance-state-root>/runtime.lock` from before control socket, listener adoption, worker start, or mutable subsystem access until final shutdown. A second runtime cannot open coordinator, cache, or other state before losing a late bind. Stale `control.sock` is removed only while holding runtime lease and after proving recorded owner dead.

Supervisor exposes owner-only `<instance-state-root>/control.sock`, verifies peer UID, and uses `authority.key`-derived live-control MAC. Connection-bound exchange covers command kind, canonical body digest, expected composite authority/routing generations, stable `proxy_instance_id`, current `runtime_instance_id`, listener generation, both nonces, expiry, and connection identity. Nonces are single-use; comparisons are constant-time; response uses separate acknowledgement label. CLI never reconnects to replay ambiguous mutation.

Mutation key is `(proxy_instance_id, listener_generation, operation_id, intent_authority_generation)`. Stable `proxy_instance_id` survives supervisor restart and owns persisted idempotency. Per-process `runtime_instance_id` binds one live control connection, readiness acknowledgement, marker publication, and restart invalidation; it never keys persisted operation identity. Lost acknowledgement triggers fresh attested read. Matching terminal operation is idempotent success; proven earlier phase may resume journal; ambiguous/replaced ownership returns pending or indeterminate. Every ordinary post-authority mutation first reconciles the parent coordinator anchor with authority `active_operation_ref` and requires `active_initialisation_ref` null; exact fresh-initialisation recovery instead reconciles the parent initialisation anchor with `active_initialisation_ref` and requires the coordinator idle. Traffic-mode changes, artifact switches, and listener/config migration use the matching coordinator chain plus `authority.lock` and one expected composite generation; single-generation pool/session/capability mutations require the coordinator and both authority active-reference fields idle and use the same lock/generation CAS. File lock releases before runtime admission gate; no disk/network I/O occurs while gate held.

### `ProxySnapshot`

Collects independent best-effort facts without creating config, refreshing credentials, contacting provider data planes, starting services, or rewriting state.

Snapshot layers:

1. Inspector: executable path, version, commit, digest.
2. Desired configuration: path, existence, parse state, permissions, redacted digest, listener.
3. Authority state: anchor/object/key parse state, desired mode, composite generation, transition, permissions, required-feature floor.
4. Lifecycle candidates: every supported plist/job, loaded/running state, PID, arguments, executable, run count, last exit, logs.
5. Listener: exact address/socket tuple, launchd activation definition, every process retaining descriptor, serving supervisor PID/UID/executable/start time, and descriptor-lineage consistency.
6. Runtime: reachability, latency, HTTP status, supervisor identity, worker identity/state, effective mode, effective generations.
7. Routing policy: desired/effective generation, pool/binding/evidence counts, inhibited/draining/degraded counts.
8. Instance authority: state-root digest, normal-config path/digest, launcher/artifact digests, global-allowlist/default digests, control-socket identity, and coordinator ownership.
9. Authorisation-sender barrier: securely re-enumerated `LocalTokenClientRegistryV1` sender rows, including the stateless `cq_config_read_per_call_v1` adapter; sender/executable and config-source binding sets; credential-domain and token-fingerprint generations; current listener/socket/job generations; selected release/migration/promotion operation when any; retained barrier receipt/protocol binding; and supported, unsupported, and unregistered sender counts. It reads no raw token or credential and emits only the privacy-safe projection below.
10. Optional data-plane probe: target, time, outcome, and quota-use acknowledgement. Absent unless explicitly requested.

Fact collection never stops at the first error. Each layer records `known`, `absent`, `invalid`, `unavailable`, or `permission_denied` plus a safe error code.

### `Supervisor` and `NormalWorker`

Managed V1 primary uses launchd socket activation. On every launchd birth, the CQ-owned stable launcher first acquires and attests the exact fixed lifecycle inode shared on its own open-file description before reading any instance root, authority, or artifact selection. It then calls `launch_activate_socket`, verifies the signed selected pair, durably publishes `RuntimeLauncherHandoffV1`, and carries exactly the frozen `listener_fd` and locked `lifecycle_fd` roles across `exec` of the exact supervisor digest, with `FD_CLOEXEC` clear only for those two roles. Before any root access, the supervisor proves same-PID/start-token/boot-token exec lineage and the inherited lifecycle kernel facts, performs only the bounded untrusted handoff lookup permitted by the frozen argv manifest, verifies the handoff MAC/digest and every role/attempt/manager/artifact field, and only then adopts other private state. Launchd retains public loopback socket across supervisor kickstart; normal worker never receives or binds public TCP. Legacy `homebrew.mxcl.cq` process-managed service remains inspectable and operable, but rescue activation first requires explicit migration to socket-activated CQ LaunchAgent. Homebrew may remain binary/package source; manager authority becomes CQ socket LaunchAgent.

Supervisor owns public HTTP server, strict Host/Origin/caller-auth gate, resource admission, ingress-mode choice, signed authority/control, identity/health, rescue relay, and worker lifecycle. Normal worker is a digest-pinned child serving one owner-only Unix socket and owns credential inventory, routing, continuity, registry, diagnostics, provider access, and its separate shared lifecycle-lock description; it opens no root or credential/routing state before verifying the private-bootstrap grant for that description. Supervisor and worker are the exact ordered holder set in the initial `RuntimeBootAckV1` and in the currently selected `RuntimeHolderCheckpointV1`. A worker replacement commits its attempt, proves the prior worker process group dead and reaped and its exact holder description released, transfers and verifies a fresh description before replacement-worker private-state access, then selects one fresh two-row checkpoint before admission reopens. The worker has no Headroom or other ambient-helper execution path. Darwin keychain access is exclusively through `darwin_security_framework_v1` in-process. Worker publishes only safe runtime facts plus runtime-only, keyed HMAC fingerprints for currently authorised downstream bearer credentials; supervisor never receives values. Fingerprint-index revision swaps atomically in admission epoch and is not persisted as composite authority mutation.

Public route/auth ownership is closed:

|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | none | constant liveness only; no worker/private state |
| native Codex | exact Codex caller index | exact caller or active delegation; local token forbidden |
| Claude provider routes | current generated local token or exact Claude caller index | local token uses configured routing; Claude bearer exact matched account |
| Anthropic-compatible model dispatch | before body, one unambiguous current generated local token, exact Claude caller, or exact Codex caller capability; after bounded body classification, exact selected-provider branch admission | Claude branch requires explicit local-owner authority or the exact Claude subject; Codex branch requires explicit local-owner authority or the exact Codex subject and any active Codex delegation; a credential authenticated only in the other provider domain has no authority |
| bounded `GET /v1/models` static projection | none | no worker/provider/private state; authenticated branch separately bounded |
| `GET /v1/registry` | local token or exact Claude caller index | bounded read-only projection |
| `POST /v1/registry/refresh` | local token only | one bounded worker refresh |
| owner control/mutation | Unix peer UID plus control MAC | never TCP |
| candidate Anthropic-compatible model dispatch | exact run-bound `CandidateSyntheticIngressAuthorityV1`-backed Codex caller capability only; every other caller domain rejects before body/worker | after the bounded classification-only worker exchange, a Codex-selected branch may proceed; a Claude-selected or invalid (including missing, malformed, noncanonical, or mismatched) classification rejects before `OpenHTTP`, inventory, planning, continuity, credential resolution, or provider dispatch |

`NormalCodexRouteCatalogV1` is the closed compile-time authority for the complete normal public matcher, including non-Codex rows whose precedence determines whether a request can reach Codex. It is `{schema_version:1,rows:[{route_id,patterns:[{method:"*|GET|POST",escaped_path,match_kind:"exact|subtree|catch_all"}],owner_features:[FeatureID],route_class,action,upstream_origin_bindings:[credential_domain],upstream_targets:[escaped_path_template],query_policy,session_coverage,terminal_401_semantics_by_provider:{claude:null|"generic_terminal_only",codex:null|"codex_pinned_direct"|"generic_terminal_only"},downstream_rejection_profiles_by_provider:{claude:null|DownstreamRejectionProfileMapV1,codex:null|DownstreamRejectionProfileMapV1},negative_behaviour,precedes:[route_id]}]}`. The canonical producer sorts rows by `route_id`, patterns by `(escaped_path,method,match_kind)`, owner features, origin bindings, and precedence targets lexically, and rejects every duplicate; the table below is the human projection and need not carry canonical order. V1 contains exactly the 20 rows below. Every field is required; both provider-specific members are null exactly when that row cannot select that provider, binding/target arrays are empty only for wholly local actions, and no unlisted route class/action/query/coverage/terminal-401/downstream-profile value is legal. `codex_pinned_direct` is legal only for the Codex-selected `codex_responses_v1`, `codex_responses_legacy`, `codex_compact_v1`, `codex_compact_legacy`, `anthropic_messages_model_dispatch`, and `claude_fallback` branches whose final upstream semantics are Responses, compact, or normal terminating Responses WebSocket; `anthropic_count_tokens_model_dispatch`, every other Codex route, and every Claude-selected route are `generic_terminal_only`. This tag is consulted only after the complete response resolves to status exactly `401`; it selects pinned/direct-versus-generic terminal-401 evidence and can neither authorise nor inhibit route-neutral Codex `403` direct-candidate classification or exact `429` hard-quota classification. `route_class` is exactly one row of the public route/auth table above: `health` uses `GET /health`, `models_projection` uses bounded `GET /v1/models` static projection, `codex_*` uses native Codex, `registry_read` uses `GET /v1/registry`, `registry_refresh` uses `POST /v1/registry/refresh`, and `anthropic_model_dispatch` uses the two-stage Anthropic-compatible model-dispatch admission row for `anthropic_messages_model_dispatch`, `anthropic_count_tokens_model_dispatch`, and the shared catch-all `claude_fallback`; there is no classifier-bypassing provider fallback route class. For a model-conditioned row, `owner_features` enumerates branch owners rather than imposing an implicit dependency: only the branch whose provider feature is active may dispatch, and selection of an inactive branch returns stable local `feature_inactive` without trying the other provider. The complete third-through-fifth table cells plus the closed profile mapping below supply the canonical action, negative behaviour, origin-target, query, coverage, and downstream error representation for that route ID; the compiler, not free-form runtime parsing, constructs these typed values.

Normal matching is a pinned implementation of baseline Go 1.22+ `ServeMux`, independent of process `GODEBUG`: it obtains `URL.EscapedPath()`, preserves CONNECT's no-clean exception, otherwise applies `cleanPath` to dot segments and repeated slashes, and emits HTTP 307 with the original raw query for a changed clean path or a method-applicable missing subtree slash before handler dispatch. Pattern comparison splits the escaped path on literal slash and unescapes each segment independently; `%2F` therefore remains data inside one segment rather than a separator. Invalid `RawPath` follows `URL.EscapedPath()` fallback to escaped `Path`. The matcher retains the original escaped path/raw query only for an already selected upstream action. `negative_behaviour` fixes these pre-handler redirects, method-specific versus catch-all precedence, Go mux GET-to-HEAD matching, and exact status, `Location`, `Allow`, body/header, worker-dispatch, and provider-dispatch results for HEAD and every method not positively accepted; it never infers a generic 405. `precedes` is exactly `claude_fallback` for every non-fallback row whose pattern intersects `/`, plus `codex_openai_unsupported` for the compact rows and for the `/realtime/calls` patterns of the live-create/sideband rows; `codex_openai_unsupported` itself precedes only `claude_fallback`. Startup constructs its matcher only from this object and refuses any overlap/shadow edge not listed by `precedes`, plus every missing handler or handler/catalogue disagreement. A compile-time enumeration test compares it to every baseline `Server.handler` registration, every member returned by `unsupportedOpenAICompatibleRoutePatterns`, the sole `RouteRequestWithCatalog` invocation beneath the baseline `/` catch-all, and `handleCodex`'s path-only count-token branch. The two named Anthropic paths are semantic partitions of that same method-independent classifier, and every remaining catch-all method/path is the third partition; any added, removed, or changed method/path/classifier branch requires an explicit catalogue, feature-owner, origin-binding, precedence edge, marker, and differential-fixture change.
