| `codex_images_v1` | `* /v1/images/` subtree | `normal_codex_v1`; only POST is native HTTP; other methods are local 405 | `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1`, remove only leading `/v1` and preserve remaining escaped suffix and raw query | global |
| `codex_images_legacy` | `* /images/` subtree | `normal_codex_v1`; only POST is native HTTP; other methods are local 405 | `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1`, preserve escaped path and raw query | global |
| `codex_search` | `POST /alpha/search` | `normal_codex_v1`; native HTTP; other methods follow `claude_fallback` | `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1`, `/alpha/search`, raw query preserved | global |
| `codex_live_create` | `POST /live`, `POST /v1/live`, `POST /realtime/calls`, `POST /v1/realtime/calls` | `normal_codex_v1`; native live-call body conversion; GET and HEAD on each slashless root emit the matcher-owned 307 to the same escaped path plus `/` because a method-applicable sideband subtree exists; other non-POST `/live` methods follow `claude_fallback`, while other non-POST `/realtime/calls` methods hit the longer unsupported subtree row | `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1`, exact `/realtime/calls?intent=quicksilver&architecture=avas`; downstream query does not alter the POST target and a redirect preserves its original raw query | global |
| `codex_live_sideband_path` | `GET /live/`, `GET /v1/live/`, `GET /realtime/calls/`, `GET /v1/realtime/calls/` subtrees | `normal_codex_v1`; account-affine terminating WebSocket; non-GET `/live/` aliases follow `claude_fallback`, while non-GET `/realtime/calls/` aliases hit the longer unsupported subtree row; HEAD follows Go's GET alias | `codex_openai_live_bearer_v1`; remove one optional downstream `/v1`, require one 1–128 byte ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen call ID, then emit exact `/v1/live/<id>` or `/v1/realtime/calls/<id>`; downstream query is ignored | global |
| `codex_live_sideband_query` | `GET /realtime`, `GET /v1/realtime` | `normal_codex_v1`; account-affine terminating WebSocket; non-GET methods follow `claude_fallback` and HEAD follows Go's GET alias | `codex_openai_live_bearer_v1`; baseline decoded query lookup selects the first `call_id`, requires the same call-ID grammar, ignores other downstream values, and emits exact `/v1/realtime?intent=quicksilver&call_id=<canonical-query-escaped-id>` | global |
| `codex_openai_unsupported` | every exact/subtree pattern in the literal set below | `normal_codex_v1`; native caller gate then fixed local 501 with zero worker/provider dispatch | local; query ignored | global |
| `anthropic_messages_model_dispatch` | `* /v1/messages` semantic partition of the catch-all | `normal_claude_v1`, `normal_codex_v1`; pre-body unambiguous local/Claude/Codex authentication then exact body-model classification and selected-provider admission for every method; an active Claude branch preserves the original method and Claude routing, an active Codex branch performs Anthropic-to-Responses translation with upstream POST, and missing branch authority or an inactive provider branch fails locally before inventory/provider dispatch | Claude branch requires explicit local-owner authority or exact Claude subject and uses `claude_access_token_v1` at original `/v1/messages`; Codex branch requires explicit local-owner authority or exact Codex subject/delegation and uses `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1` at POST `/responses`; original raw query is preserved only on the Claude branch and discarded on the translated Codex branch | canonical HTTP Responses when Codex-selected; not applicable when Claude-selected |
| `anthropic_count_tokens_model_dispatch` | `* /v1/messages/count_tokens` semantic partition of the catch-all | `normal_claude_v1`, `normal_codex_v1`; same two-stage authenticated method-independent model-conditioned rule; Codex performs the baseline path-only count-token translation for POST, GET, HEAD, and every other method, and no branch may borrow the other provider's authority or silently fall back | Claude branch requires explicit local-owner authority or exact Claude subject and uses `claude_access_token_v1` with original method at `/v1/messages/count_tokens`; Codex branch requires explicit local-owner authority or exact Codex subject/delegation and uses `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1` at POST `/v1/responses/input_tokens`; original raw query is preserved only on the Claude branch and discarded on the translated Codex branch | global when Codex-selected; not applicable when Claude-selected |
| `claude_fallback` | `* /` catch-all for every remaining method/path after every row above | `normal_claude_v1`, `normal_codex_v1`; pre-body unambiguous local/Claude/Codex authentication then the same exact body-model classifier and selected-provider admission; an active Claude branch preserves the original method/path/query, an active Codex branch performs baseline Anthropic-to-Responses translation with upstream POST, and missing branch authority or an inactive provider branch fails locally without trying the other provider. Candidate pre-body authentication accepts only the exact live `CandidateSyntheticIngressAuthorityV1`-backed Codex caller; after the bounded classification-only worker response it rejects a Claude-selected or invalid (including missing, malformed, noncanonical, or mismatched) classification before `OpenHTTP`, inventory, planning, continuity, credential resolution, or provider dispatch | Claude branch requires explicit local-owner authority or exact Claude subject and uses `claude_access_token_v1` at the original escaped target/query; Codex branch requires explicit local-owner authority or exact Codex subject/delegation and uses `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1` at POST `/responses` with query discarded | canonical HTTP Responses when Codex-selected; not applicable when Claude-selected |

The `codex_openai_unsupported` literal pattern set is exactly `[/v1/responses/,/responses/,/v1/chat/completions,/chat/completions,/v1/completions,/completions,/v1/audio/,/audio/,/v1/embeddings,/embeddings,/v1/moderations,/moderations,/v1/realtime/,/realtime/,/v1/files,/v1/files/,/files,/files/,/v1/uploads,/v1/uploads/,/uploads,/uploads/,/v1/vector_stores,/v1/vector_stores/,/vector_stores,/vector_stores/,/v1/batches,/v1/batches/,/batches,/batches/,/v1/assistants,/v1/assistants/,/assistants,/assistants/,/v1/threads,/v1/threads/,/threads,/threads/,/v1/fine_tuning/,/fine_tuning/,/v1/evals,/v1/evals/,/evals,/evals/,/v1/containers,/v1/containers/,/containers,/containers/,/v1/conversations,/v1/conversations/,/conversations,/conversations/]`; a trailing slash means subtree and every other entry means exact path. The catalogue digest and complete per-row fixture/result digest are bound by `codex.route_catalog`; local/no-dispatch rows by `codex.local_projection`; HTTP and WebSocket positive rows by `codex.http_routes` and `codex.websocket_routes`; all three Codex-selected catch-all model-dispatch partitions by `codex.anthropic_compat_routes`; every credential-bearing target by `codex.origin_policy`; and the full baseline differential plus negative matrix by `codex.differential_corpus`.

`NormalClaudeRouteCatalogV1` is the closed companion authority for Claude-owned public routing and internal Claude credential egress. It has the same canonical sorting, terminal-401 mapping, and duplicate/overlap rejection rules and exactly seven rows: every reachable Claude member is `generic_terminal_only` and every Codex member is null. `claude_public_passthrough` is the Claude-selected branch of the shared HTTP `* /` catch-all after every `NormalCodexRouteCatalogV1` precedence partition and sends the original method, escaped absolute path, and raw query to the Claude base; `anthropic_messages_model_dispatch` and `anthropic_count_tokens_model_dispatch` reference the same public semantic-partition IDs above and authorise only their Claude-selected, method-independent branches; `claude_registry_models` is internal `GET /v1/models` with empty query; `claude_profile` is internal `GET /api/oauth/profile` with empty query; `claude_usage` is internal `GET /api/oauth/usage` with empty query; and `claude_refresh` is internal `POST /v1/oauth/token` with empty query at the refresh-token origin. Public passthrough rejects absolute-form authority changes, scheme-relative paths, fragments, invalid escaped targets, and any request already owned by a preceding local or Codex row; after candidate classification-only worker IPC, its Claude-selected branch rejects before `OpenHTTP`, inventory, planning, continuity, credential resolution, or provider dispatch. Every public and internal Claude egress constructor maps to exactly one row and every row maps to exactly one `NormalCredentialOriginPolicyV1.registered_routes` member. `claude.route_catalog` binds this object and all per-row fixtures; `claude.caller_routes` binds public authentication; `claude.model_dispatch` binds the Claude-selected branches of all three catch-all semantic partitions plus the shared classifier and inactive-branch refusal, while `codex.anthropic_compat_routes` binds their Codex-selected branches; `claude.registry` binds internal model/profile/usage actions; `claude.origin_policy` binds every credential target; and `claude.differential_corpus` binds public fallback plus internal-source baseline parity.

Downstream error selection is catalogue authority, not a runtime handler guess. Closed `DownstreamRejectionProfileEntryV1={schema_version:1,transport_kind:"http"|"websocket",observation_variant:"http_response"|"ws_handshake"|"ws_postupgrade_handshake_error"|"ws_text_message",profile:"native_codex_http_v1"|"claude_reverse_proxy_v1"|"codex_live_get_set_v1"|"codex_ws_postupgrade_handshake_error_v1"|"codex_anthropic_write_error_v1"|"codex_live_sideband_local_502_v1"|"codex_ws_text_message_v1"}` and `DownstreamRejectionProfileMapV1={schema_version:1,entries:[DownstreamRejectionProfileEntryV1...]}` are duplicate-free and sorted by `(transport_kind,observation_variant,profile)`. HTTP transport has exactly one `http_response` entry. WebSocket transport has exactly one of `ws_handshake` or `ws_postupgrade_handshake_error`, never both, and additionally one `ws_text_message` entry iff the route is eligible for established-message observation; no other combination exists. The exact Codex-selected HTTP mappings are: `anthropic_messages_model_dispatch|anthropic_count_tokens_model_dispatch|claude_fallback -> codex_anthropic_write_error_v1`; `codex_live_create -> codex_live_get_set_v1`; every other credential-bearing HTTP error route -> `native_codex_http_v1`. Every Claude-selected HTTP error route uses `claude_reverse_proxy_v1`. Codex-selected normal Responses WebSocket and its prewarm use `codex_ws_postupgrade_handshake_error_v1` for `ws_postupgrade_handshake_error` because the pinned serving path accepts the downstream upgrade before the broker dials upstream, and use `codex_ws_text_message_v1` for an eligible established message. `codex_live_sideband_path|codex_live_sideband_query` remain upstream-first and use `codex_live_sideband_local_502_v1` for `ws_handshake` plus `codex_ws_text_message_v1` for an eligible established hard-quota message. The upstream rejection classifier variant remains `ws_handshake`; downstream observation variant records which side was upgraded and cannot change classifier authority. Wholly local or provider-ineligible members are null, and no unlisted route/provider/transport/variant mapping is legal. The catalogue canonical object and every route-catalogue marker/differential fixture cover the complete maps.

`GeminiProjectIDV1` is the closed post-tier value. The parser preserves the exact current source precedence—decode `cloudaicompanionProject` as a JSON string, otherwise as an object and select nonempty trimmed `id` before trimmed `projectId`—and applies the current `strings.TrimSpace` result before validation. Empty is legal and selects no project member. A nonempty value is legal only when its UTF-8 byte sequence is 1...256 bytes and matches exact ASCII grammar `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{0,255}$`; quote, reverse solidus, control, whitespace, non-ASCII, malformed UTF-8, empty first character, and byte 257 reject. Rejection after a successful tier response is the declared structured security difference `gemini_project_id_unsupported`: it returns the existing provider `parse_error` result with no raw project bytes, performs zero quota request or cache publication, and does not retry without a project. It never truncates, repairs, percent-encodes, or silently substitutes the invalid value.

`NormalGeminiRouteCatalogV1` is closed internal-only authority with exactly three lexically sorted rows and no public matcher: `gemini_quota=POST /v1internal:retrieveUserQuota`, `gemini_refresh=POST /token`, and `gemini_tier=POST /v1internal:loadCodeAssist`. Every row requires active `normal_gemini_v1` and one authenticated `operator_control_v1` `check` operation, carries empty query, permits HTTP only, and maps exactly once to the Google origin binding below; the explicit `RefreshCommandAuthorityCatalogueV1.refresh` row never selects Gemini. `gemini_tier` precedes `gemini_quota` in one check transaction and its project result is classified exactly as `GeminiProjectIDV1`. Quota body construction uses `encoding/json`, never interpolation: empty emits the two bytes `{}`; nonempty emits exactly the no-newline bytes returned by ``json.Marshal(struct{Project string `json:"project"`}{Project:id})``, which under the accepted grammar equal ASCII `{"project":"<id>"}`. Marshal failure is local `parse_error` with zero quota dispatch. The adapter first returns `no_token` for an empty access token. `gemini_refresh` is then legal only when the same selected credential generation has positive `expiry_date` strictly less than the check transaction's captured Unix-millisecond clock and a nonempty refresh token; expired-without-refresh returns `auth_expired`, while zero, equal, or future expiry does not refresh. Absent, fresh, expired-without-refresh, malformed, refresh-failed, tier-failed, quota-failed, and rejected-project results preserve the declared baseline result/error classes or exact intentional difference and never broaden route or credential authority. `gemini.credential_adapter` binds the source adapter; `gemini.origin_policy` binds all three rows; `gemini.refresh` binds refresh plus persistence-failure parity; `gemini.tier_quota` binds parser precedence, project grammar, encoder bytes, call order/body/response parsing, and rejection; `gemini.quota_cache` binds the instance-local cache; and `gemini.differential_corpus` binds complete scalar/target/floor parity and intentional security differences.

After a successful `gemini_refresh` exchange, worker creates one non-serialisable `GeminiRefreshOutcomeV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,selected_source_generation_digest,exchange_result_keyed_digest,publication_state:"committed|write_failed|rename_failed",published_generation_digest:null|string,ephemeral_generation_digest:null|string,diagnostic_code:null|"gemini_write_refreshed_creds"|"gemini_rename_refreshed_creds"}`. It contains the refreshed access/optional ID token only in locked operation memory, never in the object projection, journal, cache, receipt, marker, log, or control result. The credential owner first attempts the exact unknown-field-preserving fixed-temporary write/rename. `committed` requires non-null published generation, null ephemeral generation/diagnostic, directory durability, and generation advance before tier/quota. A write failure preserves the old source generation, emits only the baseline safe write diagnostic, leaves any uncertain fixed temporary to `gemini_credentials_tmp_v1` recovery, and selects a non-null operation-scoped ephemeral generation; a rename failure likewise preserves the old generation, emits the rename diagnostic, performs the baseline best-effort exact-temporary removal, and selects a non-null ephemeral generation. In either failure state only that same check transaction may use the refreshed in-memory token for its immediately following tier/quota calls; another operation, retry, cache fill, credential-index publication, or projection cannot resolve it. Terminal result, cancellation, deadline, channel loss, or worker crash zeroises refreshed token bytes and the ephemeral generation; recovery reports the durable safe outcome and never reconstructs or reuses them. Thus persistence succeeds before shared-generation use, while baseline persistence-failure check behaviour remains intact.

Supervisor keeps domain-separated local-token, Codex-caller, and Claude-caller fingerprint indexes. Claude entries bind exact account/candidate/revision/validity; duplicate/cross-account mapping invalidates domain index. Purpose-bound fingerprint subkey is derived by supervisor and passed to worker over authenticated private IPC as generation/key-ID capability; worker never receives `authority.key`. Route class, auth domain, index/key epoch, connection, nonce, expiry bind capability. Any raw bearer that matches more than one local-token/Claude/Codex credential domain—including byte-identical Claude and Codex entries—is universally ambiguous and fails closed before body read or provider classification; classification never disambiguates or narrows a multi-domain match. Worker failure clears provider indexes; local-token authentication may still succeed, but worker work returns 503. Supervisor never runs discovery to validate hostile request. Candidate Codex-only mode admits only the exact selected `hermetic|production_profile` member of the pre-Begin `CandidateSyntheticIngressIndexSetV1` and `CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityCatalogueSetV1` at the pre-body fingerprint gate. The supervisor reopens that member's complete authority, materialisation, index entry, tagged catalogue entry, route allowance, current authenticated route-budget head/chain, controller/run/process/index facts, and finite expiry before the bounded classification exchange and again before routed capability issue. A real provider bearer, an ordinary primary index row, or any missing, expired, exhausted, substituted, post-Begin, wrong-tag, or cross-run synthetic authority rejects before body classification or `OpenHTTP`; a Claude-selected or invalid classification likewise rejects before `OpenHTTP` or discovery.

For each Anthropic-compatible semantic partition, supervisor may read only the already resource-reserved bounded body required by the classifier after the pre-body grammar and unambiguous local/Claude/Codex fingerprint lookup succeeds. Candidate scope narrows that gate to the exact live `CandidateSyntheticIngressAuthorityV1`-backed Codex caller and its route-specific remaining budget; no provider-valid credential is an ingress alternative. The worker returns one closed `ProviderBranchClassificationCoreV1={schema_version:1,route_id,classifier_semantics_digest,request_body_digest,selected_provider:"claude|codex",selected_route_id}` over authenticated classification-only IPC without inventory, account selection, credential access, continuity, or upstream work. Let `C=CanonicalJSONV1(ProviderBranchClassificationCoreV1)`; `classification_digest = hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/provider-branch-classification/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`. In candidate scope a Claude selection or any missing, malformed, noncanonical, mismatched, or otherwise invalid classification response terminates after that exchange and before `OpenHTTP`, inventory, planning, continuity, credential resolution, or provider dispatch.

Supervisor otherwise issues one single-use admission. `ProviderBranchAdmissionCoreV1={schema_version:1,admission_id,single_use_nonce,classification:ProviderBranchClassificationCoreV1,classification_digest,ingress_credential_domain:"local_token_v1"|"claude_access_token_v1"|"codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1",caller_authority_kind:"local_owner"|"provider_subject",caller_pre_body_authentication_digest,caller_ingress_capability_digest,provider_caller_subject_hmac,caller_fingerprint_key_id,caller_index_epoch,caller_delegation_authority_digest,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest:null|string,connection_identity_digest,request_nonce,authority_generation,routing_generation,selected_origin_binding_digest,issued_at,valid_until}` is closed. `admission_id` and `single_use_nonce` are independent 128-bit OS-CSPRNG values; `valid_until` is non-null and no later than five seconds after `issued_at`. Both caller digests are always non-null, and the routed capability embeds the named exact current pre-body authentication. Local-owner admission requires null provider-subject, caller-index, delegation-authority, and synthetic-authority fields. An ordinary provider-subject admission requires non-null subject/key/epoch and complete non-null `CallerDelegationAuthorityV1` digest with literal-null synthetic digest; Claude can carry only its singleton branch, while Codex may carry any legal singleton/effective/intersection branch. Candidate synthetic admission requires Codex, non-null synthetic digest, exact equality to the complete nested authentication/capability and live controller index, and one already-consumed route-budget unit for the selected route. The embedded classification is byte-identical to the worker result, its digest recomputes exactly, selected provider matches ingress domain/subject branch, and selected route/origin matches the catalogue row. Reconstructed authentication, routed capability, subject, delegation-authority, synthetic provenance, request/connection, generation, route, and origin projections must all match byte-for-byte at consumption.

`K_provider_branch_admission = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/provider-branch-admission/v1"),L=32)` is supervisor-only. For `M=CanonicalJSONV1(ProviderBranchAdmissionCoreV1)`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_provider_branch_admission, ASCII("cq/provider-branch-admission-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(M)) || M))`; the complete object is `ProviderBranchAdmissionV1={schema_version:1,core:ProviderBranchAdmissionCoreV1,mac}`. For `J=CanonicalJSONV1(ProviderBranchAdmissionV1)`, `admission_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/provider-branch-admission/v1\0") || uint32be(len(J)) || J))`.

Consumption is separate durable supervisor authority, not an inferred property of an admission or a current clock. Its closed core is `ProviderBranchAdmissionConsumptionCoreV1={schema_version:1,admission_digest,admission_id,single_use_nonce,open_kind:"open_http"|"open_websocket",owner_kind:"journal_v4_request"|"active_non_v4_request",owner_id,request_nonce,connection_identity_digest,authority_generation,routing_generation,request_generation,consumed_at}`. `owner_id` is an independent 128-bit OS-CSPRNG value. Journal-V4 ownership requires non-null `request_generation`; active non-V4 ownership requires it null. Every other field is non-null and must equal the admission and authenticated open envelope. No prewarm reservation or later WebSocket frame is an admission consumer. For `Q=CanonicalJSONV1(ProviderBranchAdmissionConsumptionCoreV1)`, `consumption_mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_provider_branch_admission, ASCII("cq/provider-branch-admission-consumption-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(Q)) || Q))`; `ProviderBranchAdmissionConsumptionV1={schema_version:1,core:ProviderBranchAdmissionConsumptionCoreV1,mac:consumption_mac}` is closed. For `W=CanonicalJSONV1(ProviderBranchAdmissionConsumptionV1)`, `admission_consumption_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/provider-branch-admission-consumption/v1\0") || uint32be(len(W)) || W))`.

For a classified route, immediately before worker `OpenHTTP|OpenWebSocket`, one supervisor-owned durable CAS verifies the admission MAC and exact envelope, requires `issued_at <= consumed_at < valid_until`, consumes the admission ID/nonce, and creates exactly one owner row containing the complete consumption object/digest; no worker, prewarm reservation, or journal write can consume it. Codex turn-aware work places that receipt in its initial V4 request authority, and an admitted non-V4 request retains it in the purpose-bound active request authority through terminal response. A crash after the supervisor CAS leaves one non-reusable owner row, never a reusable admission; unreferenced rows retire only after the bounded request deadline and a proven absent worker/journal owner. Supervisor recovery re-verifies both MACs, the historical expiry relation, exact connection/request/generation binding, owner-row identity, and global admission/owner uniqueness before reopening durable work. Retry and restart copy the receipt byte-for-byte and never consume the admission again; the worker recomputes every unkeyed digest and object relation but never obtains or substitutes the supervisor-only MAC key.

Local owner means only a current generated CQ local token and is explicit authority for configured routing; it is not inferred from a Claude or Codex bearer. Claude selection requires that local-owner authority or the exact current Claude subject. Codex selection requires that local-owner authority or the exact current Codex subject plus any active delegation needed by the selected account. Wrong-domain-only, missing, expired, ambiguous, classifier/body drift, selected-route/origin mismatch, replay, or generation change returns `403 normal_caller_auth_scope_violation` before inventory, planning, continuity, credential resolution, or provider dispatch. Every catalogue route carries exactly one route-bound closed `ProviderBranchAuthorityV1`: `{schema_version:1,route_id,kind:"classified",classification:ProviderBranchClassificationCoreV1,classification_digest,admission:ProviderBranchAdmissionV1,admission_digest,admission_consumption:ProviderBranchAdmissionConsumptionV1,admission_consumption_digest}` is mandatory exactly for the three Anthropic-compatible semantic partitions after the one consumption CAS; every selected field is non-null and all embedded route/classification/admission/consumption bytes, owner facts, and digests agree. `{schema_version:1,route_id,kind:"not_applicable",classification:null,classification_digest:null,admission:null,admission_digest:null,admission_consumption:null,admission_consumption_digest:null}` is mandatory for every other catalogue route. A route/variant mismatch, absent union, substituted object/digest, owner mismatch, or attempted second admission consumption fails before worker `OpenHTTP|OpenWebSocket` or dispatch. `OpenHTTP`, `OpenWebSocket`, every V4/prewarm plan, and every `CallerDispatchPermit` bind the complete post-consumption union; neither worker nor retry may reclassify, erase, invent, or change provider branch.

Normal worker protocol is closed and versioned. Handshake permits only `Hello`, `FingerprintContext`, `Ready`, `CredentialIndex`; HTTP request permits `ClassifyProviderBranch`, `ProviderBranchClassification`, `OpenHTTP`, zero or more `RequestBody`, `RequestEnd`, `Cancel`, where the classification pair is legal only once for a catalogue-declared Anthropic-compatible partition; HTTP response permits `ResponseHead`, zero or more `ResponseBody`, `Flush`, then exactly one `ResponseEnd|ResponseError`; WebSocket permits `OpenWebSocket`, `UpgradeResult`, `WebSocketFrame`, `WebSocketClose`, `Cancel`. In candidate scope the classification pair is the only worker request/response exchange permitted before a Codex selection; Claude selection or an invalid response makes `OpenHTTP` illegal for that request. `OpenHTTP` binds protocol version, request ID, method, escaped target, ordered headers after Host/Authorization/hop-by-hop removal, declared framing, authenticated caller capability, exact `ProviderBranchAuthorityV1`, connection ID, ingress-mode epoch, authority/config generations, exact `normal_credential_origin_binding_digest`, and resource reservation; `OpenWebSocket` binds the same authority, caller, connection, origin-binding, framing, reservation, and provider-branch-authority fields plus its exact handshake fields. No raw local/provider credential crosses IPC. Frame, aggregate body, queue, response header, SSE progress, and WebSocket limits equal public limits. Unknown, duplicate, out-of-order, replayed, or post-terminal frame terminates request. Before response headers, protocol/worker failure is `503 normal_worker_protocol_error`; after headers, supervisor preserves emitted bytes and closes without retry.

Authenticated operator control is a disjoint frame family on the same private transport and is never legal on a public HTTP/WebSocket request stream. A fresh effect-capable operation permits exactly one `ControlKeyInit`, one `ControlKeyReady`, one `ControlBegin`, one `ControlAccepted`, one `ControlArguments`, one `ControlProceed`, zero or more bounded `ControlProgress`, one `ControlResult|ControlError`, and optional terminal `ControlResultAck`; an ordinary login additionally permits exactly one `ControlOAuthSecret`, while structured refresh permits at most one `ControlRefreshReauthPlan`, then for each of at most 64 ordered entries exactly one `ControlRefreshReauthDecision` and, only for `proceed`, one fresh `ControlOAuthChildKeyInit`, one `ControlOAuthChildKeyReady`, one child-bound `ControlOAuthSecret`, and one `ControlOAuthChildResult`. Structured refresh forbids `ControlProgress`; its authenticated decision, OAuth, mutation, and result heads are the sole intermediate safe progress authority. Operation reconciliation additionally permits at most one `ControlRecover` and at most one `ControlCancel`; operation lookup/status is exclusively the authenticated same-descriptor local store/receipt read and has no control-frame kind. The outer key exchange precedes `ControlBegin`; every refresh OAuth child performs its own fresh exchange and never reuses the outer or another child's secret. `ControlBegin` embeds the complete post-key-exchange `OperatorControlRequestV1`, selected feature/marker set digest, deadline, and resource reservation. Supervisor durably publishes the safe reserved operation object before `ControlAccepted`; the encrypted typed arguments follow acceptance. It performs no provider, credential, cache, projection, filesystem, or manager effect until the selected worker has authenticated/decrypted the exact row arguments, the matching CLI has rendered the accepted operation handle, and that CLI has sent `ControlProceed`. Only ordinary login or a planned refresh `proceed` child permits `ControlOAuthSecret`, and only its exact outer-head-selected `OperatorOAuthControlV1` child may decrypt it. CLI sends `ControlResultAck` only after the complete original-effect or `operation recover` result was successfully rendered and flushed; `operation status` never sends it, and loss before acknowledgement leaves the terminal operation discoverable without making its effect replayable. Every response binds operation ID, command row, key-exchange digest, selected generations, child ordinal when present, one-use consumption state, and safe result schema. Maximum canonical control frame is 64 KiB; encrypted typed-argument plaintext is at most 16 KiB; encrypted OAuth-secret plaintext is at most 4 KiB; refresh plan is at most 32 KiB with at most 64 entries and each safe label at most 256 UTF-8 bytes. Non-refresh operations retain the 512-frame/8-MiB bound; structured refresh instead uses the tighter exact 331-frame count and 21,692,416 wire-byte reserve in its closed capacity formula below. Unknown, missing, duplicate, cross-operation, out-of-order, replayed, nonce-reused, oversized, post-terminal, or provider/row-inapplicable frames terminate only that control operation, destroy its transient key/secret capability, and cannot open provider transport. `control.command_catalogues` binds the typed row union and cache policy below; `control.refresh_reauth` binds the plan/decision/child grammar; `control.worker_protocol` and `worker.operator_control` bind this grammar, every key exchange and encrypted carrier, ordinary/models/refresh method enumeration, resource bounds, cancellation, restart/lost-ack recovery, and the invariant that no CLI-local provider or credential fallback follows a control failure.

`ControlCancel` carries exactly `OperatorControlCancelV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,operator_control_request_digest,cause:"sigint|sigterm|forward_deadline",clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",boot_session_id,requested_at_tick_ns,sequence,mac}` inside the authenticated owner-control framing. `sequence` is the cancellation-frame ordinal and is exactly zero; it is not the operation-object successor sequence. The object uses the purpose-specific `cancel` MAC rule below, and for complete MACed canonical bytes `C`, `cancel_request_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/cancel/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`. The originating dispatcher converts the first `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` received after its command context exists, or arrival at the forward cutoff, into at most one such frame while the private channel and total deadline remain live; it closes callback/listener input immediately and ignores later signals for protocol purposes. Before durable `ControlAccepted`, cancellation returns the ordinary typed operational failure with no handle and no effect. In `reserved|accepted`, an authenticated cancel terminalises the operation as `failed` with stable safe result `operator_operation_cancelled`, consumes no `(operation_id,nonce)`, destroys transient key/argument/OAuth material, and proves zero provider, credential, cache, projection, filesystem, or manager effect. In `proceeding|effect_committed`, it durably selects the cancellation digest/cause before requesting worker stop, forbids any not-yet-issued effect, and reconciles an already issued effect only from the exact worker/credential/cache/projection journal; the result is the one proved `succeeded|failed|login_restart_required|indeterminate` outcome, never an asserted rollback or a replay. In `terminal|acknowledged`, the byte-identical cancel is an idempotent no-op returning the existing terminal result. A byte-identical duplicate at sequence zero is idempotent; different bytes or a nonzero sequence for that operation, wrong boot/domain/request/MAC, or cancel after total expiry fails only that operation and cannot start work. Forward-deadline and signal handling use only the parent's remaining reserve for this cancellation, exact reconciliation, safe snapshot, render, and acknowledgement; at total expiry all descendants stop and the durable operation remains addressable. Interruption of `operation status|recover` itself sends no new cancel: it stops that lookup/reconciliation under its own context and leaves the selected operation unchanged or pending.

Worker owns complete existing normal semantics except the explicit Headroom compatibility break: provider/model classification, exact-Claude-account versus local-ingress selection, pin/affinity/quota choice, refresh and bounded retry, body replay, continuity, registry rendering, external projections, diagnostics/payload consent, upstream construction, SSE flush, and WebSocket routing, subject to the provider-rejection authority contraction below. A complete `401` for the exact ingress Claude or Codex provider subject may drive the credential-owner refresh transaction and publish the refreshed credential/index, but that provider-bearer-authenticated HTTP or WebSocket request retains and relays the rejection with zero dispatch under the refreshed revision; null/unknown caller expiry never weakens this rule. A Codex provider-bearer request delegated to a different outbound account/candidate/revision follows the distinct immutable different-outbound terminal reason and has the same retained-`401`, zero-replay result after owner publication; it never borrows local-owner refresh authority. Every complete `401` on a Claude-selected request—including independently current local-owner ingress—may update owner state/index only for future ingress; the current request retains and relays that `401` and performs zero same-request direct or refreshed replay because Claude has no V4 durable dispatch journal. Same-request refreshed dispatch is legal only for a Codex-selected V4 request that entered with an independently current local-owner capability which remains valid through final admission, never by converting, retaining, or bridging a rejected provider subject. Supervisor owns parsing, authentication, resource admission, cancellation, backpressure, public response transport, and crash isolation. The exact `RequiredMarkerChildren(normal_codex_v1)` and `RequiredMarkerChildren(normal_claude_v1)` feature-child sets—not markers named after either feature—bind exact launcher/supervisor/worker artifacts, protocol revision, route catalogue, origin policy, fixture/result digests, and validation run. Candidate remains Codex-only; its complete `normal_codex_v1` catalogue corpus uses synthetic in-memory Codex accounts and fixed fake TLS origins, while its sandboxed Claude validation uses synthetic in-memory Claude accounts and fixed fake TLS upstream. CU-3 owns both protocol/differential corpora; CU-9 regenerates target and floor children. Candidate evidence never satisfies primary marker set.

If normal worker fails while desired mode remains normal, supervisor returns local `503 normal_worker_unavailable`; it never auto-enters rescue. Entering rescue closes worker outbound-admission gate, joins autonomous work, and removes worker. Exiting rescue starts fresh worker and admits normal ingress only after readiness acknowledgement.

Supervisor owns runtime worker-crash machine `ready -> failed -> backoff -> starting -> ready|crash_loop`. Unexpected exit clears readiness and credential-index epoch immediately. At most three automatic starts occur in rolling 10 minutes with monotonic backoff 1s, 5s, 30s; counters are runtime-only but boot-ID/process-exit facts appear in health. Fourth failure enters `crash_loop`, serves 503, and performs no more automatic spawn. `service restart` or successful explicit `worker_switch` starts new budget after exact runtime/authority proof; traffic-mode mutation does not. Automatic restart always uses already-selected artifact/config generation and is not artifact-switch authority. Supervisor exit loses runtime counter, but launchd restart performs one normal boot attempt and new supervisor still reports preceding process-exit evidence from manager.

Stable V1 launcher and immutable artifacts are owner-only. Launcher contract is frozen; launcher upgrade is separate manager-binding transaction. Payloads and manifests use separate content-addressed stores: `artifacts/payloads/<artifact_payload_digest>/cq` and `artifacts/manifests/<artifact_manifest_digest>.json`. Each payload is at most 268,435,456 bytes and each canonical manifest at most 65,536 bytes. Each store permits exactly nine logical slots including content, staging, temporary, and orphan entries; aggregate regular-file cap is 2,416,508,928 bytes = `9 × 268,435,456 + 9 × 65,536`. The nine-slot proof is current target three + staged target three + accepted/staged rollback floor two (the rollback floor is the independently accepted floor and therefore the same two objects) + one publication temporary. Selecting any different floor through this V1 store refuses. Before reserving a release operation, deterministic reconciliation reopens every unreferenced temporary/orphan, adopts an exact complete digest or removes the inert entry with directory sync, then requires that occupancy fits this proof; referenced, ambiguous, or unreconciled residue blocks before source copy or semantic mutation. Exact ninth payload/manifest slots and exact byte cap succeed; slot ten or first excess byte refuses. Physical reserve and directory metadata are preflighted separately.

Under `import.lock` before authority or `authority.lock` later, publication streams the same retained source FD through a size sentinel into a random-exclusive payload temporary, hashes while copying, writes the separate canonical manifest, syncs both files and their directories, revalidates source/destination, performs no-replace content-addressed renames, syncs both store roots, then reopens/verifies both. Existing digest succeeds only on exact byte/identity/signature/manifest equality. A manifest becomes usable only after its named payload and signed release-set membership both verify; payload publication alone never selects or authorises bytes. Authority anchor performs selection.

`scripts/build-proxy-release` is sole release-artifact producer. It requires clean exact source commit, pinned Go toolchain/GOOS/GOARCH/CGO/build flags, and explicit roles. `ReleaseBuildAuthorityV1={schema_version:1,authority_id,ed25519_public_key,repository_identity_digest,blueprint_sha256,review_attestation_aggregate_sha256,review_authority_baseline_commit,lineage_root_commit,lineage_root_tree_digest,toolchain_identity,created_at}` is explicitly approved and digest-pinned by initialisation/import or existing bootstrap authority. Its blueprint/review fields must equal the current recursively clean sibling attestation and baseline, and its lineage root is the later accepted CU-8 source commit/tree. For `A=CanonicalJSONV1(authority)`, `release_build_authority_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/release-build-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`; every signed object below names that digest, uses exactly its Ed25519 public key, and any other key refuses. Same-UID replacement remains inside local trust boundary.

Release command and result digests are literal byte constructions. For UTF-8 purpose `P`, repository-relative UTF-8 working directory `W`, and ordered UTF-8 argv bytes `A_i`, `CommandDigestV1(P,W,[A_i])=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/release-command/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P || uint32be(len(W)) || W || uint32be(argc) || each (uint32be(len(A_i)) || A_i)))`; counts and lengths that do not fit unsigned 32-bit refuse. Purpose is exactly `ancestry`, `release-<floor|target>-<build|vet|race>`, `role-<launcher|supervisor|worker>-build`, or `verify-<CU-0..CU-9>` as applicable. The builder runs a hermetic toolchain invocation and admits one secret-free, byte-sorted, duplicate-free environment vector whose keys are exactly `CGO_ENABLED,GOAMD64,GOARCH,GOARM,GOARM64,GOEXPERIMENT,GOFLAGS,GOOS,GOTOOLCHAIN,LC_ALL,SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH,TZ`; inapplicable architecture fields remain present with empty values. For `E=uint32be(count) || each (uint32be(len(K_i)) || K_i || uint32be(len(V_i)) || V_i)`, `build_environment_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/release-build-environment/v1\0") || uint32be(len(E)) || E))`. Unknown/ambient/missing keys, duplicates, wrong byte order, locale/toolchain/flag drift, or a secret-bearing value refuse before execution; working/cache/temp paths are isolated inputs and cannot enter argv, environment, debug paths, or output bytes. For signed 32-bit exit status `X`, exact ASCII termination reason `T` in `exited|signalled|timeout`, and uninterpreted raw stdout/stderr byte strings `O` and `R`, `ExecutionResultDigestV1(X,T,O,R)=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/release-execution-result/v1\0") || int32be(X) || uint32be(len(T)) || T || uint64be(len(O)) || O || uint64be(len(R)) || R))`; no newline, encoding, terminal, or truncation normalisation is permitted. The producer bounds capture before execution, records `X=-1` when no process exit status exists, and never emits a passed object for a non-`exited` result.

`SourceAncestryReceiptV1={schema_version:1,kind:"source_ancestry_v1",release_build_authority_digest,repository_identity_digest,floor_source_commit,floor_source_tree_digest,target_source_commit,target_source_tree_digest,merge_base_commit,verification_command_digest,verified_at,signer_public_key,signature}` is signed by that authority and proves `merge_base_commit == floor_source_commit`, target is a strict descendant, and floor equals the authority lineage root; its verification digest is exactly `CommandDigestV1("ancestry",W,argv)`. `ReleaseBuildReportV1={schema_version:1,kind:"build|vet|race",purpose:"target|floor",release_build_authority_digest,source_commit,source_tree_digest,toolchain_identity,build_environment_digest,command_digest,role_executions:[{role,build_command_digest,artifact_payload_digest,artifact_manifest_digest}],outcome:"passed",exit_code:0,race_enabled,execution_result_digest,started_at,ended_at,signer_public_key,signature}` is at most 64 KiB and is signed by the same authority. `command_digest` is the exact `CommandDigestV1("release-<purpose>-<kind>",W,argv)` and `execution_result_digest` is the exact `ExecutionResultDigestV1` of that invocation. `role_executions` is empty for vet/race; for build it is sorted and is exactly `supervisor,worker` for floor or `launcher,supervisor,worker` for target. A signed ancestry receipt or build report is digested over its complete canonical bytes with the same framed construction and respective `cq/source-ancestry-receipt/v1\0` or `cq/release-build-report/v1\0` domain. `race_enabled` is true exactly for `kind="race"` and false otherwise. The producer emits a report only after the exact command exits zero without signal or timeout and, for the race report, after proving `go test -race` remained enabled; failure, skip, empty test selection, signal, timeout, or race-disabled execution emits no successful report. A verifier requires all three distinct passed reports and rejects a substituted command/environment/result record even when its exit code is zero.

For ancestry and build reports, Ed25519 signature covers `CanonicalJSONV1(object with signature omitted)` and `signer_public_key` equals the authority key. A build report's `exit_code` equals the `X` encoded by its execution-result digest; passed requires exactly `X=0,T="exited"`.

CU wrapper evidence is one signed aggregate per source snapshot, never an unconstrained digest list or wrapper-produced report. For each required CU, `scripts/build-proxy-release` records `started_at`, invokes the exact checked-in wrapper as a child with no report file descriptor, report-output path, precomputed result digest, or caller-supplied report entry, captures its bounded raw stdout/stderr through process termination, records the exact termination reason/exit status and `ended_at`, then computes `ExecutionResultDigestV1` and constructs the closed CU entry out of band. The wrapper emits verification diagnostics only and never serialises an accepted entry; bytes it emits are merely part of `O` or `R`. A closed `ConstructionUnitReportV1` entry is `{schema_version:1,kind:"construction_unit_report_v1",cu_id:"CU-0".."CU-9",verification_manifest_digest,invocation_digest,outcome:"passed",exit_code:0,race_enabled:true,execution_result_digest,started_at,ended_at}`. `verification_manifest_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/construction-unit-verification-manifest/v1\0") || uint32be(len(M)) || M))` for the exact canonical checked-in manifest bytes `M`; invocation is `CommandDigestV1("verify-<cu_id>",W,argv)`, and result is the exact digest of the builder-captured `X,T,O,R` with `X=exit_code`; passed requires exactly `X=0,T="exited"`. A report-shaped byte sequence emitted by the wrapper remains ordinary captured output, while any separate wrapper/caller-supplied report input is rejected. The builder cannot construct the accepted entry until both capture streams are closed, so the captured result never contains the entry whose digest it names. `ConstructionUnitReportSetV1={schema_version:1,kind:"construction_unit_report_set_v1",purpose:"target|floor",release_build_authority_digest,blueprint_sha256,review_attestation_aggregate_sha256,review_authority_baseline_commit,legacy_atomic_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest,source_commit,source_tree_digest,toolchain_identity,build_environment_digest,reports:[ConstructionUnitReportV1],signer_public_key,signature}` is closed, at most 64 KiB, and signed by the exact build authority over canonical bytes with `signature` omitted. Reports are ordered by numeric CU ID, duplicate-free, and are exactly CU-0…CU-8 for floor or CU-0…CU-9 for target; `legacy_atomic_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest` equals the complete regenerated signed-catalogue digest for the authority baseline and is identical in floor and target sets; every entry has the same manifest digest and exact builder invocation for its ID. For complete signed canonical bytes `U`, `construction_unit_report_set_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/construction-unit-report-set/v1\0") || uint32be(len(U)) || U))`. A skipped, absent, duplicated, reordered, wrong-source, wrong-blueprint/review/reachability-catalogue, substituted-manifest/command/result, separately wrapper- or caller-supplied entry, race-disabled, nonzero, signalled, or timed-out CU makes the set invalid.

`ReleaseArtifactManifestV1={schema_version:1,role,release_build_authority_digest,source_commit,source_tree_digest,toolchain_identity,build_command_digest,build_environment_digest,architecture,build_id,supported_features,minimum_floor_features,launcher_abi_digest,private_abi_digest,code_signature_digest,artifact_payload_digest}` excludes own digest. Launcher requires non-null launcher ABI and null private ABI; supervisor requires both; worker requires null launcher ABI and non-null private ABI. Digest is `hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/release-artifact-manifest/v1\0") || uint32be(len(CanonicalJSONV1(manifest))) || CanonicalJSONV1(manifest)))`. `ReleaseArtifactSetV1={schema_version:1,purpose:"target|floor",release_build_authority_digest,signer_public_key,source_commit,source_tree_digest,toolchain_identity,build_environment_digest,build_report_digest,vet_report_digest,race_test_report_digest,construction_unit_report_set_digest,legacy_atomic_writer_reachability_catalogue_digest,source_ancestry_receipt_digest,launcher_abi_digest,required_launcher_abi_digest,roles:[{role,artifact_payload_digest,artifact_manifest_digest}],supported_features,minimum_floor_features,set_signature}` has sorted duplicate-free roles. Target roles are exactly `launcher,supervisor,worker`; its ancestry/launcher ABI are non-null and required-launcher ABI is null. Floor roles are exactly `supervisor,worker`; its ancestry/launcher ABI are null and required-launcher ABI is non-null. Target launcher/supervisor launcher ABI values equal the set launcher ABI; floor supervisor launcher ABI equals the required launcher ABI; each supervisor/worker pair has one equal private ABI. No other role or nullability is legal. Its reachability digest equals the named construction-unit report set and the regenerated catalogue for that source; target and accepted floor values must be byte-identical. Signature covers the canonical object with `set_signature` omitted. For `S=CanonicalJSONV1(set)` after the signature is present, `release_artifact_set_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/release-artifact-set/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S)) || S))`.

Release provenance is an exact equality graph, not a collection of independently valid signatures. Within each set, the three build reports and CU report set have the set purpose, authority digest, source commit/tree, toolchain identity, and build-environment digest exactly; their signer keys equal the authority key. Every role manifest has that authority/source/tree/toolchain/environment exactly, its payload/manifest digests equal the corresponding set role, and its `build_command_digest` is `CommandDigestV1("role-<role>-build",W,argv)`. The build report's `role_executions` is an exact role-by-role bijection with the set and repeats those command, payload, and manifest digests; vet/race contain no role execution. Every toolchain identity in both paired floor and target objects equals the authority `toolchain_identity`, and their build-environment digests are byte-equal. The floor set source commit/tree equals the authority lineage root. The target set source commit/tree equals ancestry target commit/tree; ancestry floor commit/tree equals the same authority lineage root, ancestry repository identity equals authority repository identity, and ancestry signer equals authority. The CU report set blueprint/review/baseline fields equal the authority fields. Bundle purpose/authority/set/ancestry/CU-report fields and every entry digest equal these selected objects. Any missing equality, extra role/execution, cross-purpose report, source/tree/toolchain/environment skew, role swap, or individually signed but inconsistent graph refuses before canonical copy or artifact selection.

`ReleaseBundleV1` is the only external release import unit. Its owner-only local-APFS directory contains exact canonical `bundle.json`, `release-build-authority.json`, `release-artifact-set.json`, `reports/{build,vet,race,construction-units}.json`, target-only `source-ancestry.json`, and exactly the role-indexed `manifests/<role>.json` and `payloads/<role>` named by the set. `bundle.json` is at most 64 KiB and is closed `{schema_version:1,purpose:"target|floor",release_build_authority_digest,release_artifact_set_digest,construction_unit_report_set_digest,source_ancestry_receipt_digest,entries:[{relative_path,kind:"file",digest,size}],signer_public_key,bundle_signature}`. `entries` is sorted by relative-path bytes, duplicate-free, and lists every non-`bundle.json` regular file exactly once: exactly 13 target entries or ten floor entries. `bundle.json` never lists itself; `reports`, `manifests`, and `payloads` are structural directories and never entries. Each `size` is the exact raw file-byte count; each payload digest is raw SHA-256 and each typed canonical JSON digest uses its named domain formula. The CU entry is exactly `reports/construction-units.json` and its digest equals both the bundle and set `construction_unit_report_set_digest`. `signer_public_key` must equal the named build authority key and the Ed25519 signature covers the canonical object with `bundle_signature` omitted. Let `B=CanonicalJSONV1(bundle.json)` after the signature is present; `release_bundle_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/release-bundle/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))`. Floor forbids ancestry file/digest; target requires it. The physical tree permits at most 17 descendants, depth two, 1-GiB aggregate, regular files plus those three exact structural directories only, and no links, nested mounts, unknown names, or residual temporaries. Secure same-descriptor verification binds the computed release-bundle digest, authority, set, build/CU reports, ancestry, manifests, and payloads before any copy. Initialisation/import/rollback/staged-release input manifests retain locator, parent/file identities, bundle fingerprint, computed bundle digest, accepted-floor receipt digest when purpose is floor, and set digest until canonical copies are durable; legacy-import bundle locators remain pinned until terminal finalisation. Exact canonical `bundle.json` is copied to the provenance store with the rest of its referenced objects before the source locator may be released; a source bundle may then disappear without invalidating selected canonical provenance.

Pre-authority validation receipts are consumed through one retained-parent claim store, never by an unrecorded verifier check. Beneath the already retained target parent, `.<target-basename>.preauthority-validation-claims/` is owner-only local APFS and contains no-replace immutable `claims/<receipt-digest>.json`. `PreauthorityValidationReceiptAuthorityV1` is the closed tagged union `{authority_kind:"controller_signed_candidate_receipt",receipt_kind:"candidate_confinement|candidate_preflight",receipt_digest,receipt_issuer_key_digest,receipt_not_after}` or `{authority_kind:"parent_mac_candidate_release_promotion",receipt_kind:"candidate_release_promotion",candidate_release_promotion_receipt_digest,candidate_release_promotion_receipt_object_identity_digest,rollback_floor_validation_receipt_digest,rollback_floor_validation_receipt_object_identity_digest,rollback_floor_validation_receipt_issuer_key_digest,rollback_floor_validation_receipt_not_after,promotion_mac_authority_digest}`. Closed `PreauthorityValidationClaimV1={schema_version:1,claim_id,receipt_kind:"candidate_confinement|candidate_preflight|candidate_release_promotion",receipt_digest,receipt_issuer_key_digest,receipt_not_after,receipt_authority:PreauthorityValidationReceiptAuthorityV1,target_parent_identity_digest,target_basename,operation_kind:"fresh_primary|legacy_import",operation_id,initialisation_input_manifest_digest,prepared_commit_object_digest,created_at}` binds exactly one expiring candidate authority to the already materialised initialisation record or import-ticket object. For either controller-signed branch, the three top-level receipt members equal the tagged receipt digest, issuer-key digest, and signed expiry. For the promotion branch, top-level `receipt_digest` equals the outer promotion digest, while top-level issuer and expiry equal the recursively reopened inner `RollbackFloorValidationReceiptV1` issuer and `not_after`; `promotion_mac_authority_digest` is the framed digest of the exact retained source bootstrap/authority/controller-store-key relation used to verify the outer MAC, and the outer/inner digest-and-object-identity pairs must equal the canonical import selector and receipt. The parent verifies the outer MAC first, recursively reopens and verifies the inner signature and expiry, then publishes the claim; outer-Q substitution, inner-R substitution, Q/R identity drift, an expiry copied from Q rather than R, or direct `R || LF` authority refuses. Reusable non-expiring floor acceptance is pinned by exact digest/signature but is never represented as one-ticket authority. Every claimed receipt has non-null `receipt_not_after`; for the promotion branch its effective expiry is exactly the inner receipt expiry. Claim digest uses domain `cq/preauthority-validation-claim/v1` over the complete tagged authority. While holding stable lifecycle lock, prepare writes, file-syncs, no-replace publishes, directory-syncs, and reopens every required candidate claim before publishing ticket/bootstrap/authority selector. An existing byte-identical claim for the same operation and prepared object resumes; any different operation/object is `validation_receipt_already_claimed`. An unexpired, active, or recovery-referenced claim is never rewritten or deleted. Once the effective receipt expiry has passed and its operation terminal/history checkpoint released every outer and inner reference, replay is independently impossible, so GC may unlink and parent-sync the full claim. Store admits 256 live claims/32 MiB including one temporary; if expiry/reference GC cannot create capacity, prepare blocks before manager, floor, ticket-anchor, or authority action. This claim plus its tagged original authority is pre-bootstrap one-ticket authority.

Canonical sets live content-addressed under `release-sets/`; build/vet/race/CU report sets and ancestry receipts under `release-reports/`; exact canonical `ReleaseBuildAuthorityV1` objects live under `release-provenance/authorities/<release-build-authority-digest>.json`; exact canonical signed `ReleaseBundleV1` objects live under `release-provenance/bundles/<release-bundle-digest>.json`; exact canonical `RollbackFloorAcceptanceReceiptV1` objects live under `release-provenance/floor-acceptance/<floor-acceptance-receipt-digest>.json`; and exact canonical MACed bytes `Q` of `CandidateReleasePromotionReceiptV1` objects selected by primary staged releases live under `release-provenance/validation/<candidate-release-promotion-receipt-digest>.json`, while recursively pinned inner signed `RollbackFloorValidationReceiptV1` bytes `R` live under `release-provenance/validation-inner/<rollback-floor-validation-receipt-digest>.json`. The exported terminal LF is never part of either canonical object. Each set/ancestry object ≤1 MiB and each build report, CU report set, build-authority object, bundle object, floor-acceptance receipt, and validation receipt ≤64 KiB. The set/report store admits at most eight sets and 40 build/CU-report/ancestry objects plus four temporaries under 64 MiB; this covers eight all-target sets at five referenced report objects each. The separate provenance store admits at most eight authority objects, eight bundle objects, eight acceptance receipts, eight outer promotion receipts, eight recursively pinned inner validation receipts, and four temporaries under 3 MiB; its regular-file arithmetic is `44 × 65,536 = 2,883,584`, below the fixed `3,145,728`-byte cap. Both stores use streamed bounded reads, file sync, content-addressed no-replace rename, directory sync, and same-descriptor reopen verification; an existing digest is accepted only on exact canonical-byte equality. Every operation that first imports or selects a floor bundle must provide a registered exact acceptance-receipt locator and expected digest outside that bundle, verify its authority signature and `floor_release_bundle_digest` against the computed bundle digest, and canonically copy it, the exact signed bundle object, and the bundle's build authority before the source locator may be released. Initialisation input, import ticket, candidate preflight, staged-target selector, staged-rollback-floor selector, floor receipt, marker children, selected authority, and finalisation receipts reference exact bundle/set/build-report/CU-report-set/build-authority/acceptance/ancestry/validation digests as applicable. Current target, staged target, staged rollback floor, independently accepted floor, active operation, and last final release pin provenance; the accepted-floor bundle, authority, acceptance receipt, and its complete release equality graph are permanently pinned, while GC removes only unreferenced older non-floor objects after authority/history checkpoint. Artifact quota reserves set/report and provenance bytes separately. CU-0 owns build authority/script/schema/store/negative fixtures; CU-3 owns the first launcher/supervisor/worker implementation build but produces no promotion receipt; CU-8 builds, signs, and retains the independently accepted floor set/bundle/receipt; CU-9 builds only the descendant target set/bundle and must consume, never regenerate, CU-8 floor. Dirty tree, flag/toolchain drift, role swap, rebuilt bytes, forged/untrusted signer, missing/non-passed signed build/CU report/ancestry/acceptance, launcher/private ABI mismatch, provenance skew, self-reference, same-source regenerated floor, or source-to-selected-artifact break refuses.

The set/report bound has an explicit all-target worst case: `8 × 1,048,576` set bytes + `8 × 1,048,576` ancestry bytes + `32 × 65,536` build/CU-report bytes + `4 × 1,048,576` temporary bytes = `23,068,672`, below the fixed `67,108,864`-byte store cap. Exact object cardinalities still apply before the byte cap; a ninth set, 41st report/ancestry object, fifth temporary, or first byte above either limit refuses pre-publication.

Current, staged-target, staged-rollback-floor, permanently accepted floor, import-ticket, active-transition, and marker references pin artifacts and their complete release/provenance equality graphs. GC runs under same lock after authority/history anchors, unlinks only unreferenced content, and syncs artifact root. ENOSPC, short write, drift, collision mismatch, sync/rename ambiguity, or crash leaves prior selection effective; recovery reopens possibly published digest and never repeats ambiguous rename. Failure injection covers every read/write/sentinel/file sync/temp-dir sync/rename/root sync/selection/unlink/GC boundary. Rollback selects recorded artifact then kickstarts same socket label; manager never resolves `PATH`/Cellar alternative.

`PrimaryStagedReleaseStoreV1` is the only post-authority release-import selector and is one closed discriminated store for independently coexisting `target` and `rollback_floor` stages. It lives at `release-staging/{anchors/{target.json,rollback-floor.json},selectors/<selector-digest>.json,operations/{anchor,objects/<operation-object-digest>.json,receipts/<operation-id>.json}}` beneath the selected primary root. Every registered temporary is an owner-only regular file named `.tmp.<32-lower-hex>` in its destination directory and created with exclusive no-follow semantics; no other name is a temporary. Let `K_psr=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/primary-staged-release/v1"),L=32)`. The five keys are exactly `K_selector_object=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_psr,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/primary-staged-release-selector-object/v1"),L=32)`, `K_selector_anchor=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_psr,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/primary-staged-release-selector-anchor/v1"),L=32)`, `K_operation_object=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_psr,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/primary-staged-release-operation-object/v1"),L=32)`, `K_operation_anchor=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_psr,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/primary-staged-release-operation-anchor/v1"),L=32)`, and `K_operation_receipt=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_psr,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/primary-staged-release-operation-receipt/v1"),L=32)`. For complete MACed canonical bytes `X`, selector, selector-anchor, operation-object, operation-anchor, and operation-receipt digests are each `hex(SHA256(ASCII(D') || uint32be(len(X)) || X))` with respective exact domains `cq/primary-staged-release-selector/v1\0`, `cq/primary-staged-release-selector-anchor/v1\0`, `cq/primary-staged-release-operation/v1\0`, `cq/primary-staged-release-operation-anchor/v1\0`, and `cq/primary-staged-release-operation-receipt/v1\0`; filename digest and recomputed digest must agree wherever the object is content-addressed.

The immutable discriminated selector is closed `PrimaryStagedReleaseV1={schema_version:1,stage_kind:"target|rollback_floor",release_bundle_digest,release_artifact_set_digest,release_build_authority_digest,source_ancestry_receipt_digest,floor_acceptance_receipt_digest,build_report_digest,vet_report_digest,race_test_report_digest,construction_unit_report_set_digest,validation_receipt_digest,validation_receipt_object_identity_digest,accepted_floor_release_artifact_set_digest,required_launcher_abi_digest,manager_binding_digest,staged_at,mac}`. The subordinate coordinator child is closed `PrimaryStagedReleaseOperationV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,coordinator_intent_digest,stage_kind:"target|rollback_floor",action:"stage|clear",intent_authority_generation,external_reference_binding:null|CandidateControllerExternalReferenceBindingV1,credential_owner_key_fingerprint,receipt_created_at,phase:"intent_unselected|intent|selector_committed|terminal",sequence,previous_object_digest,prior_anchor_digest,target_anchor_digest,prior_selector_digest,target_selector_digest,release_bundle_digest,release_artifact_set_digest,authorising_receipt_digest,authorising_receipt_object_identity_digest,reference_proof_digest,selector_commit_proof_digest,terminal_outcome:null|"staged"|"cleared"|"prior_restored",terminal_proof_digest,mac}`. Every selector, anchor, operation object, and compact receipt is at most 65,536 bytes.
