Every Brew/launchctl/plist action commits its attempt ID before invocation. An active or ambiguous journal blocks every mutation except `recovery transition status|resolve|restore`, which reconciles fresh topology and never repeats an ambiguous action. Import refuses while this journal is active; after an exact terminal outcome it archives a compact terminal receipt and its object digest into the import input/ticket before authority creation. Each immutable object is at most 1 MiB and each terminal receipt at most 64 KiB; the complete store admits one active chain of at most sixteen objects, sixteen terminal receipts, two temporaries, and 32 MiB. Before publishing intent it reserves the maximum remaining chain, terminal receipt, and temporary budget; exact-cap succeeds and +1 refuses before any Brew/launchctl/plist action. Active anchor, import input/ticket, or recovery reference pins its chain/receipt. Once terminal topology is proven and no such reference remains, reference-aware GC retains the newest fifteen receipts, removes and parent-syncs older receipt/chains, and resets the anchor for the next operation; an orphan or indeterminate object counts against capacity and blocks rather than permitting replay or growth. These exceptions cannot authorise rescue, policy, configuration, artifact, listener migration, floor, initialisation activation, or any non-legacy root.

Legacy lifecycle proof is state- and action-specific; no stopped topology is required or permitted to fabricate a live PID, listener, or serving challenge:

| Initial topology and command | Required proof before intent/action | Committed external action | Required terminal proof |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live `start` | exact manager/plist/job/PID-start/executable/config/listener correlation and fresh serving-attestation challenge | none; journal records an idempotent already-effective result without a manager invocation | a fresh repetition of the same live correlation/challenge |
| Stopped `start` or stopped `restart` | securely retained supported-manager plist/service definition, exact configured executable/config/listener, and proved absence of its job, CQ process/listener, conflicting manager, and foreign listener | commit one attempt ID, then exact manager start/restart | one fresh supported job, PID-start/executable/config/listener correlation and fresh serving-attestation challenge |
| Live `restart` | exact live correlation/challenge plus every independently required drain/release proof | commit attempt ID before exact manager restart | one fresh post-action job/PID-start/executable/config/listener correlation and serving-attestation challenge; PID/start identity may change only through that attempt |
| Live `stop` | exact live correlation/challenge plus every independently required drain/release proof | commit attempt ID before exact manager stop | selected job, owned CQ process, and owned listener all absent, with no foreign replacement |
| Already-stopped `stop` | exact supported-manager configuration plus absence of selected job, CQ process/listener, conflicting manager, and foreign listener | none; journal records an idempotent already-effective result without invoking the manager | fresh repetition of the same absence proof |
| Live LaunchAgent `uninstall` | exact live correlation/challenge, exact selected owner-only plist identity, and every independently required drain/release proof | commit stop/bootout attempt and prove stopped; then commit a distinct unlink attempt before removing only that plist | selected job, CQ process/listener, and exact plist identity all absent, with no foreign replacement |
| Stopped LaunchAgent `uninstall` | exact selected owner-only plist/config/executable identity plus absence of job, CQ process/listener, conflicting manager, and foreign listener | commit unlink attempt before removing only that plist | selected job, CQ process/listener, and exact plist identity all absent |

Every fresh proof is collected under the same stable lifecycle lock and binds boot-session identity and PID start token where a process exists. A live challenge can prove only the exact process/listener tuple that answered it; an absence proof can prove only stopped topology. Permission failure, stale challenge, mixed before/after facts, action without its committed attempt, or a post-action foreign bind remains indeterminate/conflicted and routes to the exact recovery operation without replay.

Candidate removal is recoverable entirely from parent stores after the candidate root and control directory cease to exist. Under exclusive stable lifecycle lock it first requires the parent validation-controller anchor to select terminal, the controller terminal receipt's exact job identity/attempt and job-absence proof revalidated, both controller and candidate jobs/process groups/sockets absent, every successful receipt unreferenced, every receipt export either absent because no promotion receipt was created or parent-terminal-retired with its export anchor absent, the candidate service plist either present with its exact retained identity or absent with a same-descriptor proof, and the controller plist/socket observations byte-equal the receipt's closed removal-target rows. It then publishes an inert parent `QuarantineLedgerV1` intent whose bounded manifest has candidate control/root as its only quarantined roots and those three ordered objects as its only direct-leaf targets; the controller plist/socket rows are copied byte-for-byte from that receipt and are never inferred from their path. The parent coordinator selects that digest; candidate authority CAS selects the matching `active_operation_ref`; coordinator checkpoints exact selected authority generation/object digest; and only then the anchored ledger successor may act. Root/control move to random operation quarantine through no-replace parent-synced renames. Each present direct leaf advances `pending→removing` with a fresh attempt before exact-identity unlink, parent sync, absence proof, and `removed`; a pre-existing absent target is already `removed` only through its manifest proof. Ledger commits terminal no-job/no-listener/no-process/no-active-tree/no-controller-plist-or-socket topology only after all three actions are removed. Existing `candidate remove` state-loss confirmation authorises the recorded tree-manifest-bounded purge; tree-purge attempt, manifest-wide absence proof, and signed tombstone follow, then the parent coordinator selects its terminal object and publishes its compact terminal receipt. With that receipt durable and the run-scoped authority capsule/index pin already selected, the same lock retires and parent-syncs the controller anchor, then the quarantine anchor, then the coordinator anchor; a crash at any boundary resumes only the remaining retirement suffix from the terminal receipts/tombstone. The lifecycle inode, coordinator verifier/store, controller terminal receipt, ledger tombstone, and bounded coordinator receipt remain. Recovery opens only parent lifecycle/coordinator/controller/ledger state, never a moved inner lock, and finishes the exact recorded boundary without guessing or replaying an ambiguous rename/unlink. Fresh preparation at the same basename requires all three live anchors absent, the exact terminal controller and coordinator receipts, matching quarantine tombstone, and proven absence of every root/direct-leaf manifest identity; it needs no separate unbounded-quarantine acknowledgement.

First Homebrew/process-managed migration is two-phase and keeps compatibility floor unchanged until socket manager is serving compatible normal traffic:

1. While legacy listener remains live, prepare and verify CQ launcher/supervisor/worker artifacts, unloaded socket plist, retained Homebrew restoration receipt, and exact universal request-sender preflight receipt. Preflight runs every registered HTTP, compact, retained, and WebSocket sender—including the exact installed Codex executable/build and selected stateless CQ executable/config through `cq_config_read_per_call_v1`—against the isolated harness, proves each bearer falls in its authorised fingerprint domain, proves CQ local token cannot authenticate either installed-client transport, and seals request-sender/client/config/artifact/protocol/header/credential-index fingerprints plus validation-run ID and whole-request zero-byte foreign-bind results.
2. Require client stopped, normal work drained, and no bearer transmission; commit migration intent without raising required features or floor. Stop exact Homebrew job, prove process exit, then bootstrap prepared socket LaunchAgent on same port. Any foreign bind is conflict; client remains stopped.
3. New socket supervisor starts `compatibility_mode`: normal worker preserves pre-feature routing semantics, rescue/session-policy controls remain inhibited, and authority/floor still permit legacy restoration. Prove public socket/control/runtime and one dependency-free normal-auth fixture. Failure before this proof bootouts socket job and restores exact Homebrew receipt once; injected non-hostile failures must end with one working legacy listener and unchanged scalar floor.
4. Only after compatibility-mode proof does transaction validate rollback floor against union of current plus target intent features, advance structured compatibility receipt, and activate target authority. After floor advance, rollback target is retained feature-compatible CQ socket artifact only; Homebrew/pre-feature binary is never restarted. Terminal failure preserves launchd socket and either selected CQ rollback runtime or visible pending state. No sensitive request sender may connect, construct, queue, or write application bytes until final universal request-sender/transport proof.

This one-time handoff has a process-release-to-launchd-bind interval, so migration is prohibited until every authoritatively enumerated stateful or stateless sender capable of emitting any `Authorization` value is registered and proves `ClientBearerBarrierV1` enforcement for cold login, initial connect, reconnect, and the release window. This includes the selected `cq_config_read_per_call_v1` executable/config source even though it retains no token between calls. A foreign bind then makes every sender withhold `Authorization` and makes migration fail closed; no acknowledgement permits an unregistered sender or credential transmission. Subsequent compatible CQ upgrades retain activation socket.

### `RuntimeIdentity`

Supervisor serving exact connection exposes versioned identity:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "proxy_instance_id": "stable-opaque-instance-id",
  "runtime_instance_id": "random-per-supervisor-process",
  "boot_session_id": "opaque-os-boot-identity",
  "pid": 12345,
  "version": "0.22.0",
  "commit": "abcdef0",
  "started_at": "2026-08-13T12:00:00Z",
  "desired_mode": "normal",
  "effective_mode": "normal",
  "authority_generation": 8,
  "routing_generation": 42,
  "listener_generation": "opaque-digest",
  "instance_state_root_digest": "opaque-digest",
  "supervisor_artifact_sha256": "opaque-digest",
  "worker": {
    "state": "ready|starting|failed|backoff|crash_loop|not_loaded",
    "pid": 12346,
    "artifact_sha256": "opaque-or-null",
    "automatic_start_attempts": 1,
    "restart_window_started_tick_ns": 123456789,
    "next_retry_tick_ns": null,
    "last_exit": {
      "kind": "exit|signal|unknown",
      "code": 1,
      "signal": null,
      "observed_tick_ns": 123456788,
      "executable_sha256": "opaque-digest"
    }
  },
  "effective_config_fingerprint": "keyed-fingerprint-or-null",
  "global_authority_fingerprint": "keyed-fingerprint-or-null",
  "routing_default_fingerprint": "keyed-fingerprint-or-null"
}
```

Detailed identity comes from authenticated Unix-control supervisor and is correlated with separately observed TCP listener. `proxy_instance_id` must equal signed bootstrap/authority identity; `runtime_instance_id` is a new OS-CSPRNG value on each supervisor exec and invalidates old control capabilities, readiness acknowledgements, and runtime marker publications. `boot_session_id` is the OS boot identity used to interpret every runtime monotonic tick. Socket activation may leave launchd and supervisor both retaining same listener descriptor, so snapshot proves inherited socket tuple/definition/descriptor lineage and serving supervisor identity; it does not require one kernel-owner PID. It reconciles launchd job PID, supervisor executable/digest, launcher selection, and exact control instance. Worker PID/executable separately reconciles parentage and Unix-socket identity. Mismatch is `conflicted`, never healthy. `automatic_start_attempts` is required and counts the current rolling window; window/retry/exit fields are explicit null when unavailable. `backoff` requires a same-boot future `next_retry_tick_ns`; `crash_loop` requires it null and suppresses automatic spawn. `last_exit` records the last observed selected-worker termination without logs or arguments; `code` is nonnull only for `exit`, `signal` only for `signal`, and both are null for `unknown`. Rescue reports normal-only fields null with `worker.state=not_loaded`, zero automatic attempts, and null worker timing/exit fields; null never means empty authority.

Public TCP health proves only constant CQ-shaped bytes served on one connection. Lifecycle mutation uses owner-only control/HMAC, then reconciles control identity with TCP activation-socket lineage, launchd job/supervisor, executable, state-root digest, and serving-attestation proof. No control secret or detailed identity is sent to unknown TCP origin.

### `RescueRelay`

Owns fixed path mapping, strict caller-auth validation, sanitised upstream requests, byte-preserving responses, streaming, and WebSocket relay. It has no dependency on credential files, normal inventory, credential coordinator, continuity, routing, registry, Headroom, payload diagnostics, or account mutation.

### `RoutingPolicyStore`

Owns named pools, explicit caller delegations, keyed session bindings, capability evidence, and routing generation nested inside one `ProxyAuthorityStore` object. Routing-only mutation increments both routing and composite authority generation in same anchor commit. Candidate instances receive separate empty routing authority unless validation explicitly supplies a sealed read-only policy snapshot copy.

### `RoutingPolicyController`

Validates complete desired generation, publishes one immutable effective snapshot through `RoutingPolicyAdmissionGate`, and acknowledges exact routing plus composite authority generations through runtime control. Invalid generations never partially replace current effective state. Binding publication and rescue entry share authority lock: rescue checks desired and effective bindings and records suspension in same generation; binding addition refuses after unsuspended rescue intent begins.

### `RoutingPolicyAdmissionGate`

Controller performs file I/O and validation outside gate. Publication takes exclusive side only to swap immutable pointer. Request, retained, retry, WebSocket, and prewarm paths take shared side, verify composite/routing generation, binding, effective membership digest, evidence-scope digest, and evidence-valid-until, cross one durable prepare/send/adoption fence, then release before network I/O. Changed authority before first dispatch-admitted slot abandons prepared-unsent work and may rebuild complete envelope. After first dispatch admission, any later retry or continuation revalidation may only narrow originally frozen candidate slots.

Gate is always acquired before invoking lease/account/prewarm transitions. Publisher never acquires lease, credential, lifecycle, or prewarm locks. No request path performs policy-store I/O while holding gate or lower-level locks.

### `SessionPolicyResolver`

Consumes canonical strong turn metadata, full globally authorised inventory, durable continuity snapshot, and one immutable routing-policy snapshot. It returns one hard eligible account set, policy generation, binding digest, and safe typed failure.

## Private-state durability and concurrency

`CanonicalJSONV1` means RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme encoded as UTF-8. Closed schemas forbid duplicate/unknown fields, floating-point numbers, and `null` unless a field explicitly permits it. Digest is exactly 32 decoded bytes rendered as 64 lower-case hex; public key/signature is canonical unpadded base64url; signed time is UTC RFC3339 `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.NNNNNNNNNZ`. Every signature covers `CanonicalJSONV1` bytes with `signature` omitted.

All new private state follows one shared contract:

- Resolve only absolute clean paths. Starting from trusted `/`, walk every existing component with `openat(O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC)`. Require root-owned non-writable system ancestors or current-UID-owned non-group/world-writable user ancestors; reject symlink, mount/owner substitution, unsafe mode, and unsafe extended ACL. On Darwin inspect `ACL_TYPE_EXTENDED` through retained descriptor before use and after create/replace. Private ancestors/finals permit no non-owner/root allow ACE; external read-only rows may permit read/execute only when row says so, but reject untrusted write, append, delete, delete-child, chown, or write-security authority. Restrictive ACE is allowed; inheritable broadening ACE blocks creation. Newly created object is descriptor-ACL-verified before secret bytes. Parent must already exist; create only missing final state-root component with `mkdirat(..., 0700)`, immediately reopen without following, and retain final directory capability. Fixed application-owned parent creation uses only `ApplicationParentBootstrapV1`; every other parent is pre-existing and recursive arbitrary-path creation is forbidden.
- Before mutation and after final sync, `fstatfs` every authority, credential, compatibility, external-input, and state-root retained descriptor. V1 accepts only local APFS with tested advisory-lock, same-directory rename, link, file-sync, and directory-sync behavior. Reject non-local, NFS, SMB, WebDAV, FUSE, mount-identity change, and roots beneath `~/Library/Mobile Documents` or `~/Library/CloudStorage`; no override exists for secret/authority stores. Same-UID sync agents copying another APFS directory remain explicit residual. Doctor exposes only safe filesystem class/code.
- Use relative `openat`-style operations with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`; create private files at `0600`, never chmod from wider mode. Revalidate retained device/inode/owner/ACL identity at operation boundaries and race ACL mutation in fixtures.
- Current effective UID owns directories/files; every private regular file has link count one and same descriptor identity before/after read or sync.
- Reads are bounded and reject duplicate JSON members where authority could become ambiguous.
- Mutations retain `authority.lock` descriptor from generation read through object and anchor directory sync. No separate control/routing lock exists.
- Mutation supplies expected generation; stale generation returns a conflict without writing.
- Writer creates random exclusive temporary, writes complete canonical JSON, applies mode, syncs file, atomically renames, then syncs directory. Authority uses immutable-object-plus-anchor protocol above.
- A committed-but-unsynced error is reported distinctly from a pre-commit failure.
- Secrets use separate random files when they should not churn with policy JSON.
- Runtime parses and validates a complete generation before atomic publication.
- Readers capture one immutable snapshot pointer and never hold policy-store I/O under lease, routing, credential, or prewarm locks.

External normal configuration is import source, opened through retained, securely walked parent capability. Read is bounded to 1 MiB, uses same final descriptor for parse/fingerprinting, rejects duplicate authority fields, and never follows final symlink. Adoption writes immutable owner-only snapshot under `bootstrap/config-objects/`, syncs it, then authority anchor selects exact snapshot; runtime never reads mutable source directly. Candidate preparation performs same validated snapshot, rejects every configured writable path outside root, and never follows later source changes. Whole-config, global-authority, and routing-default identities are domain-separated HMAC-SHA256 values over length-prefixed canonical objects under instance-derived keys. No raw whole-config SHA-256 appears in TCP health, Unix control, CLI output, logs, markers, receipts, or filenames; this prevents published digest becoming offline oracle for `local_token` or identity-bearing configuration.

Baseline `9fe30df8` enables Headroom exactly when parsed `headroom` is true or parsed `headroom_mode` is nonempty. Its startup then prefers `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` on arm64, then `/usr/local/bin/python3`, then `python3` from ambient `PATH`, executes the selected interpreter as `python3 -u -c <embedded-bridge>`, and imports ambient `headroom-ai`; interpreter, package, and dependency bytes are not CQ release artifacts. V1 deliberately does not admit that ambient descendant into the three-role release/confinement model. After ordinary baseline parse/default/validation, fresh-primary initialisation, legacy import, `config adopt`, and candidate preparation reject any config for which baseline `HeadroomEnabled()` is true—equivalently `headroom=true` or any valid nonempty `headroom_mode`, including `token` and `cache`—before coordinator or initialisation intent, config-object publication, Python path lookup/stat, process execution, package import, credential discovery, or network access. The stable result is `headroom_unsupported`, names only the rejected config fields, and gives safe remediation to set `headroom=false` and remove `headroom_mode`; acknowledgement cannot override it. `config validate|diff` exposes the same non-secret failure without mutation. Frozen preauthority `proxy start` and an already-running legacy source retain baseline Headroom behaviour only until structured import, which remains blocked until Headroom is disabled; no target, floor, candidate, or structured primary launches Python or claims Headroom compatibility.

Legacy import additionally constructs one closed `LegacyHeadroomCompatibilityProofV1={schema_version:1,prior_topology:"live_managed|stopped_managed|live_foreground|stopped_foreground",source_config_keyed_fingerprint,baseline_headroom_enabled:false,source_process_identity_digest:null|string,source_listener_identity_digest:null|string,serving_health_projection_digest:null|string,source_absence_proof_digest:null|string}` in memory before coordinator or initialisation intent and binds its digest into the selected initialisation input and import ticket. The config fields and keyed fingerprint come from the same retained, bounded, duplicate-rejecting descriptor used for baseline parse and `HeadroomEnabled()`. A live variant requires non-null process, listener, and projection digests and null absence proof. Its projection is the closed verifier output `LegacyHeadroomServingProjectionV1={schema_version:1,source_process_identity_digest,source_listener_identity_digest,health_body_digest,serving_proof_digest,headroom:false}` obtained by a fresh serving-proof challenge to the exact already attested source process/listener; the bounded duplicate-rejecting health parser requires exactly one Boolean `headroom` member. Editing `proxy.json` cannot disable a bridge created from the process's startup config. Therefore a current `headroom:true` projection returns `headroom_unsupported` before intent with remediation to stop the source or restart it under the disabled config; a missing, malformed, ambiguous, wrong-process, or invalid serving proof fails the existing live-source attestation gate before intent. A stopped variant requires null process, listener, and projection digests plus the complete fresh source-process/job/listener absence proof and the same disabled same-FD config. No live/stopped substitution or confirmation waives either variant.

For exact bounded raw health body bytes `B` and the one validated serving-proof header value's ASCII bytes `H`, `health_body_digest=hex(SHA256(B))` and `serving_proof_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/legacy-headroom-serving-proof/v1\0") || uint32be(len(H)) || H))`. For complete canonical projection bytes `S` and proof bytes `P`, `serving_health_projection_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/legacy-headroom-serving-projection/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S)) || S))` and `legacy_headroom_compatibility_proof_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/legacy-headroom-compatibility-proof/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`. Activation produces closed `LegacyHeadroomCompatibilityRevalidationV1={schema_version:1,ticket_proof_digest,prior_topology,source_config_keyed_fingerprint,baseline_headroom_enabled:false,source_process_identity_digest:null|string,source_listener_identity_digest:null|string,serving_health_projection_digest:null|string,source_absence_proof_digest:null|string}` with the same live/stopped nullability. The complete object is embedded in the selected pre-action legacy-import phase object; for its canonical bytes `R`, `legacy_headroom_activation_revalidation_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/legacy-headroom-compatibility-revalidation/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R)) || R))` is repeated in composite journal details. Both stores commit that object/digest before any external action, and recovery reopens them rather than reconstructing evidence from the digest.

`OperatorOAuthAuthorizationURLCatalogV1` is closed and contains exactly two rows. `claude_login_authorize` emits scheme/authority/path exactly `https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize` and exactly one value for each query key: `code=true`, `client_id=9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e`, `response_type=code`, `redirect_uri=http://localhost:<assigned-ephemeral-port>/callback`, `scope=org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference user:sessions:claude_code user:mcp_servers user:file_upload`, `code_challenge=<base64url-no-padding(SHA256(verifier))>`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, and `state=<fresh-256-bit-base64url-no-padding-state>`. `codex_login_authorize` emits scheme/authority/path exactly `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize` and exactly one value for each query key: `response_type=code`, `client_id=app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann`, `redirect_uri=http://localhost:1455/auth/callback`, `scope=openid profile email offline_access api.connectors.read api.connectors.invoke`, `code_challenge=<base64url-no-padding(SHA256(verifier))>`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, `id_token_add_organizations=true`, `codex_cli_simplified_flow=true`, `state=<fresh-256-bit-base64url-no-padding-state>`, and `originator=cq`. Both render with exact `go_net_url_values_encode_v1`: UTF-8 query keys sort ascending, each row has one value, space encodes as `+`, percent escapes use upper-case hexadecimal, no empty/duplicate/unknown key is emitted, default port 443 is omitted, and userinfo/fragment are forbidden. Before browser invocation the CLI constructs and commits the complete `OAuthStateCommitmentV1`, `OAuthPKCECommitmentV1`, `OAuthCallbackEndpointProjectionV1`, and `OAuthAuthorizationURLProjectionV1`; their recomputed purpose-separated keyed/public digests bind the exact callback URI, state, verifier/challenge, provider, operation, catalogue row, and rendered wire URL. Verifier, code, token, raw URI, and rendered URL are never persisted.

Authorisation display remains provider-specific baseline behaviour. Claude writes `Opening browser to sign in…` to stdout, invokes the browser once, and only on opener failure writes `Open this URL to sign in:\n  <url>\n`; Codex first writes `Starting local login server on http://localhost:1455.\nIf your browser did not open, navigate to this URL to authenticate:\n\n`, invokes the browser once, and writes `  <url>\n\n` whether opening succeeds or fails. No other login output contains the URL. `control.oauth_callback` binds the complete authorisation catalogue, encoder, browser call, provider-specific stdout bytes, all four callback-prepared safe projection objects, and every `OAuthBind`/`OAuthProjectionDigest` relation; `control.oauth_exchange` additionally binds the complete callback-acceptance, decrypted-secret, and exchange projections. An endpoint, member, value, ordering, escaping, callback, PKCE, projection, purpose label, output, or opener-count mismatch invalidates the corresponding marker.

`OperatorOAuthRouteCatalogV1` is closed and contains exactly two rows. `claude_login_exchange` is `POST https://platform.claude.com:443/v1/oauth/token` with empty query and exact `application/json` duplicate-free object `{grant_type:"authorization_code",code,redirect_uri,client_id:"9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e",code_verifier,state}`. `codex_login_exchange` is `POST https://auth.openai.com:443/oauth/token` with empty query and exact `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` fields `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id=app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann`, and `code_verifier`, each once. Both require one current `OperatorOAuthControlV1` operation. After decrypting the one-use carrier, the worker independently recomputes and exact-matches the state, verifier/challenge, callback acceptance, redirect URI, decrypted-secret, rendered request body, and exchange projections before selecting `exchange_consumed` or producing any request byte; neither route accepts a refresh token or another route's projection. Any extra/duplicate field, content-type, redirect, method, path, query, commitment/projection mismatch, or second exchange rejects before a request body or credential byte leaves the worker.

`NormalCredentialOriginPolicyV1` is closed compile-time authority for credential-bearing normal egress. Its duplicate-free rows bind `{credential_domain,scheme,host,port,base_path,tls_server_name,certificate_policy,proxy_policy,redirect_policy,registered_routes}`; each `registered_routes` member binds exact `source_route_id`, method, escaped path template, query policy, `http|websocket` transport, and `request_semantics_id`. `source_route_id` is an exact public, Claude, Gemini, or operator-OAuth catalogue row or one of the closed internal IDs named below; no free-form internal route exists. V1 official rows are exactly ten: the existing `claude_access_token_v1` row at `https://api.anthropic.com:443`; `claude_authorization_code_v1` at sole `claude_login_exchange`; the existing `claude_refresh_token_v1` at sole `claude_refresh=POST https://platform.claude.com:443/v1/oauth/token`; `codex_authorization_code_v1` at sole `codex_login_exchange`; the existing `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1`, `codex_chatgpt_usage_bearer_v1`, `codex_openai_live_bearer_v1`, and `codex_refresh_token_v1` rows with their exact previously defined routes; `gemini_access_token_v1` at `https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com:443` with empty base path and only `gemini_tier=POST /v1internal:loadCodeAssist` plus `gemini_quota=POST /v1internal:retrieveUserQuota`; and `gemini_refresh_token_v1` at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com:443` with empty base path and sole `gemini_refresh=POST /token`. Existing Claude/Codex public/internal route, method, escaped-path, query, transport, live-call, client-version, usage, selected-account, and affinity semantics remain byte-identical. The new request semantics are closed: `claude_login_authorization_code_json_v1` and `codex_login_authorization_code_form_v1` are the two exact bodies above; `gemini_refresh_form_v1` is form fields `client_id=681255809395-oo8ft2oprdrnp9e3aqf6av3hmdib135j.apps.googleusercontent.com`, the compile-time public installed-client secret, selected `refresh_token`, and `grant_type=refresh_token`, each once; `gemini_tier_json_v1` is exact JSON `{"metadata":{"ideType":"GEMINI_CLI","pluginType":"GEMINI"}}`; and `gemini_quota_json_v1` is exactly the two-byte `{}` body or the exact no-newline `encoding/json` object bytes defined by `GeminiProjectIDV1` from the immediately preceding tier result. An invalid nonempty project selects `gemini_project_id_unsupported` before this constructor and cannot dispatch the quota route. Every other route uses its catalogue-defined request semantics ID. The sealed client version remains the exact bounded ASCII installed-Codex value; invalid values fail readiness rather than broadening query grammar. Gemini tier/quota may resolve only the access token produced by or equal to the same selected `gemini_oauth_credentials_v1` generation; no independent selection, cross-generation substitution, alternate Google host, or ambient credential fallback is legal.

The six retained Claude/Codex rows remain exact rather than prose aliases. `claude_access_token_v1` has empty base path and registers `claude_public_passthrough`, the Claude branches of both named `anthropic_*_model_dispatch` rows, `claude_registry_models=GET /v1/models`, `claude_profile=GET /api/oauth/profile`, and `claude_usage=GET /api/oauth/usage`; only the public passthrough preserves its validated original raw query. `claude_refresh_token_v1` registers only `claude_refresh` with empty query. `codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1` is `https://chatgpt.com:443/backend-api/codex`, registers every catalogue-declared Codex HTTP/Responses-WebSocket route, the three Codex-selected Anthropic-compatible branches at their exact translated POST targets, and `codex_registry_models=GET /models` with empty query or the sole canonical `client_version=<sealed-client-version>` pair. `codex_chatgpt_usage_bearer_v1` is `https://chatgpt.com:443/backend-api` and registers only `codex_usage=GET /wham/usage` with empty query. `codex_openai_live_bearer_v1` is HTTPS base `https://api.openai.com:443/v1`, has no HTTP route, and registers only the exact GET WebSocket projections `/live/<call-id>`, `/realtime/calls/<call-id>`, and `/realtime?intent=quicksilver&call_id=<call-id>`; call ID remains 1–128 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen bytes and emitted query order/escaping is canonical. `codex_refresh_token_v1` is `https://auth.openai.com:443` and registers only `codex_refresh=POST /oauth/token` with empty query. Usage/live material comes only from the exact already selected Codex account/candidate/revision, and live affinity additionally binds its successful live-call choice and call ID.

Explicit and implicit port 443 canonicalise to the same origin. Every row requires HTTPS, exact TLS SNI and HTTP authority, platform certificate verification, no userinfo/query/fragment in configured base, environment proxy disabled, and redirects refused. The sole scheme projection is `https` to `wss` for a registered WebSocket route beneath the same host, port, base path, SNI, certificate, proxy, redirect, and credential-domain policy; it is not a second origin. The `codex_openai_live_bearer_v1` row therefore authorises only its three WSS projections and never an HTTPS request. Config, downstream request, DNS result, response, affinity, and retry cannot change scheme, authority, port, base path, credential domain, route, method, query policy, TLS policy, or selected credential revision. Path construction appends only a registered provider route beneath the bound base and rejects encoded traversal, authority form, scheme-relative form, second origin, invalid call ID, duplicate/unknown fields in an emitted upstream live query, or a non-canonical emitted query. The `codex_chatgpt_usage_bearer_v1` endpoint is an exact sibling authority, not a path escape from `/backend-api/codex`.

Every credential-bearing constructor and dispatch call site is compile-time inventoried against exactly one `(route-catalogue row,credential-domain,registered-route,request-semantics)` tuple. The inventory includes the Claude- and Codex-selected branches of all three catch-all model-dispatch semantic partitions; Claude model/profile/usage/refresh and authorization-code clients; Codex model-registry, usage, refresh, authorization-code, native HTTP/compact/image/search/live calls and both WebSocket origin families; and all three Gemini constructors. Build fails for an unregistered constructor, a registered route without exactly one constructor and fixture, or any method/path/query/transport/body/content-type mismatch; runtime refuses a permit whose catalogue row, binding member, request-semantics ID, and current control/credential generation do not agree.

Discovered Claude/Codex/Gemini provider credentials and transient authorization-code capabilities may be sent only under their exact official row. During import, fresh initialisation, `config adopt`, and candidate preparation, baseline empty-to-default handling runs first and then `claude_upstream` must equal the canonical official origin/base `https://api.anthropic.com` and `codex_upstream` must equal `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`; Gemini and OAuth-login origins are compile-time-only and have no config override. Explicit port 443 canonicalises equivalently, but userinfo, fragment, query, alternate scheme/host/port/base path, and a trailing-path change do not. Any other previously parseable legacy value fails before coordinator intent, config-object publication, credential discovery, or network access with stable `custom_upstream_unsupported`, the rejected field name, and safe remediation to restore the official value; it is never silently replaced or activated. `config validate|diff` exposes the same non-secret failure. Future custom support requires a separate compile-time adapter and separately provisioned origin-scoped credential domain whose row names the exact HTTPS origin. Operator acknowledgement cannot re-scope an official credential. Synthetic candidate validation may use its sealed fake-TLS origin only with synthetic in-memory credentials and a validation-run-bound non-production row; that row is invalid in primary authority.

`NormalCredentialOriginBindingV1={schema_version:1,policy_revision,policy_digest,credential_domain,canonical_origin_base_digest,tls_proxy_redirect_contract_digest,config_object_digest}` is closed. Its digest is domain-separated SHA-256 over length-prefixed `CanonicalJSONV1`. The complete sorted binding set contains exactly one binding for each of the ten V1 official rows above and no other member; its set digest is a mandatory field of immutable config and composite authority and worker readiness reconstructs the same ten-member set. Every credential-bearing request envelope and single-use dispatch permit binds the exact member digest and request-semantics ID. Existing closed validation receipts bind it without schema ambiguity: `ProductionCallerProfileReceiptV1.endpoint_substitution_digest`, `RealClientValidationReceiptV1.endpoint_binding_digest`, and `InstalledCandidatePreflightReceiptV1.protocol_semantics_digest` are each domain-separated framed digests that include the exact origin-binding digest; their enclosing receipts and finalisation evidence therefore bind it transitively. `RuntimePolicyAckV1.effective_policy_digest` likewise includes the complete binding-set digest. A receipt or acknowledgement made under any other binding cannot satisfy current authority.

Config prepare and selection validate the binding; worker start reconstructs it; immediately before every credential-bearing HTTP write, WebSocket dial, retry, registry refresh, primer usage read, model fetch, OAuth exchange, or Gemini tier/quota call, the transport revalidates exact domain/origin/route/method/query/request semantics/policy against the credential and control revision. Missing, custom-with-official-credential, HTTP where only WSS is registered, authority drift, redirect, proxy substitution, TLS mismatch, or account/candidate/revision/control drift fails before credential/body bytes with a safe origin-policy error and zero alternate attempt. Corpus covers every official provider path; both authorization-code exchanges and every body/content-type/callback binding; exact Google refresh/tier/quota URLs, bodies, call order, and credential generation; exact `GET /backend-api/wham/usage` with empty query; all three `api.openai.com` live/realtime WSS forms and call-ID boundaries; explicit/default port equality; wrong method/transport; HTTP live-sideband attempts; userinfo; query/fragment; duplicate, reordered, missing, encoded, or extra fields; alternate host/port/base; encoded escape; environment proxy; redirect; DNS/TLS authority mismatch; cross-domain or cross-revision credential substitution; affinity mismatch; and synthetic-row use outside candidate validation. Adjacent or unregistered Claude/Codex/Google paths reject before credential bytes.

Each immutable config object is at most 1 MiB. `bootstrap/config-objects/` retains only current selected object, one object named by active transition, and one explicitly selected rollback dependency; count cap is three and directory cap including one temporary is 4 MiB. Adoption preflights capacity before write. After later authority anchor and history checkpoint are durable, reference-aware GC unlinks every other object and syncs directory; crash before anchor leaves new object inert, crash after anchor retains every referenced object, and crash during GC cannot remove a reference. Doctor reports orphan count/bytes, never values. Unlink is retention control, not secure erasure on APFS or backups.

`ExternalAuthoritySourceRegistryV1` is closed compile-time authority for every path-bearing option. Each row fixes command/option, source kind, file/tree shape, parser/schema, byte/entry/depth limits, owner/mode/link/mount rules, sensitivity, fingerprint domain, and copy-or-retain semantics. Unknown option/source kind rejects before opening; no catch-all authority JSON exists. Rows are: normal/source config strict JSON 1 MiB; credential manifest strict JSON 64 KiB/16 entries; each referenced registered-adapter credential regular file 1 MiB and 16 MiB aggregate; `--local-token-client-registry` exact `LocalTokenClientManifestV1` strict JSON 64 KiB/16 entries, copied into selected control authority with fingerprint domain `cq/external/local-token-client-registry/v1`; candidate policy strict JSON 8 MiB; pool predicate strict JSON 64 KiB; migration preflight/receipt strict JSON 64 KiB; endpoint snapshot/ticket strict JSON 16 KiB; installed client Mach-O 1 GiB; CQ launcher/supervisor/worker Mach-O 268,435,456 bytes; each `--floor-release-bundle|--target-release-bundle|--release-bundle` exact `ReleaseBundleV1` tree, 1 GiB/17 descendants/depth two, copied into canonical release stores while locator/fingerprint is retained through its operation; every command option set that supplies a `purpose="floor"` bundle through `--floor-release-bundle` or rollback `--release-bundle` must pair `--floor-acceptance-receipt-file`, which accepts one exact closed signed `RollbackFloorAcceptanceReceiptV1` regular canonical JSON file at most 64 KiB, fingerprint domain `cq/external/floor-acceptance-receipt/v1`, requires its separately supplied expected digest and computed floor-bundle digest to match, and copies the verified canonical bytes into `release-provenance/floor-acceptance/`; `authority initialise prepare --preactivation-receipt-file` and `service release stage --validation-receipt-file` each accept one exact exported `CandidateReleasePromotionReceiptV1` regular file with bytes `E=Q || 0x0a` and `len(E)≤65,536`, where `Q` is the byte-identical `CanonicalJSONV1` encoding of the closed parent-MACed promotion receipt and contains no trailing whitespace. Their input identity, size, and fingerprint under domain `cq/external/candidate-floor-validation-receipt/v1` bind all of `E`; each importer requires exactly one terminal LF, strips only that LF, duplicate-rejecting parses `Q`, re-renders byte-identical `Q`, verifies its parent MAC through the retained source controller chain and the separately supplied promotion-receipt digest over `Q`, recursively reopens/verifies the inner signed `R`, and securely publishes canonical `Q` plus its pinned canonical inner `R` into the owning validation stores. Missing/duplicate LF, CRLF, any other leading/trailing whitespace, normalisation, `E` stored as either canonical object, or failure to reconstruct exact `E=Q || LF` on reopen refuses; no caller path or exported `E` remains authority after the canonical copy. Fresh `authority initialise prepare --candidate-instance-state-root` registers the retained sealed-candidate root capability described below and may open only its exact bootstrap/authority/controller/run chain plus the canonical barrier receipt/case set named by imported `Q` and its inner `R`; `feature activate prepare --preactivation-receipt DIGEST` resolves only canonical `Q` already selected by the staged target release and recursively reopens its inner `R` and never opens a caller path; and `authority import-legacy prepare --source-executable` accepts exact legacy foreground CQ Mach-O regular file, 268,435,456-byte maximum, retained for attestation without copying, fingerprint domain `cq/external/legacy-foreground-executable/v1`. Binary/tree rows never use JSON-file rules. Every unregistered source rejects before opening.

Every row uses retained-parent walk, absolute-clean path where baseline semantics allow, owner/mode/link/type, `O_NOFOLLOW`, stable same-descriptor read, and before/after identity. Intent/object bind domain-separated keyed content fingerprint plus device/inode/size. Credential manifest cannot introduce adapter/kind/limit. Legacy tree registry above separately caps 18 sources, 64 MiB/source, 512 MiB aggregate, 4,096 entries/source, 32,768 aggregate, depth 16; only current-UID directories and link-count-one regular files on retained APFS mount are accepted. Symlink, hard link, device, socket, FIFO, nested mount, unknown name, overflow, rename, in-place/mode/owner replacement, or second path parse refuses before mutation.

Candidate read-only credentials use registered adapter only. Prepare securely walks credential parent, opens exact regular file with `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`, requires current-UID owner, mode `0600`, link count one, adapter-specific size bound, stable device/inode/mtime/size through complete same-FD read, and records keyed content fingerprint plus identity in sealed candidate manifest. Start reopens/revalidates before snapshot and supplies the immutable record only to `CandidateProviderCredentialVaultV1` inside the trusted controller-owned broker. The vault copies the minimum bearer and account/revision projection into locked, non-dumpable memory, immediately closes the source descriptor, exposes only broker-local lookup by the exact keyed account/candidate/revision tuple, and has no refresh, adoption, keychain, persistence, delete, external callback, or candidate-readable interface. Raw credential bytes are never placed in candidate argv, environment, files, inherited descriptors, IPC, request capabilities, responses, receipts, errors, or logs and are zeroised when the run terminates. Replacement makes candidate proof stale and blocks use; it is never followed live. Tests install candidate read/inheritance, write/refresh/keychain, and broker-vault sentinels and race rename/link/permission/content replacement.

Live-provider validation cases are controller authority fixed before candidate execution. Closed `CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityCoreV1={schema_version:1,validation_run_id,candidate_proxy_instance_id,candidate_runtime_instance_id,controller_key_id,validation_case_id,validation_case_ordinal,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority:CandidateSyntheticIngressAuthorityV1,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest,selected_provider:"codex",source_route_id,request_semantics_id,transport:"http"|"websocket",phase:"http_dispatch"|"http_retry"|"retained_dispatch"|"ws_upgrade"|"ws_first_send"|"prewarm_dial"|"prewarm_probe_send"|"prewarm_adoption"|"prewarm_first_send"|"websocket_application_send",account_key_hmac,candidate_id_hmac,credential_revision_hmac,normal_credential_origin_binding_digest,final_route_choice_core:FinalRouteChoiceCoreV1,final_route_choice_digest,websocket_application_send_derivation_kind:CandidateProviderWebSocketApplicationSendDerivationKindV1|null,candidate_provider_websocket_application_send_derivation_kind_digest:null|string,encoded_request_digest:null|string,expected_caller_set_digest,expected_member_digest,expected_evidence_scope_digest,response_body_or_event_byte_limit,response_event_count_limit,credential_echo_scan_decision_budget:CandidateProviderCredentialEchoScanDecisionBudgetV1,credential_echo_scan_decision_budget_digest,credential_echo_scan_clear_slot_reservation_count,credential_echo_scan_store_byte_reservation,planned_provider_connection_nonce:null|string,planned_provider_connection_identity_digest:null|string,connection_generation:null|integer,issued_at,valid_until,nonce}` is closed. Thus the fixed catalogue structurally authorises a later derivation but never predicts a provider response ID, output item, live socket, attempt, phase event, or incremental frame.

For every other case, response limits are positive, equal the later kind-selected capability projections, and determine the complete credential-scan reservation before Begin. Closed `CandidateProviderCredentialEchoScanDecisionBudgetV1={schema_version:1,decision_profile:"http_response_v1"|"websocket_handshake_v1"|"websocket_application_v1"|"not_applicable",response_event_count_limit,metadata_clear_slots,identity_event_clear_slots,terminal_suffix_clear_slots,encoded_dual_view_clear_slots,postupgrade_generated_clear_slots,total_clear_slots}` is closed. For `ws_upgrade|prewarm_dial`, its profile is `websocket_handshake_v1`, only `postupgrade_generated_clear_slots=2` is nonzero, and `total_clear_slots=2` for the atomic generated Text-plus-Close pair. For `prewarm_probe_send|ws_first_send|prewarm_first_send|websocket_application_send`, its profile is `websocket_application_v1`, only `identity_event_clear_slots=response_event_count_limit` is nonzero, and `total_clear_slots=response_event_count_limit`. `prewarm_adoption` alone uses `not_applicable` with every count zero. For canonical budget bytes `B`, `credential_echo_scan_decision_budget_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-credential-echo-scan-decision-budget/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))`. Let `E_scan=4,096`; every case requires `credential_echo_scan_clear_slot_reservation_count=credential_echo_scan_decision_budget.total_clear_slots` and `credential_echo_scan_store_byte_reservation=credential_echo_scan_clear_slot_reservation_count*E_scan` with checked arithmetic. No case reserves the run-terminal sentinel. Every non-null final-route, origin, semantics, phase, caller/member/evidence, exact-request, response limit, complete budget/digest, reservation, and planned-connection fact is selected independently by the trusted controller from the attested route, policy, credential, and validation-case catalogues. `validation_case_id`, each present planned nonce, and `nonce` are independent 128-bit OS-CSPRNG values; ordinal is contiguous from one; validity is finite and no later than the run, synthetic authority, selected credential, and validation-operation endpoints. For `C=CanonicalJSONV1(CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityCoreV1)`, `signature=Ed25519.Sign(controller_private_key,ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-validation-case-authority-signature/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C)`; `CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityV1={schema_version:1,core:CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityCoreV1,issuer_public_key,signature}` is closed, the issuer equals selected Ready, and for complete canonical bytes `V`, `candidate_provider_validation_case_authority_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-validation-case-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(V)) || V))`. Complete canonical `V` is at most 524,288 bytes.

The controller publishes two distinct case partitions after Ready and before the runtime-authority CAS. Closed `CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityCatalogueV1={schema_version:1,source_kind:"hermetic"|"production_profile",validation_run_id,candidate_proxy_instance_id,candidate_runtime_instance_id,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest,production_caller_source_manifest_digest:null|string,cases:[CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityV1...],case_digests:[string...]}` requires the production-source digest non-null exactly for `production_profile`; its arrays are equal-length, non-empty, sorted by contiguous partition-local ordinal then ID, duplicate-free, and each digest recomputes from the same-position complete case. Every case embeds the byte-identical synthetic authority named by the catalogue, uses the catalogue tag, and is one of that authority's `allowed_routes`; neither partition may contain a case for the other authority. For complete canonical bytes `L`, `candidate_provider_validation_case_authority_catalogue_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-validation-case-authority-catalogue/v1\0") || uint32be(len(L)) || L))`; complete `L` is at most 1,048,576 bytes.

Closed `CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityCatalogueSetEntryV1={schema_version:1,source_kind:"hermetic"|"production_profile",production_caller_source_manifest_digest:null|string,production_caller_source_manifest_object_identity_digest:null|string,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority:CandidateSyntheticIngressAuthorityV1,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest,candidate_synthetic_ingress_index_member_digest,catalogue:CandidateProviderValidationCaseAuthorityCatalogueV1,candidate_provider_validation_case_authority_catalogue_digest}` embeds one complete partition and its complete synthetic authority. Complete `S` is at most 2,097,152 bytes, so the member and set bounds are joint and two individually maximal catalogues are not promised to fit. Production source discovery and publication of the production manifest, both synthetic authorities, the fixed index set, and this complete set all precede broker policy, runtime-authority CAS, and Begin. Runtime authority, Begin, broker policy, every routing authority, preflight, receipt, close, seal, recovery, export/import, promotion, and finalisation reopen the exact set, both entries, their complete authorities, reservations, and the selected member digest; post-Begin insertion, replacement, reconstruction, or partition substitution invalidates the run before candidate or provider I/O.

`CandidateProviderValidationSourceStoreV1` is the controller-owned durable source closure at exact `validation-evidence/provider-broker/validation-sources/runs/<validation_run_id>/`. A final is `<source-kind>-<content-digest>.json`; the only temporary in the active run is `.<source-kind>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`. `source-kind` is exactly `production_caller_source_manifest|validation_case_catalogue_set|synthetic_ingress_authority|synthetic_ingress_materialisation|synthetic_ingress_index_set|broker_policy|candidate_runtime_resource_envelope|controller_runtime_authority`. The complete catalogue-set object is at most 2,097,152 canonical bytes; every other complete source is at most 65,536 bytes; the exact joint live-byte maxima, including the sole substitutive temporary, are `2,097,152 + 23*65,536 = 3,604,480` per run and `3*3,604,480 = 10,813,440` across the active and newest two retained sealed runs. A second temporary, twenty-fifth final, fourth run, any non-catalogue source byte 65,537, catalogue-set byte 2,097,153, per-run byte 3,604,481, global leaf 73, or global byte 10,813,441 refuses before source signing, Begin, capability issue, candidate exec, or provider I/O.

Every source uses current-UID local-APFS `0700` directories and a current-UID, link-count-one, mode-`0600` regular leaf. The controller exclusively creates the random no-follow temporary, writes complete canonical bytes, file-syncs, verifies the schema/signature/content digest on the same description, no-replace renames to the digest-derived final, syncs the run directory, and verifies the same inode and bytes both on that description and a no-follow final-path reopen. Existing finals are adoptable only inside the same run on byte equality, valid selected-Ready signature, safe identity, and equal dependency DAG; collision or ambiguity invalidates the run. Closed `CandidateProviderValidationSourceObjectIdentityV1={schema_version:1,validation_run_id,source_kind,relative_path,device,inode,current_uid,mode:384,link_count:1,mount_identity_digest,byte_count,content_digest}` names one reopened final; for its canonical bytes `O`, `candidate_provider_validation_source_object_identity_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-validation-source-object-identity/v1\0") || uint32be(len(O)) || O))`. For every selected source prefix, canonical rows `S_i={ordinal,source_kind,content_digest,candidate_provider_validation_source_object_identity_digest,byte_count}` are sorted by `(source_kind,content_digest)`, ordinal-contiguous, and duplicate-free; `candidate_provider_validation_source_set_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-validation-source-set/v1\0") || uint32be(count) || concat(uint32be(len(CanonicalJSONV1(S_i))) || CanonicalJSONV1(S_i))))`. The pre-Begin set contains exactly the production manifest, two synthetic authorities, index set, catalogue set, broker policy, and candidate runtime envelope; the runtime authority binds that predecessor set and is then its sole successor. Later materialisations each bind the exact runtime authority, index-set object and selected member digest.
