Because a state contains only seven bounded cursors, one active scalar action, and the constant-size accumulator—not any action vector—the checked-in 1,063-action maximum state and its exact action 1,064 rejection both remain attainable within 65,536 canonical bytes.

After all ten directory actions are complete, the parent publishes closed at-most-8,192-byte `CandidateProviderBrokerRunRetirementReceiptV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_provider_broker_run_retirement_receipt_v1",retirement_id,validation_run_id,manifest_digest,manifest_object_identity_digest,terminal_state_digest,terminal_state_object_identity_digest,inventory_digest,generated_control_action_count,credential_echo_scan_action_count,routing_authority_action_count,route_budget_action_count,journal_action_count,validation_source_action_count,run_directory_action_count:10,final_proof_set_digest,run_directory_absence_proof_set_digest,completed_at,nonce,mac}`. Its six file-action counts plus `run_directory_action_count` equal manifest `action_count`; `final_proof_set_digest` equals `D_action_count`, and the separately framed directory-absence set is exactly the final ten accumulator inputs. For omitted-MAC canonical receipt bytes `R0`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_candidate_provider_broker_retirement_receipt,ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-broker-run-retirement-receipt-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R0)) || R0))`; for complete MACed bytes `R`, `candidate_provider_broker_run_retirement_receipt_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/candidate-provider-broker-run-retirement-receipt/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R)) || R))`. Manifest, state, and receipt publication each random-exclusively creates the sole destination `.object` temporary, bounded-writes and file-syncs it, no-replace renames it to the digest-derived final, syncs the destination directory, then same-descriptor/no-follow reopens exact bytes and stable identity before an anchor may name it. A manifest temporary substitutes for its absent sole manifest final; once that final exists, the object temporary is capped at 65,536 bytes because only state or receipt publication remains. Collision succeeds only on complete byte/MAC/digest/identity equality. Receipt publication precedes one state successor that binds its digest/identity pair and one anchor CAS selecting `receipt_committed`; a crash at any boundary exposes only an inert unpublished object, the exact prior anchor, or the exact complete successor, and recovery never invents a cursor, receipt, or deletion from absence alone.

The parent first selects the broker manifest and `intent` state while leaving `CandidateValidationControllerAuthorityIndexV1` byte-identical and performs no unlink. It next publishes `CandidateValidationEvidenceRetirementV1` `intent` binding that manifest and intent-state digest/object-identity pairs plus the exact authority-index predecessor and evidence pin, then selects the exact-prior broker `evidence_handoff_committed` state binding the reopened evidence-retirement digest/object identity. Only that handoff authorises the broker action sequence. After all broker actions, the parent publishes and reopens the broker receipt and selects `receipt_committed`, still leaving the authority index byte-identical, then advances the exact-prior evidence-retirement state to `broker_retired` with that receipt pair. Only after `broker_retired` reopens may evidence retirement perform its existing `index_unpinned` CAS; those evidence-retirement CASes remain the sole owner of authority-index row removal, and the broker retirement key, anchor, state, manifest, or receipt has no authority-index write capability. Once `broker_retired` pins the broker receipt, the parent may remove the broker anchor, current/predecessor state, and manifest and sync their parents. A crash after broker intent but before evidence intent resumes the inert broker intent; after evidence intent but before handoff it selects only the matching handoff successor; after handoff it resumes only the fixed next broker action; after receipt publication it resumes `receipt_committed`; and after that state but before `broker_retired` it binds only the reopened receipt. No recovery path reconstructs a pin, skips the handoff, removes broker metadata before `broker_retired`, or advances the authority index from absence alone. The newest three compact broker receipts remain. One active manifest is at most 786,432 bytes; current and predecessor state, anchor, object/anchor temporaries are each at most 65,536; each of three receipts is at most 8,192; there is one manifest, two state finals, one anchor, two temporaries, and three receipts at most: nine leaves and `786,432 + 5*65,536 + 3*8,192 = 1,138,688` bytes within the reserved 1,179,648-byte cap. During manifest publication its at-most-786,432-byte substitutive temporary exists only while the manifest final and every state/anchor/receipt are absent, so it cannot increase that peak. A second active manifest, tenth leaf, manifest action 1,064, state `proof_count` 1,064, cursor/count/accumulator mismatch, manifest byte 786,433, state/anchor byte 65,537, receipt byte 8,193, or aggregate byte 1,179,649 refuses before unlink. The checked-in maximum-action fixture encodes all 1,063 accumulator successors and proves every complete state remains within 65,536 bytes without padding or an action-sized vector. Controller loss merely selects the exact `invalidated|temporary_only|absent` journal disposition and raw-prefix authority after parent cleanup; it never permits signing, tail repair, replay, or post-intent inventory. If three run capsules already exist, fourth-run preparation first selects or resumes broker retirement for the oldest eligible run, reopens its manifest/current anchor/state or terminal broker receipt as applicable, completes the ten directory absences, then completes the dependent evidence-retirement `index_unpinned`/receipt/terminal-index sequence and evidence/authority directory absences; no new run object, temporary, controller, or provider traffic may exist until both receipts and the terminal authority-index successor reopen. An identity-mismatched temporary is never unlinked, and a pinned, controller-loss-ambiguous, or otherwise ambiguous oldest run blocks rather than exceeding the three-run cap.

Authority key is never derived from `local_token`, continuity keys, access tokens, or account identity. Canonical unpadded base64url decoding to 32 bytes is format only, never entropy proof. Token provenance is closed: `generated_v1` means CQ generated 32 OS-CSPRNG bytes and committed MACed operation/config/token receipt; `legacy_preserved_v1` proves only exact same-FD legacy continuity and is valid solely for still-running legacy source/pre-floor restoration; `unproven` means everything else. Only `generated_v1` may authenticate socket-supervisor target. `legacy_preserved_v1` never authenticates target, native Codex, rescue, delegation, pool routing, registry, credential resolution, or cross-account dispatch.

`LocalTokenClientRegistryV1` is closed authority for clients that can receive or retain CQ `local_token` and, independently, for every stateful or stateless process that can send a sensitive application request to the public loopback endpoint, whether or not that request can contain `Authorization`. It is `{schema_version:1,registry_revision,enumeration_context_digest,adapter_results,clients,client_set_digest,request_senders,request_sender_set_digest,authorization_sender_set_digest}`; each sorted duplicate-free stateful client is `{client_identity_digest,adapter_id,source_capability_digest,client_executable_digest,config_binding_digest,attestation_key_id,attestation_public_key}`, and each sorted duplicate-free request sender is `{sender_identity_digest,adapter_id,client_identity_digest:null|string,sender_executable_digest,config_binding_digest,credential_domains,request_transports,barrier_protocol_digest}`. `credential_domains` is a sorted duplicate-free subset of the closed `cq_local_token|claude_bearer|codex_bearer` literals and may be empty only for an attested payload-bearing sender that can never emit `Authorization`; `request_transports` is a non-empty sorted duplicate-free subset of `http|compact|retained|websocket`. Unknown or omitted domains/transports, an empty-domain sender that can emit `Authorization`, or an unenumerated payload-bearing path refuses. `authorization_sender_set_digest` is the exact projection of request senders with non-empty credential domains and never substitutes for the complete `request_sender_set_digest`. Client and sender identities are domain-separated HMACs over their adapter, retained source identity, executable identity, and config binding; no path, account, raw token, or payload enters registry output. Every stateful client that can send a sensitive request maps to exactly one request sender, while a stateless sender has null client identity and needs no token-cutover acknowledgement. Attestation keys are distinct per stateful client, generated outside CQ's token domain, and the private key is never present in CQ configuration, handoff output, supervisor, or another client's state. V1 adapter catalogue is literal and exhaustive:

| Adapter | Exact enumeration authority | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `cq_config_read_per_call_v1` | Selected signed CQ executable/release identity plus selected immutable `proxy.json`; it proves the built-in registry-refresh client reopens config for every operation and has no persistent token store | Exactly one stateless `cq_local_token` request sender with exact executable/config/transport binding and barrier-protocol digest, never a client/ACK entry; before every connection or application write it must obtain the universal barrier permit, and executable, config-source, domain, transport, or protocol mismatch is unavailable |
| `managed_external_client_manifest_v1` | Exact `LocalTokenClientManifestV1` supplied through `--local-token-client-registry`, securely copied beneath control, then selected by authority | Zero to 16 stateful clients; every entry requires adapter literal `managed_external_client_v1`, exact executable digest, source/config-binding capability digest, unique Ed25519 attestation key ID/public key, and exactly one corresponding request-sender entry with every supported transport and every credential domain it can emit; a payload-bearing no-Authorization client still contributes the empty-domain request-sender row |
| `known_projection_audit_v1` | Selected normal config plus exact registered Claude/Codex external-projection sink manifests and retained same-FD target snapshots | Produces no client; any recognised token-exporting or sensitive-request path or live registered control peer not matched by the managed manifest is `unregistered_local_token_client` and blocks |

`LocalTokenClientManifestV1={schema_version:1,registry_revision,clients:[{adapter_id:"managed_external_client_v1",client_executable_digest,source_capability_digest,config_binding_digest,credential_domains,request_transports,barrier_protocol_digest,attestation_key_id,attestation_public_key}]}` is closed canonical JSON, sorted/duplicate-free, at most 16 entries/64 KiB, and contains no token, payload, or private key. File may be explicitly empty. An authoritatively empty `clients` array means all three adapters completed, exact stateless CQ sender result verified, explicit managed manifest was present and empty, projection audit found no token exporter, sensitive-request sender, or unmatched peer, and activation re-enumeration matched prepare; it never means the `request_senders` set is empty because the built-in CQ sender remains present. Missing/unreadable source, unknown adapter, unsafe manifest, projection ambiguity, or unmatched peer is unavailable/conflicted, never empty. Same-UID token or payload-sender copies outside every registered source remain an explicit local-user trust-boundary residual and are not claimed detectable; operator must register such clients before cutover. Registry revision, adapter results, both complete enumerations/set digests, and keyed source fingerprints are sealed before prepare and revalidated at activation. The complete registry admits at most 16 stateful clients, 17 `request_senders` including the mandatory stateless CQ sender, 49 sender/credential-domain memberships, and 68 sender/transport memberships; exact caps succeed, while client 17, sender 18, credential membership 50, transport membership 69, unknown domain/transport, or byte +1 is `resource_capacity_exhausted` before token generation or state mutation.

Fresh primary initialisation and legacy import require explicit `--local-token-client-registry`, including an explicit empty manifest. Existing-authority config adoption or listener migration may omit it only to reuse the exact currently selected registry generation; supplying it proposes a replacement in the same parent operation and revalidates every existing client binding before token generation. A token-changing operation cannot select a registry after handoff, and registry-only replacement is a separate config-adopt operation that never changes token. Unknown legacy distribution, missing manifest on first import, or any known projection/live peer outside the manifest blocks before creating target token. CLI never synthesises empty registry from “no process currently connected.”

Enumeration is fail closed. Every registered adapter must resolve to exact `present|absent`; unsafe, unavailable, ambiguous, over-limit, or unsupported sources are `client_enumeration_incomplete`, never absence. Any observed current or retained local-token client or any stateful/stateless sender of sensitive request bytes—including one incapable of `Authorization`—that does not map to exactly one entry in its corresponding complete set also makes enumeration incomplete. An empty client set is authoritative only when every client adapter proves absence and there is no unmatched current or retained client; the request-sender set still contains `cq_config_read_per_call_v1`. Operator confirmation, process absence, a quiet listener, or zero credential domains cannot manufacture absence. Activation repeats complete enumeration and requires byte-identical registry revision, client/request/authorisation sender sets and digests, credential-domain and request-transport sets, barrier-protocol digests, source identities/fingerprints, executable identities, and config bindings. Drift expires the prepared acknowledgement set and every barrier receipt and requires new prepare.

Every fresh initialisation, import, config adoption, or migration that introduces or changes a target token uses `LocalTokenCutoverV1`; direct target selection is forbidden. Adopt and migrate use distinct `prepare|status|activate|abort` invocations; import and fresh initialisation use their existing split transaction phases. Prepare generates 32 OS-CSPRNG bytes and stages target config/provenance while an existing prior service/token remains effective; the fresh-initialisation variant requires canonical null prior-config/prior-token fingerprints and has no effective service. Immutable intent projection is exactly `{schema_version:1,operation_id,prior_config_fingerprint,target_config_fingerprint,prior_token_fingerprint,target_token_fingerprint,client_registry_revision,client_set_digest,client_enumeration_context_digest,handoff_nonce_digest,prepared_at,expires_at}`; `expires_at` is exactly 24 hours after `prepared_at`. For the independently generated raw 32-byte nonce `N`, `handoff_nonce_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/local-token-handoff-nonce/v1\0") || uint32be(32) || N))`. `local_token_cutover_intent_digest` is domain-separated SHA-256 over length-prefixed `CanonicalJSONV1` of that projection.

Cutover state is digest-chained immutable object `{schema_version:1,operation_id,local_token_cutover_intent_digest,handoff_secret_object_digest,state:"token_handoff_pending|clients_acknowledged|activated|aborted|expired",state_sequence,previous_state_digest,challenge_set_digest,ack_set_digest,state_at,mac}`. Initial pending object has sequence zero, previous digest null, and empty challenge/acknowledgement-set digests. Every later state increments sequence once and names exact prior state-object digest; the object never contains its own digest, and `handoff_secret_object_digest` remains byte-identical for that cutover generation. State-object digest is domain-separated SHA-256 over length-prefixed exact `CanonicalJSONV1` bytes including MAC. MAC is domain-separated HMAC-SHA256 over `CanonicalJSONV1` with `mac` omitted. The relevant config-adopt/listener-migration/legacy-import journal or ticket, or fresh `InitialisationPhaseV1` chain, binds immutable intent digest plus current state-object digest/state/sequence, handoff-secret object digest, token fingerprints, client-registry revision, enumeration-context/client/challenge/ack-set digests, and expiry in one authority generation. Raw handoff is exactly `LocalTokenHandoffFrameV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,local_token_cutover_intent_digest,target_config_fingerprint,target_token,handoff_nonce,expires_at}` where `target_token` is the canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the generated 32 OS-CSPRNG token bytes, `handoff_nonce` is the canonical unpadded base64url encoding of an independent 32 OS-CSPRNG bytes, and all other fields byte-match the selected unexpired intent/config. Its wire bytes are exactly `CanonicalJSONV1(LocalTokenHandoffFrameV1) || LF`, are at most 1 KiB, and contain no BOM, prefix, suffix, second object, or platform-dependent newline. They are emitted only through mandatory `--local-token-handoff-fd FD`: FD≥3, not stdio/TTY, duplicated CLOEXEC; a regular file is additionally current-UID-owned `0600`, single-link, local APFS, and either empty at offset zero or already contains the one byte-identical complete frame. The writer never truncates or appends. It loops across `EINTR` and short writes under the leaf context until every frame byte is written; for a regular file it then file-syncs and same-descriptor verifies exact size and bytes before reporting success. A byte-identical already-complete regular file is an idempotent success without a write; any other nonempty file rejects. A pipe or local socket succeeds only after the complete frame was written to that fresh stream; on partial write, peer close, deadline, or sync/verification failure, `handoff_emitted=false`, the operation remains pending, and retry requires a newly supplied empty regular file or fresh stream rather than appending to the partial sink. Consumers accept only one complete newline-terminated canonical frame and discard EOF/close without that terminator. `handoff_emitted=true` means this complete-write contract succeeded, never merely that a write was attempted. No token enters argv, stdout/JSON, stderr, logs, receipts, or fingerprints. Exact unexpired pending operation may re-emit the same byte-identical frame after owner authentication; no general reveal exists.

The raw handoff nonce has one durable owner and is never reconstructed from its digest. `LocalTokenHandoffSecretV1={schema_version:1,kind:"local_token_handoff_secret_v1",operation_id,cutover_generation,local_token_cutover_intent_digest,target_config_fingerprint,target_token_fingerprint,handoff_nonce,created_at,expires_at,mac}` is canonical JSON at most 1 KiB; `handoff_nonce` is the same canonical unpadded base64url 32-byte value used by the frame and hashes to the intent's `handoff_nonce_digest`. Its parent authentication key is `initialise.key` for `fresh_initialisation|legacy_import` and `authority.key` for `config_adopt|authority_migrate`; `K_local_token_handoff_secret=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=parent_authentication_key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/local-token-handoff-secret/v1"),L=32)`. For `S=CanonicalJSONV1(secret with mac omitted)`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_local_token_handoff_secret,ASCII("cq/local-token-handoff-secret-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S)) || S))`; for complete MACed bytes `J`, `handoff_secret_object_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/local-token-handoff-secret/v1\0") || uint32be(len(J)) || J))`. Writer publishes it no-replace at `local-token-cutover/secrets/<operation_id>.<cutover_generation>.json` as a current-UID-owned `0600`, link-count-one regular file on local APFS, file-syncs and directory-syncs it, and same-descriptor reopens exact bytes before publishing the pending state that selects its digest. Re-emission reopens both that exact authenticated secret and the staged config through retained directories, verifies operation/generation/intent/config/token-fingerprint/nonce-digest/expiry equality, and constructs the frame only from those two same-descriptor objects. The secret never enters the input manifest, authority/history receipt, status, human/JSON output, diagnostics, or logs.

Every emission-capable invocation returns the closed safe projection `LocalTokenHandoffOutputV1={schema_version:1,requirement:"inapplicable|not_requested|required",attempt:"not_reached|complete|failed",handoff_emitted:boolean,frame_size_bytes:null|integer,failure_class:null|"sink_invalid"|"sink_nonempty"|"write_incomplete"|"peer_closed"|"deadline"|"sync_failed"|"verification_failed"}`. The emission-capable set is exact: initialise/import/adopt/migrate `prepare`, the four explicit `handoff` leaves, and `recovery initialise resume`; no activate, abort, finalise, status, authority-inspection, quarantine-reset, or transition-recovery leaf may contain a `handoff_output` member, and present-null is invalid rather than equivalent to omission. `inapplicable` is used only by adopt/migrate prepare when secure comparison proves no cutover is needed; `not_requested` is used only by `recovery initialise resume` without its optional FD; both require `not_reached`, false, and null size/failure. `required/not_reached` means another typed pre-emission failure and likewise has false/null/null. `required/complete` requires true, exact frame size `1...1024`, and null failure; `required/failed` requires false, the exact complete frame size, and one failure literal. The object never contains FD number, sink type/path/identity, token, nonce, or frame bytes. Its `handoff_emitted` member is the sole human/JSON completion boolean for those emission-capable invocations.

`LocalTokenCutoverStore` owns `local-token-cutover/anchor`, content-addressed `objects/`, and operation/generation-keyed `secrets/`, and is subordinate to exactly one enclosing selection. Anchor is MACed `{schema_version,operation_id,intent_digest,cutover_generation,parent_selection_kind:"authority_transition|fresh_initialisation",parent_selection_digest,current_state_object_digest,handoff_secret_object_digest,state_sequence,mac}`; ordinary prepare uses generation zero. For `authority_transition`, the selection digest is the canonical `active_operation_ref` digest and the existing authority journal plus coordinator select the inert object. For `fresh_initialisation`, prepare may publish the inert intent/state/secret objects in the staged root, but selection is forbidden until the parent initialisation anchor has committed `floor_committed` and the first inhibited authority selects the matching `active_initialisation_ref`; the canonical digest of that reference is the anchor's parent selection. Every later anchor advance revalidates the unchanged parent operation ID, handoff-secret digest, and discriminated reference. The cutover never creates or clears a coordinator slot or either authority active reference. Store retains active intent/state chain, selected handoff secret, client-registry snapshot, at most one live challenge-digest object and one signed-ack object per each of 16 clients, two terminal chains for idempotence, and at most one retired-secret crash predecessor during rekey. Each object is ≤64 KiB; the complete store cap is 130 regular files/16 MiB including two temporaries and the complete maximum active rekey subcycle. Prepare reserves the complete maximum registry/challenge/ack/state-chain/secret/rekey budget before generating token or nonce. Challenge issue and acknowledgement consumption publish immutable objects and advance the anchored state under the same parent selection; only the challenge digest, never the raw challenge nonce, is persisted. Recovery accepts exactly one successor named by matching initialisation-or-journal/authority/anchor/secret references, never reconstructs token or handoff nonce from fingerprints/digests, and exposes status/abort/re-emission/rekey only according to current state. Pending and acknowledged states pin the selected secret. Activated, aborted, or non-rekeyable expired state forbids emission and retains the secret until its terminal state, config disposition, parent history/recovery checkpoint, and every reference are durable; GC then unlinks only its exact operation/generation basename and syncs `secrets/`. An unselected secret is inert and collectible only after proving no intent, state, anchor, staged config, journal, initialisation, authority, history, or recovery reference can name it. Authority/history checkpoint pins the terminal chain until config/reference GC; deletion sync follows pin removal. Crash/capacity/expiry tests cover every object/secret/anchor/authority/initialisation/coordinator/challenge/ack/rekey ordering and exact/+1 clients, files, and bytes.

An expired selected fresh-primary cutover has one closed recovery path, `FreshInitialisationRekeyV1`, invoked only by the owning `authority initialise handoff --operation-id ... --local-token-handoff-fd ...` while the same `active_initialisation_ref` and inhibited boot-verified supervisor remain selected. The first `boot_verified` object is the operation's immutable `rekey_base_phase_object_digest`; no later checkpoint, challenge, or acknowledgement object may become that base. Rekey increments both `cutover_generation` and `rekey_epoch` from zero without wrap, generates a new 32-byte target token and independent handoff nonce, re-enumerates the unchanged client registry, and publishes inert replacement config, provenance, cutover intent, handoff-secret, and pending-state objects before `token_rekey_prepared`. That phase is closed and binds `{rekey_epoch,rekey_generation,retired_cutover_intent_digest,retired_state_object_digest,retired_handoff_secret_object_digest,replacement_config_object_digest,replacement_cutover_intent_digest,replacement_handoff_secret_object_digest,replacement_pending_state_object_digest,replacement_target_token_fingerprint,replacement_handoff_nonce_digest,rekey_base_phase_object_digest,prior_rekey_checkpoint_object_digest,prior_rekey_accumulator_digest}`. Both secret digests equal their corresponding authenticated state/anchor and replacement publication; `prior_rekey_checkpoint_object_digest` and `prior_rekey_accumulator_digest` are both null at epoch one and thereafter name the immediately prior checkpoint and its accumulator. The next inhibited authority CAS preserves the byte-identical initialisation reference, floor, manager, artifacts, listener, and boot identity while atomically selecting only the replacement config/cutover fingerprints and deny set; `token_rekey_authority_committed` records its generation and object digest.

Recovery may then select the already named replacement cutover anchor. `token_rekey_checkpointed` is the sole compacting phase edge and adds `{compacted_from_phase_object_digest,compacted_tail_digest,rekey_accumulator_digest}`. `compacted_from_phase_object_digest` equals the immediately selected `token_rekey_authority_committed` object. Starting at that object, verifier follows ordinary `previous_phase_object_digest` links backwards until it reaches the fixed base at epoch one or the immediately prior checkpoint named by `prior_rekey_checkpoint_object_digest` thereafter; the tail must be acyclic, contain only legal selected phase successors, and end at exactly that boundary. Let `L` be the ordered oldest-to-newest digest list for that verified tail; it therefore covers any intervening prior checkpoint, challenge, acknowledgement, prepared, and authority-committed objects without a cardinality assumption. Let `Q=uint32be(count(L)) || each hexdecode(digest)[32]`, and define `compacted_tail_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/initialise-rekey-compacted-tail/v1\0") || uint32be(len(Q)) || Q))`. Let `K_initialise_rekey=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=initialise.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/initialise-rekey-accumulator/v1"),L=32)`, let `C=CanonicalJSONV1({operation_id,initialisation_intent_digest,rekey_base_phase_object_digest,rekey_epoch,prior_rekey_accumulator_digest,compacted_tail_digest,retired_cutover_intent_digest,retired_state_object_digest,retired_handoff_secret_object_digest,replacement_config_object_digest,replacement_cutover_intent_digest,replacement_handoff_secret_object_digest,replacement_pending_state_object_digest})`, and define `rekey_accumulator_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_initialise_rekey,ASCII("cq/initialise-rekey-accumulator-step/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`; epoch one uses canonical null for the prior checkpoint and accumulator. The checkpoint's `sequence` is exactly the immediately selected authority-committed sequence plus one, but its `previous_phase_object_digest` is the fixed base. This non-chain edge is legal only when the current anchor still selects `compacted_from_phase_object_digest`, the complete derived tail/digest and prior accumulator verify, and the epoch/sequence relations hold; the anchor CAS is its linearisation point. This special validation rule replaces ordinary anchor-chain traversal only for a checkpoint: verifier authenticates the fixed base, current checkpoint, its compacted accumulator, and any retained crash predecessor, and never requires GCed tail objects. Every other phase edge retains ordinary immediate-predecessor chaining.

Before that authority CAS, replacement objects are inert; after it, the exact named cutover-anchor and checkpoint successors are the only legal recovery and no action is replayed. After the checkpoint anchor and directory sync, authority/cutover agreement, and proof that the old config has no authority/reference, descriptor-relative GC removes and syncs every verified tail object except the fixed base and current checkpoint, plus retired raw-token config, retired handoff secret, challenge/ack, cutover, and intermediate rekey objects; it retains the current cutover and at most one crash predecessor. Thus arbitrarily repeated expiry has constant active-store occupancy and never consumes the 64-object initialisation reserve. Missing FD leaves the prepared successor resumable without emission; FD failure never rolls back selection and exact unexpired re-entry reopens the same selected secret and config and re-emits the committed replacement. Rekey never changes operation ID, initialisation intent, floor, manager attempt, boot proof, bootstrap identity, or target artifacts and never admits the data plane.

Registered token clients acknowledge through owner-only control before token activation. After peer-UID verification, the supervisor additionally proves the live peer PID/start token and executable digest match exactly one prepared registry member, then issues one OS-CSPRNG 32-byte, single-use `LocalTokenClientChallengeV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,client_registry_revision,client_identity_digest,challenge_nonce,target_config_binding_digest,target_token_fingerprint,handoff_nonce_digest,issued_at,expires_at}` with `expires_at` exactly five minutes after `issued_at`. Fresh initialisation may issue no challenge until `manager_action_committed` and `boot_verified` or `token_rekey_checkpointed` proves the exact inhibited supervisor is serving owner control; it then commits `token_challenges_committed`, the complete valid ack set, `clients_acknowledged`, and only then `token_activated`. Only the challenge digest is retained. `LocalTokenClientAckV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,client_registry_revision,client_identity_digest,attestation_key_id,challenge_digest,target_config_binding_digest,target_token_fingerprint,handoff_nonce_digest,acked_at,signature}` is Ed25519-signed over domain-separated length-prefixed `CanonicalJSONV1` with `signature` omitted by the exact client-specific registry key. Before token activation, an expired challenge has one write-ahead `challenge_superseded` successor naming the old digest and a fresh challenge for the same client/config/token/registry; selecting it clears that client's stale acknowledgement, and reference-aware GC retains only the live challenge, its live acknowledgement, and one crash predecessor. Token activation atomically consumes each challenge, requires issue/ack/activation inside its validity interval, and rejects reused, cross-operation, cross-client, cross-config, cross-token, stale-registry, or duplicate acknowledgement. Public admission stays inhibited until the later marker, policy-acknowledgement, and active-authority commits.

Possession of the shared target token or handoff nonce is never client-identity authentication and derives no acknowledgement key. One client cannot acknowledge another, and owner/operator confirmation never substitutes for a missing client signature. The ack set must contain exactly one valid consumed challenge for every member of the prepared and freshly re-enumerated client set; an authoritatively empty set alone needs none. `activate` is later invocation and requires exact unexpired pending object, complete ack set, conditional `--confirm-local-token-clients-updated`, fresh client-stop proof, and zero bearer senders. While the cutover remains unexpired it may issue the exact challenge-supersession successor instead of failing solely because a five-minute challenge expired; an expired cutover itself requires fresh prepare when abort remains legal or the fresh-primary rekey path above after handoff. It atomically selects generated token and accepts only it; no dual-token grace exists. Corpus covers authoritative empty versus unavailable enumeration, unmatched senders, registry/source/executable drift, cross-client forgery, shared-token forgery, challenge replay, expiry, and crash before/after challenge supersession or consumption.

Before activation, abort leaves prior service/token effective and removes staged reference after synced terminal receipt; fresh initialisation instead has no prior token and abort is no longer legal once its floor/authority handoff begins. At exact expiry, supervisor/controller atomically exposes `expired`; the prior token remains sole authority for an existing service, while fresh initialisation remains non-serving under its active initialisation reference. Existing-authority activation/re-emission refuses and permits only owning status/abort; fresh primary permits only owning status or the rekey handoff above until a replacement pending cutover is selected. Retry requires new prepare/new token whenever abort remains legal and a new rekey generation otherwise. Crash before prepare commit leaves no cutover; after commit recovery resumes exact object; after selection but before acknowledgement remains pending and never selects the token; after `token_activated` recovery observes the exact selected state and never reselects. Pre-floor restoration may restore exact legacy service/token only while clients remain stopped and reports required client token generation before resume. After floor advance no current/rollback config accepts legacy token. Weak/noncanonical/zero/repeated/source-unbound/forged provenance refuses. Rotation never prints token; doctor reports provenance enum only.

Authority commits `local_token_deny_set_digest` plus domain-separated HMAC fingerprints for every current, active-transition, and rollback-referenced config. Selection, restoration, reference change, and GC update set in same authority generation. Supervisor receives fingerprints only and compares rescue bearer against exactly three padded slots in constant work; any match returns `401 rescue_local_token_refused`. Missing classification blocks rescue unless unclassified-bearer acknowledgement binds exact reference-set digest; membership change expires it. Normal local-token auth uses failed-auth throttling below.

V1 non-data-plane maxima, lowerable but not widenable: external client executable 1 GiB; CQ executable payload 268,435,456 bytes; artifact payload store nine slots/2,415,919,104 bytes and manifest store nine slots/589,824 bytes, for 2,416,508,928 bytes combined including staging/temp/orphans after mandatory reconciliation; one external `ReleaseBundleV1` 1 GiB/17 descendants/depth two; release set/report store eight sets plus 40 build/CU-report/ancestry objects and four temporaries/64 MiB; release provenance store eight build authorities plus eight signed bundle objects plus eight floor-acceptance receipts plus eight inner signed floor-validation receipts plus eight outer MACed release-promotion receipts and four temporaries, with maxima of 44 regular files and 3 MiB, each provenance object at most 64 KiB; primary staged-release selector side eight files/1 MiB and operation side 23 files/4 MiB, each object at most 64 KiB; each scope-local runtime-policy-ack selection current plus one temporary/two files/131,072 bytes, each file at most 65,536 bytes; primary base runtime-evidence store 100 files/4,587,520 bytes, candidate base runtime-evidence store 53 files/3,473,408 bytes, and 153 files/8,060,928 bytes combined; candidate historical installed-marker store exactly 360 objects plus four temporaries/364 files/5,963,776 bytes under 6 MiB, primary historical installed-marker store exactly 720 objects plus four temporaries/724 files/11,862,016 bytes under 12 MiB, and 1,088 files/17,825,792 bytes across both scopes, each marker at most 16,384 bytes; candidate stage-source store exactly 16 receipts, 16 selectors, four receipt temporaries, and four selector temporaries/40 files/1,392,640 bytes under 2 MiB, primary stage-source store exactly 32 receipts, 32 selectors, four receipt temporaries, and four selector temporaries/72 files/2,506,752 bytes under 3 MiB, and 112 files/3,899,392 bytes across both scopes, with 65,536-byte receipts and 4,096-byte selectors; local-token client registry exactly three adapter results/16 clients/64 KiB and cutover store 130 regular files/16 MiB including secrets and temporaries; parent quarantine four live trees/1-GiB tree bytes/32,768 entries/34-MiB canonical manifests/36-MiB metadata; candidate controller parent selector exactly 51 leaves/4,194,304 bytes plus the independent external-reference stable three-run base exactly 90 leaves/2,949,120 bytes and mandatory retirement-coexistence reserve exactly 121 leaves/4,980,736 bytes, with exact capacity succeeding and a 122nd leaf or aggregate byte `+1` refusing before candidate selection or reference deletion, and one controller process at its sealed 1,260s/180s CPU/512-MiB resident/258-FD/128-socket/32-KiB-output envelope, including 64 prepared-manifest and exactly two late release-input FD slots; recognised legacy source 64 MiB each, 18 sources, 512 MiB aggregate including workspace; legacy-sensitive diagnostics one 64-MiB source object per kind and two final plus two temporary/orphan objects/256 MiB aggregate; registered external authority JSON uses its exact row limit, never a catch-all, with 8 MiB maximum; candidate validation-run wall 960s partitioned into at most 510s pre-release, an untouched 420s release-validation reserve, and an untouched 30s terminal stop/reap reserve; candidate runtime CPU 300s/resident 2 GiB/576 FDs/one live process per launcher-supervisor-worker role and three total/16 births/16 execs/64 live sockets/256 connections/64-KiB output/16-MiB file/256-MiB incremental mutable root; installed validation 90s, one client process, zero descendants, 4 KiB combined output, 64 entries, 8 MiB/file, 64 MiB root; each build report, CU report set, rollback/candidate/primary promotion receipt, and import-finalisation receipt 64 KiB, with candidate receipt export's trailing LF included in that 64-KiB file cap and every other receipt using its named exact cap; one active candidate-confinement run and two retained runs within the exact 144 MiB/150,994,944-byte candidate-validation-state cap; sensitive-retention index nine entries/64 KiB across the closed payload and legacy namespaces; refresh store 10,000 receipts/128 MiB per owner; service/routing logs five 10-MiB files each and 100 MiB combined. Every irreversible operation reserves current plus maximum temporary space. Exact aggregate or per-object cap succeeds when every other limit remains satisfied; first exceeded limit fails pre-mutation with `resource_capacity_exhausted`. Referenced/unresolved dependencies pin storage and block new work rather than being deleted. Candidate-runtime, controller-runtime, or installed-child breach kills/reaps its complete controller-owned group and invalidates the receipt set.

Within that candidate-validation state, the receipt-export store has the independent exact maximum of eleven regular files/1 MiB: one anchor, one six-object active chain, two parent-MACed compact `published|conflicted` result files, and two publication temporaries, with every object at most 64 KiB.

Continuity V4 preserves current 16-MiB exact canonical serialised journal ceiling and reserves another 16 MiB for temporary publication. Hard cardinality maxima are 10,000 lane records, 20,000 lease records, and 40,000 bounded attempt/history records, each also subject to byte ceiling; one authenticated caller subject may create at most 1,024 new lane identities in rolling hour and 10,000 retained total. Migration retains at most eight raw archives/128 MiB including temporary. Writer canonicalises to counting sink before `DispatchAdmitted`; growth beyond any cap returns stable `resource_capacity_exhausted` before send while existing pinned/active continuity remains usable and compactable. Compaction removes only terminal unpinned history under exact retention rules. Restart reads same 16-MiB ceiling. Tests cover exact/+1 bytes and counts, unique-session flood, active-pinned saturation, compaction, restart, archive cap, and ENOSPC.

Continuity remains separate append journal because request admission must commit per-turn state. New journal schema v4 embeds `(authority_generation, routing_generation, lane_digest, caller_request_authority, resolver_result_core, provider_branch_authority_with_consumption, binding_digest, pool_digest, member_digest, evidence_scope_digest, membership_valid_until, account_key_hmac, credential_revision, refresh_transition)` inside same signed lease record as turn state. CU-7 performs quiesced migration before activating `session_pools_v1`; active legacy records follow exact migration table below. After activation, any v1-v3 current record is incompatible and fails closed. No policy sidecar or cross-file lease commit exists.

Provider connection selection becomes authority only through one post-consumption journal record. Closed signed `CandidateProviderConnectionRealisationV1={schema_version:1,kind:"candidate_provider_connection_realisation_v1",validation_run_id,candidate_proxy_instance_id,journal_record_sequence,request_ordinal,candidate_request_id,issued_record_digest,consumption_receipt_digest,candidate_provider_request_capability_digest,candidate_provider_broker_routing_authority_digest,candidate_provider_broker_routing_authority_object_identity_digest,candidate_provider_broker_dispatch_tuple_digest,candidate_synthetic_route_budget_capability_issue_nonce,candidate_synthetic_route_budget_consumption_digest,candidate_synthetic_route_budget_head_digest,attempt_digest,phase_event_digest,transport:"http"|"websocket",planned_provider_connection_identity_digest,actual_provider_connection_identity_digest,connection_generation,provider_connection_open_ordinal,realised_tick_ns,realised_at,nonce,signature}` has no other member and is at most 4,096 bytes including its four-byte journal prefix. It exists exactly once when a consumed base `broker_request` creates an actual provider connection, never for a pre-connect failure or `websocket_application_send`; it follows that request's consumption and precedes every provider read, scanner decision, downstream delivery result, or terminal that names the actual identity. Planned identity byte-matches issued/consumption authority; actual identity, positive generation, and global contiguous provider-open ordinal come only from counted successful connection. For signature-omitted bytes `R0`, signature uses `cq/candidate-provider-connection-realisation-signature/v1\0`; complete canonical bytes use framed domain `cq/candidate-provider-connection-realisation/v1\0`, producing `candidate_provider_connection_realisation_digest`. Every later actual-connection fact for that request, including WebSocket parent/send authority, scan evidence, delivery binding/result, terminal, socket count, and generated-control observation, must join the unique same-run/request realisation and byte-match its digest, identity, and generation; missing, duplicate, later, cross-request, or substituted record invalidates the run. The journal record-kind union includes `connection_realisation` between `consumption` and any scan, delivery, or terminal row and exposes `candidate_provider_connection_realisation_digest`; it follows the existing canonical framing, signature, complete-record digest, sequence, tail-reopen, and no-repair rules. Close and seal independently fold ordinal rows `{request_ordinal,candidate_provider_connection_realisation_digest,actual_provider_connection_identity_digest,connection_generation,provider_connection_open_ordinal}` into `candidate_provider_connection_realisation_set_digest`, require `connection_realisation_count<=consumed_count<=256`, and require count to equal `provider_connection_open_count`; signed raw checkpoint/journal digests bind that fold transitively through accounting, floor, confinement, export/import, promotion, finalisation, and recovery.

### Non-proxy auxiliary command authority

The retained non-proxy command surface is closed rather than an unmodelled bypass. In the ten Kong-dispatched ordinary effect forms plus the help and version forms at the start of the grammar below, `G*` denotes a duplicate-preserving sequence of zero or more root Boolean-flag occurrences from `--json|-j|--refresh|-r` using the pinned Kong Boolean-token grammar. `RefreshCredentialMutationSourceActionMapEntryV1={schema_version:1,source_row_ref_digest,catalogue_row_ordinal,entrypoint_id,entrypoint_symbol,implementation_symbol,call_chain_digest,source_id,writer_kind:"atomic_file|file_delete|native_keychain_upsert|native_keychain_delete",legacy_operation_shape:null|"file_unlink|descriptor_unlink|platform_update_or_add|cq_set_delete_retry_set|platform_repeated_service_delete|cq_manifest_selector_delete",provider:"claude|codex",source_kind:"anonymous_sync|automatic_claude_persistence|cq_store_persistence|codex_refresh_persistence|oauth_reauth",action_kind:"replace|file_delete|native_keychain_upsert|native_keychain_delete|cache_generation_invalidate",target_selector_kind:"replace_file|delete_file|native_upsert|native_delete|cache_generation",target_semantics_rule:"atomic_replace_from_catalogue_grammars_v1|file_delete_from_catalogue_grammar_v1|quota_cache_generation_from_callsite_v1|claude_platform_update_or_add_v1|claude_cq_set_delete_retry_set_v1|claude_platform_repeated_delete_v1|claude_cq_manifest_selector_delete_v1"}` is closed.
