The mapping relation is one-to-one and source-derived, not an enum-name equality. It contains exactly one entry for every current baseline writer/callsite reachable from structured refresh and no entry for an unrelated writer. `atomic_file` with null legacy shape maps only to `replace|replace_file|atomic_replace_from_catalogue_grammars_v1`; ordinary destructive `file_delete` with `file_unlink|descriptor_unlink` maps only to `file_delete|delete_file|file_delete_from_catalogue_grammar_v1`; the exact Claude/Codex cache-invalidation callsite rows that are refresh-reachable map instead to `cache_generation_invalidate|cache_generation|quota_cache_generation_from_callsite_v1` and derive provider plus expected/next generation from the selected owner cache record, never from a legacy unlink target. Ordinary-only invalidation rows remain in the signed writer catalogue but are absent from the refresh source-action map. The two native upsert shapes map only to their matching `native_keychain_upsert|native_upsert` platform/CQ rule, and the two native delete shapes map only to their matching `native_keychain_delete|native_delete` platform/CQ rule. Each rule deterministically projects the retained parent/final grammar or exact native namespace/selector source, provider, expected-before identities/content commitments, failure policy, and generation fields into both the phase-`intent` action and `RefreshCredentialMutationTargetSelectorV1`; recomputing either projection must yield the reservation's action and selector digests. A missing, extra, multiply mapped, wrong-source-kind, wrong-provider, unsupported writer kind/shape, ordinary-delete/cache substitution, grammar/namespace/policy drift, or map/catalogue/signature/source-commit mismatch rejects before lease selection or plan publication.

`RefreshCredentialMutationSlotV1={planned_slot_ordinal,source_action_map_entry_digest,oauth_entry_ordinal:null|integer}` and `RefreshCredentialMutationPlanV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,source_action_map_digest,slots:[RefreshCredentialMutationSlotV1],slot_count,max_actual_mutations:256,plan_digest}` are closed. The plan embeds no catalogue row, source-row reference, or complete source-action-map entry. Verification reopens the signed source-action map by `source_action_map_digest`, resolves exactly one complete entry by each slot digest, then reopens that entry's exact signed catalogue row by `source_row_ref_digest`; the row and entry byte-match on catalogue ordinal, row/callsite tuple, source kind, provider, writer kind, action kind, selector kind, and target-semantics rule. All detailed reservation fields derive from those reopened objects. Slots are duplicate-free in exact baseline effect order, `planned_slot_ordinal` is contiguous from one, `slot_count=len(slots)<=256`, the complete canonical plan is at most 96 KiB, and `plan_digest` is framed SHA-256 of the complete canonical object with that member omitted under `cq/operator-control/refresh-credential-mutation-plan/v1\0`. Each slot represents one possible selected `CredentialOwnerCommitV1` action, not one account or API call: the conservative plan enumerates every mapped signed writer row reachable from anonymous synchronisation, each automatic Claude persistence and nested/direct CQ-store call, every Codex refresh persistence branch, both provider cache invalidations, and every proceeded OAuth reauth. Branch alternatives receive distinct slots. OAuth entry ordinal is non-null exactly when the reopened map entry has `source_kind="oauth_reauth"`; all other slots require null. An actual mutation selects exactly one previously unused slot before its credential-owner reservation; actual order is a strictly increasing subsequence of planned slots and no unplanned or unmapped writer row may reserve or act.

`RefreshCredentialMutationTargetSelectorV1` is the closed tagged union `replace_file={kind:"replace_file",retained_parent_identity_digest,final_basename,expected_final_state,expected_final_identity_digest:null|string,expected_final_content_digest:null|string}`; `delete_file={kind:"delete_file",retained_parent_identity_digest,final_basename,expected_final_identity_digest,expected_final_content_digest}`; `native_upsert={kind:"native_upsert",adapter_id,namespace,operation_shape,selector_source,service_row,account_name_keyed_digest,selector_provenance_bundle_digest}`; `native_delete={kind:"native_delete",adapter_id,namespace,operation_shape,service_row,account_name_keyed_digest,selector_keyed_digest,expected_persistent_ref_keyed_digest:null|string}`; or `cache_generation={kind:"cache_generation",provider,expected_cache_generation,expected_cache_object_digest:null|string,next_cache_generation}`. Every member is the exact action-specific target/selector projection of one complete `CredentialOwnerMutationV1` at `phase="intent"`; cross-kind, omitted, extra, plaintext, or later-attempt fields reject. For canonical selector bytes `T`, `credential_mutation_target_selector_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-mutation-target-selector/v1\0") || uint32be(len(T)) || T))`. For complete canonical intent-action bytes `A`, `credential_mutation_intent_action_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-mutation-intent-action/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`.

`RefreshCredentialMutationReservationCoreV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,refresh_credential_mutation_plan_digest,refresh_capacity_lease_object_digest,credential_child_id,credential_child_ordinal,planned_slot_ordinal,credential_commit_id,provider,source_kind,source_row_ref:RefreshCredentialMutationSourceRowRefV1,source_row_ref_digest,source_action_map_entry_digest,writer_reachability_entry_digest,action_kind,target_selector:RefreshCredentialMutationTargetSelectorV1,credential_mutation_target_selector_digest,credential_mutation_intent_action_digest,oauth_child_id:null|string,oauth_child_ordinal:null|integer,oauth_child_object_digest:null|string}` is closed. It byte-matches one unused plan slot, its exact signed one-to-one map entry, the currently selected capacity-lease chain, the next contiguous actual ordinal, a fresh 32-lower-hex child ID and commit ID, the complete map-derived intent action and selector projection, and the matching reopened and outer-head-selected OAuth `exchange_consumed` object only for `oauth_reauth`; all OAuth fields are otherwise null. For canonical bytes `B`, `refresh_credential_mutation_reservation_core_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-mutation-reservation-core/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))`. This core and digest are embedded in every child phase and outer head and remain immutable.

`RefreshCredentialMutationChildV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,reservation_core:RefreshCredentialMutationReservationCoreV1,reservation_core_digest,phase:"mutation_reserved|credential_parent_terminal|credential_receipt_bound|terminal",terminal_disposition:null|"committed"|"abandoned_pre_effect",refresh_capacity_lease_consumption_digest:null|string,credential_terminal_object_digest:null|string,credential_owner_receipt_digest:null|string,parent_completion_digest:null|string,credential_owner_absence_proof:null|CredentialOwnerReservationAbsenceProofV1,credential_owner_absence_proof_digest:null|string,sequence,previous_object_digest,mac}` is closed, at most 65,536 bytes, and bound to one selected plan slot. For `J0=CanonicalJSONV1(child with mac omitted)`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_operator_operation,ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-mutation-child/mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(J0)) || J0))`; for complete canonical bytes `J`, `refresh_credential_mutation_child_object_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-mutation-child/v1\0") || uint32be(len(J)) || J))`. Publication uses the operator store's sole mutation-child random-exclusive temporary, file sync, content-addressed no-replace rename, directory sync, and same-descriptor byte/MAC/digest reopen before either child or outer successor is usable. The child repeats no independently mutable identity field: operation, plan, lease, child/actual/planned ordinals, commit ID, provider, source kind/row/map, signed writer row, action/selector, and OAuth relation are read only from the embedded core and recomputed digest. Credential child IDs are distinct 32-lower-hex values and actual ordinals are contiguous `1...N`, `N<=256`; planned ordinals strictly increase but may have gaps for unrealised conservative branches. `mutation_reserved` is sequence zero with null predecessor, disposition, lease-consumption, terminal, receipt, completion, and absence fields. `credential_parent_terminal` is its immediate successor, requires the exact selected lease-consumption successor plus credential terminal and reservation-bound owner commit, and keeps receipt/completion/absence/disposition null. `credential_receipt_bound` adds the reopened receipt and parent-completion digests and keeps absence/disposition null. Committed `terminal` preserves the lease-consumption and all three credential digests, requires `terminal_disposition="committed"`, and keeps both absence fields null. Abandoned `terminal` is an immediate successor of `mutation_reserved`, requires `terminal_disposition="abandoned_pre_effect"`, the exact selected lease-consumption digest, every credential digest null, and the complete reopened `CredentialOwnerReservationAbsenceProofV1` whose recomputed digest equals the non-null digest member and whose reservation/lease/outer/lock/enumeration tuple byte-matches; it can never follow owner reservation.

`RefreshReauthPlanHeadV1={schema_version:1,plan_digest,entry_count,ordered_reauth_ref_commitment}` is the persistence-safe plan projection; it contains no label or account identity. `RefreshReauthDecisionHeadV1={schema_version:1,ordinal,reauth_ref,decision:"proceed|skip|input_eof",decision_digest}` is closed. `OperatorOAuthChildHeadV1={schema_version:1,oauth_child_id,ordinal,phase:"callback_prepared|code_transferred|exchange_consumed|credential_committed|terminal|result_bound",oauth_child_object_digest,control_oauth_child_result_digest:null|string}` and `RefreshCredentialMutationChildHeadV1={schema_version:1,credential_child_id,credential_child_ordinal,planned_slot_ordinal,phase:"mutation_reserved|credential_parent_terminal|credential_receipt_bound|terminal",child_object_digest}` are the sole compact outer-head projections. The closed `OperatorControlOperationV1` schema above therefore has additional members `refresh_capacity_lease_object_digest:null|string`, `refresh_credential_mutation_plan:null|RefreshCredentialMutationPlanV1`, `refresh_reauth_plan_head:null|RefreshReauthPlanHeadV1`, `refresh_reauth_decision_heads:[RefreshReauthDecisionHeadV1]`, `oauth_child_heads:[OperatorOAuthChildHeadV1]`, `refresh_credential_mutation_child_heads:[RefreshCredentialMutationChildHeadV1]`, and `refresh_capacity_lease_terminal_digest:null|string` immediately before `recovery_observation`. An outer head never repeats a provider, reauth reference, reservation core, source/map/writer/action/selector projection, terminal outcome, receipt, proof, or completion field. Those complete details remain only in the content-addressed object named by the head and are reopened and byte-/MAC-/digest-verified before the head or any successor is accepted.

Capacity, mutation plan, reauth-plan head, decision heads, mutation heads, and terminal lease digest are null/empty for non-refresh. `oauth_child_heads` is empty except that an ordinary login has exactly one ordinal-zero head and refresh has exactly one head per proceeded decision. For refresh, capacity-lease object publication and reopen precede the existing first plan successor; that one successor and one outer-anchor CAS simultaneously select its first non-null lease digest, the mandatory credential-mutation plan, and the reauth-plan head exactly when entry count is positive. Decision heads are ordinal-contiguous until all entries or the first `input_eof`, byte-match the selected safe plan commitment, and are selected before skip output or child creation. OAuth heads sort by proceeded plan ordinal, and mutation heads sort by contiguous actual mutation ordinal; only the greatest head in either independently ordered array may be nonterminal. An OAuth head through `terminal` requires null `control_oauth_child_result_digest`; `result_bound` preserves the already selected terminal OAuth-object digest and requires the recomputed non-null digest of the complete reopened `ControlOAuthChildResultV1` object. Every mutation or OAuth phase object is published/synced/reopened first, then one immediate outer-operation successor changes only its matching compact head and ordinary sequence/predecessor fields, and only the reopened outer-anchor CAS selects it. A result object is likewise published and reopened after its terminal OAuth object and before the `result_bound` successor. Every phase transition, decision, result binding, committed/abandoned mutation, and terminal lease release uses that object-first/outer-successor-second relation. A child/result object or outer successor without its required counterpart is inert; a foreign plan/ordinal/ID/row/map/action/selector/OAuth/lease binding, stale predecessor, skipped phase, later decision after `input_eof`, reverse terminal-to-result digest dependency, or owner reservation before selected outer CAS rejects with zero effect.

Structured-refresh capacity is one closed admission ledger. Operator-store occupancy reserves exactly `1,505` outer operation objects—`32` base/cancel/recovery/effect/result objects including the terminal-result and acknowledged-result heads, `1` shared plan/selected-lease successor, `64` decision-head successors, `64 * 6 = 384` OAuth-head successors including the acyclic `result_bound` successor, and `256 * 4 = 1,024` mutation-head successors—plus `256 * 4 = 1,024` mutation-child objects, `64 * 5 = 320` OAuth-control objects, 64 content-addressed OAuth-result objects, and eight infrastructure slots: one outer-object temporary, one mutation-child temporary, one OAuth-phase temporary, one OAuth-result temporary, anchor plus anchor temporary, and terminal receipt plus receipt temporary. Thus the operator-store subtotal is `1,505 + 1,024 + 320 + 64 + 8 = 2,921`. The expanded credential-store subtotal is the exact `573` files defined above. Wire admission reserves exactly ten outer frames (`ControlKeyInit`, `ControlKeyReady`, `ControlBegin`, `ControlAccepted`, `ControlArguments`, `ControlProceed`, one `ControlResult|ControlError`, optional `ControlResultAck`, at most one `ControlCancel`, and at most one `ControlRecover`), one `ControlRefreshReauthPlan`, 64 `ControlRefreshReauthDecision`, and `64 * 4 = 256` OAuth child frames consisting of key-init, key-ready, encrypted secret, and `ControlOAuthChildResult`; structured refresh permits exactly zero `ControlProgress`. The wire subtotal is `10 + 1 + 64 + 256 = 331`, and the complete object-or-frame reserve is exactly `2,921 + 573 + 331 = 3,825` units.

The category-byte formula is equally exact and conservative: `1,505 * 262,144 = 394,526,720` outer-object bytes; `1,024 * 65,536 = 67,108,864` mutation-child bytes; `320 * 65,536 = 20,971,520` OAuth-control bytes; `64 * 65,536 = 4,194,304` OAuth-result-object bytes; `2 * 4,096 + 2 * 262,144 + 262,144 + 3 * 65,536 = 991,232` operator anchor/receipt/temporary bytes; `12,656,640` expanded credential-store bytes; and `331 * 65,536 = 21,692,416` wire bytes. Total encoded reservation is exactly `522,141,696` bytes. Outer operation objects and terminal receipts are at most 262,144 bytes; mutation, OAuth-phase, and OAuth-result objects are at most 65,536; plans retain their 96-KiB/32-KiB bounds; operator anchors are at most 4,096; every wire frame is at most 65,536.

Refresh outer-object construction is independently and conservatively bounded before publication. Let `B_fixed` be the canonical-byte delta for the complete ordinary outer fields, all refresh member names/array delimiters, and empty/null refresh values; `B_plan`, `B_reauth`, `B_decision[i]`, `B_oauth[i]`, and `B_mutation[i]` are the exact canonical replacement/append deltas, including commas, for the compact plan, reauth-plan head, and each head entry. `B_lease_selected` and `B_lease_terminal` are the exact canonical replacement deltas when `refresh_capacity_lease_object_digest` and `refresh_capacity_lease_terminal_digest`, respectively, change from the four-byte literal `null` already charged to `B_fixed` to a quoted 64-lower-case-hex SHA-256 digest; each is exactly `2 + 64 - 4 = 62` bytes. Admission enforces `B_fixed<=32,768`, `B_plan<=98,304`, `B_reauth<=512`, `B_lease_selected<=62`, `B_lease_terminal<=62`, every `B_decision[i]<=256`, every compact `B_oauth[i]<=384`, and every compact `B_mutation[i]<=320`. The sum of those independently enforced schema-category encoded-byte limits is the conservative admission ceiling `32,768 + 98,304 + 512 + 62 + 62 + (64 * 256) + (64 * 384) + (256 * 320) = 254,588`, leaving 7,556 bytes beneath the immutable 262,144-byte storage cap. It is not an assertion that one closed canonical object can attain every category limit simultaneously: canonical JSON has no padding member, and the maximum legal constructed fixture uses maximum cardinalities and longest legal field values but need not reach this ceiling. The verifier measures deltas from byte-identical canonical encodings rather than summing field estimates, independently exercises every category limit and its `+1` refusal, and rejects any complete constructed or reopened `OperatorControlOperationV1` whose actual canonical encoding exceeds 262,144 bytes before object publication or acceptance.

Exact 256 mutations, 64 OAuth children/results, 64 decisions, 2,921 operator slots, 573 credential files, 331 frames, 3,825 total units, 522,141,696 reserved bytes, and both exact 62-byte lease-digest transition deltas succeed. Mutation/slot 257, OAuth child/result 65, decision 65, any `ControlProgress`, outer base object 33, OAuth-result object 65, any head/object/temp/receipt/proof/lease/frame category `+1`, a fixed/plan/reauth category delta of 32,769/98,305/513 bytes, a selected-/terminal-lease-digest transition delta of 63/63 bytes, a compact decision/OAuth/mutation delta of 257/385/321 bytes, an actual canonical outer-object encoding of 262,145 bytes, credential file 574, frame 332, operator slot 2,922, unit 3,826, any per-type storage byte `+1`, or aggregate reserved byte 522,141,697 refuses before lease/plan publication, `ControlAccepted` when the overage is already knowable, reserved-child selection, credential-owner reservation, or effect. The capacity-lease object is published, synced, and reopened separately, but no lease-only outer successor exists: the existing first plan successor changes `refresh_capacity_lease_object_digest` from null to that reopened lease digest while selecting the complete credential-mutation plan and, when nonempty, the reauth-plan head in the same object and one outer-anchor CAS. The independent first non-null `refresh_capacity_lease_terminal_digest` successor selects only the reopened terminal-release object after terminal release. A crash immediately before or after the shared plan/selected-lease outer-anchor CAS exposes either the unchanged null-plan/null-lease predecessor or that one exact reopened plan-and-lease-bound successor; a crash around the independent terminal-release CAS exposes its null-digest predecessor or exact digest-bound successor. Recovery resumes only the missing CAS without reconstructing, substituting, clearing, or republishing either digest or splitting the shared plan/lease transition. Skipped branches remain reserved until terminal lease release.

Every operation successor containing `recovery_observation` and every later successor or terminal receipt that preserves it also preserves the observation's complete `operator_control_recovery_request_digest` member byte-for-byte. That nested member is non-null exactly for `observation_kind="control_recover"` and null for `owner_restart|worker_restart|cancel_reconcile`; no top-level duplicate field may diverge or substitute for the nested authenticated value.

`OperatorControlRecoveryRequestV1={schema_version:1,kind:"operator_control_recovery_request_v1",operation_id,instance_id,selected_operation_object_digest,caller_control_capability_digest,action:"recover",clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",boot_session_id,started_tick_ns,forward_deadline_tick_ns,total_deadline_tick_ns,issued_at,valid_until,nonce,mac}` is the sole authenticated recovery request. After exact selector and active-chain authentication, an `operator_recover` invocation that requires `ControlRecover` constructs it from the unchanged `DispatchOperatorRecoveryCommandV1` context, with the selected object digest byte-matching that chain, `valid_until` only the wall correlation for the forward cutoff, and `nonce` a fresh 128-bit OS-CSPRNG value encoded as 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters; it MACs only with the `recovery-request` purpose key, and `ControlRecover` carries the complete object as its sole payload through the authenticated owner-control connection. Supervisor verifies the MAC, framed digest, caller/instance/operation/selected-object binding, selected authority generation, current request boot, non-regressed start tick, both exact dispatcher deadlines, and the current connection's independently authenticated runtime-instance/listener-generation tuple before recovery admission. The current `runtime_instance_id` may differ from the originating connection after supervisor/service restart and is copied into the recovery observation rather than compared with a nonexistent persisted originating-runtime field; listener generation still must satisfy the selected operation's mutation-key/journal relation and is copied into that observation as the current proof. Once admitted, the complete request's `operator_control_recovery_request_digest` is copied into the recovery evidence and independently MACed observation before any recovery successor can be selected. A retained receipt is projected directly without this request or another acknowledgement. `operator_status` never constructs this object, opens its key for creation, opens owner control, or sends any control frame.

`OperatorControlAcknowledgementContextV1={schema_version:1,source:"original_command"|"operation_recover",request_digest,clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",boot_session_id,forward_deadline_tick_ns,total_deadline_tick_ns}` is closed, and `request_digest` is exactly the 64-lower-hex framed digest for the selected source kind. For `original_command`, its digest and clock/boot/deadline tuple byte-match the complete authenticated `OperatorControlRequestV1` already bound to the same still-open owner-control connection. For `operation_recover`, they byte-match the complete authenticated `OperatorControlRecoveryRequestV1` on that same still-open connection, the selected terminal chain contains a `control_recover` observation whose non-null `operator_control_recovery_request_digest` equals that `request_digest`, and the terminal object is either the request's selected object or a legal same-chain successor of it. No digest from one source is legal under the other source tag.

Terminal receipt authority is closed and self-contained. After flushing the complete result, the owner CLI sends exactly `ControlResultAcknowledgedV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,selected_terminal_operation_object_digest,result_renderer:"human|json",acknowledgement_context:OperatorControlAcknowledgementContextV1,acknowledged_tick_ns,acknowledged_at}` through the source request's already authenticated owner-control connection. Supervisor accepts it only while the anchor still selects that exact terminal object, the operation/request/caller/connection binding agrees, the acknowledgement tick is on the context's exact clock and boot without regression, and `acknowledged_tick_ns < acknowledgement_context.total_deadline_tick_ns`; equality is expired. `original_command` additionally requires the tick to be at least the operation's `created_tick_ns` and every selected same-boot recovery observation, while `operation_recover` requires it to be at least the recovery request's `started_tick_ns` and every selected observation on that request boot. An original-command acknowledgement therefore uses only the original request's total deadline on its originating boot. A recovery acknowledgement uses only that fresh recovery request's fixed 30-second total deadline—even when the operation's originating deadline expired or its boot changed—and never reconstructs or extends the originating deadline; the recovery request itself must have been admitted before its own 15-second forward cutoff, while acknowledgement may use only its remaining 15-second reserve. `operator_status` never sends an acknowledgement, and no status render can select `acknowledged` or a receipt. The frame contains no result payload or new effect authority. Acceptance selects the one immediate `acknowledged` operation successor and begins receipt publication. A lost, duplicate, wrong-source, wrong-request, mismatched, pre-flush, regressed, cross-connection, or expired acknowledgement cannot select another successor or claim rendering.

`OperatorControlTerminalReceiptV1={schema_version:1,kind:"operator_control_terminal_receipt_v1",operation_id,receipt_generation,instance_id,operator_control_request_digest,selected_terminal_operation_object_digest,selected_acknowledged_operation_object_digest,caller_control_capability_digest,command_catalogue_id:"ordinary|models|refresh",command_row_id,key_exchange_digest,argument_keyed_digest,authority_generation,config_generation,credential_index_generation,cache_generation,clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",boot_session_id,forward_deadline_tick_ns,total_deadline_tick_ns,effect_committed:null|boolean,cancel_request_digest:null|string,cancel_cause:null|"sigint"|"sigterm"|"forward_deadline",terminal_outcome:"succeeded|failed|login_restart_required|indeterminate",terminal_code:null|"operator_operation_cancelled"|"operator_operation_failed"|"operator_login_restart_required",safe_result_digest:null|string,credential_owner_receipt_digests:[string],recovery_observation:null|OperatorControlRecoveryObservationV1,result_render_state:"acknowledged",result_renderer:"human|json",acknowledgement_context:OperatorControlAcknowledgementContextV1,acknowledged_tick_ns,acknowledged_at,published_at,nonce,mac}`. Operation ID and both selected-object digests are complete canonical values; `nonce` is a fresh 128-bit OS-CSPRNG value encoded as 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters; times use the common UTC format. It byte-matches the selected terminal and immediately following acknowledged operation objects for every operation/result field, and its renderer/acknowledgement fields, including the complete context, byte-match `ControlResultAcknowledgedV1`; the acknowledged object names the terminal object as its immediate predecessor. `credential_owner_receipt_digests` is a canonical lexically sorted duplicate-free array: zero or one complete receipt digest for an ordinary outer-result completion, zero through 256 for committed refresh mutation children, and empty exactly when the selected operation has no committed credential-owner child. An ordinary member reopens its live receipt and exact `operator_control_acknowledged` completion; a refresh member resolves from each committed terminal mutation-child head whose durable `credential_receipt_bound` predecessor proved that receipt and completion before collection. Every committed selected credential mutation child appears exactly once. An `abandoned_pre_effect` child contributes no receipt digest and instead must remain in the terminal outer head with its exact reservation and credential-owner absence-proof digests. Publication occurs only after every committed scope-exact parent binding is durable, every corresponding credential anchor is cleared, and every abandoned reservation's absence proof reopens. The live ordinary receipt remains pinned through publication; a bound refresh receipt is a non-resolving authenticated commitment and is not repinned by the outer receipt. `acknowledged_tick_ns` belongs to the acknowledgement context's named clock/boot, is strictly before its total deadline, and cannot regress relative to a selected recovery observation on that boot; wall times are audit correlations only. Determinate outcomes require the same non-null effect/result/code relations as the operation chain; `indeterminate` requires null effect, result digest, and terminal code. Cancellation and recovery-observation nullability must also equal the selected acknowledged object. `result_renderer` records the flushed renderer only and grants no replay authority.

The receipt schema additionally has `refresh_credential_mutation_plan_digest:null|string`, `refresh_reauth_plan_digest:null|string`, `refresh_reauth_decision_digests:[string]`, `oauth_child_terminal_object_digests:[string]`, `control_oauth_child_result_digests:[string]`, `credential_owner_absence_proof_digests:[string]`, and `refresh_capacity_lease_terminal_digest:null|string` immediately before `recovery_observation`. Refresh requires the mutation-plan and terminal-lease digests, the reauth-plan digest exactly when a nonempty plan head was selected, decision digests in ordinal order through EOF/all entries, OAuth terminal and result digests in proceeded-decision order, and absence-proof digests in abandoned-mutation ordinal order; every array is duplicate-free and at its 64/64/256 bound. Non-refresh requires every refresh member null/empty; an ordinary login alone has exactly one OAuth terminal-object digest and no child-result digest, while every other non-refresh row has both arrays empty. Receipt publication recursively reopens every selected plan/decision/OAuth/result/mutation/proof/lease head, every compact-head-named complete MACed child object, and every complete content-addressed OAuth-result object, recomputes each digest, and verifies the selected terminal lease consumed the exact terminal mutation set before acknowledgement. Omission, reordering, a digest-only OAuth/result/proof claim, stale plan/lease, a live child, or a released lease without its terminal outer binding rejects before receipt MAC or anchor clear.

A receipt carrying a `control_recover` observation requires the observation's non-null `operator_control_recovery_request_digest` to equal both the admitted recovery request and an `operation_recover` acknowledgement context's `request_digest`; a receipt carrying another observation kind requires that nested member null. Receipt publication re-verifies this nullability and equality through the selected terminal and acknowledged successors before computing the receipt MAC.

For a refresh outer receipt, `credential_owner_receipt_digests` is exactly the lexical duplicate-free projection of all non-null receipt digests in the terminal operation's 1...N `refresh_credential_mutation_child_heads`; each head must be `terminal`, and N is at most 256. Publication reopens the complete selected outer chain and every committed mutation-child reservation/parent-terminal/bound object, verifies each credential receipt, reservation, and parent-completion digest was equal when each successor was selected, and never requires a credential receipt already made collectable by that durable binding. It separately reopens every abandoned child's `mutation_reserved -> terminal` relation and exact no-owner absence proof. The outer receipt MAC converts the array into non-resolving audit commitments; it does not repin collected credential-store objects. For an ordinary outer-result completion, the sole live credential receipt is reopened and included before publication. Mixed provenance, an omitted committed child, a receipt for an abandoned child, more than 256 refresh-mutation digests, more than one ordinary digest, or more than 256 total digests rejects. This replaces the earlier generic statement that every array member remains live and pinned until outer-receipt GC.

Refresh recovery and observation are head-exact. `OperatorControlRecoveryEvidenceV1.oauth_journal_digest` is the framed digest of the complete selected reauth-plan/decision/OAuth/result-head projection and every reopened OAuth phase/result object; its credential journal projection also contains the selected capacity-lease, lease-consumption, mutation-plan/map, mutation-child, receipt, and complete absence-proof digests. Recovery may publish only the first missing child-object/outer-head, lease, credential, terminal-result, result-object/`result_bound`-head, or receipt suffix already authorised by those selected projections; it cannot reconstruct a label-bearing plan, decision, OAuth object, result object, absence proof, source-action map entry, or lease counter from current inventory. `operation status` performs the same MAC/digest/ordering/nullability/cap validation and exposes only safe plan/decision/OAuth/mutation counts, phases, terminal digests, and lease state—never labels, reauth refs, selectors, or credential facts—and remains non-creating. Until terminal receipt publication, every selected OAuth phase/result object, plan/decision/result head, complete abandoned proof, live capacity-lease chain, and terminal mutation child is pinned. Afterwards the receipt's non-resolving commitments permit directory-synced GC in dependency order `OAuth/mutation publication temporaries -> OAuth result objects -> OAuth phase objects -> absence proofs -> lease predecessors -> terminal lease object -> outer predecessors`; any active, pending, indeterminate, unacknowledged, or cross-referenced member remains pinned and blocks new admission.

The receipt uses only the purpose-specific receipt key: `K_operator_receipt=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=operator-control/key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/operator-control/receipt/key/v1"),L=32)`. For `R0=CanonicalJSONV1(receipt with mac omitted)`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_operator_receipt,ASCII("cq/operator-control/receipt/mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R0)) || R0))`; for complete MACed bytes `R`, `operator_control_terminal_receipt_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/receipt/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R)) || R))`. No request, operation, anchor, cancel, or recovery-observation key/domain may substitute. Under the retained `operator-control/receipts/` descriptor, the only final basename is `<operation_id>.json` and the only publication temporary is `.<operation_id>.receipt.tmp`; both are current-UID-owned `0600`, link-count-one regular files on the retained local-APFS store. While holding the operation-store exclusion, `receipt_generation` is zero when no valid receipt remains and otherwise exactly one greater than the greatest retained generation; it is an unsigned 64-bit non-wrapping integer, and exhaustion refuses the next operation before acceptance.

Publication order is exact. The supervisor same-descriptor reopens the anchor, selected terminal object, and its selected acknowledged successor; verifies their complete chain, result, acknowledgement, key, generation, deadline, and boot bindings; constructs one receipt; securely writes or resumes the exact temporary; file-syncs and same-descriptor verifies it; no-replace renames it to `<operation_id>.json`; directory-syncs `receipts/`; and reopens the final identity and byte-identical canonical receipt before clearing anything. It then reopens the anchor and clears it only if it still selects that acknowledged object, syncs the anchor directory, and only afterwards releases operation-object references. If the final basename already exists, only byte-identical bytes and identity-consistent same-operation adoption are legal; another object or a second receipt is `conflicted`. `operation status|recover --operation-id` opens the exact final basename without following links, verifies its receipt MAC/digest and all closed relations, and projects it directly after anchor retirement. During the narrow receipt-published/anchor-live interval, both must agree; status remains non-creating and recover may finish only that anchor-clear suffix. A receipt without its required publication proof, an anchor/receipt disagreement, duplicate generation, unsafe identity, malformed bytes, or an acknowledged chain without a receipt after bounded recovery is conflicted or indeterminate and never reconstructed from current command arguments.

Crash recovery is suffix-only: before acknowledged selection the terminal anchor remains authority; after acknowledged selection but before a valid temporary, recovery may construct the sole receipt from that exact selected chain; after any temporary byte exists it may adopt only the byte-identical valid temporary or remove that exact invalid partial temporary while the unchanged anchor proves no final receipt exists; after rename it reopens/syncs the final receipt; after final sync it clears only the agreeing anchor; and after anchor clear the receipt alone is terminal authority. No boundary repeats an effect, terminal reconciliation, result rendering, cancellation, or receipt generation. The archive retains at most sixteen receipts total: every referenced receipt is pinned, and remaining slots retain the newest unreferenced receipts ordered by `(receipt_generation,operation_id)`. Before accepting another operation, descriptor-relative GC removes and directory-syncs only the oldest unreferenced receipt until the sixteen-receipt cap has room, and refuses before acceptance if all sixteen are pinned. Active, unacknowledged, pending, indeterminate, credential/cache/projection/OAuth-journal-referenced, or recovery-referenced state is never collected. After receipt publication, anchor clear, and reference release, selected operation objects and safe carrier residue may be collected in dependency order; receipt removal is never evidence that the underlying effect may be repeated.

Recovery evidence and its clock observation are closed rather than prose-only. `OperatorControlRecoveryEvidenceV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,operator_control_request_digest,operator_control_recovery_request_digest:null|string,selected_operation_object_digest,worker_journal_digest:null|string,credential_journal_digest:null|string,cache_journal_digest:null|string,projection_journal_digest:null|string,oauth_journal_digest:null|string,zero_effect_absence_proof_digest:null|string}` contains only safe authenticated digests. A `reserved|accepted` zero-effect terminalisation requires every journal digest null and a non-null complete absence-proof digest; `proceeding|effect_committed` reconciliation requires every applicable journal digest and forbids an absence proof from substituting for an issued effect. For canonical evidence bytes `E`, `evidence_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/recovery-evidence/v1\0") || uint32be(len(E)) || E))`. `OperatorControlRecoveryObservationV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,operator_control_request_digest,operator_control_recovery_request_digest:null|string,observation_kind:"control_recover|owner_restart|worker_restart|cancel_reconcile",origin_clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",origin_boot_session_id,observed_clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",observed_boot_session_id,observed_runtime_instance_id,observed_listener_generation,observed_tick_ns,relation_to_origin:"same_boot|cross_boot",evidence_digest,mac}` is independently MACed by the `recovery-observation` rule above and embedded byte-for-byte in the successor. For `control_recover`, both recovery-request-digest members are non-null, equal each other, and equal the framed digest of the one complete MACed `OperatorControlRecoveryRequestV1` admitted on that connection; for `owner_restart|worker_restart|cancel_reconcile`, both are null. The observation byte-matches the operation/originating request and exact evidence, and its MAC covers the complete recovery-request digest and nullability; its runtime/listener fields byte-match the current authenticated supervisor control connection for `control_recover` and the equivalent retained current-runtime attestation for the other three observation kinds. Runtime identity is not compared with the originating runtime tuple; listener generation separately satisfies the selected operation's mutation-key/journal relation. `same_boot` requires equal boot IDs, while `cross_boot` requires different boot IDs. Every recovery-created successor carries exactly one such observation, and no ordinary forward successor may carry one.

Operator-control duration authority is monotonic and boot-scoped. `created_tick_ns`, both deadline ticks, `expires_tick_ns`, and every cancel/recovery observation are values from `mach_continuous_time_v1`; they are comparable only when `boot_session_id` and `clock_domain` byte-match and the observed tick has not regressed. `created_at`, `expires_at`, `issued_at`, and `valid_until` are display/audit correlations and never extend or reconstruct a monotonic deadline. On the originating boot, recovery requires `relation_to_origin="same_boot"`, rejects an observed tick below `created_tick_ns` or the most recent same-boot recovery observation, and treats a tick at or after the total deadline as expired before any new effect. Across a boot change, recovery requires `relation_to_origin="cross_boot"`; observations on the same new boot must not regress relative to the immediately preceding observation on that boot, but no originating deadline tick is reconstructed or compared across boots. `reserved|accepted` is definitely pre-`ControlProceed` and may be terminalised `failed` with zero effect after authenticating the chain and complete absence proof; `proceeding|effect_committed` may become terminal only from the exact durable worker, credential, cache, projection, or OAuth journal evidence, and absent or ambiguous evidence is `indeterminate`/4. Cross-boot recovery never reconstructs a remaining duration, opens a provider transport, restarts OAuth, or repeats an effect. Terminal/acknowledged receipts remain readable across boots because their outcome is already durable. Every recovery successor preserves the originating boot/deadline tuple byte-for-byte and embeds its independently authenticated current observation/evidence proof. That immutable operation tuple governs only originating work and original-command acknowledgement; an `operation_recover` acknowledgement is authorised solely by its distinct current-boot recovery-request tuple and mirrors that tuple without rewriting the originating fields.

`OAuthStateCommitmentV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,provider:"claude|codex",state_encoding:"base64url_no_padding",state_encoded_length:43,state_octet_length:32,state_value_keyed_digest}` is closed and contains no state bytes. `OAuthPKCECommitmentV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,provider:"claude|codex",verifier_encoding:"base64url_no_padding",verifier_encoded_length:43,verifier_octet_length:32,verifier_value_keyed_digest,challenge_method:"S256",challenge_encoding:"base64url_no_padding",challenge_encoded_length:43,challenge_b64url}` is closed and contains the public challenge but no verifier. `OAuthCallbackEndpointProjectionV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,provider:"claude|codex",callback_route_id:"claude_loopback_callback|codex_loopback_callback",bind_address:"127.0.0.1",bind_port,advertised_host:"localhost",accepted_method:"GET",redirect_uri_keyed_digest}` requires port `1...65535`, exact provider route/port rules, and contains no URI string. `OAuthAuthorizationURLProjectionV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,provider:"claude|codex",authorization_url_catalogue_digest,authorization_url_row_id:"claude_login_authorize|codex_login_authorize",callback_endpoint_projection_digest,state_commitment_digest,pkce_commitment_digest,rendered_url_keyed_digest}` is closed. `OAuthCallbackAcceptanceProjectionV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,provider:"claude|codex",authorization_url_projection_digest,callback_endpoint_projection_digest,state_commitment_digest,accepted_method:"GET",code_length,code_value_keyed_digest,canonical_query_keyed_digest,accepted_tick_ns}` requires code length `1...512`. `OperatorOAuthDecryptedSecretProjectionV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id:null|string,oauth_child_ordinal:null|integer,provider:"claude|codex",transient_secret_frame_digest,callback_acceptance_projection_digest,code_value_keyed_digest,verifier_value_keyed_digest,state_value_keyed_digest,redirect_uri_keyed_digest}` is recomputed only inside the decrypting worker. `OperatorOAuthExchangeProjectionV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,provider:"claude|codex",exchange_route_id:"claude_login_exchange|codex_login_exchange",method:"POST",credential_origin_route_id:"claude_authorization_code_v1|codex_authorization_code_v1",request_semantics_id:"claude_login_authorization_code_json_v1|codex_login_authorization_code_form_v1",callback_acceptance_projection_digest,decrypted_secret_projection_digest,request_body_keyed_digest,state_forwarding:"included|omitted"}` requires `included` only for Claude and `omitted` only for Codex. These seven complete projections contain only public protocol facts and keyed commitments; no code, verifier, state, redirect URI, raw URL, callback query, or exchange body is persisted.

Let `K_oauth_binding=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_commit,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/operator-oauth/binding/key/v1"),L=32)`. For exact bytes `B`, `OAuthBind(label,B)=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_oauth_binding,ASCII("cq/operator-oauth/" || label || "/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))`, where the closed labels are `state-value|verifier-value|redirect-uri|rendered-url|callback-code|callback-query|exchange-body`. The state and verifier inputs are their exact 43-byte canonical ASCII encodings after base64url decoding proves 32 bytes; `challenge_b64url` must equal the 43-byte unpadded base64url of `SHA256(ASCII(verifier))`. Rendered URL and exchange-body inputs are the exact catalogue-produced wire bytes. The callback-query input is instead exactly `Q=CanonicalJSONV1(OAuthAcceptedCallbackQueryV1)` produced by the closed callback parser above; raw request-target/query spelling never enters the bind. For complete `CanonicalJSONV1` bytes `J`, `OAuthProjectionDigest(label,J)=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-oauth/" || label || "/v1\0") || uint32be(len(J)) || J))`, with closed labels `state-commitment|pkce-commitment|callback-endpoint|authorization-url|callback-acceptance|decrypted-secret|exchange`. Each named `*_projection_digest` or `*_commitment_digest` is the matching formula over the complete embedded object. CLI computes `OAuthBind("callback-query",Q)` from its accepted callback and embeds byte-identical `OAuthAcceptedCallbackQueryV1` inside the one encrypted carrier. The worker parses that complete canonical nested object, independently enforces its closed field set, grammar, size, and outer `code|state` equality, reconstructs byte-identical `Q`, and recomputes the same bind before accepting `exchange_consumed`; a digest alone is never sufficient. CLI and worker independently recompute every other applicable `OAuthBind` while `K_oauth_binding` and plaintext are live; they zeroise that key, `Q`, the nested object, raw parser buffers, and duplicate outer secret fields with `K_commit`. Supervisor and recovery recompute every safe complete-object digest, MAC, phase/nullability relation, and cross-projection equality without reconstructing a secret. Deterministic CU/release fixtures additionally recompute both keyed and public formulas from fixed test keys and secret inputs. A digest-only projection, omitted complete object, wrong purpose label/key, unequal inner/outer digest, noncanonical nested query object, or query/outer-field mismatch is invalid.

`OperatorOAuthControlV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,parent_command_row_id:"ordinary_claude_login|ordinary_codex_login|refresh_refresh",oauth_child_id,ordinal,reauth_ref:null|string,provider:"claude|codex",authorization_url_catalogue_digest,oauth_state_commitment:OAuthStateCommitmentV1,oauth_state_commitment_digest,oauth_pkce_commitment:OAuthPKCECommitmentV1,oauth_pkce_commitment_digest,oauth_callback_endpoint_projection:OAuthCallbackEndpointProjectionV1,oauth_callback_endpoint_projection_digest,oauth_authorization_url_projection:OAuthAuthorizationURLProjectionV1,oauth_authorization_url_projection_digest,oauth_callback_acceptance_projection:null|OAuthCallbackAcceptanceProjectionV1,oauth_callback_acceptance_projection_digest:null|string,oauth_decrypted_secret_projection:null|OperatorOAuthDecryptedSecretProjectionV1,oauth_decrypted_secret_projection_digest:null|string,oauth_exchange_projection:null|OperatorOAuthExchangeProjectionV1,oauth_exchange_projection_digest:null|string,key_exchange_digest,transient_secret_frame_digest:null|string,exchange_route_id:"claude_login_exchange|codex_login_exchange",phase:"callback_prepared|code_transferred|exchange_consumed|credential_committed|terminal",sequence,previous_object_digest,terminal_result_digest:null|string,mac}` is the closed one-use OAuth child. Common state/PKCE/endpoint/authorisation objects and digests are non-null and preserved from `callback_prepared`; callback-acceptance object/digest is null there and non-null from `code_transferred`; decrypted-secret/exchange objects and digests plus `transient_secret_frame_digest` are null before and non-null from `exchange_consumed`. Every inner operation/child/ordinal/provider/catalogue/route/commitment digest byte-matches the outer object and every later projection names the exact prior projection digests. Ordinary login requires ordinal zero, null `reauth_ref`, provider matching its command row, and one child ID for the operation. Refresh requires provider Claude, ordinal `1...64`, exact opaque plan `reauth_ref`, and a distinct 32-lower-hex child ID for each proceeded entry. Persisted objects contain only the complete safe projections, keyed commitments, and safe digests above. Let `C0` be the originating command context start tick as defined above. The CLI alone creates the loopback callback listener and browser interaction under the exact endpoint projection. Each listener accepts only GET on its projected provider path, requires the byte-exact committed 256-bit state, rejects an absent code or a code longer than 512 bytes or outside `^[A-Za-z0-9\-._~+/]+=*$`, and lets only the first valid callback consume the one-use slot; invalid callbacks do not consume it and later valid duplicates receive the benign already-completed page. Listener/header/read/write limits and the ordinary/refresh absolute deadline partitions remain exact. Shutdown is bounded to three seconds inside remaining context. No child resets an absolute cutoff or receives a fresh wait. Authorisation output and browser failure follow the provider catalogue; persisted state contains neither URL nor its state, verifier, code, or token.

`OperatorOAuthControlV1` has no `control_oauth_child_result_digest` or other forward reference to `ControlOAuthChildResultV1`; that member is forbidden in every phase, including terminal. Let `O0=CanonicalJSONV1(object with mac omitted)` and `K_operator_oauth_control` be the `oauth-control` purpose key derived above. Its `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_operator_oauth_control,ASCII("cq/operator-control/oauth-control/mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(O0)) || O0))`; for complete MACed bytes `O`, `operator_oauth_control_object_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/oauth-control/v1\0") || uint32be(len(O)) || O))`. No operation, receipt, request, child-exchange commitment, or credential-owner key/domain may substitute. Each object is at most 65,536 bytes and uses final `oauth-objects/<operation_id>.<oauth_child_id>.<canonical-sequence>.<operator_oauth_control_object_digest>.json` plus sole random-exclusive temporary `oauth-objects/.<operation_id>.<oauth_child_id>.<sequence>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`. Supervisor writes, file-syncs, no-replace renames, directory-syncs, and same-descriptor reopens exact bytes/MAC/digest before publishing the immediate `OperatorControlOperationV1` successor whose matching `oauth_child_heads` row names that object; only outer-anchor CAS/reopen selects the child phase. Collision is legal only for byte-identical same-operation/child/sequence content.

Phase selection is effect-order authority. After the selected proceed decision, CLI may bind the one transient loopback listener solely to learn its exact endpoint, but it cannot accept a callback, display an authorisation URL, or invoke a browser until `callback_prepared` sequence zero/null predecessor embeds and reopens the complete state, PKCE, callback-endpoint, and authorisation-URL projections and is outer-selected. `code_transferred` is outer-selected after the sole valid callback and embeds the complete callback-acceptance projection before `ControlOAuthSecret`; `exchange_consumed` embeds and reopens the exact decrypted-secret and exchange projections plus carrier digest and is outer-selected before the token-exchange request body or network dispatch; `credential_committed` is outer-selected only after every bound credential-mutation child is terminal; and `terminal` is outer-selected with only the exact safe terminal-result digest before any refresh result object, later decision, or outer result. Every phase increments sequence, names the prior complete OAuth object digest, preserves every earlier complete projection byte-identically, and satisfies the closed nullability transitions above. An object without its outer head, an outer head without the reopened object, a phase jump, wrong predecessor, changed URL/callback/PKCE/key/carrier/route/reauth binding, missing complete projection, result forward reference, or second terminal is inert and fails closed. Recovery reopens both chains, recomputes every safe projection digest and cross-projection relation, and rejects any mismatch: before selected `exchange_consumed` it destroys transient material and selects `login_restart_required` without reconstructing or replaying callback/exchange secrets; at or after consumption it resumes only the selected credential-owner suffix, terminal OAuth object, result-object, and `result_bound` head suffix and never reconstructs or resends the exchange. OAuth and result objects remain pinned through the terminal outer receipt; receipt-selected digest commitments then permit object/temporary GC in child-ordinal/dependency/sequence order after every mutation and capacity-lease reference clears.

For a refresh OAuth child, `OperatorOAuthControlV1` retains its ordinary phase union and does not itself carry credential-owner receipt fields. After `exchange_consumed`, every persistent action reached while committing that OAuth result is a distinct planned `RefreshCredentialMutationChildV1` whose reservation core binds the OAuth triple to that exact reopened exchange-consumed object; each such mutation must reach `mutation_reserved -> credential-owner reservation/terminal -> credential_parent_terminal -> credential_receipt_bound -> credential-anchor clear -> terminal` before the next persistent action. A reserved child may instead reach only `abandoned_pre_effect` from complete credential-owner absence, after which that slot and actual ordinal remain consumed. Only after all plan slots reached by that exchange are committed or abandoned terminal may the OAuth child select `credential_committed` and then `terminal`. Ordinary-login credential completion remains `outer_result`. A missing, skipped, duplicate, reordered, cross-child, cross-slot, cross-plan, cross-commit, action/selector-drifted, or digest-mismatched phase refuses before the next mutation, OAuth child, or outer result.

PKCE verifier/state are fresh per OAuth child and remain in locked transient CLI memory. After one valid callback, CLI recomputes the callback-acceptance commitments and sends exactly one child-bound `ControlOAuthSecret` carrying encrypted `OperatorOAuthSecretV1` under that child's key/AAD/framing contract. The persisted `transient_secret_frame_digest` is that child's `K_commit` commitment, not a hash oracle for plaintext. Supervisor forwards the still-encrypted one-use carrier only to the selected worker transaction and has neither `K_aead` nor plaintext; no log, receipt, authority JSON, diagnostic, retry object, or filesystem write may contain code, verifier, state, redirect URI, raw URL/query/body, or refresh label. Worker decrypts inside the matching child transaction; independently recomputes every applicable `OAuthBind`, PKCE challenge, complete decrypted-secret and exchange projection, and `OAuthProjectionDigest`; exact-matches them to the reopened child, route catalogue, carrier, and callback projections; zeroises plaintext and `K_oauth_binding`; then selects `exchange_consumed` before producing the request body or dispatching network. It executes the exact authorization-code origin row once and commits provider credentials before returning only the redacted baseline result. CLI never receives bearer, refresh, or ID tokens. Crash before `exchange_consumed` terminalises that child `login_restart_required`, destroys its carrier and keys, and requires a fresh command rather than child replay; crash or lost acknowledgement after consumption recovers exact credential-owner journal and may report its result but never derives another key, resends code, or repeats exchange. `control.oauth_callback`, `control.oauth_exchange`, `control.one_use_recovery`, `control.refresh_reauth`, `control.worker_protocol`, and `worker.operator_control` fixtures bind every complete projection and purpose formula, phase, key/AAD/nonce/size/deadline boundary, duplicate/invalid callback, ciphertext/transcript/projection substitution, crash, destruction, and zero-secret persistence rule.

Structured refresh adds closed safe `ControlRefreshReauthPlanV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,entries:[RefreshReauthEntryV1],plan_digest}` where `RefreshReauthEntryV1={ordinal,reauth_ref,display_label}`. After the authenticated outer operation has selected its bounded worker transaction, but before anonymous synchronisation, automatic refresh, provider dispatch, prompt/browser work, any effect-authorising child, credential/cache mutation, or plan publication, the worker performs one read-only classification of the exact discovered Claude inventory. It constructs the ordered conservative `potential_reauth` set from every row that the baseline loop can append directly or after a failed refresh, validates every row's exact baseline `acctLabel` output as well-formed UTF-8 of 1...256 bytes, and requires at most 64 rows. More than 64 returns exact safe code `refresh_reauth_plan_unsupported`, message `structured refresh supports at most 64 interactive reauth accounts`, and exit 3; an invalid or 257-byte-or-longer label returns exact safe code `refresh_reauth_label_unsupported`, message `structured refresh account label must be valid UTF-8 and at most 256 bytes`, and exit 3. Both are declared structured-only compatibility breaks, terminalise the already accepted outer operation with zero effect commitment, and perform zero synchronisation, HTTP, OAuth, credential/keychain/cache/projection mutation, or label publication; labels are never truncated, repaired, hashed into output, or partially published. The accepted baseline refresh/synchronisation pass may only remove rows from that preflight set, so the resulting exact `needsReauth` order is bounded by 64; an unclassified added or relabelled row is generation drift and refuses with the same zero-effect compatibility result rather than widening the plan.

For `Q0=CanonicalJSONV1(ControlRefreshReauthPlanV1 with plan_digest omitted)`, `plan_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_commit,ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-reauth-plan/v1\0") || uint32be(len(Q0)) || Q0))`; this keyed commitment prevents persisted label/account guessing. `ordered_reauth_ref_commitment=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_commit,ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-reauth-ref-order/v1\0") || uint32be(entry_count) || each ordinal and length-prefixed reauth_ref in order))`. After both in-memory plans pass all bounds, the worker selects `CredentialOwnerRefreshCapacityLeaseV1` under `mutation.lock`; supervisor then publishes/reopens one outer successor containing the complete credential-mutation plan, the selected lease digest, and, only for nonempty reauth, `RefreshReauthPlanHeadV1` with these commitments. Only after outer-anchor CAS/reopen may it send the single `ControlRefreshReauthPlan` frame. Labels remain solely in that authenticated transient frame and CLI memory. A frame without the selected head, a head without the lease and mutation plan, a digest mismatch, or a zero-entry head/frame refuses without prompt, provider, or mutation effect.

The same read-only preflight constructs `RefreshCredentialMutationPlanV1` before either plan is published. It walks the exact discovered Claude and Codex inventories plus the signed exhaustive writer-reachability catalogue and signed one-to-one source-action map, and conservatively emits one slot for every persistent mutation that any baseline branch can reach, in source order: anonymous sync at `syncAnonymousToIdentifiedWithChange`; each `PersistRefreshedToken` credentials-file, platform-keychain, nested CQ-store and manifest edge; the following direct `StoreCQAccount` CQ-store and manifest edges; Claude cache invalidation; every `CredentialCoordinator.Refresh` managed-store transition and recovery branch; Codex cache invalidation; then each potential OAuth reauth's CQ-store, manifest, active-credentials, and platform-keychain edges. Every compact slot retains only its ordinal, exact signed map-entry digest, and nullable OAuth ordinal; preflight and reservation reopen the complete map entry and signed source row to derive all other fields. Branch outcomes may skip slots but never add or reorder them. More than 256 slots, a plan whose canonical bytes exceed 96 KiB, a missing/mismatched/ambiguous signed map or writer row, an unclosed source-row reference, or arithmetic overflow returns safe code `refresh_credential_mutation_plan_unsupported`, message `structured refresh supports at most 256 persistent credential or cache mutations`, exit 3, and the same zero-effect/no-plan-publication compatibility result. The complete in-memory plans then select the 3,825-unit/522,141,696-byte `CredentialOwnerRefreshCapacityLeaseV1` under `mutation.lock`; only its reopened anchor permits the matching shared plan/selected-lease successor and outer-anchor CAS. An actual mutation constructs its exact map-derived action/target reservation core and selects/reopens the `mutation_reserved` child and matching outer-head successor before taking the shared lock. Under that lock, the committed branch selects/reopens the immediate lease-consumption successor and revalidates the outer relation before sequence zero; the abandonment branch selects/reopens that same reservation-bound successor first, then publishes/reopens its bound absence proof, abandoned child, matching outer-head successor, and outer-anchor CAS in order. Only the committed branch may then enter `credential terminal -> credential parent terminal -> receipt -> credential_receipt_bound -> credential-anchor clear -> child terminal`; either complete terminal branch finishes before any later provider, credential, cache, or OAuth effect.

Accepted entries preserve the exact baseline `needsReauth` order, ordinals are contiguous `1...N`, `N<=64`, each `reauth_ref` is an opaque fresh keyed 32-lower-hex reference to one selected inventory row, and `display_label` is the already validated exact baseline `acctLabel`; neither account identity nor label persists outside the encrypted transient plan/CLI memory. The worker emits no plan when zero accounts need reauth. For non-TTY input it immediately returns exact baseline error `<N> account(s) need interactive reauth (run \`cq refresh\` in a terminal)` and opens no OAuth child. For TTY it emits the exact heading, then CLI creates exactly `bufio.NewScanner(os.Stdin)` with `ScanLines`, the default 64-KiB token limit, and no `Buffer` override, and processes entries in order with the exact baseline label and prompt. `ControlRefreshReauthDecisionV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,ordinal,reauth_ref,decision:"proceed|skip|input_eof",previous_decision_digest}` is one-use and ordered: byte-exact baseline `strings.TrimSpace(line)=="s"` alone skips and increments `failed`; every other successful scan proceeds. Any `Scan()==false`—clean EOF, `bufio.ErrTooLong`, or another scanner read error—records the same `input_eof`, emits no scanner error, does not inspect or surface `Scanner.Err()`, starts no child, leaves that and all later entries unattempted, and does not increment `failed`, exactly matching the current source loop. Skip prints exact `  skipped\n`. Proceed is equivalent to `RunLogin(...,false)`: it starts one fresh Claude child with fresh child key exchange, state, PKCE, callback listener and carrier; success commits through the credential owner, failure prints exact `  login failed: <safe baseline error>\n` and increments `failed`, and either result destroys child secrets before the next decision. After all decisions, `failed>0` returns exact `<failed> account(s) still need reauth`; zero, including any `input_eof` with no prior failure, returns success.

For complete canonical decision bytes `D`, `control_refresh_reauth_decision_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/refresh-reauth-decision/v1\0") || uint32be(len(D)) || D))`; ordinal one requires null `previous_decision_digest`, and every later decision names the immediately selected prior digest. Supervisor verifies the authenticated frame against the live transient plan, publishes/reopens the immediate outer-operation successor containing the complete safe `RefreshReauthDecisionHeadV1`, and CAS-selects/reopens the outer anchor before skip output, child key creation, callback work, or a later decision. `input_eof` is terminal for the decision array. A duplicate, gap, altered reauth ref, wrong prior digest, decision without selected plan head, or selected head without an admitted frame fails closed.

`ControlOAuthChildResultV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,reauth_ref,oauth_child_terminal_object_digest,terminal_outcome:"succeeded|failed|login_restart_required",terminal_result_digest,terminal_mutation_child_count,terminal_mutation_child_set_digest}` is both the sole safe refresh-child result frame payload and its durable content-addressed result object. For complete canonical bytes `U`, `control_oauth_child_result_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/operator-control/oauth-child-result/v1\0") || uint32be(len(U)) || U))`. It writes `U` through sole random-exclusive `oauth-results/.<operation_id>.<oauth_child_id>.<32-lower-hex>.tmp`, file-syncs, no-replace renames it to `oauth-results/<operation_id>.<oauth_child_id>.<control_oauth_child_result_digest>.json`, directory-syncs, and same-descriptor reopens exact bytes/digest. It then publishes and selects the immediate `result_bound` outer successor whose compact head preserves the terminal OAuth-object digest and adds this result-object digest; only afterwards may it emit byte-identical `U` once on the authenticated wire or begin a later decision. A collision is legal only for byte-identical same-operation/child content. The terminal OAuth object never contains or depends on the result digest, so the dependency graph is strictly terminal object -> result object -> outer `result_bound` head. Success requires every OAuth-bound mutation child terminal committed or abandoned; failure/restart requires the exact selected pre/post-consumption recovery outcome and the complete terminal mutation subset. A missing result object/head/frame, result 65, duplicate, foreign child/decision/plan, nonterminal mutation, changed result digest, reverse dependency, or later work before `result_bound` selection rejects without replay.

`OperatorOAuthChildKeyInitV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,reauth_ref,provider:"claude",parent_key_exchange_digest,clock_domain:"mach_continuous_time_v1",boot_session_id,forward_deadline_tick_ns,total_deadline_tick_ns,issued_at,valid_until,client_public_key_b64url,client_nonce_b64url}` and matching `OperatorOAuthChildKeyReadyV1={schema_version:1,operation_id,oauth_child_id,ordinal,reauth_ref,key_init_digest,worker_transaction_id,credential_index_generation,worker_public_key_b64url,worker_nonce_b64url}` use the exact X25519 validation, SHA-256 transcript framing, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, nonce, AAD, size, and zeroisation rules above with domain strings `cq/operator-oauth-child-key-init/v1`, `cq/operator-oauth-child-key-exchange/v1`, `cq/operator-oauth-child-kdf-salt/v1`, `cq/operator-oauth-child-aead/v1`, and `cq/operator-oauth-child-commit/v1`. The child clock/boot/deadline tuple byte-matches the outer request and `valid_until` is only its wall correlation; a child cannot reset or extend either parent deadline. A child is admitted only after its exact selected proceed-decision head and current inventory-generation revalidation; account drift returns a safe login failure without browser or exchange. Crash before outer-head-selected `exchange_consumed` terminalises only that child as `login_restart_required` and the outer refresh as failed/pending for explicit operation recovery; recovery never asks another prompt or starts a later child. Crash after consumption resolves only through the source-ordered reserved `RefreshCredentialMutationChildV1` chains, then may advance the existing OAuth and outer transcripts. Before the shared plan/selected-lease successor is selected, `CredentialOwnerRefreshCapacityLeaseV1` reserves the complete 3,825-unit/522,141,696-byte formula, including all 64 five-object/six-head OAuth chains, all 64 content-addressed `ControlOAuthChildResult` objects, their wire frames and `result_bound` heads, 64 decisions and heads, the shared plan/selected-lease successor and plan frame, and the complete 256-slot four-phase child/four-head budget. It persists only safe keyed plan commitments, decisions, OAuth phase/result objects and compact heads, mutation heads, and lease/proof digests and cannot be acknowledged, released, or collected while an OAuth child or credential mutation remains referenced; OAuth children own no credential receipts. Target and accepted-floor fixtures cover 0/1/64/+1 OAuth entries, skip/proceed/EOF mixtures, repeated children, inventory drift, every OAuth, decision, terminal-object/result-object/`result_bound`-head, lease, proof, and reserved mutation-child crash boundary, every 3,825/3,826 and 522,141,696/522,141,697 category boundary, deadline-minus-one/exact/plus-one, and zero secret/account-label persistence.

| `check` | exact baseline provider selection, quota-cache bypass policy, provider-owned automatic credential refresh, report, render, and `burn_history_v1` semantics | one authenticated owner-control request carries the exact `CheckCachePolicyV1` and drives bounded normal-worker Claude/Codex/Gemini provider, credential, and network work plus instance-local per-provider quota-cache use; `--refresh` bypasses only the initial cache serve and neither forces nor broadens credential refresh; provider fetch, valid-cache transient-error backfill, and usable-row publication remain enabled; CLI renders the returned report and remains the sole external `burn_history_v1` writer but performs zero legacy quota-cache, credential, keychain, or provider-network work |
| `claude_login` | exact baseline OAuth, CQ account store, optional active credentials/keychain projection, and cache invalidation | exact `OperatorOAuthControlV1` Claude callback/PKCE/code-exchange transaction followed by credential-owner save/optional projection and registered cache-generation invalidation; CLI performs only bounded browser/user interaction and rendering, never receives or persists bearer/refresh-token bytes |
| `claude_accounts` | exact baseline discovery and active-account rendering | owner-authenticated bounded worker returns only the existing redacted account projection; zero CLI credential/keychain read |
| `claude_switch` | exact baseline discovery, switch/refresh/projection, and cache invalidation | owner control plus one bounded worker credential-owner switch transaction and registered cache-generation invalidation |
| `claude_remove` | exact baseline account removal and cache invalidation | owner control plus one bounded worker credential-owner removal transaction and registered cache-generation invalidation |

| `codex_switch` | exact baseline coordinator-owned activation/projection and cache invalidation | owner control plus one bounded worker credential-owner activation transaction and registered cache-generation invalidation |
| `codex_remove` | exact baseline coordinator-owned removal journal/transaction and cache invalidation | owner control plus one bounded worker credential-owner removal transaction and registered cache-generation invalidation |
