Structured stopped/unavailable control, unsupported worker operation, timeout, lost acknowledgement, partial provider result, or worker failure is surfaced without a scalar/local fallback, duplicate transaction, direct cache invalidation, or credential projection. Every mutating control operation binds instance, caller, command row, arguments by keyed digest, authority/config/credential/cache generations, deadline, and one-use operation ID. After `ControlAccepted` and before `ControlProceed`, every human or structured invocation writes exact `cq: operation <operation_id> accepted\n` to stderr and flushes it; this safe side-channel is not a second JSON object and is the sole intentional structured-command stderr addition. The handle contains no argument or account information and is always available before any effect-capable phase. A pre-acceptance failure has no handle and no effect. Recovery queries that exact ID and never replays an ambiguous login, activation, switch, remove, refresh, or projection. No raw email, account ID, credential, token, OAuth code, provider response, or filesystem path enters command authority objects or safe diagnostics. After one successful ordinary effect row, the existing post-dispatch hook may invoke only `implicit_ensure_agent` through `DispatchRefreshCommandV1`. It derives a child context from the still-live parent ordinary context and starts only when the complete fixed 10-second child interval fits before the parent's absolute total deadline. In the pre-authority cell, an interval that cannot fit or a child failure preserves the ordinary result and exact existing safe warning. In the structured cell, or if post-result reclassification is no longer exact pre-authority, the hook is a silent zero-effect no-op; inability to fit is likewise silent. The child uses exactly 5 seconds forward plus 5 seconds reserve, is cancelled when either child or parent expires, and never resets or extends the parent's total. No ordinary dispatcher directly inspects or installs the agent.

Ordinary rows retain baseline human/JSON report envelopes and stdout/stderr except for the safe accepted-operation stderr line above. On `check`, the effective inherited `--json|-j` value alone selects its baseline renderer and the effective inherited `--refresh|-r` value alone selects cache bypass. On every other ordinary effect row, inherited `G*` changes no renderer, schema, result byte, warning, error, or exit relative to the flag-free argv; help/version/usage retain their exact Kong output and precedence. Help/version are 0; baseline usage, unsupported Gemini account management, provider/worker operational failure, and pre-effect timeout are 1; authority conflict or unsupported structured operation is 3; required classification/control unavailability or indeterminate durable outcome is 4. `OrdinaryCommandErrorV1={code,exit_code:1|3|4,cause_class:"usage_or_operational|conflict|unavailable",operation_id:null|string,remediation_command:null|string}` selects non-baseline exits without string matching and contains no raw argument, account, path, credential, or provider response. `operation_id` is null before durable acceptance and otherwise is the complete safe recovery handle; a pending or indeterminate accepted operation always sets remediation to `cq operation status --operation-id <ID>`.

`cq operation status` is a read-only, non-creating lookup against the default-primary operator-control store. With `--operation-id`, it requires the full 32-lower-hex handle and returns that exact active object or retained terminal receipt. Without a selector, zero active objects returns `idle`, one returns that object, and multiple valid anchors/active chains return `conflicted`; terminal history is never selected implicitly. `cq operation recover` requires the full handle. A valid retained receipt is returned directly with no recovery request, control frame, acknowledgement, or receipt rewrite. For an active chain with matching live authenticated owner control, recover same-descriptor reopens and authenticates the selected chain, admits one complete `OperatorControlRecoveryRequestV1`, queries owner and worker journals with `ControlRecover`, and may only (a) retire an accepted-but-never-proceeded operation as `failed` with zero effect, (b) finish already-issued exact credential/cache/projection reconciliation, (c) publish or return an already terminal safe outcome/digest, or (d) return `pending|indeterminate`. If that complete request is rejected while the matching authenticated connection remains live, recovery selects no successor and returns the closed `admission_failed` projection below; loss or unreachability before an authenticated admission result instead selects `unavailable`. A live authenticated connection whose caller, authority, runtime-attestation, or listener relation conflicts with the selected chain sends no request and selects `conflicted`; absence of a matching reachable control follows the zero-mutation `unavailable` branch. It never invokes OAuth browser/callback work, resends a secret frame or code, repeats provider exchange, creates a new credential/cache/projection transaction, reproduces the original result payload, or substitutes current arguments/generations. A pre-consumption login recovers `login_restart_required`; a post-consumption login resolves only from the exact credential-owner journal. Recovery remains operation-addressed across CLI, supervisor, or worker restart and boot-ID change. Terminal acknowledgement permits reference-aware GC only after the safe result has been rendered and no credential-owner, cache, projection, worker, or recovery reference remains. The sixteen-receipt archive pins every referenced receipt and fills only its remaining slots with newest unreferenced receipts by the closed retention order above; an explicit collected handle returns `requested_object_absent`, and an active, unacknowledged, pending, indeterminate, or referenced result is never collected.

Both operation leaves accept only `--operation-id`, `--json`, and lexical help in the shown positions. Human output is a bounded safe state summary plus the full handle and exact next command, never the original arguments or result payload; recovery reports only the authenticated terminal outcome and safe result digest. JSON uses the new proxy-style envelope below. `DispatchOperatorRecoveryCommandV1` creates its fixed context after lexical help/usage and full-selector validation but before topology/store inspection, propagates that one context through same-descriptor open, local store/receipt authentication and selection, safe snapshot, render, and flush; only an admitted active-chain recover additionally propagates it through `ControlRecover`, journal reconciliation, successor/receipt publication, and sync, and no path resets it. Status performs only that authenticated same-descriptor local store/receipt read: it never opens owner control, constructs an authenticated recovery request, sends a control frame, reconciles or selects a successor, or acknowledges a rendered result. An active-chain recover may construct exactly one recovery request only after authenticating the selected chain and a matching live owner-control connection; if it renders a selected terminal result, only that same admitted request and connection may form the post-flush acknowledgement. A live authenticated connection whose caller-capability, authority-generation, current-runtime attestation, or listener-generation mutation-key relation fails sends no request and creates no successor, receipt, or acknowledgement. It preserves every safely authenticated operation fact but returns `recovery_control=conflicted`, envelope state `conflicted`, `ok:false`, exit 3, null remediation, and exactly one top-level `CommonErrorV1`: `ownership_conflict` for caller-capability mismatch, `generation_conflict` for authority/listener mismatch, or `runtime_identity_mismatch` for current-runtime attestation mismatch. If no matching live authenticated connection is reachable, including an absent, stopped, inhibited, or unreachable matching primary or connection loss before an authenticated admission result, recover constructs no request or creates no successor, receipt, or acknowledgement. That closed `unavailable` precondition preserves every safely authenticated result fact, including operation/catalogue/row identity, `phase`, `terminal_outcome`, `terminal_code`, cancellation, effect, safe-result, acknowledgement, receipt, and time fields, but forces envelope state `indeterminate`, `ok:false`, exactly one top-level `CommonErrorV1` with code `operator_operation_indeterminate`, exit 4, and exact `cq proxy service start --manager launchagent` remediation. If the matching authenticated connection remains live but rejects the complete request before admission for any framing, MAC, binding, replay, boot, clock, deadline, or protocol reason, no recovery action or durable operation mutation has been admitted. That closed `admission_failed` result preserves the same authenticated operation facts, forces envelope state `indeterminate`, `ok:false`, exactly one top-level `operator_operation_indeterminate`, exit 4, and null remediation; the received rejection remains a safe nested diagnostic fact and cannot be reinterpreted as service unavailability. Direct retained-receipt projection constructs no request, requires no live control, and cannot acknowledge again. The phase/outcome oracle is total: no selected operation is `idle`; `reserved|accepted` requires null terminal outcome/code/digest, false effect commitment, and maps to `accepted`; `proceeding` requires null terminal outcome/code/digest and null effect commitment and maps to `pending`; `effect_committed` requires null terminal outcome/code/digest and true effect commitment and maps to `pending`; `terminal|acknowledged` requires exactly one non-null terminal outcome, requires a non-null safe-result digest for `succeeded|failed|login_restart_required` and null digest/effect commitment for `indeterminate`, requires terminal code null for `succeeded|indeterminate`, one of the two exact failure codes for `failed`, and `operator_login_restart_required` for its namesake outcome, and maps `succeeded` to `succeeded`, `failed|login_restart_required` to `failed`, and `indeterminate` to `indeterminate`. `result_available` is false for idle, every nonterminal phase, and indeterminate, and true exactly for the other three terminal outcomes. Any other phase/outcome/code/digest/effect/nullability combination, cancellation-field mismatch, acknowledgement-context nullability or source/request/deadline mismatch, sequence conflict, or multiple selected chain maps to `conflicted`; required authenticated inspection failure maps to `indeterminate`. `operation_action` is the invoked `status|recover` and does not alter authenticated result facts. Except for the three closed active-recover precondition overrides `conflicted|unavailable|admission_failed`, idle and succeeded emit `ok:true`, no top-level error, and exit 0; accepted or pending emits `operator_operation_pending`, while terminal failed emits its exact authenticated `terminal_code`, and each is `ok:false`/1. Other conflicted results emit the exact conflict code and exit 3; other indeterminate results emit `operator_operation_indeterminate` and exit 4. A selector miss is state `failed`, code `requested_object_absent`, and exit 3; grammar failure is `proxy_usage`/64. Status and recover project identical envelope state/error/exit from the same authenticated selected object except for those three closed recover-only precondition overrides; a legal recovery successor is a different selected object, not action-dependent reinterpretation. A post-flush acknowledgement rejection, loss, or deadline expiry cannot retroactively alter the already emitted JSON/human result or selected exit; it leaves the terminal chain addressable, status remains read-only, and a later recover may re-render and acknowledge under one fresh recovery request without replaying the effect. Both use a fixed 30-second total, 15-second forward window, and 15-second reserve; status performs no effect, control-socket access, or reconciliation and may use only its forward window for local authenticated selection/snapshot plus terminal render, while recover reserves the final fifteen seconds for exact reconciliation, safe snapshot, render, sync, and acknowledgement.

For `admission_failed`, the safe rejection diagnostic is represented only by bounded identifier-free `evidence_refs` on that single `CommonErrorV1`; it adds no result member, warning, second error, or remediation. If more than one live-control relation fails, the one emitted conflict code uses exact precedence `ownership_conflict` over `generation_conflict` over `runtime_identity_mismatch`; the JSON, human result, exit oracle, and help use the same order.

Receipt and acknowledgement projection is likewise total. An active anchor, including one selecting `acknowledged` before its publication suffix finishes, returns null `terminal_receipt_digest`, `terminal_receipt_generation`, and `receipt_acknowledged_at`; a retained `OperatorControlTerminalReceiptV1` returns its exact framed digest, generation, and acknowledgement time. `acknowledgement_context` is null for idle, selector miss, and every active phase through `terminal`; it is non-null and exact for an active `acknowledged` object and a retained receipt. The safe projection contains only its closed source/request/clock/boot/deadline members plus `acknowledged_tick_ns` and `acknowledged_at`; for a retained receipt its `acknowledged_at` equals `receipt_acknowledged_at`. Because acknowledgement follows output flush, the invocation performing it projects the pre-ack terminal state; a later lookup alone can project the durable acknowledged context. Presence of only part of the receipt tuple, acknowledgement context in a pre-ack phase, missing context in an acknowledged object/receipt, a receipt projected while a disagreeing anchor is selected, or a context whose source/request/deadline relation or mirrored outcome changes the phase/outcome oracle is `conflicted`/3. Human output identifies `active|retained_receipt` without printing receipt paths, publication metadata, MAC bytes, or request bytes.

`RefreshCommandAuthorityCatalogueV1` has exactly four semantic rows: `refresh`, `agent_install`, `agent_uninstall`, and non-user-visible `implicit_ensure_agent`. `refresh` is selected only by its exact public spelling and retains its baseline rejection of every non-help argument. `agent_install` and `agent_uninstall` first require the literal two-token prefixes `agent install` and `agent uninstall`; after that prefix, any tail containing exact token `--help`, `-h`, or `help` selects the corresponding help result before state, while an empty tail or any duplicate-preserving sequence of other argument bytes selects the same semantic row and discards that complete tail before authority classification or typed control-argument construction. Thus ignored tail bytes never enter `OperatorControlArgumentsV1`, a keyed digest, a manager/plist request, output, or diagnostics. `implicit_ensure_agent` is selected only after a successful ordinary Kong-dispatched baseline command that currently reaches the post-dispatch `ensureAgent` hook, never after help, usage/error termination, or an intercepted `refresh`, `agent`, `proxy`, `models`, `codex validate`, or `codex canary` command. Lexical help for `refresh`, `agent`, `agent install`, and `agent uninstall` terminates before compatibility initialisation, environment resolution, lifecycle/authority inspection, path, keychain, provider, process, or network access. Every non-help row enters `DispatchRefreshCommandV1`; direct `main` interception and the post-dispatch hook are parsing locations, not effect authority.

The dispatcher classifies the default primary by non-creating floor, lifecycle/initialisation/coordinator, bootstrap, and authority inspection before resolving `HOME`, cache/config directories, credential sources, the refresh plist/log, or any provider endpoint. Exact absent-or-compatible-scalar state with no structured bootstrap, authority, or selected initialisation/import enters the pre-authority cell; scalar compatibility initialisation, when required, occurs only after classification while holding the same exclusion. A signed structured floor, structured bootstrap/authority, or selected initialisation/import selects the structured cell even while stopped, inhibited, incompatible, or unreachable. Partial, conflicting, higher-floor, or unavailable classification refuses before any credential, cache, plist, `launchctl`, or network effect; `implicit_ensure_agent` alone preserves the already completed parent command's exit, emits no warning, and performs zero effect.

In the pre-authority cell, `refresh` preserves the baseline ordered Claude discovery/synchronisation/refresh/persistence/cache-invalidation, Codex credential-owner refresh/cache-invalidation, and TTY-only reauthentication behaviour. It acquires the stable lifecycle/compatibility exclusion before its first source or network access, revalidates the same absent/scalar facts immediately before each credential or cache mutation, and holds exclusion through the last write and result snapshot; authority appearance therefore selects either the complete legacy operation or a zero-effect conflict, never overlapping structured activation. Explicit `agent_install` and `agent_uninstall` and the absent-source branch of `implicit_ensure_agent` use `LegacyLifecycleActionStore` kinds `legacy_refresh_agent_install|legacy_refresh_agent_uninstall`; install additionally binds `trigger:"explicit|implicit"`. Explicit install preserves baseline unload, exact plist rewrite, and load semantics, implicit install is admitted only after same-descriptor proof that the exact plist and user-domain job are both absent, and uninstall preserves the baseline unload-then-remove semantics. Every unload, plist create/replace/remove, parent sync, and load has a committed attempt ID before invocation; recovery reconciles the exact `cq_refresh_v1` plist/job topology and never repeats an ambiguous action.

In the structured cell, `refresh` sends one authenticated owner-control request bound to the selected primary, current authority/config/credential generations, command deadline, and exact refresh operation. The bounded normal worker alone performs ordered Claude discovery/synchronisation/automatic refresh/persistence, Codex owner refresh, and registered cache-generation invalidation/reload. It then returns either no reauth plan, the exact non-TTY error, or the bounded encrypted `ControlRefreshReauthPlanV1`; for a TTY the CLI supplies only ordered skip/proceed/EOF decisions and one fresh callback/browser/encrypted-secret child for each proceed. Worker revalidates the referenced account before every child and commits through `CredentialOwnerCommitV1`; supervisor returns only safe progress and terminal results. CLI performs zero direct credential, cache, keychain, provider-network, public-registry, or token work. The outer operation preserves baseline ordering, exact prompts/output/failure count, and a single absolute deadline across every child. Stopped/unavailable control, unsupported worker method, worker/child failure, partial provider result, inventory drift, and lost acknowledgement are surfaced or operation-addressed without legacy/local fallback, repeated exchange, or a second refresh. A refresh LaunchAgent restored after import is non-TTY, invokes this same structured row, receives the exact needs-interactive error when applicable, and gains no pre-authority privilege from label or argv.

Structured `agent_install|agent_uninstall` are exact standalone `LifecycleActionStore` kinds `refresh_agent_install|refresh_agent_uninstall` under the ordinary coordinator and authority reference. They accept only the sealed default-primary LaunchAgent manager binding and exact `dev.jacobcx.cq.refresh` plist/job: install reconciles the signed selected executable, argv `[resolved-cq-executable,"refresh"]`, `RunAtLoad=true`, positive sealed interval, and registered refresh-log sink; uninstall bootouts and removes only that exact topology. Plist/job identity and before/after loaded state are revalidated before the action and terminal CAS. Every plist/launchctl effect is write-ahead and ambiguous issuance remains recoverable through `recovery transition`. Structured `implicit_ensure_agent` is an unconditional silent zero-effect no-op before even `HOME` or plist resolution; it emits no stderr and never installs, repairs, wakes, or journals a refresh source.

All four rows retain baseline raw stdout. Pre-authority `refresh`, both pre-authority and structured `agent install|uninstall`, and every `implicit_ensure_agent` branch retain exact baseline stderr; structured `refresh` also retains baseline stderr except that an invocation reaching `ControlAccepted` first emits the one exact accepted-operation line required above. Pre-acceptance failure emits no such line, and no refresh row emits another structured-only diagnostic. No row has a `--json` renderer or caller-controlled `--timeout`; `refresh` rejects those non-help arguments, while exact `--json` or `--timeout` after either agent leaf is merely an inert non-help tail under the rule above and cannot change rendering or deadline. For the three public rows, `DispatchRefreshCommandV1` creates and propagates its fixed command context through classification, exclusion, owner control, worker/provider calls, filesystem operations, manager calls, recovery reconciliation, and final sync. For `implicit_ensure_agent`, it accepts only the derived 10/5/5 child context described above and rejects a fresh, detached, reset, or longer context. No branch uses `context.Background()` below the boundary. Help is 0; baseline usage/operational failure and pre-effect timeout are 1; authority conflict is 3; required inspection/control or indeterminate durable outcome is 4. A typed `RefreshCommandErrorV1={code,exit_code:1|3|4,cause_class:"usage_or_operational|conflict|unavailable",operation_id:null|string,remediation_command:null|string}` selects non-baseline exits without string matching and carries no path, account, credential, or provider response. `operation_id` is null before durable acceptance and the exact accepted handle afterwards; an accepted pending or indeterminate result requires the corresponding `cq operation status --operation-id <ID>` remediation.

Help/usage dispatch precedes every state, environment, path, keychain, process, and network access. `models refresh` and `models overlay prune` preserve the same baseline tail rule as the implementation: after the literal command prefix, any tail containing exact token `--help`, `-h`, or `help` selects that leaf's help before state; an empty tail or any duplicate-preserving sequence of other argument bytes selects the named row and discards that complete tail before classification or typed owner-control construction. Ignored tail bytes never enter an authority object, keyed digest, worker or overlay request, output, or diagnostics. Every other models row retains the shown option grammar and rejects unparsed input. `ModelsCommandAuthorityCatalogueV1` then classifies the default primary by non-creating floor, initialisation/coordinator, bootstrap, and authority inspection before a mutating models command resolves `HOME`, `CODEX_HOME`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, the overlay, legacy config, or a projection target. Its exact rows are:

| Command | No structured primary authority | Valid structured primary authority | Direct external writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `models list` | read existing overlay and compatibility caches only | same role-neutral bounded read; never refresh | none |
| `models refresh` | call an exact live legacy refresh endpoint when available; only connection-unavailable or baseline 404 may enter the legacy local refresher | owner-authenticated control request, one bounded normal-worker refresh, then supervisor `ExternalProjectionPublisher`; stopped/unavailable/unsupported control fails | legacy local publisher only in the left cell |
| `models overlay add` | same-FD overlay CAS, then the legacy refresh rule above | same-FD overlay CAS under one owner-control permit, generation notification, worker reload/render, supervisor publication | overlay only; projections follow the cell's publisher |
| `models overlay remove` | same as add | same as add | overlay only; projections follow the cell's publisher |
| `models overlay prune` | legacy refresh, same-FD overlay CAS against that native snapshot, then legacy publication | owner-control worker refresh, overlay CAS bound to returned registry generation, generation notification, worker reload/render, supervisor publication | overlay only; projections follow the cell's publisher |

A signed structured floor, structured bootstrap/authority, or selected initialisation/import intent selects the structured column even when its service is stopped, inhibited, incompatible, or unreachable. Invalid, partial, conflicting, higher-floor, or unavailable classification refuses every mutating row before overlay/config/cache/network access; it never guesses legacy. In the structured column the CLI never reads a local token and never falls back to the public registry route or local publisher. Control loss returns `structured_models_control_unavailable`/4; an unsupported worker/control method, including a legacy/public 404, returns `structured_models_refresh_unsupported`/3; either result performs zero local provider refresh and zero projection-sink write. Worker failure is surfaced without retrying in the CLI. The existing authenticated public `POST /v1/registry/refresh` route remains a normal compatibility surface, but it is not structured `cq models` fallback authority.

Legacy local publication is legal only while the default primary has a compatible scalar floor and no structured bootstrap, authority, initialisation, or import. Immediately before the overlay CAS and before each individual projection temporary/rename, the command acquires the existing compatibility lock in the mode excluding structured floor/authority selection, reopens the same non-creating classification, and requires the same scalar floor and absence facts. Appearance or change returns `models_authority_changed`/3, discards any uncommitted temporary, and performs no later projection write. The lock is held through each target rename and directory sync; structured activation consequently cannot cross that publication commit. A prior sink already durably committed remains observable legacy output and is replaced by the structured publisher after activation; it does not authorise another local sink write.

`ModelOverlayGenerationV1` is the keyed digest of resolver-context digest, retained parent/target identity, exact canonical overlay bytes, and overlay schema revision. A structured overlay mutation first obtains one single-use owner-control permit binding current instance, authority/config/routing/registry generations, prior overlay generation, operation, and deadline. The CLI writes only `M`: random-exclusive `0600` temporary, file sync, same-descriptor prior identity/digest CAS, atomic rename, directory sync, and reopen. Prior-target or authority drift rejects before rename; drift after rename causes no projection publication and returns `model_overlay_notification_pending` with the safe new generation digest. Notification carries no model IDs or paths. Worker reopens the registered capability, requires the notified bytes/generation, increments its runtime overlay generation once, renders immutable root-local objects, and supervisor publishes them. Exact re-notification is idempotent; another content generation supersedes it. Concurrent external change before CAS, between rename and notification, during worker reopen, or during projection CAS produces `model_overlay_concurrent_writer`, never publishes a stale overlay, and is covered across service restart and lost acknowledgement. `models list` may observe either complete generation and never invents a merge.

`LegacyCodexAuxiliaryCommandCatalogueV1` has exactly six semantic rows: `validate_capture`, `validate_http`, `validate_websocket`, `canary_start`, `canary_status`, and `canary_stop`; the three canary spellings select their corresponding row. `validate_capture` is an authority-independent explicit-file utility in every primary state and dispatches before compatibility initialisation. It reads only the caller-named input with the existing 10-MiB-plus-sentinel bound, performs the existing sanitising parser, and confines writes to the caller-named output namespace: `0700` parent-directory creation as needed, the exact `OUTPUT.tmp` `0600` write, and rename to `OUTPUT`. It reads or writes no proxy config, epoch, root, readiness, canary, credential, service, or network state and launches no process.

Every other row is pre-authority legacy-only. Its gate requires compatible scalar floor; no structured bootstrap/authority or selected initialisation/import; and exact default legacy resolution. It runs before opening default or caller-supplied `--state-dir`, config, readiness/canary/stop files, client executable, lock, or process authority. `validate_http` retains the exact baseline read-only marker/path/argument semantics. `validate_websocket` retains the exact installed-client process, isolated-listener, marker invalidation/publication, default versus arbitrary `--state-dir`, and client-executable semantics. Canary start/status/stop retain the exact baseline default-path config/readiness/protected-source/state/owner-lock/stop-request semantics; they never target an instance root. Read rows revalidate the gate immediately before their first open. Mutating/process rows hold the pre-authority lifecycle/compatibility exclusion through the final process reap or marker/canary/stop directory sync, so structured selection cannot race a legacy effect. Partial, unavailable, or newly appeared authority returns `legacy_auxiliary_authority_conflict`/3 or the underlying unavailable/4 before those effects.

With structured authority, `validate_http|websocket` always refuses with exact remediation `cq proxy validate-installed --help`; `canary start`, `status`, and `stop` respectively remediate to `cq proxy candidate prepare --help`, `cq proxy candidate status --help`, and `cq proxy candidate stop --help`. Rejection precedes even an arbitrary `--state-dir` open and precedes installed-client resolution or launch. No structured command reads, refreshes, revives, or appends the archived legacy readiness/canary namespaces. The dispatcher and gates are `DispatchAuxiliaryCommandV1`; no direct `main` interception may bypass them.

Non-proxy auxiliary grammar remains fixed and exposes no caller-controlled `--timeout`. Every row except `agent install|uninstall`, `models refresh`, and `models overlay prune` rejects that token according to its existing grammar; on those four leaves it is an inert ignored non-help tail and cannot change the compiled deadline. After lexical help/usage termination and before the first environment, authority, path, lock, network, or process access, `DispatchAuxiliaryCommandV1` creates one command-scoped deadline from the exact auxiliary row below. That context and its remaining deadline propagate through every authority classification, owner-control request, provider refresh, filesystem operation, compatibility exclusion, listener/server, child version probe and execution, marker publication, process reap, and final directory sync. No auxiliary implementation may introduce `context.Background()` beneath that boundary. Forward work stops before the row's reserve; the reserve performs only already-authorised exact reconciliation, child/server stop and reap, and a final bounded result snapshot. Nothing runs after the total deadline. Expiry before any durable effect is `auxiliary_timeout`/1; if an output, overlay, marker, canary, or stop-request commit may have occurred, reserve reconciliation returns its proven success, pending, conflict, or unavailable result and never repeats an ambiguous effect.

Auxiliary commands retain baseline raw stdout rather than the proxy envelope; successful `models list --json` remains the baseline bare JSON array. Baseline stderr is exact for `models list`, every pre-authority models row, every legacy Codex auxiliary row, and every pre-acceptance structured failure. A structured `models refresh|overlay add|overlay remove|overlay prune` invocation reaching `ControlAccepted` adds only the exact accepted-operation stderr line above before its baseline diagnostics; it never adds another structured-only line. Help is 0. Baseline usage and ordinary operational failure, `auxiliary_timeout`, worker failure, and `model_overlay_notification_pending` are 1; `structured_models_refresh_unsupported`, `models_authority_changed`, `model_overlay_concurrent_writer`, and `legacy_auxiliary_authority_conflict` are 3; `structured_models_control_unavailable`, required authority/classification inspection unavailability, and an indeterminate durable outcome are 4. `DispatchAuxiliaryCommandV1` returns these nonzero outcomes through closed in-process `AuxiliaryCommandErrorV1={code,exit_code:1|3|4,operation_id:null|string,remediation_command:null|string,cause_class:"usage_or_operational"|"pending"|"conflict"|"unavailable"}`. `operation_id` is null before durable acceptance and the exact accepted handle afterwards; an accepted pending or indeterminate result requires the corresponding `cq operation status --operation-id <ID>` remediation. The top-level dispatcher unwraps only this type to select 3 or 4 and otherwise preserves baseline exit 1; it never classifies strings. Safe baseline error text remains the human diagnostic, and the typed object carries no path, model/account identifier, credential, or raw provider response.

Omitted `INSTANCE` selects primary default. Explicit root must pass secure capability acquisition. Manager selects lifecycle mechanism inside selected instance; it never selects instance. `MANAGER` is broad only because canonical `service start|restart|stop` may enter the pre-authority legacy lifecycle matrix; canonical `service uninstall` has literal `--manager launchagent` grammar and may enter only its LaunchAgent cell, while canonical `service install` has the same literal manager grammar but is never a pre-authority exception. `STRUCTURED_MANAGER`, `MIGRATION_MANAGER`, `ROLLBACK_MANAGER`, and every candidate/authority validation path accept only `auto|launchagent`, and `auto` must resolve to the sealed CQ LaunchAgent. At the user surface the frozen `proxy start --port` form remains only a pre-authority manual/foreground source runner and never creates structured authority; its exact non-user-visible managed/installed-validation process dispatch is closed by `DispatchLegacyStartV1`, and after authority exists every other invocation refuses with exact `service start` remediation. `rescue enter --listener` is only an equality assertion against the selected primary's sealed canonical listener: omission uses the sealed listener, mismatch is `instance_mismatch`/3 with exact `authority migrate` remediation before intent, and rescue never creates, binds, or retargets a listener. `--port` is otherwise accepted only by candidate prepare, root candidate validation as assertion, and frozen legacy status; authority initialisation/import/migration use mandatory `--listener`. `DURATION` is exactly `[1-9][0-9]*(ms|s|m)`; it may lower a command's compiled total only when supplied total remains at least `minimum_forward + reserve`, and cannot raise compiled total. Fresh initialisation and legacy-import activation use fixed compiled totals. `candidate validate-release` instead uses the non-overridable selected Begin run deadline from its command-entry `C0`; all three reject `--timeout`. `logs --follow` also rejects `--timeout`; only its fixed initial attachment is bounded. New blocking commands shown with `TIMEOUT` accept it once; pure reads not shown with `TIMEOUT` complete inside snapshot/config 10-second maximum. Frozen status, endpoint, and port-only `validate-http` use the literal fixed deadlines below and reject `--timeout`.

Every `operation_id` is an OS-CSPRNG 128-bit value rendered as exactly 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters. CLI selectors require the full value and reject prefixes. Every durable-intent result emits it; pre-intent failure emits null. Retry and recovery preserve the original value. Generated `ticket_digest` is exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters and successful import prepare always returns it after durable ticket commit. Generated `delegation_id` is exactly 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters and successful grant always returns it after policy commit. Generated `validation_run_id` is an OS-CSPRNG 256-bit value rendered as exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters; `candidate prepare` creates it and every later `--validation-run` requires the full value. Generated candidate receipt-export `attempt_id` is exactly 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters, and `candidate receipt show --attempt-id` requires the full value. No operation, ticket, delegation, validation-run, or receipt-attempt value is a prefix selector. A malformed operation/ticket/validation-run/receipt-attempt selector is usage 64 before state access. A well-formed explicit selector that has no exact active object or retained terminal object returns the selected leaf's envelope kind with `state:"failed"`, `requested_object_absent`, and exit 3; it never collapses to `idle`. A known explicit selector returns that exact nonterminal or terminal object. With no selector, a status leaf selects its sole addressable anchored nonterminal operation; zero returns `idle`, more than one returns `conflicted`/3, and terminal history is never selected implicitly. For initialisation specifically, `recovery initialise status` owns the pre-`prepared_waiting_activation` phases and `authority initialise status` owns that phase and every later fresh phase. In the applicable leaf, no anchored initialisation reports `state:"idle"`, `operation_id:null`, `initialise_state:"absent"`, exit 0; an unfinished exact chain returns `pending`/1, an invalid or multiply addressable chain `conflicted`/3, and unavailable inspection `indeterminate`/4. `feature activate status` applies the same no-selector rule: no active activation is `idle` with both IDs null and exit 0, while an exact retained terminal result is never selected implicitly.

Instance role is immutable bootstrap authority. Legacy import or explicit `authority initialise` creates `role=primary`; only `candidate prepare` creates `role=candidate`. Resolved default-primary root is permanently primary-reserved, including absent/partial state. Candidate prepare compares retained parent identity plus basename and rejects equivalent spellings/symlinks before any write. Its numeric loopback listener must also differ from the compiled default primary `127.0.0.1:19280`, the listener in securely inspected legacy proxy configuration when present, and the canonical listener in any securely selected current/default primary bootstrap plus authority, whether or not that listener is currently bound or its service is stopped. If any required primary-listener comparison is malformed, ambiguous, or unavailable, preparation refuses before creating lifecycle/key/state. A free port or stopped primary never makes the tuple a candidate port. The frozen public `cq proxy start` spelling is not `service start`: outside the two closed internal `DispatchLegacyStartV1` branches it is only the pre-authority foreground runner below and never calls `EnforcePrimary`, `EnforceLegacyLifecycle`, or `EnforceCandidateRun`. Canonical `service start|restart|stop|uninstall` may use `EnforceLegacyLifecycle` only for the exact pre-authority manager/action cells below and otherwise require `EnforcePrimary`; canonical `service install` always requires an existing sealed primary, never enters `EnforceLegacyLifecycle`, and never initialises state. Every `service` mutation rejects candidate role. Candidate lifecycle and validation use only the exact commands admitted by `EnforceCandidateRun`.

`EnforceCandidateRun` is the only post-preparation candidate mutation gate and is a closed `live_controller|parent_invalidation|parent_cleanup` union. All variants require a securely acquired `role=candidate` bootstrap/authority, exact candidate and controller store/label/root/listener tuples, exact full validation-run ID, both prepared-core and capability-manifest digest/object-identity pairs, exact resource-envelope digest, one matching store anchor, and the canonical Ready-public-key-to-key-ID derivation whenever Ready was selected. `live_controller` additionally requires the authenticated ready process/socket plus controller signature under the prepared public key: exact `candidate start`, `candidate artifact switch`, `candidate client-bearer-barrier refresh`, root-form `validate-http`, candidate-targeted `validate-installed`, `validate-production-profile`, and `candidate validate-release` require the one open unbreached confinement run, while exact `candidate stop` may close ingress and reap its exact group. `parent_invalidation` requires selected `intent|launch_attempted|plist_published|job_bootstrap_attempted|socket_published|ready|runtime_authority_committed|begin_committed`, null invalidation-authority fields in that state, the retained parent lifecycle capability, lifecycle-then-`mutation.lock` ownership, and either the exact verified live-controller proposal or a complete fresh parent-loss proof. It permits only publication/reopen of that one authority object and the exact legal `invalidated` state/anchor CAS; it cannot write validation evidence, select a success field, act on the listener or process tree, or skip into cleanup. This is the sole controller-loss `candidate stop` and recovery bridge into parent cleanup. `parent_cleanup` requires selected `invalidated|cleanup_attempted|cleanup_committed|terminal invalidated_cleanup` store state authenticated under the trusted parent store MAC and its implementation path permits only exact `candidate stop` reap/cleanup or terminal `candidate remove`, never a success transition or call into the controller-evidence writer. Removal additionally requires retained terminal controller/confinement-or-invalidation chain, stopped/reaped/unreferenced proof, and its parent-owned coordinator transaction. No variant authorises frozen `proxy start`, an internal `DispatchLegacyStartV1` branch, or any `service` command, including `service install`. The gate same-descriptor reopens both manifest objects and every sealed run/build/executable/release input, recomputes the exact prepared-core-to-capability projection, never reads or writes primary authority, and restricts every effect to candidate/controller-owned roots, jobs, listener, children, registered output, and parent controller cleanup state. For `candidate validate-release`, it additionally requires the exact sealed release-input manifest digest/object-identity pair, selected single-use transfer receipt, and two retained canonical descriptor identities before admission, and restricts floor reads to those descriptors. A missing, foreign-paired, mismatched, terminal-for-forward-work, multiply selected, unauthenticated, unlisted predecessor, or loss-proof/reason mismatch refuses before side effects. Candidate preparation remains the parent-transaction creation exception and cannot invoke this gate until candidate `authority_committed` is durable.

`EnforceClientBearerBarrierStage` is a distinct role-polymorphic store gate used only by `client-bearer-barrier status|stage`; it never falls through to `EnforcePrimary` or `EnforceCandidateRun`. Status is non-creating inspection. Stage requires a valid sealed primary or candidate bootstrap/authority, the retained lifecycle and authority locks, a safely reopened source candidate bootstrap/controller/run chain, and either no active listener-release operation with omitted `--operation-id` or one exact matching active release operation with the full ID supplied. It may copy and atomically select only the signed barrier receipt and its canonical case set under the target readiness subtree. It cannot start, stop, signal, bind, unload, change a listener/config/token/registry, advance candidate success evidence, or clear an operation. A source/target root alias, wrong role/build/executable/run/signer/registry/sender/config/domain/token-generation/protocol binding, expired receipt, selector conflict, or unrelated active operation refuses before the target anchor CAS.

Fresh `authority initialise prepare` requires absent root/control/floor, exclusive stable lifecycle initialisation, exact floor/target `ReleaseBundleV1` locators and set digests, exact external floor-acceptance receipt locator/digest, one distinct sealed source candidate selected by `--candidate-instance-state-root`, exact preactivation receipt file/digest with durable preauthority claim, generated local token cutover, and complete `ProxyReleaseFeatureSetV1`; it verifies signed authority/acceptance/ancestry/passed-reports/ABI and the source candidate/run/barrier relation, canonically copies and same-descriptor reopens release provenance, artifacts, barrier receipt and case set, publishes the staged idle barrier selection and the existing floor-validation preauthority claim that pins its referenced barrier objects, then stages the remaining synced trees, config, socket definition, bootstrap object, structured floor, inert cutover state, and inhibited target authority but starts no service and admits no data plane. `status` is pure inspection. `activate` reopens the exact anchored input object, phase chain, and canonical release objects, commits `floor_committed`, selects and checkpoints the first inhibited authority with matching `active_initialisation_ref`, selects `lifecycle_handoff_prepared`, converts the retained exclusive lock descriptor to shared, selects `lifecycle_handoff_shared`, and commits the manager action attempt. That action enters the closed primary launcher protocol: the stable launcher acquires and attests its own shared description before private-state read, carries that same description across `exec`, the supervisor completes the closed pre-root/MAC bootstrap, and the worker validates a distinct private-bootstrap description before its own private-state access. The initialisation issuer retains its separate shared hold until the exact two-holder `RuntimeBootAckV1`, matching initial `RuntimeHolderCheckpointV1`, and owning journal references are all synced; only then may it release that hold. It issues and records client challenges through that inhibited supervisor, commits the complete acknowledgement set, atomically selects the generated token, commits the installed marker set and `RuntimePolicyAckV1`, selects active authority while clearing the initialisation reference, checkpoints bootstrap, writes the terminal receipt, and retires the initialisation anchor. No supervisor bootstrap is permitted before the shared handoff phase, and no boot is verified unless the ordered live supervisor/worker holder set and launcher/worker grant lineages are current in both boot acknowledgement and holder checkpoint. Any failure before floor leaves no selected primary authority and exact resumable/abortable staged state; after floor it leaves inhibited activation state resumable only through the same `authority initialise status|handoff|activate` operation and never falls back to an uninitialised listener. Expired post-handoff cutover invokes the bounded rekey subcycle without repeating floor/manager/boot work; expired client challenges are superseded within the same unexpired generation. `abort` is legal only before floor/manager action and follows the initialisation-owned quarantine receipt protocol. Initial desired mode is normal only; V1 has no fresh-rescue initialisation path.

Candidate label key is `K_label=HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/candidate-label/v1"),L=32)`, created after candidate `authority.key` and before bootstrap/plist publication and preserved across reset with that key. Input is `ASCII("cq/candidate-label-state-root/v1\0") || uint32be(len(CanonicalJSONV1({parent_identity_digest,basename,state_root_digest}))) || CanonicalJSONV1(...)`; suffix is first 16 lower-case hex characters of HMAC-SHA256. Label is `dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy.candidate.<suffix>`. Sealed manifest records full label/root/listener tuple. Baseline singleton candidate label remains exclusive to frozen port-only compatibility validation.

Flat aliases are spelling compatibility only and never import or mutate legacy global policy implicitly. Alias parsing wins before new-tree `--json`; aliases reject `--json` with legacy usage exit 1 except when retained legacy help precedence below has already terminated dispatch. Accepted lifecycle forms are `install [--confirm-payload-capture]`, `uninstall --confirm-client-stopped`, and `restart [--confirm-client-stopped]`, expanding to the same canonical CQ LaunchAgent service operations. Pre-authority Homebrew accepts the flat restart alias only after exact manager reconciliation; it has no flat uninstall expansion, and prints exact canonical Homebrew stop remediation instead. Alias recognition precedes dynamic confirmation inspection. Missing dynamically required confirmation or universal `Authorization`-sender barrier proof performs no mutation, prints exact canonical command, and exits legacy code 1; aliases never emit new-tree exit 64 or JSON. Read aliases may inspect legacy values without conversion. Pre-authority `pin --clear|ACCOUNT`, `codex-default --clear|ACCOUNT`, and `prime enable|disable` refuse with `instance_uninitialised`/3 plus exact import remediation; after authority they map to canonical settings transaction. Documented alias positional grammar remains one deprecation cycle; extra arguments reject. Restart replaces legacy launchctl-113 fallback with exact reconciled manager and refuses ambiguity. Existing endpoint maintenance remains fixed-default credential authority, not instance-selected.

Flat `install` is recognised for help and post-authority spelling compatibility but is not a pre-authority lifecycle exception. With absent default authority and no exact legacy source it prints `cq proxy authority initialise prepare --help`; with one exact live or stopped legacy source it prints `cq proxy authority import-legacy prepare --help`; with partial, ambiguous, or unavailable inspection it prints `cq proxy status --strict` before the exact inspection error. Each refusal exits legacy code 1 and creates no lifecycle inode/key, initialisation state, legacy journal, plist, directory, configuration, or manager action. It never calls `EnforceLegacyLifecycle`. Only an already valid sealed primary may expand flat `install` to canonical `service install --manager launchagent`; candidate role refuses with legacy code 1. Retained any-position baseline help still wins before this inspection.

`authority import-legacy` is sole initial bridge from pre-authority Homebrew, old CQ LaunchAgent, or explicitly declared foreground primary into default authority. `auto` selects exactly one live attested managed source and never stopped state. Live mode requires matching job/process/listener/serving identity plus the live `LegacyHeadroomCompatibilityProofV1` variant from the exact process. Stopped managed mode requires explicit manager, securely acquired plist/config identity, absence of job/process/listener/client connection/competing manager, and the stopped Headroom-proof variant. Live foreground requires exact PID/executable/listener plus the live Headroom-proof variant; stopped foreground requires secure legacy state, absence of supported job, CQ process/listener/client connection, the stopped Headroom-proof variant, and explicit confirmation. Closed `prior_topology` is `live_managed|stopped_managed|live_foreground|stopped_foreground`; stopped activation performs no source-stop action and restoration preserves stopped/no-listener topology without inferring an executable.

`prepare` is sole pre-authority staging operation. Under stable exclusive lifecycle lock and the matching parent initialisation anchor/input/phase chain, it verifies and canonically copies the exact target/floor bundle objects, common build authority, accepted-floor receipt, sets, passed reports, ancestry, manifests, and payloads; then it stages default control/root, keys, target and digest-distinct rollback artifacts, canonical socket plist, legacy restoration receipt, bootstrap identity, and immutable `import-ticket`. It performs no manager, listener, floor, or authority-anchor action. Ticket binds exact source topology, complete `LegacyHeadroomCompatibilityProofV1` digest, candidate preflight/confinement/production-profile and universal sender-set barrier receipts, release bundle/build-authority/acceptance/set/report/ancestry/artifact digests, plist/manager, config/payload acknowledgement, restoration, target feature intent, root/key identities, and the non-null `real_client_session_binding_hmac` plus `real_client_session_emission_fixture_digest` obtained only through the required privacy-preserving session authority below. The raw session bytes are never a ticket field or durable object. Random-exclusive ticket write/file sync, `import-ticket.anchor` replace, stable-control sync, then anchored `prepared_waiting_activation` phase-object commit make preparation durable. Before ticket anchor, `recovery initialise` owns resume/abort; afterwards import status/activate/abort/finalise owns it. Same ticket resumes idempotently. Pre-action abort uses parent transaction to quarantine every present staged or canonical control/root tree together, syncing parent after each no-replace move, then commits one terminal abort receipt. It deletes nothing. The two quarantine-supersession flags are one paired grammar branch: both absent is ordinary fresh preparation; both present is legal only while the exact named active real-client quarantine inhibits this instance; either alone, use without that exact quarantine, or combination with any validation-successor command is a usage/conflict failure before staging. The paired branch has one required pre-exclusive handoff. While the selected quarantined supervisor is still live under its shared lifecycle description, the parent writes and syncs a complete fresh inert import-preparation input/ticket in the parent-owned staging store, including fresh release/profile/session/policy authority and a fresh session HMAC; that object has no canonical-root selector, routing effect, manager/listener effect, public admission, or validation authority. The live supervisor securely reopens the active anchor/quarantine and the complete staged ticket and mints the dedicated authenticated `supersede_quarantine` validation-control request plus complete prepared `RealClientValidationQuarantineSupersessionHandoffV1` below. Before any shutdown, one parent intent-publication CAS injects its own clock, proves that request unexpired at that exact CAS, constructs the authenticated `RealClientValidationQuarantineSupersessionArmV1`, and publishes, syncs, and same-descriptor reopens the fresh parent import-preparation intent with the byte-identical ticket, request, handoff, arm object, and recomputed digests as separate fields. That successful publication CAS is the sole handoff arm linearisation point; the request, handoff, and arm object are never ticket fields, and the ticket digest is fixed before any is minted. Only after the parent-selected arm is durable may the parent close ingress, drain, stop/reap that exact supervisor, record its terminal holder checkpoint and shared-description release, and acquire the stable exclusive lifecycle lock. Under that lock the parent reopens the same old anchor/quarantine, staged ticket, preparation-intent-embedded request/handoff/arm triple, shutdown/checkpoint/release proof, and every fresh input; one parent preparation CAS consumes all three ID/nonce pairs and selects the fresh preparation. The post-release CAS never rechecks wall time: it validates the immutable authenticated arm-time relation and every bound shutdown/release fact. Crash before arm selection resumes only with the same live supervisor and may not begin shutdown; crash after arm selection reopens the byte-identical intent/request/handoff/arm tuple without reminting; crash after supervisor release resumes only the exclusive consumption CAS. A stopped/replaced supervisor cannot mint or arm, a prepared handoff cannot freeze request expiry, and the exclusive holder cannot substitute a ticket, request, handoff, arm object, or shutdown attempt. The transition preserves the complete old quarantine closure by digest and creates no manager, listener, routing release, public admission, or validation action.

`activate` securely reopens ticket/receipts/artifacts/source topology, the exact unexpired universal request-sender barrier receipt, and obtains `ClientStopProofV1`. Before source stop, listener release, floor action, or authority mutation, it rereads the source config through the same retained descriptor contract and requires the disabled baseline fields plus keyed fingerprint to equal the ticket. For a live variant it also requires the same exact process/listener identities and a fresh serving-proof-bound health projection with `headroom=false`; for a stopped variant it re-proves the exact stopped source/job/process/listener absence set. The fresh live response/proof/body digests may differ because the challenge and unrelated health fields are dynamic, but process, listener, config fingerprint, projection schema, and Boolean result must agree; source replacement, config drift, `headroom:true`, missing proof, or live/stopped topology change fails closed and cannot be adopted as another mode. Proof records exact target, manager/listener identities, ingress-fence generation, closed client-set, request-sender-set, authorisation-sender-set, request-transport-set, and barrier-receipt digests, connected/admitted HTTP/WS counts, validation streams, kernel connection observation, collection time, and evidence digest. Structured/candidate source must close ingress and report counts zero. Live legacy source qualifies only when signed `legacy_quiescence_v1` challenge binds exact process/listener/nonce, closes ingress, and reports zero connections/admitted work; otherwise operator first stops it and uses a newly prepared stopped-source ticket. `--confirm-client-stopped` confirms operator intent only; it never substitutes for observed proof, Headroom proof/revalidation, whole-request barrier integration, or authoritative sender/transport enumeration. Any unsupported/unregistered sender, credential domain, or transport, expired/mismatched receipt, sender executable/config/token-generation drift, or failed cold-login/reconnect/foreign-bind/release-window case refuses before source stop, listener release, floor advance, or authority mutation.

Activation first commits initial primary `legacy_import` intent without floor advance and stops the exact live source. After the last target-tree rename it selects `lifecycle_handoff_prepared`, converts the retained exclusive lifecycle descriptor to shared, selects `lifecycle_handoff_shared`, and only then invokes the compatibility-mode socket manager. That action enters the same closed primary launcher protocol: the launcher obtains the lock before private-state read and transfers that description across `exec`; the supervisor validates it before its narrow bootstrap/private-state sequence; the worker validates a distinct description before worker-private access. The activator retains its separate shared hold until the content-addressed initial `RuntimeBootAckV1`, matching initial `RuntimeHolderCheckpointV1`, and owning journal references are synced. Only the exact ordered live supervisor/worker holder set plus fresh topology proves normal serving or permits floor/target authority advance. A pre-floor failure enters the closed initialisation-owned restoration branch: it selects the target-retirement attempt before bootout, retires and reaps the target, records shared release, acquires the same inode exclusively, durably unlinks the distinct target plist or restores the ticketed prior bytes, performs only the sealed tree-restoration plan, restores each registered prior source through the existing `WriterQuiescenceAttemptV1` action IDs, and commits terminal prior-topology proof before quarantine/abort retirement. It never follows the normal boot suffix or advances floor after selecting restoration. Candidate root remains stopped/referenced until installed target/floor proofs and finalisation. No generic start/install/config read imports implicitly.

The first successful activation may intentionally return `pending` after target authority is installed but before primary marker/policy proof exists. After installed validation, exact re-entry of `authority import-legacy activate` with the same ticket and confirmations reopens the committed external-action evidence, performs no source stop, manager action, floor advance, token selection, or runtime boot again, and commits terminal `legacy_import=target_effective` only when exact target `RuntimeBootAckV1`, marker set, `RuntimePolicyAckV1`, and topology all match. It then checkpoints the selected bootstrap identity, publishes the matching terminal initialisation receipt, and clears and parent-syncs the legacy-import initialisation anchor while retaining the import-ticket anchor/object. Until the terminal import history, bootstrap checkpoint, terminal initialisation receipt, and anchor retirement all exist, runtime-bundle switch, real-client validation, generic authority mutation, and import finalisation refuse. Crash before or after the terminal import CAS, bootstrap checkpoint, receipt publication, or anchor clear resumes that exact suffix from the same evidence and never repeats activation action.

`finalise` takes no proof digest from argv. A second reachable path never creates an alias edge, and a duplicate source path with inconsistent kind/digest is a conflict rather than a deduplication rule. Recovery scans only those exact bounded basenames under the retained descriptors and verifies every file before use. Argv forms warn about history/process visibility.

`candidate receipt show --attempt-id ID` requires an inspected candidate and is the sole explicit receipt-export lookup leaf. The external source registry permits only the candidate chain and those two canonical objects needed by the named preactivation receipt. For fresh initialisation, `--candidate-instance-state-root` is a mandatory secure source selector distinct from target `INSTANCE`; lexical omission or an equivalent target/source spelling is `proxy_usage`/64 before either root opens. After lexical parsing, a missing, non-candidate, invalid or unavailable source returns the exact instance conflict/indeterminate result with zero target initialisation object, claim, copy or selection write. ### Inspection meanings

- `health` uses owner-only Unix control and returns detailed supervisor health only after peer-UID plus nonce/HMAC authentication. `health --public` performs one direct numeric-loopback request with proxy/compression disabled, redirects refused, and body cap 128 bytes plus sentinel. Accepted tuples are exactly `Content-Type: application/json` with HTTP 200/body `{"schema_version":1,"status":"ok"}` or HTTP 503/body `{"schema_version":1,"status":"degraded"}`. Raw mode writes canonical body plus LF; JSON wraps `proxy_health`. Any other status/header/body/trailing byte is conflict 3 and is never echoed. Public health exposes no identity or routing detail.
- `status` reconciles desired state, service candidates, listener owner, runtime identity, and effective generations into one fast verdict.
- `info` emits the full privacy-safe snapshot and succeeds when proxy is stopped or config is invalid, provided inspection itself completes.
- `doctor` evaluates deterministic invariants and prints exact suggested commands. It never changes state, restarts, refreshes, contacts or probes providers, or adopts a process. Optional provider evidence means only a previously committed, locally readable, unexpired provider-probe receipt; absence is encoded and never triggers network work.
- `probe codex` is explicit exact-account provider data-plane operation using canonical `model.invoke` fixture and one-attempt/no-fallback contract below, but it never writes capability evidence and always maps to `proxy_probe`. `codex capability probe ... model.invoke` uses the same adapter, may commit evidence after exact success, and always maps to `codex_policy_transition`; it never also emits `proxy_probe`. Neither is implied by `health`, `status`, `info`, or `doctor`.
- `logs` defaults to `--source service` and selects attested instance-owned stream. For each closed source, derive separate header and pointer HMAC-SHA256 keys from `authority.key` with HKDF info `cq/log-header/v1/<source>` and `cq/log-pointer/v1/<source>`. MAC input is source-specific ASCII domain, `uint32be` JCS length, and `CanonicalJSONV1` with `mac` omitted. Each directory has `<source>.current.json` and `<source>.<20-digit-sequence>.log`; first exact JCS+LF record is `{type:"cq_log_header",schema_version:1,source,stream_id,sequence,previous_generation_digest,created_at,boot_session_id,created_tick_ns,mac}`. Stream ID is 32 random lower-case hex, sequence starts zero, predecessor null only at zero, and otherwise `previous_generation_digest` covers every exact predecessor byte. Header digest covers exact header record including LF. Pointer is exact `{type:"cq_log_current",schema_version:1,source,stream_id,sequence,header_digest,updated_at,mac}`; sequence determines filename. Header counts toward file cap, never `--lines`, never display. Rotation closes/syncs/hashes old, creates/syncs successor with exact predecessor, atomically replaces/syncs pointer, then appends. After crash, exactly one valid successor of pointer-selected generation resumes pointer publication; multiple successors conflict, while unrelated valid objects remain retained orphans. Reads verify chain newest-to-oldest. Follow retains current inode through EOF and attaches every valid successor without count limit; retention gap emits one fixed omission marker and attaches current. Ownership/MAC/source/stream/predecessor/sequence mismatch is conflict 3.

Default is last 200 complete LF records; `--lines` accepts 1–10,000. Records escape independently and selection bounds stdout including markers to 1,048,576 bytes. Oversize record becomes `[cq: oversized log record omitted]`; older overflow adds fixed leading marker. Bounded logs use the admitted deadline. `--follow` rejects `--timeout`, uses a fixed 10-second initial attachment deadline, and becomes unbounded only after attachment. Valid empty read 0; absent attested source/initial timeout 2; ownership/path/header/inode conflict 3; permission/platform 4; other I/O 1. After first success signal exit 0; later error preserves stdout and mapped exit. Standard records retain identifier/prompt/secret ban; payload uses separate consent/content contract. Before any payload byte, read/follow verifies the non-mutating retention attestation below against its exact snapshot; it never invokes cleanup or writes retention state, and missing/stale/conflicting attestation returns `sensitive_retention_unavailable` with no payload output. Legacy shared log is never displayable.
- `config show` is strict non-secret allowlist: listener, traffic/routing mode enums, boolean feature enablement, fixed upstream hostnames, numeric resource bounds, and presence/count facts. It replaces `local_token`, account keys/default, emails/IDs, credential references, diagnostic/payload/log paths, and every future or unknown field with `{present,count,keyed_fingerprint}` as applicable; no raw value or path appears. `config diff` compares securely read desired object with runtime effective keyed whole-object fingerprint and same allowlisted field-state projection; absent worker fields are `unknown`, never inferred. No reveal flag exists.
- Command parser identifies help, renderer, instance, and exact auxiliary/refresh spelling before state access. Help/usage exits first. Every listed models or legacy Codex auxiliary spelling passes `DispatchAuxiliaryCommandV1`; exact `refresh`, `agent install|uninstall`, and the post-Kong hook pass `DispatchRefreshCommandV1`; direct `main` interception and direct `ensureAgent` invocation are not effect authority. Read-only proxy commands call the role-matrixed `InspectInstance`, continue independent collectors, and encode absent/invalid/incompatible facts. Every primary listener/runtime start, provider probe, data-plane admission, service/policy mutation, feature activation, structured refresh/agent row, and structured mutating models command calls `EnforcePrimary`, the ordinary coordinator-bound lifecycle gate, or the stricter owner-control catalogue gate before side effects. First primary initialisation, candidate preparation, the exact parent-transaction/recovery store-matrix cells, `client-bearer-barrier stage` through `EnforceClientBearerBarrierStage`, authority-independent `validate capture`, exact pre-authority rows of the models, legacy Codex auxiliary, and refresh-command catalogues, the exact internal managed/installed-validation process branches through `DispatchLegacyStartV1`, canonical pre-authority `service start|restart|stop|uninstall` in only the manager/action-matrixed cells through `EnforceLegacyLifecycle`, the remaining frozen pre-authority foreground runner through `EnforceLegacyForegroundStart`, the frozen singleton validation command through `EnforceLegacyCandidateHTTPValidation`, and the exact closed candidate command/state matrix through `EnforceCandidateRun` are the only exceptions. `Service install` is never an exception and always passes `EnforcePrimary`. Only import or feature-raising activation advances primary floor; candidates advance candidate-local floor only.
- Frozen bare `status` also uses a non-creating configuration read. If legacy `proxy.json` is absent, it uses the in-memory legacy default port `19280` without generating a token, directory, or file; malformed existing configuration remains an error. Its output stays frozen even though its state access becomes read-only.

Candidate-provider-broker inspection is a local, same-descriptor projection of the selected `CandidateProviderBrokerPolicyV1`, `CandidateProviderBrokerJournalHeaderV1`, `CandidateProviderRequestIssuedRecordV1`, `CandidateProviderRequestConsumptionReceiptV1`, `CandidateProviderRequestTerminalReceiptV1`, `CandidateProviderBrokerJournalCloseV1`, `CandidateProviderBrokerJournalSealV1`, checkpoint, final digest, routing-authority and credential-echo scan-evidence source objects, or parent-retained terminal receipt; it never wakes the controller, opens a provider transport, reads the credential vault, or reconstructs state from candidate files or a directory scan. The closed privacy-safe object is
