nvalidation",first_breach_code:null|"capability_count"|"concurrent_upstream_socket_count"|"provider_connection_open_count"|"candidate_to_broker_bytes"|"broker_to_candidate_bytes"|"request_limit"|"response_limit"|"event_limit"|"journal_record_count"|"journal_bytes"|"off_plan_request"|"direct_provider_egress"|"credential_boundary"}`. All counts and counters are non-negative when non-null; routing-authority object count is at most 256 and routing-authority store byte count is at most 8,388,608; credential-echo scan-evidence object count is at most 257 and its store byte count is at most 1,052,672. Every digest is the full lower-case digest of the architecture-owned authority named by that field, never a digest invented from display data. `state=not_applicable` iff the inspected topology is not candidate and requires every other member null. For a candidate, a proved conflicting policy, identity, chain, count, ordered-set, routing-authority or credential-echo scan-evidence source tuple, counter, close, seal, or final relation is `conflicted`; otherwise inability to complete any required bounded read, routing-authority-source reopen, or credential-echo scan-evidence-source reopen is `indeterminate`; otherwise a valid `closing` journal, a valid controller-loss invalidation, a sealed invalidated outcome, or another selected non-complete terminal/breach code is `degraded`; and only a phase-valid `open` journal or `sealed` complete journal with no breach is `healthy`. This precedence is exact: conflicted, indeterminate, degraded, healthy.

For a valid `open|closing` candidate journal, policy and journal-identity digests, all three request counts, all three ordered request-record set digests, and the three-member routing-authority-source tuple are non-null only at a verified complete-frame prefix. The request-set digests represent those authenticated ordered prefixes, including the canonical empty prefixes. The routing tuple is indivisible: all three members are null, or the object count and store-byte count plus set digest are all non-null after same-descriptor reopening every authority object named by the issued prefix; then `candidate_provider_broker_routing_authority_object_count=issued_count`, store byte count is the checked canonical-byte sum in `0..8,388,608`, and set digest is the exact ordinal-row digest. A verified empty issued prefix therefore has object count zero, store-byte count zero, and the canonical empty routing-authority set digest. For every valid `open|closing` prefix, the credential-echo scan aggregate triple and scan-evidence source tuple are non-null. The aggregate triple exactly folds the authenticated terminal rows in request-ordinal then scan-ordinal order into `credential_echo_scan_evidence_count`, `candidate_provider_credential_echo_scan_evidence_run_set_digest`, and `credential_echo_scan_delivered_prefix_byte_count`. The source tuple exactly same-descriptor reopens every immutable evidence object in that fold and has `candidate_provider_credential_echo_scan_evidence_object_count=credential_echo_scan_evidence_count`, a checked canonical-byte sum in `0..1,052,672`, and the distinct identity-and-byte-count-bound `candidate_provider_credential_echo_scan_evidence_store_set_digest`. A verified empty terminal prefix therefore has scan count zero, canonical empty scan-evidence run-set digest, delivered-prefix count zero, evidence-object count zero, evidence-store byte count zero, and the canonical empty evidence-store set digest. Each remaining aggregate byte/control/socket/connection member and `generated_control_observation_run_set_digest` is non-null only when its entire run-prefix value is exactly derivable from that authenticated prefix; otherwise it is null, never a partial live-effect estimate or a per-request observation-set digest. Counts satisfy `0 <= consumed_count <= issued_count <= 256` and `0 <= terminal_count <= issued_count`. In `open`, close/seal/final digests, seal outcome, terminal code, and first-breach code are null, while checkpoint may still be null before the first durable checkpoint. In `closing`, close digest is non-null, the routing tuple is non-null and final for issuance, and it byte-matches the close frame and same-descriptor reopened sources; both credential-echo scan triples are non-null current-prefix facts: at the close boundary they byte-match the close frame's `preclose_*` tuple, and afterward they may only append ordinal-contiguous same-description-reopened evidence for already consumed work; seal/final digests plus seal outcome remain null. In `sealed`, close, seal, final-journal, and the seal's exact pre-seal checkpoint digests are non-null, `issued_count=terminal_count`, and all counts, request sets, the routing tuple, both credential-echo scan triples, generated-control observation run set, and aggregate counters are non-null and final. The routing tuple byte-matches close and seal, has object count equal to issued and terminal count, and recomputes from the same no-follow reopened final authority objects. The final scan aggregate and source tuples byte-match the seal and exactly fold terminal rows and no-follow reopened evidence objects; their initial prefix byte-matches the close frame's `preclose_*` tuple, and object count equals scan-evidence count. A complete seal additionally requires `consumed_count=issued_count`, `seal_outcome="complete"`, `terminal_code="complete"`, and null first-breach code. An invalidated seal requires `seal_outcome="invalidated"` and one of the four non-complete terminal codes; `policy_breach` requires one of `off_plan_request|direct_provider_egress|credential_boundary`, `resource_breach` requires one of the ten resource-limit literals, and `upstream_indeterminate|controller_invalidation` require null first-breach code. A lifecycle `invalidated` journal preserves only its independently verified prefix facts: checkpoint and close are non-null only when their complete frames precede the invalidation; the routing tuple is all non-null only when it recomputes from that exact last verified prefix and every same-descriptor source object, and is otherwise all null; both credential-echo scan triples are all non-null only when they exactly fold that prefix and every named evidence object reopens through the same retained descriptions, and are otherwise all null; seal, final-journal digest, and seal outcome are null; and terminal/first-breach codes are non-null only when an exact signed record or parent invalidation authority selects them. A conflicted or indeterminate projection likewise retains only independently authenticated, non-disputed safe members and uses null for every disputed or unreadable member; the routing tuple and each credential-echo scan triple remain all-or-null, and it never guesses a zero, empty-set digest, lifecycle state, terminal code, or breach code.

Every human result for `candidate prepare|start|stop|remove|status|validate-release` contains one bounded `provider broker` block carrying exactly the same state, lifecycle, full safe digests, request counts, routing-authority object count/store-byte count/set digest, credential-echo scan count/run-set/delivered-prefix aggregates, scan-evidence object count/store-byte count/store-set digest, aggregate counters, terminal code, and first-breach code as its JSON projection; null is rendered as unavailable and outside-candidate state as not applicable. Successful prepare projects only the authoritative post-publication `healthy/open` second-gate state, while successful start projects the authoritative pre-effect `healthy/open` state. Stop and validate-release may project `closing` only as durable pending; their terminal result projects `sealed|invalidated`, and release success requires `sealed`, `complete`, no breach, and final routing and credential-echo scan tuples equal to the close, seal, accounting, confinement, floor, export/import, and promotion authorities. Remove projects those same byte-identical tuples from the parent-retained terminal broker closure even after the candidate root is gone. Pre-intent failures project only safely collected pre-state and never represent prepare's separate parent absence proof as a fabricated broker inspection; usage/help never constructs an inspection. Neither renderer, check, warning, error, evidence reference, nor remediation may contain a credential, credential revision, account or candidate identity, individual capability or individual capability digest, individual routing-authority, credential-echo scan-evidence, or object-identity digest, request-envelope or individual request/response/event content digest, raw request/header/body/frame/event, routing-authority, or scan-evidence bytes, origin/path/query value, provider connection identity, PID, socket address, basename, or raw path. The schema's explicitly listed aggregate request/routing/credential-echo scan set digests, routing-authority and scan-evidence object counts, their store-byte counts, and other aggregate counts are permitted; their member bytes and member digests are not.

Doctor always includes `candidate.provider_broker` and includes the same `candidate_provider_broker:CandidateProviderBrokerInspectionV1` result member, including the three routing-authority-source fields, the credential-echo scan aggregate triple, and the three scan-evidence-source aggregate fields. Outside candidate topology the check is exactly `not_applicable/info` and changes no exit. Candidate state maps exactly as follows: `healthy` to `pass/info` and no broker diagnostic; `degraded` to `warn/warning`, code `candidate_provider_broker_degraded`, and exit 1 when it is the highest-precedence finding; `conflicted` to `fail/critical`, code `candidate_provider_broker_conflict`, and exit 3; and `indeterminate` to `unknown/critical`, code `candidate_provider_broker_indeterminate`, and exit 4. The three codes are stable. A routing or credential-echo scan tuple that disagrees with its count, close, seal, another selected authority, or any reopened source is conflicted; an otherwise required tuple that cannot be completely derived within the bounded read is indeterminate. Doctor carries degraded as `CommonWarningV1`; a prepare/start/release broker gate blocked by that state instead carries the same code as `CommonErrorV1` category `runtime`/exit 1. Conflict and indeterminate use `CommonErrorV1` with category `authority` and `io` respectively. Candidate status applies the same state/exit mapping through the existing snapshot precedence. `candidate prepare` does not require `healthy` before it creates the first broker authority: its pre-effect gate accepts only the parent transaction's exact absence/no-conflict proof and parent-creation authority, and its post-publication gate requires the same-descriptor `healthy/open` inspection above before success or candidate exposure. `candidate start` and `candidate validate-release` retain their pre-effect `healthy` broker gate and cannot create or repair a missing policy, journal, or routing source. Stop and remove may use an exact degraded terminal authority for cleanup, but a broker conflict or required-inspection indeterminacy still refuses with 3 or 4. Broker inspection never converts a successful exact stop/remove cleanup into failure merely because the retained run terminal code records failed validation.

### Lifecycle meanings

- `--manager auto` succeeds only when the snapshot proves one supported managed source responsible for the listener or one stopped configured manager with no conflicting listener. Structured primary authority is always the CQ socket LaunchAgent; Homebrew is accepted only as a pre-authority legacy source/lifecycle manager and is migrated to that LaunchAgent. `foreground` is not a legal structured manager value. A live or stopped foreground topology is import-only and must complete `authority import-legacy` before any rescue, service, listener migration, artifact, or policy mutation.
- Homebrew means exact formula `cq`, label `homebrew.mxcl.cq`, user domain, canonical `/opt/homebrew/bin/brew` or `/usr/local/bin/brew`, and only selectable plist `<os.UserHomeDir()>/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.cq.plist` acquired beneath retained home descriptor. `brew services info cq --json`, prefix, plist label/args, launchctl job, process, and listener must agree. Formula/Cellar templates are provenance only. LaunchDaemons, another user's tree, symlink aliases, or any other reported plist path are `ownership_conflict`. Mutation invokes exact absolute `brew services start|stop|restart cq`; feature migration targets CQ socket LaunchAgent.
- Primary CQ LaunchAgent label is exactly `dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy`, plist `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.jacobcx.cq.proxy.plist`, socket group `cq-proxy-listener`. Operations bind selected label/socket/launcher/artifact/plist/job/listener. Install atomically writes/syncs plist and bootstraps `Sockets`; start bootstraps/kickstarts and proves identity; restart retains socket definition/descriptor lineage and proves acknowledgement. Stop/uninstall and every listener/manager/socket-ABI release require immediate fresh `ClientStopProofV1`, the exact currently selected unexpired universal `ClientBearerBarrierReceiptV1`, zero unsupported/unregistered stateful or stateless sensitive request senders, credential domains, or request transports, zero connected/admitted work, and confirmation. `--confirm-client-stopped` is mandatory for stop, uninstall, candidate stop after listener exposure, launcher replacement, and any restart that may release listener/manager/socket ABI, but it never substitutes for either proof. LaunchAgent restart may omit only after proof same socket definition and descriptor lineage remain loaded; Homebrew restart always requires the full release gate. Missing conditional confirmation is usage failure; missing barrier readiness before intent refuses with exact `client-bearer-barrier stage` remediation. Readiness lost after safe quiescence selects `barrier_waiting`, retains the trusted launchd socket/inert-supervisor lineage, and returns pending rather than booting out or closing it. Barrier remains until target socket is loaded or terminal no-listener state. Stop bootouts job/socket only after the gate; uninstall then unlinks/syncs plist. Candidate stop retains plist; a proved never-exposed candidate may cleanup without a release proof, and remove unlinks only after terminal proof.
- Manual or foreign listeners are inspectable but not service-mutable. An exact live or stopped legacy foreground source remains inspectable and importable only; no structured command may adopt, hot-switch, start, stop, or persist desired state against it.
- Before composite authority exists, legacy lifecycle uses the exhaustive live/stopped action-proof table above; public `/health` alone never qualifies. Live evidence requires exact plist/job/PID-start/executable/listener correlation plus a fresh serving-attestation challenge, while stopped evidence requires exact supported-manager configuration and proved job/process/listener/competitor absence and never a fabricated challenge. CQ LaunchAgent permits start/restart/stop/uninstall; Homebrew permits start/restart/stop; foreground permits none. A permitted start/restart returns mutation success 0 only after exact fresh target-live proof; stop/uninstall returns 0 only after its exact absence proof. Each external manager/plist action has its own precommitted attempt ID through the parent `LegacyLifecycleActionStore`; an already-effective live start or stopped stop records a terminal idempotent result without external invocation. Reconciled status remains `legacy`/1. Unsupported manager/action pairs create no intent and print the exact stop or import remediation. Active/ambiguous journal state routes only to `recovery transition`, and no legacy proof can authorise rescue, routing-policy acknowledgement, artifact switch, or compatibility-floor advance.
- Ambiguous managers, plist/service-process/listener executable disagreement, or foreign ownership are hard conflicts. Difference between inspector binary and internally consistent service/runtime binary is version skew and warning, not conflict.
- `service artifact switch` and candidate artifact switch accept only the full digest of an already-published signed release set in the selected instance; bare executable paths and implicit artifact import are forbidden. The command resolves the unique role manifest/payload from that set, reopens and verifies the signed set and payload before intent and action, and rejects an absent/ambiguous role or any launcher/private ABI and feature mismatch with the retained counterpart. Worker rejects manager, commits `worker_switch`, and restarts only the private child. Supervisor requires exact LaunchAgent, commits verifying generation and one kickstart, inherits the socket, then acknowledges. Runtime-bundle resolves and switches the matched supervisor/worker pair atomically. Launcher requires client-stop/drain/no-bearer proof plus flag, commits `launcher_upgrade`, and proves old/new launcher/plist/socket ABI. Candidate switching additionally requires the exact sealed validation run and a release set retained by that run. None changes listener/config identity.
- Rollback-floor clear refuses while an artifact is active, referenced by a transition or marker, required by the compatibility floor, or the sole last verified compatible artifact. Rescue exit never substitutes that floor worker into the current supervisor. A failed exit stays rescue; changing the selected pair requires explicit `service artifact switch --role runtime-bundle --manager launchagent` while rescue, followed by a new exit operation. No legacy foreground source can become a rollback floor or rescue runtime.
- Before mutation, a structured lifecycle command prints exact target manager, label, listener, signed release-set digest, and resolved executable digest. A pre-authority legacy lifecycle command instead prints manager, label, listener, and resolved executable digest plus `release_set=not_applicable`; it never invents signed release provenance.
- Deadlines use boot-wide monotonic clock and exhaustive table below. `Total` is compiled maximum, `Minimum forward` is shortest admitted forward-action window, and `Reserve` is untouched recovery/terminal-snapshot window. User total `T` is legal exactly when `minimum_forward + reserve <= T <= Total`; forward work stops at `T - reserve`. Unsafe value rejects before locks/writes. Every child/control call gets nested deadline. At `T` a bounded command returns terminal result or durable pending; no unbounded cleanup follows. `logs --follow` instead obeys its fixed attachment deadline and, only after successful attachment, streams until interruption or a mapped follow error.

`CandidateProviderBrokerInspectionV1` creates no child deadline and never widens or resets a leaf context. Candidate status and doctor complete broker inspection and receipt-export selection inside their existing ten-second pure-read/reconciled-read totals. Receipt-export selection performs only the bounded same-descriptor parent-anchor, selected-attempt, selected-terminal-relation, and exact named-receipt reopens below; it never creates a child deadline, lists a directory, or scans retained receipts. Prepare, start, stop, remove, and validate-release perform their first broker-authority read only after lexical help/usage and before their first candidate or provider effect, then derive the result from authorities durably selected within the same existing 300/120/30, 90/15/15, 30/15/15, or Begin-bound 420/30 partition respectively. Final rendering, including a parent-retained removal projection, stops at the leaf's effective total cutoff; timeout leaves a safely selected pending authority observable and never starts an extra read, controller wake, journal append, seal, provider operation, or post-deadline cleanup merely to populate the projection.

Rows select exact command leaves, not an operation-family prefix. Ordinary and operation-recovery rows are fixed, accept no `--timeout`, begin after lexical help/usage and before classification or store access, and use only their command-scoped dispatcher context. Inherited `G*` on an ordinary non-`check` row selects the same row and exact total/forward/reserve tuple as flag-free argv; discarding it cannot create, reset, shorten, or extend a context. `check` includes every selected provider operation, mixed-provider join, instance-cache work, report render, and `burn_history_v1` commit. Account mutation includes discovery/refresh and credential/cache/projection reconciliation. Login callback acceptance ends at the absolute command-start-plus-300-second cutoff and exchange/commit forward work ends at command-start-plus-315 seconds; no callback, browser wait, exchange, or fresh owner effect begins during the 45-second reserve. The operation-recovery status leaf remains non-mutating even though it shares the 30/15/15 budget with recover: it spends forward time only on authenticated same-descriptor local store/receipt selection and safe snapshot, never opens owner control, sends a control frame, creates a recovery request, reconciles a journal, selects a successor, or acknowledges. An active-chain recover first proves a matching live authenticated owner-control connection and every caller/authority/runtime/listener relation; a live authenticated relation mismatch stops before request construction and uses only the remaining forward window to produce conflict/3 with null remediation. Only a fully matching connection may construct its authenticated request from the one dispatcher context after selected-chain authentication and before the 15-second forward cutoff. `ControlRecover` admission and every new recovery action stop at that cutoff. If the complete request is rejected while the matching authenticated connection remains live, the dispatcher performs no new action or durable mutation and uses the remaining reserve only for safe snapshot and render/flush of `recovery_control=admission_failed`, state `indeterminate`, `operator_operation_indeterminate`/4, with null remediation. If no matching control is reachable, including absent/stopped/inhibited/unreachable service or connection loss before an authenticated admission result, it creates no request or other durable object, uses the remaining forward time only for safe classification/snapshot work, and reserves the final fifteen seconds only for safe snapshot and render/flush of `recovery_control=unavailable`, state `indeterminate`, `operator_operation_indeterminate`/4, plus the exact service-start remediation. Direct retained-receipt projection creates no request. Reserve after an admitted recovery may finish only already-authorised exact reconciliation, safe snapshot, render/flush, sync, and acknowledgement, and the acknowledgement is legal exactly while its current-boot tick is strictly below the recovery request's 30-second total deadline. The operation's original deadline neither shortens nor extends this recovery acknowledgement window; original-command acknowledgement instead remains bound to the original request's own boot and total deadline. The four named `handoff` leaves match only their 10-second/1-second/1-second row and never inherit the surrounding adopt, initialise, import, or migrate budget; their minimum legal caller-supplied total is therefore two seconds. Those surrounding rows expressly exclude both `status` and `handoff`. For every emission-capable invocation, the FD writer receives only the forward child context and must stop before `T-reserve`; it may neither begin nor continue a write at that cutoff. A first emission performed by adopt/initialise/import/migrate prepare remains inside that prepare leaf's forward window; `recovery initialise resume` emission remains inside its 30-second forward window. The untouched reserve is used only to authenticate and durably retain the still-pending selected state, form the safe `LocalTokenHandoffOutputV1`, render/flush the typed result, and perform already-authorised bounded sync; it never writes the FD, retries emission, advances cutover state, or starts another effect. Optional resume without an FD performs no handoff work. Gate selection does not change a lifecycle leaf's budget: an admitted pre-authority legacy `service start|restart|stop|uninstall` uses the same exact service-leaf row as its structured counterpart, while `service install` has only the structured-primary row. Barrier stage and refresh each use only their dedicated row; stage against `barrier_waiting` does not inherit transition-recovery time. The separate `recovery transition resume` leaf uses only 180/120/60, begins before reopening the selected child/barrier facts, propagates that one deadline through fresh proof and the resumed lifecycle suffix, and never borrows or resets the earlier lifecycle or stage budget. Candidate prepare's bootstrap stays inside its 300-second total. The validation rows enumerate every non-release validation leaf explicitly; primary-versus-candidate selection never changes the `validate-installed` budget. The release-validation row is the sole Begin-relative exception to a command-start duration: it records `C0` before first access, uses Begin+960 seconds as its absolute outer command deadline, includes all pre-admission work, admits only by Begin+510 with 450 seconds still available, and then narrows to its signed 420/30 partition without reset. Auxiliary rows have fixed deadlines and no caller-controlled timeout: every ordinary auxiliary spelling rejects `--timeout`, while `agent install|uninstall`, `models refresh`, and `models overlay prune` discard that exact token only as an inert non-help tail under their baseline rules. Public auxiliary rows create the command-scoped `DispatchAuxiliaryCommandV1` or `DispatchRefreshCommandV1` context, while `implicit_ensure_agent` uses only a complete 10/5/5 child interval derived within the still-live parent ordinary total and is skipped with zero effect when that interval cannot fit. Interactive refresh reauthentication input is part of the 270-second forward window and timeout closes the prompt without starting another login or refresh; reserve performs only exact already-committed credential/cache or refresh-agent topology reconciliation.

The fixed endpoint-inspect timer begins after lexical/help dispatch and before the first configuration, process, or network access. For endpoint transition, interactive confirmation and bounded ticket framing complete before the 60-second action timer; once confirmed, every lock, credential-owner call, endpoint action, child process, and final snapshot inherits that deadline. Port-only `validate-http` begins its 30-second timer after bounded argument parsing and before singleton authority inspection; request publication, lock acquisition, restart, cancellation/poisoning, marker invalidation, and the final identity check all inherit it. None of these compatibility paths may use `context.Background()` or continue cleanup after expiry. Timeout preserves every already durable request, poison, ticket, or transition state, emits no false success, and exits legacy code 1.

Quarantine reset requires stopped job/listener, exclusive stable lifecycle lock, valid bootstrap reset identity, and no active coordinator except the matching reset operation. It follows the parent-scoped coordinator/ledger replacement protocol above; every crash resumes or restores by exact identities. It never recursively copies, guesses identity, or deletes quarantine before terminal topology. After rollback becomes illegal, the command's existing confirmation authorises only the recorded bounded finaliser and tombstone.

`ClientBearerBarrierV1` is sender-enforced and never inferred from process absence, confirmation, launch order, public health, or successful port connection. It covers every stateful or stateless `LocalTokenClientRegistryV1.request_senders` member capable of sending sensitive application bytes to the public loopback endpoint, whether or not that sender can emit `Authorization`, including `cq_config_read_per_call_v1`. Immediately before opening every cold-login initial connection, reconnect, or other HTTP/1, HTTP/2, compact, retained, or WebSocket transport—and before constructing, queueing, or writing any application byte—the sender obtains one single-use owner-control-MAC permit binding `{schema_version:1,proxy_instance_id,operation_id:null|string,sender_identity_digest,adapter_id,sender_executable_digest,config_binding_digest,credential_domain:null|string,request_transport,token_fingerprint_generation:null|string,listener_generation,socket_definition_digest,launchd_job_generation,barrier_protocol_digest,sender_pid,sender_start_time,nonce,issued_at,valid_until}` with lifetime at most five seconds. Null credential domain and token generation are legal only for a registry-attested no-Authorization sender. `operation_id` is null during ordinary steady operation and equals the exact selected listener-release, migration, or promotion operation while its barrier is active. The stateless CQ adapter reopens its selected immutable config source before each permit and retains neither token nor permit between calls. Permit issue shares the exclusive listener-release gate and succeeds only while the complete current request-sender registry, credential-domain/token-fingerprint and request-transport projections, and exact launchd socket/supervisor lineage attest; release waits for every permit to be consumed or expire. Failure to obtain or validate a permit forbids connect and write; if a connect raced before failure was observed, the sender closes it with `application_bytes_written=0`. Application bytes mean the complete request target, every header including `Authorization`, HTTP/1 body/chunks, HTTP/2 header/data frames, compact or retained bytes, WebSocket upgrade request, and every WebSocket frame; TLS and kernel transport bytes are not application bytes. No request serializer, streaming producer, retry, prewarm, or WebSocket writer may run before permit validation. Any missing hook, sender/domain/transport omission, unknown/manual sender, or executable/config/protocol mismatch is unsupported or unregistered and blocks every listener release, migration, and promotion.

`ClientBearerBarrierReceiptV1={schema_version:1,client_build,client_executable_digest,sender_registry_revision,request_sender_set_digest,authorization_sender_set_digest,sender_executable_set_digest,config_binding_set_digest,credential_domain_set_digest,request_transport_set_digest,token_fingerprint_generation_digest,barrier_protocol_set_digest,barrier_case_set_digest,cold_login_result:"passed",initial_connect_result:"passed",reconnect_result:"passed",foreign_bind_result:"application_withheld",release_window_result:"passed",issued_at,not_after,nonce,issuer_public_key,signature}` is produced only by a selected candidate controller running the universal request-sender corpus, has `not_after` no later than `issued_at+24h`, and proves the complete sender/domain/transport corpus rather than only the installed Codex process or bearer confidentiality. Barrier bootstrap or refresh may precede installed-client preflight; when a preflight receipt names it, both receipts must have the same controller/run identity and the barrier receipt expires no later than that preflight receipt. `barrier_case_set_digest` is the domain-separated digest of closed canonical `RequestSenderBarrierCaseSetV1={schema_version:1,cases:[{sender_identity_digest,credential_domain:null|string,release_member:null|"service_stop|service_uninstall|candidate_stop|process_managed_legacy_restart|legacy_import_activation|listener_migration|launcher_upgrade_socket_abi",phase:"cold_login|initial_connect|reconnect|release_window|foreign_bind",local_token_state:"changed|unchanged|not_applicable",transport_results:{http:null|BarrierTransportResultV1,compact:null|BarrierTransportResultV1,retained:null|BarrierTransportResultV1,websocket:null|BarrierTransportResultV1}}]}` where closed `BarrierTransportResultV1={result:"permit_accepted|application_withheld",connection_attempted:boolean,application_bytes_written:integer}` and the integer is 0–65,536 only for a positive isolated-harness `permit_accepted` case and exactly zero for `application_withheld`. Null transport entries equal the sender's unsupported transports; every registered transport is non-null. Cases are sorted and duplicate-free; they contain one positive ordinary cold-login/initial-connect/reconnect case for every request-sender/domain-or-null membership, the complete request-sender/domain-or-null Cartesian product for every closed release member's release-window and foreign-bind cases, and both changed and unchanged token cases for `cq_local_token`. Every release-window or foreign-bind transport result is `application_withheld` with `application_bytes_written=0`; the harness independently captures and proves zero request-target, header, body/chunk, HTTP/2 frame, compact/retained, WebSocket-handshake, and WebSocket-frame bytes. With fixed 17-sender, 49 domain-or-null-membership, four-transport, and seven-release-member maxima this remains at most 1,071 cases, each carrying four bounded results: `3 × 49 + 2 × 7 × (49 + 17)`. The canonical case-set object is at most 4 MiB, contains no raw request, header, credential, or payload, is stored and same-descriptor reopened under candidate runtime evidence, and is pinned by barrier selection, preflight, and release provenance before its external locator may be released; case 1,072, byte 4,194,305, fifth transport result, nonzero withheld byte, missing request component, extra, wrong-result, or cross-sender/domain/transport/release-member case refuses the receipt. The read-only collector and release gate derive closed in-memory `RequestSenderBarrierBindingV1={schema_version:1,operation_id:null|string,sender_registry_revision,request_sender_set_digest,authorization_sender_set_digest,sender_executable_set_digest,config_binding_set_digest,credential_domain_set_digest,request_transport_set_digest,token_fingerprint_generation_digest,listener_generation,socket_definition_digest,launchd_job_generation,barrier_protocol_set_digest,barrier_case_set_digest,barrier_receipt_digest}` from current authoritative sources; its domain-separated canonical digest is the exact readiness binding. The receipt and binding are tied through the selected barrier anchor, preflight, confinement, import ticket or listener-migration/promotion intent, CU-9 marker children, and release provenance. `ClientStopProofV1` binds the exact operation ID, readiness-binding digest, listener/socket/job generations, complete request/authorisation-sender, executable, config, domain, transport, token-generation, protocol, case-set, and barrier-receipt digests, observed PID/start tuples, zero active permits, zero connected/admitted work, observation time, five-second expiry, and authority MAC. A field mismatch or unavailable enumeration makes readiness false and the release gate fail closed. At login/reboot another UID may bind first, but every conforming sender, including a no-Authorization sender and the stateless CQ adapter, writes zero application bytes because it cannot obtain the permit. There is no acknowledgement-only release path.

The privacy-safe projection is closed `ClientBearerBarrierProjectionV1={state:"ready|unsupported|unregistered|stale|unavailable",sender_registry_revision_hint:null|string,sender_set_digest_hint:null|string,binding_digest_hint:null|string,supported_senders:null|integer,unsupported_senders:null|integer,unregistered_senders:null|integer,credential_domain_count:null|integer,request_transport_count:null|integer,receipt_state:"valid|absent|expired|mismatched|unavailable",receipt_not_after:null|string,operation_bound:boolean,ready:boolean}`. A non-null count is non-negative; hints are bounded opaque prefixes and never identify a sender, executable, configuration source, credential domain, request transport, token fingerprint, or operation. State derivation is deterministic in this precedence: unavailable authoritative enumeration/binding/receipt inspection gives `unavailable`; otherwise any unsupported sender gives `unsupported`; otherwise any unregistered sender gives `unregistered`; otherwise an absent, expired, mismatched, or binding-drifted receipt gives `stale`; only complete current request-sender enumeration, zero unsupported/unregistered senders, a valid unexpired exact receipt, and exact `RequestSenderBarrierBindingV1` equality gives `ready`. `receipt_state=absent|expired|mismatched` therefore always maps to `state=stale`; `ready=true` iff `state=ready`. For snapshot and doctor, a completed derivation is a known `client_bearer_barrier:Fact<object>` even when not ready, while unavailable required inspection is an unavailable fact with null value; detailed owner health instead emits the direct `unavailable` projection. Barrier absence or staleness alone does not make an otherwise serving data plane unhealthy. Doctor check `client.bearer_barrier` is `pass/info` when ready, `warn/warning` when not ready but no listener-release/migration/promotion operation is selected, `fail/critical` when such an operation is selected, and `unknown/critical` when its required inspection is unavailable. The selected-operation fail is a policy conflict and maps to exit 3; the required-inspection unknown maps to exit 4; idle warning maps to exit 1.

`ClientBearerBarrierSelectionStoreV1` is the per-instance crash authority at `readiness/client-bearer-barrier/`. Closed `ClientBearerBarrierSelectionV1={schema_version:1,selection_generation,previous_selection_digest,proxy_instance_id,role:"primary|candidate",receipt_digest,barrier_case_set_digest,source_candidate_proxy_instance_id,validation_run_id,client_build,client_executable_digest,sender_registry_revision,request_sender_set_digest,authorization_sender_set_digest,sender_executable_set_digest,config_binding_set_digest,credential_domain_set_digest,request_transport_set_digest,token_fingerprint_generation_digest,barrier_protocol_set_digest,selected_for_operation_id:null|string,issued_at,not_after,selected_at,mac}` contains no sender identity, path, token, credential, header, payload, or signing key. Its authority-MACed anchor is `{schema_version:1,selection_digest,selection_generation,mac}`. Generation zero is physical anchor absence. Every later selection increments once, names the prior selection digest or canonical null at generation one, and is valid only while every receipt field equals the same-descriptor reopened signed receipt/case set and the target's current complete registry/build/executable/config/domain/transport/token-generation/protocol facts. `selected_for_operation_id` is null for idle/bootstrap selection and the exact active listener-release operation ID for an operation-addressed stage. Readiness additionally requires exact equality between that field and the current active listener-release operation ID, including null on both sides; an operation-bound selection is stale after that operation terminalises and cannot silently become ordinary readiness.

Barrier receipt, case set, selection, and anchor publication is ordered: securely reopen the source candidate bootstrap, controller/run chain, signed receipt and content-addressed case set; verify every signature/digest/expiry/cap/binding; copy each canonical object through random-exclusive temporary, file sync, no-replace rename, directory sync, and same-descriptor reopen; publish the immutable selection; then compare-and-replace and sync the one anchor from the exact prior bytes. A crash before anchor CAS leaves the prior selection effective and new objects inert; a crash after CAS resolves only by reopening exact old/new anchor digests. The subtree retains current plus previous selection/receipt/case set and two temporaries: at most nine regular files and 16 MiB; each selection/receipt is at most 64 KiB and each case set at most 4 MiB. Active listener-release, preflight, import, migration, feature, release, history, or recovery references pin their exact objects. Reference-aware GC removes only unselected, unreferenced old objects after anchor/operation checkpoints and directory sync. Collision inequality, a tenth file, first byte over a component or aggregate cap, or ambiguous residue refuses before target anchor CAS.

`candidate client-bearer-barrier refresh` produces the source objects without a protected-listener release. `client-bearer-barrier stage` copies/selects them in a target primary or candidate. If a listener-release operation is active, `--operation-id` is required and must equal it; if none is active the flag is forbidden. Stage performs no process, manager, listener, config, registry, token, authority-generation, candidate-success, or coordinator transition. It is one semantic selection-anchor CAS, not a multi-phase coordinator operation; every preceding object publication is inert and cannot affect readiness. Fresh primary initialisation uses its mandatory distinct `--candidate-instance-state-root` capability to copy and select the exact barrier receipt/case set named by the imported preactivation receipt in its staged root, and legacy import does the same from its claimed candidate preflight, before any target listener action; candidate prepare performs its bootstrap selection before candidate listener exposure. Thus first activation never depends on a post-release stage or ID-to-path inference. A later stale primary or failed candidate can obtain a fresh selection by preparing/refreshing another isolated candidate and staging its receipt while the protected listener remains continuously owned. If no valid source exists, status reports stale and every release stays refused or `barrier_waiting`; no command releases the port to create validation evidence.

`client-bearer-barrier status` is a non-creating selection/binding inspection. It reports the privacy-safe projection plus selection state `absent|selected|operation_bound|invalid|unavailable`, selection generation, full receipt and case-set digests only when safely selected, `selected_for_operation_id`, and receipt expiry; it never wakes a controller or opens a source-candidate path. Its `proxy_setting.state` is exactly `effective` for ready `selected|operation_bound`, `degraded` for absent or expired stale selection, `invalid` for unsupported, unregistered, mismatched, or otherwise invalid selection, and `unavailable` for required-inspection unavailability. `stage` reports old/new selection digests, source validation-run and receipt digests, operation binding, proof, and deadline, but no raw path or source identity. Refresh reports the selected candidate/run, prior/new receipt and case-set digests, expiry, corpus result, proof, and deadline. Missing/expired source receipt is conflict/3, a completed but unsuccessful corpus is failed/1, a safely durable unresolved publication is pending/1, and required inspection unavailability is 4.

For barrier CLI parsing, `--receipt` is exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters and `--source-candidate-state-root` is a distinct required secure root selector, never the target `INSTANCE`; malformed digest, missing source, a source/target alias, or a prefix is `proxy_usage`/64 before either root opens. The optional `--operation-id` obeys the global full-ID grammar and its presence rule is decided only after both lexical parsing and non-mutating target operation inspection; wrong presence or a well-formed nonmatching ID is conflict/3 with zero selection write.

Candidate prepare's mandatory `--local-token-client-registry` is the exact same closed manifest grammar used by fresh initialisation/import. It is securely copied and bound into the prepared-core input, complete sender enumeration, barrier bootstrap receipt, and candidate authority before the corpus runs. A later preactivation/import/stage target must select a byte-identical registry revision and client/sender/domain set; omission, unsafe source, or mismatch refuses before candidate initialisation or receipt creation.

### JSON envelope

New proxy JSON uses one discriminated additive envelope:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "kind": "proxy_snapshot",
  "ok": true,
  "state": "healthy",
  "result": {},
  "warnings": [],
  "errors": []
}
```

`schema_version`, `kind`, `ok`, `state`, `result`, `warnings`, and `errors` are always present. `schema_version` is integer `1`; `ok` is true exactly when exit code is 0; `result` is an object even on failure and contains any safe facts collected. `warnings` and `errors` are arrays, never null. Unknown object fields are additive and consumers must ignore them; producers never emit an unknown enum under schema 1. Human output is explicitly not machine-stable.

This envelope also governs `cq operation ... --json`; the section name “proxy JSON” denotes the schema family, not a required `proxy` argv prefix. Ordinary `check --json` otherwise retains its baseline report envelope, including after a terminal recovered check result.

Errors affecting exit live in top-level `errors`; best-effort collector failures live in fact object so `info` may remain successful. Common `Fact<T>` is `{status: known|absent|invalid|unavailable|permission_denied, value: T|null, error_code: string|null}` and requires null value unless status is `known`. `CommonErrorV1` is `{code:string,category:usage|authority|configuration|ownership|runtime|policy|network|io|internal,exit_code:1|2|3|4|64,message:string,field:string|null,retryable:boolean,evidence_refs:[string]}`. `CommonWarningV1` is `{code:string,category:authority|configuration|ownership|runtime|policy|network|io|privacy|compatibility,message:string,field:string|null,evidence_refs:[string],remediation_command:string|null}`; warning has no exit code, never changes `ok` by itself, and is sorted by `(category,code,field,message)`. Error/warning `code` and `Fact.error_code` are additive open strings; only fields explicitly named as closed enums are closed in schema 1. Common check is `{id:string,status:pass|warn|fail|unknown|not_applicable,severity:info|warning|error|critical,summary:string,evidence_refs:[string],remediation_command:string|null}`. Times are UTC RFC3339 with fractional seconds allowed; durations/deadlines are non-negative integer milliseconds; counts/generations are non-negative JSON integers; digests are lower-case full hexadecimal unless a field is explicitly named `hint`. Messages and evidence are safe, bounded, and identifier-free unless command explicitly requests identity.

The closed privacy-safe `CandidateReceiptExportProjectionV1={active_attempt:null|{attempt_id,export_generation,phase:"intent|temporary_created|temporary_synced|renamed|parent_synced"},compact_terminal_receipt:null|{kind:"candidate_receipt_export_terminal_receipt_v1",attempt_id,export_generation,candidate_receipt_export_terminal_receipt_digest,terminal_outcome:"published|conflicted"}}` is an output projection only, never a third receipt-export authority, selector, key, derivation domain, or result form. Exactly the selected-parent rule below determines its two members.

Every result row requiring `instance:Fact<object>` projects the matrix through closed `InstanceInspectionProjectionV1={selector_kind:"default_primary|explicit",topology:"legacy_primary_live|legacy_primary_stopped|primary|candidate",sealed_role:null|"primary"|"candidate",role_source:"legacy_attestation|bootstrap_authority"}` when the fact is `known`; its `error_code` is null and its values exactly equal the corresponding `InspectInstanceResultV1` fields. An absent fact has null value and `instance_uninitialised`; an invalid fact has null value and the same precedence-selected `authority_invalid|ownership_conflict|generation_conflict|instance_mismatch` code; a permission-denied fact has null value and `permission_denied`; another unavailable fact has null value and the exact stable collector code. Safe locator/config/service facts remain in their independent projections. Fact projection alone never promotes its error into top-level `errors`: after all independent collectors finish, the selected leaf's closed topology×role requirement matrix decides whether that fact is required. A primary-semantic, candidate-only, or mutation leaf that the matrix rejects promotes the exact fact error once and uses its matrix exit. A role-neutral `info` or `config path` keeps partial-invalid, absent, permission-denied, and unavailable operational state nested when its own path/collector requirements succeed, retains empty top-level `errors`, and follows its read-side exit oracle; failures of those commands' own required path acquisition remain top-level. Thus JSON never invents `role=primary` for an absent reserved root, never omits a role failure fact when the selected leaf rejects that role, and never turns best-effort role-neutral inspection into a false command failure.

Kind states are closed in schema 1: `proxy_usage` uses `invalid`; `operator_operation` uses `idle|accepted|pending|succeeded|failed|conflicted|indeterminate`; `proxy_snapshot`/`proxy_checks` use `healthy|legacy|rescue_draining|rescue|rescue_exit_draining|degraded|down|conflicted|indeterminate`; `proxy_health` uses `healthy|degraded|down|conflicted|indeterminate`; `proxy_mode` uses `normal|rescue_draining|rescue|rescue_exit_draining|pending|degraded|down|conflicted|indeterminate`; `proxy_config` uses `valid|absent|invalid|unavailable`; `proxy_setting`, `codex_delegations`, `codex_pools`, `codex_sessions`, and `codex_capabilities` use `effective|pending|degraded|unavailable|invalid`; transition kinds use `idle|committed|effective|pending|failed|conflicted|indeterminate`; `proxy_probe` uses `succeeded|unknown|unsupported|failed`; `proxy_recovery` uses `idle|inspected|committed|pending|failed|conflicted|indeterminate`; `proxy_validation_transition` uses `validated|pending|failed|conflicted`. `idle` is legal only for an initialise/import/adopt/migrate or feature-activation status view, `recovery initialise status`/`recovery transition status`, or operation status with no active operation in that leaf. Status without an explicit operation selector chooses exactly one anchored nonterminal operation; no active operation returns `idle`, more than one returns `conflicted`, and retained terminal history is never chosen implicitly. An explicit selector may reopen its exact retained terminal object; a well-formed selector miss is `failed`/`requested_object_absent`/3 in the leaf kind, while malformed or prefix selectors are `proxy_usage`/64 before state access. Each result projection field named in table is required; unavailable scalar/object uses null, unavailable collection uses empty array plus companion `Fact` or error, never omitted. Schema fixtures define nested snapshot/transition structures and are checked as canonical JSON Schema documents shipped with CLI. Every envelope-producing command in the canonical tree and operation-recovery tree has one table mapping success/failure to exactly one kind.

Candidate status and doctor each run receipt-export inspection as an independent bounded read after common instance inspection has authenticated the exact selected bootstrap's `candidate_proxy_instance_id` and `validation_run_id`. The collector accepts only that pair, returns one complete `Fact<CandidateReceiptExportProjectionV1>`, creates or changes no authority, and neither consumes nor derives a result from `candidate_validation` or `candidate_provider_broker`. Result composition always places the fact at top-level `result.candidate_receipt_export`; the candidate-status producer never emits `candidate_validation.value.receipt_export`. Failure or absence in this collector does not erase independently collected base-snapshot, validation, or broker facts, and a failure in another collector does not rewrite an independently authenticated receipt-export fact. Every candidate-status envelope requires a non-null top-level Fact object. Outside candidate topology it is exactly `{status:"absent",value:null,error_code:null}` without export-store inspection. For an inspected candidate, authenticated exact absence uses `known` with the non-null both-null projection below; an invalid binding uses `invalid`, null value, and `candidate_receipt_export_conflict`; an unavailable bounded read or required permission denial uses respectively `unavailable|permission_denied`, null value, and `candidate_receipt_export_indeterminate`. No other status/value/error nullability is legal.

Candidate status and doctor resolve receipt export only from the current parent-selected authority for the inspected bootstrap's exact `candidate_proxy_instance_id` and `validation_run_id`. Selection is total and ordered. First, when the authenticated export anchor selects a nonterminal `CandidateReceiptExportAttemptV1`, `active_attempt` is that exact attempt and `compact_terminal_receipt` is null. This branch wins even when either or both older retained compact receipts exist and even after a same-generation compact receipt file has been durably published but before the terminal-attempt anchor CAS. Second, only when the anchor selects the matching terminal attempt, or after anchor retirement the authenticated row-three `receipt_export_terminal_v1` relation selects that same terminal attempt and compact receipt with its exact anchor-absence proof, `active_attempt` is null and `compact_terminal_receipt` is that selected generation's exact receipt. Third, exact pre-promotion absence or authenticated legal row-three/result retirement yields a known value with both members null. A retained compact receipt without that current selected terminal relation never enters implicit status or doctor; it remains available only through exact `candidate receipt show --attempt-id ID`. No path lists `receipts/`, orders filenames, scans retained results, or infers authority from the numerically greatest retained generation.

Every selected attempt or terminal relation must byte-match the inspected candidate and validation run, its anchor and row-three `export_generation`, attempt ID, promotion receipt, journal/routing-source tuple, terminal selection, and output relation. Active generation remains the generation already authenticated when the attempt was created; the reader never recomputes it from retained files. A cross-candidate, cross-run, cross-generation, multiple-selected-anchor, selected-attempt, terminal-receipt, anchor-absence, or row-three mismatch makes the fact `invalid` with null value and `candidate_receipt_export_conflict`. Inability to complete a required bounded same-descriptor reopen makes it `unavailable` with null value and `candidate_receipt_export_indeterminate`; required permission denial uses `permission_denied`. Known active, selected terminal, and legal-empty states use `status=known`, non-null `CandidateReceiptExportProjectionV1`, and null `error_code`; no other nullability is legal. Controller loss before promotion yields legal empty, while loss after promotion preserves the same active parent attempt until the selected terminal relation exists.

Candidate status maps a known active attempt to `degraded`/exit 1 with `candidate_receipt_export_pending`; a selected compact `published` receipt and legal empty state add no degradation; a selected compact `conflicted` receipt or invalid relation maps to `conflicted`/exit 3 with `candidate_receipt_export_conflict`; and unavailable or permission-denied required inspection maps to `indeterminate`/exit 4 with `candidate_receipt_export_indeterminate`, subject to the existing snapshot precedence. Human candidate status emits exactly one corresponding safe line: `receipt export: active attempt <attempt-id> generation <export-generation> phase <phase>`, `receipt export: terminal <published|conflicted> attempt <attempt-id> generation <export-generation> receipt <digest>`, `receipt export: none`, `receipt export: conflicted`, or `receipt export: indeterminate`.

Doctor always emits top-level `candidate_receipt_export` and stable check `candidate.receipt_export`. Outside candidate topology its fact is absent with null value/error and its check is `not_applicable/info`; a candidate legal-empty value is likewise `not_applicable/info`. A known active attempt is `warn/warning`, emits `candidate_receipt_export_pending` as `CommonWarningV1`, and produces exit 1 when highest precedence. A selected compact `published` receipt is `pass/info`. A selected compact `conflicted` receipt or invalid fact is `fail/critical`, emits `candidate_receipt_export_conflict` as `CommonErrorV1` category `authority`, and produces exit 3. Unavailable or permission-denied required inspection is `unknown/critical`, emits `candidate_receipt_export_indeterminate` as `CommonErrorV1` category `io`, and produces exit 4. Given the same authenticated inspection snapshot, candidate status and doctor project byte-identical top-level Fact bytes; only their enclosing snapshot/check state composition differs. Doctor human and JSON projections byte-match the same selected branch. Neither candidate status nor doctor exposes an output locator, basename, temporary basename, parent identity, final identity, conflict-proof digest, promotion or receipt bytes, observed output bytes, key material, raw path, or any unselected or older retained attempt ID/digest.

Every bounded new-tree mutator supports `--json` except the frozen raw `proxy start` spelling, including its foreground and sealed internal process branches. Frozen status, flat aliases, port-only `validate-http`, and endpoint maintenance retain legacy output and exits without envelopes. Bounded `logs` and unbounded `logs --follow` are raw escaped-record commands and have no JSON mode. Root-form `validate-http` supports JSON but preserves empty success stdout without it. Detailed/public health without `--json` emits its explicitly specified canonical raw object. No other raw-output exception exists.

Stable envelope codes include `invalid_usage`, `confirmation_required`, `requested_object_absent`, `candidate_provider_broker_degraded`, `candidate_provider_broker_conflict`, `candidate_provider_broker_indeterminate`, `candidate_receipt_export_pending`, `candidate_receipt_export_conflict`, `candidate_receipt_export_indeterminate`, `instance_uninitialised`, `instance_mismatch`, `config_absent`, `config_invalid`, `headroom_unsupported`, `authority_invalid`, `permission_denied`, `unsupported_platform`, `manager_absent`, `manager_ambiguous`, `ownership_conflict`, `listener_conflict`, `runtime_unavailable`, `runtime_identity_mismatch`, `compatibility_incompatible`, `feature_inactive`, `generation_conflict`, `policy_invalid`, `stale_generation`, `transition_pending`, `timeout_pending`, `operator_operation_pending`, `operator_operation_cancelled`, `operator_operation_failed`, `operator_login_restart_required`, `operator_operation_indeterminate`, `probe_unsupported`, `probe_failed`, `sensitive_confirmation_required`, `sensitive_retention_unavailable`, `resource_capacity_exhausted`, `handoff_output_failed`, `io_precommit_failed`, `io_commit_sync_unknown`, and `internal_error`. Doctor always emits stable check catalogue: `instance.root`, `config.exists|parse|permissions|local_token_strength|object_retention|payload_consent`, `authority.integrity|config_match|history_capacity|transition_recovery`, `compatibility.epoch|writer_quiescence`, `service.unique|arguments|executable|socket`, `listener.owner`, `runtime.reachable|identity|authority_generation`, `routing.integrity|effective_generation|coverage`, `coordinator.owner`, `client.bearer_barrier`, `candidate.provider_broker`, `candidate.receipt_export`, `logs.permissions|payload_retention`, and `protocol.revision`; irrelevant checks are `not_applicable`.

Dispatch order is exact frozen forms, flat compatibility aliases, the intercepted operation-recovery tree, then the new proxy command tree and retained Kong ordinary surface. Operation-recovery help is lexical and non-mutating: exact `cq operation --help|-h`, `cq operation help [status|recover]`, and terminal `--help|-h` after either recognised leaf emit human help/0 before default-primary classification or store access; another mixed or unknown form is usage 64 and `--json` selects one `proxy_usage` envelope. Proxy help is likewise a lexical, non-mutating termination with this closed grammar and precedence. Root accepts `cq proxy --help|-h` and ignores later tokens exactly as baseline, while `cq proxy help [RECOGNISED_PATH...]` treats every later token as the help path and succeeds only for an exact registered baseline-or-new path. For direct baseline leaves `start|install|uninstall|restart|validate-http|status|pin|codex-default`, presence anywhere in remaining argv of `--help`, `-h`, or literal `help` emits that leaf's human help/0 before operand, extra-argument, confirmation, renderer, compatibility, or state inspection and ignores the other tokens. Baseline `prime` accepts first-token root help, `prime help [RECOGNISED_PRIME_PATH...]`, and exactly `prime status|enable|disable --help|-h|help`; its other mixed forms remain legacy usage 1. Baseline `endpoint` keeps its existing any-position help scan and chooses root versus `inspect-legacy|transition-legacy` help solely from the first endpoint token. These retained baseline help forms win over a co-present `--json`.

For the new tree, the root `help RECOGNISED_PATH` form above and one terminal `--help|-h` immediately after a recognised command node emit that node's help/0 before instance or input access; literal `help` is not a new-tree operand-position help token. Unknown help path, multiple help tokens, or a new-tree help token mixed with any operand/flag is `proxy_usage`/64; new-tree help plus `--json` is also `proxy_usage`/64. Generated help lists exact legal children, options, fixed-versus-lowerable timeout status, raw/JSON availability, and alias deprecation. Frozen `start` help identifies its public form as the pre-authority foreground runner and names `service start` as the post-authority command; `service` help lists the exact pre-authority lifecycle cells and labels `service install` sealed-primary-only; `candidate` help lists `status` and `receipt show` as candidate-only non-mutating reads, lists only the exact mutation leaves admitted by `EnforceCandidateRun` including `client-bearer-barrier refresh`, and states that prepare/start/stop/remove/status/validate-release project only the privacy-safe broker state, digests, counts, counters, and codes defined by `CandidateProviderBrokerInspectionV1`. It explicitly states that help performs no broker inspection and that no credential, capability, request bytes, or raw path can be displayed. `client-bearer-barrier` help distinguishes non-creating status from receipt staging, states the source-candidate and optional exact active-operation selector rules, and names stage as the recovery for stale release readiness without listener release. Flat-install help states that execution requires a sealed primary and lists initialise/import preparation for pre-authority state. Golden fixtures derive the registered baseline path matrix from `manualHelpByPath`, preserve all baseline placements above with absent HOME/XDG, and prove no config/epoch/key/file/process/provider/service access.

Without a terminating help form, alias recognition wins before renderer scan and aliases reject `--json` with legacy exit 1. New-tree parsing completes only after token grammar and inline-stdin framing are bounded, decoded, duplicate-checked, and validated. Inline stdin grammar failure emits `proxy_usage`/64. Referenced config, release-bundle, receipt, predicate, local-token client registry, credential-manifest, policy, and executable content is operation input; failures after leaf selection use operation kind. Conditional confirmation discovered by snapshot/config inspection also uses operation kind, `state=failed`, and exit 64.

All new `--json` paths emit exactly one UTF-8 envelope to stdout, including usage/failure; stderr is progress only. Presence of `--json` anywhere under new command tree selects JSON usage rendering even when parser cannot identify complete leaf: one `proxy_usage`, `ok:false`, `state:invalid`, code `invalid_usage`, exit 64. `logs`, including `--follow`, has no JSON mode. Status dispatch is lexical and unambiguous: exact no-argument form and exact `--port PORT` form are legacy; presence of `--instance-state-root`, `--json`, `--human`, `--strict`, or `--timeout` selects reconciled status. The standalone default-primary timeout spelling is exactly `status --timeout DURATION [--strict]`; omission of `--timeout` from that grammar collapses to the separately recognised frozen no-argument form, not an empty new-tree form. `--port` combined with any new-selector flag is usage 64. Reconciled status defaults to human when selected by root, strict, or timeout; `--json` and `--human` conflict. Non-strict reconciled status returns 0 when collection completes; strict uses verdict. Thus default-primary reconciled human is `status --human`, not bare status.

Frozen status performs one 5-second public `/health` and preserves output/exit compatibility: it prints any decodable JSON object regardless HTTP status and exits 0; transport/decode/usage failure remains 1. Transport is nevertheless hardened: exact numeric loopback target only, direct dial, environment proxy and automatic compression disabled, redirects refused with `http.ErrUseLastResponse`, response body bounded to 1 MiB plus one-byte sentinel, and decoder requires exactly one JSON object followed only by whitespace. Redirect, compressed bomb, oversize, trailing object/data, or non-loopback resolution fails 1 without following/dereferencing. It injects no snapshot fields. Detailed `health` uses Unix control; public raw `health --public` is constant-shaped TCP JSON. Without `--json`, each prints exact runtime object and no envelope. Existing port-only `validate-http` and endpoint maintenance keep current raw/no-output shapes and exit 1 for usage/operation errors until separately versioned; every other new usage error is 64.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 0 | Healthy/effective success, compatible non-strict status, or `info` collection completed |
| 1 | Valid but degraded, rescue, draining, or durable desired state pending |
| 2 | Down or required runtime unavailable |
| 3 | Identity, ownership, configuration, generation, or policy conflict |
| 4 | Required evidence or operation outcome indeterminate |
| 64 | Invalid command usage |

Verdict precedence is: proven conflict (3), required evidence indeterminate (4), down (2), degraded/legacy/rescue/pending (1), healthy (0). A proven conflict remains 3 even when optional evidence is unavailable. Permission failure for required service/listener/runtime identity makes status indeterminate; optional log metadata failure is warning. `info` returns 0 once base instance paths and independent collectors ran, with unavailable facts encoded. Doctor maps any critical ownership/authority/policy conflict to 3; required inspection unknown to 4; required listener/runtime absence to 2; remaining error/warning/degraded check to 1; all pass/not-applicable to 0.

Mutation proof is operation-specific. Grammar/framing failure or missing required confirmation is 64. Authority, identity, configuration, ownership, listener, generation, policy, requested-object, or initialisation conflict is 3. Required inspection unavailable or durable commit outcome indeterminate, including `io_commit_sync_unknown`, is 4. Required manager/listener/runtime absent or unreachable before durable intent is 2. Durable pending/degraded result, provider/probe/network failure, `resource_capacity_exhausted`, `io_precommit_failed`, other I/O, or `internal_error` is 1. Usage terminates alone; otherwise multiple errors use precedence 3, 4, 2, 1. Transition confirmation failure keeps operation kind, `state=failed`, and exit 64. Runtime mode or routing policy returns 0 only after exact listener acknowledgement, 1 when safely durable but pending. Start/restart requires exact listener/runtime proof. Stop requires re-snapshot proving target job stopped and its owned listener absent; intentional absence is success, not a missing acknowledgement. Uninstall additionally requires job/plist absence. File-only recovery requires durable commit proof. Incompatible schema/epoch/key or effective generation newer than desired is conflict; desired generation newer than a feature-aware effective runtime is pending/degraded.

Read-side exits are closed:

| Read command | Exact exit |
|---|---|
| `config path` | 0 after deterministic path resolution; 4 when resolution itself unavailable |
| `config show|validate|diff` | valid/complete 0; absent or invalid 3; required inspection unavailable 4; missing runtime during `diff` is encoded unknown and remains 0 |
| client-bearer-barrier status | ready current selection 0; absent/expired stale selection 1; unsupported/unregistered/mismatched/invalid selection 3; unavailable required inspection 4 |
| service/candidate/Codex status | healthy 0; legacy/rescue_draining/rescue/rescue_exit_draining/degraded 1; down 2; conflicted 3; indeterminate 4 |
| `candidate receipt show` | matching parent-MACed compact `published` result 0; matching selected nonterminal parent attempt 1; selector miss, compact `conflicted` result, or mismatched/multiple authoritative result chain 3; required inspection unavailable 4 |
| operation status/recover | idle or authenticated terminal success 0; active/pending, authenticated terminal operational failure, or `login_restart_required` 1; selector miss, invalid/conflicting chain, multiple active chains, or live authenticated control-relation mismatch 3; unavailable or indeterminate outcome 4; recover-only precedence overrides preserve authenticated operation facts but map a live relation mismatch to `recovery_control=conflicted`, its precedence-selected conflict code/3, and null remediation, a rejected request on a still-live matching connection to `recovery_control=admission_failed`, `operator_operation_indeterminate`/4, and null remediation, and absent/stopped/inhibited/unreachable matching control to `recovery_control=unavailable`, `operator_operation_indeterminate`/4, and exact service-start remediation; status and direct retained-receipt projection remain available |
| rescue status | normal 0; rescue_draining/rescue/rescue_exit_draining/pending/degraded 1; down 2; conflicted 3; indeterminate 4 |
| service release status | absent, staged, or referenced with no active staged-release operation 0; sole valid nonterminal stage/clear operation `pending` 1; invalid/conflicting selector, operation, or reference 3; unavailable inspection 4 |
| rollback-floor status | absent, staged, or referenced with no active rollback-floor staged-release operation 0; sole valid nonterminal stage/clear operation `pending` 1; invalid/conflicting selector, operation, or reference 3; unavailable inspection 4 |
| pin/default/prime reads | effective, including intentionally unset/disabled, 0; pending/degraded 1; invalid 3; unavailable 4 |
| feature list/show | known active or inactive 0; unmatched activation/degraded 1; unknown/incompatible/invalid 3; unavailable inspection 4 |
| feature activation status | no active operation, exact `target_effective`, or exact `aborted_before_floor` 0; unfinished exact activation 1; explicit selector miss, `rollback_inhibited`, failed, or conflicted activation 3; unavailable inspection 4 |
| delegation/pool/session/capability list | valid collection, including empty, 0; pending/degraded 1; invalid 3; unavailable 4 |
| delegation/pool/session show | found 0; requested object absent or invalid 3; unavailable 4 |
| capability show | valid evaluated result, including unknown because no evidence exists, 0; conflicting/invalid evidence 3; unavailable 4 |
| authority recovery inspect | completed inspection, even when authority invalid, 0; collector indeterminate 4 |
| authority initialise status | no applicable active chain, or exact committed/aborted terminal, 0; unfinished exact chain 1; explicit selector miss, invalid/conflicting chain, or failed terminal 3; unavailable 4 |
| authority import status | imported/terminal or no prepared ticket 0; prepared/activating/restoring 1; explicit selector miss or invalid/conflicting ticket 3; unavailable 4 |
| config adopt/migrate status | no pending operation or terminal activated/aborted/expired operation 0; handoff-pending/clients-acknowledged/cleanup-pending 1; explicit selector miss or invalid/conflicting operation 3; unavailable 4 |
| initialisation recovery status | idle/absent or exact terminal 0; unfinished exact chain 1; explicit selector miss or invalid/conflicting chain 3; unavailable 4 |
| transition recovery status | idle/no active or exact terminal transition 0; unfinished transition 1; explicit selector miss or conflict 3; indeterminate 4 |

These read-side exits apply only after the `InspectInstance` matrix admits the leaf, except that a `parent_transaction_recovery` leaf uses the separate retained-store matrix above. Matrix role rejection is exact and takes precedence over the leaf oracle: absent required authority or candidate state is `instance_uninitialised`/3; primary-versus-candidate mismatch is `instance_mismatch`/3; malformed/conflicting inspected state is the exact conflict/3; and unavailable required inspection is indeterminate/4. The explicit reserved-default `service status` exceptions are absent state (`down`/2), exact stopped legacy configuration (`down`/2), and exact live legacy topology (`legacy`/1). Role-neutral collectors keep their command-specific exit rules and collected facts.

`recovery transition resume` always emits `proxy_recovery` with `recovery_domain="transition"`, `recovery_action="resume"`, the full operation ID, transition/lifecycle kind and state, authority generation, exact `barrier_selection_digest`, `client_stop_proof_digest`, `lifecycle_action_digest`, `deadline`, fresh topology proof and terminal outcome or null. Those three resume-proof digests and `deadline` are non-null after the resume intent is durably selected and null on a pre-intent refusal; no root path, sender identity or credential appears. Exact terminal target proof is `state="committed"`, `ok=true`, exit 0; a durably selected unfinished suffix is `pending`, exit 1; wrong operation/kind/phase, stale selection or proof conflict is `failed|conflicted`, exit 3; unavailable or ambiguous required evidence is `indeterminate`, exit 4; malformed ID or either missing confirmation is `proxy_usage`, exit 64 before state access. Human output exposes the same safe IDs/digests and remediation without raw paths.

## Status reconciliation

Status does not collapse contradictory evidence. It reports both facts and one verdict.

Primary states:

- `healthy`: the one sealed CQ LaunchAgent activation definition has coherent socket authority; inherited descriptor lineage and serving runtime identity match; desired/effective generations match; normal runtime reports healthy.
- `legacy`: one pre-authority Homebrew/LaunchAgent/foreground listener is coherently attested by plist/job/PID/executable/listener plus existing serving-attestation challenge, but has no composite control authority. CQ LaunchAgent lifecycle start/restart/stop/uninstall and Homebrew start/restart/stop may succeed only through the exact legacy manager proof and parent journal; foreground has no lifecycle mutation, and every unsupported pair reports stop/import remediation without intent. Reconciled status remains exit 1 and rescue/session-policy mutations require import.
- `rescue_draining`: new traffic uses rescue, autonomous normal workers are stopped, but admitted normal operations remain.
- `rescue`: exact CQ runtime serves rescue; signed authority and runtime acknowledgement match; caller-auth relay contract is active. Exit remains 1 because normal routing guarantees are unavailable or explicitly suspended.
- `rescue_exit_draining`: desired mode is normal and an exact-generation worker may be ready, but both new normal and new rescue ingress remain closed while already admitted rescue HTTP drains and rescue WebSockets are closing. It remains exit 1 until rescue HTTP, WebSocket, and connected-unsent relay counts are all zero and the worker still acknowledges the exact boot/authority generation; only then may reconciliation publish terminal `normal`.
- `degraded`: exact CQ runtime serves but one subsystem, policy, or desired/effective relation is unhealthy.
- `down`: no listener and no serving runtime.
- `conflicted`: foreign listener, duplicate managers, listener/service PID mismatch, executable mismatch, malformed required state, or incompatible generations.
- `indeterminate`: permissions or platform-tool failure prevent a required judgement.

Required evidence and oracle:

| Command | Required evidence | Optional evidence | Judgement |
|---|---|---|---|
| detailed `health` | owner Unix-control connection, peer/HMAC authentication, bounded structured result | service/listener identity | `ok` 0; valid degraded/rescue/worker-unavailable 1; absent/refused/timed-out control 2; malformed/wrong-instance 3; inspection permission/platform failure 4 |
| `health --public` | configured address, bounded HTTP result, exact minimal schema | service/listener identity | HTTP 200/`ok` 0; HTTP 503/`degraded` 1; connection failure 2; any other status/body/content type 3 |
| `status --strict` | control/config parse state, listener ownership, supported jobs, runtime identity when reachable | log metadata, package metadata | precedence above |
| `info` | resolvable instance paths and collector completion | every operational layer | exit 0 with unknown facts encoded |
| `doctor` | same facts as strict status plus deterministic check catalogue | locally cached, unexpired provider-probe receipt only | highest failed-check severity |
| lifecycle mutation | fresh exact target topology | unrelated jobs | refuse conflict/indeterminate before mutation |

Representative multi-fault rules are normative: foreign listener plus unreadable logs is conflict 3; no listener plus one stopped manager is down 2; no listener plus permission-denied manager inspection is indeterminate 4; matching runtime plus desired generation ahead is degraded 1; listener/service mismatch plus runtime 200 is conflict 3.

Important contradictory examples remain explicit:

```text
service: homebrew crash-looping
listener: unmanaged CQ process
runtime: reachable
overall: conflicted
```

```text
desired_mode: rescue
effective_mode: normal
authority_generation: desired=9 effective=8
overall: degraded
```

Per-session inspection reports desired/effective policy generations, exact-listener acknowledgement, pool kind, effective-member count and digest, HTTP/WS coverage, membership-valid-until, and continuity-conflict state. It never returns raw identifiers or member identities unless explicitly requested through `pool show`.

## Rescue mode

### Common downstream admission

Supervisor authenticates every normal/rescue Codex HTTP request and WS upgrade before reading body byte, sending `100 Continue`, parsing turn metadata, contacting worker, enumerating inventory, planning, or dialing upstream. Require origin-form target, exact configured loopback Host, no Origin/`Sec-Fetch-*`/preflight/proxy form/CONNECT, and target ≤8 KiB. Reject any identity or end-to-end field nominated by `Connection` or `Trailer`; WebSocket may nominate only its exact `Upgrade` transport token.
