Reject semantic duplicates, comma joining, and case-variant ambiguity.

Bearer grammar is one `Authorization` field containing literal `Bearer`, one ASCII space, then non-empty opaque RFC 6750 `b64token` bytes, total value ≤16 KiB; no OWS/trim/normalisation. `ChatGPT-Account-Id` is optional, but if present exactly one non-empty valid field value ≤512 bytes. `x-openai-fedramp` is absent or exactly one ASCII `true`; optional residency is exactly one `us`. Token provenance is opaque on wire: CQ does not claim syntax distinguishes ChatGPT OAuth, PAT, API key, or another bearer.

In normal mode, ready worker publishes one live-control-MAC-authenticated index bound to composite generation, monotonic index epoch, and purpose-bound fingerprint-key ID. Each entry binds bearer fingerprint plus optional account-ID fingerprint to exactly one logical `AccountKey`, exact candidate ID/revision HMACs, optional authoritative tenancy/residency scope, and caller credential `valid_from`/`valid_until`. Duplicate/ambiguous bearer-to-subject mapping invalidates complete index. Known-expired entries are omitted atomically. Unknown expiry may authorise exact same-account dispatch only; it can never issue cross-account delegation permit. Supplied account ID must match entry. CQ `local_token` never authorises native Codex credential injection.

Provider caller identity is one exact tagged union. `CodexCallerSubjectV1={schema_version:1,credential_domain:"codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1",caller_fingerprint_key_id,bearer_fingerprint,account_id_fingerprint,caller_account_key,caller_candidate_id_hmac,caller_credential_revision_hmac,caller_credential_valid_from,caller_credential_valid_until,caller_tenancy_scope_digest}` permits only `account_id_fingerprint` and `caller_credential_valid_until` to be null. `ClaudeCallerSubjectV1={schema_version:1,credential_domain:"claude_access_token_v1",caller_fingerprint_key_id,bearer_fingerprint,caller_account_key,caller_candidate_id_hmac,caller_credential_revision_hmac,caller_credential_valid_from,caller_credential_valid_until}` permits only `caller_credential_valid_until` to be null. Every other branch field is non-null and times use signed-time grammar above. `ProviderCallerSubjectV1={schema_version:1,provider:"claude"|"codex",claude_subject:ClaudeCallerSubjectV1|null,codex_subject:CodexCallerSubjectV1|null}` requires exactly the tag-matching subject non-null and the other exactly null.

`K_provider_caller_subject = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/provider-caller-subject-hmac/v1"),L=32)`. For `U=CanonicalJSONV1(ProviderCallerSubjectV1)`, let `D=ASCII("cq/provider-caller-subject/claude/v1\0")` for the Claude branch and `D=ASCII("cq/provider-caller-subject/codex/v1\0")` for the Codex branch; `provider_caller_subject_hmac = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_provider_caller_subject, D || uint32be(len(U)) || U))`. The `caller_subject_hmac` field in Codex delegation records is exactly this value for the Codex-tagged union; a Claude-tagged value is illegal in delegation storage. Thus provider tags, field sets, and HMAC domains cannot be substituted even when raw bearer bytes collide.

Pre-body authentication is route-independent. Its exact closed core is `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationCoreV1={schema_version:1,kind:"local_owner"|"provider_subject",credential_domain:"local_token_v1"|"claude_access_token_v1"|"codex_chatgpt_bearer_v1",ingress_fingerprint_key_id,ingress_bearer_fingerprint,ingress_index_epoch,provider_caller_subject:ProviderCallerSubjectV1|null,provider_caller_subject_hmac,caller_account_key_hmac,caller_candidate_id_hmac,caller_credential_revision_hmac,caller_valid_from,caller_valid_until,caller_tenancy_scope_digest,caller_delegation_authority:CallerDelegationAuthorityV1|null,caller_delegation_authority_digest,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest:null|string,authority_generation,routing_generation,request_nonce,connection_identity_digest,issued_at,valid_until}`. Local owner requires local credential domain, null `provider_caller_subject` through `candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest`, and non-null ingress fingerprint/key/index. An ordinary primary provider subject requires the provider-matching credential domain and tagged subject, all subject/account/candidate/revision/start and complete delegation-authority fields non-null, and literal-null synthetic-authority digest. A candidate synthetic Codex provider subject instead requires a non-null digest that reopens the exact live `CandidateSyntheticIngressAuthorityV1`, `CandidateSyntheticIngressMaterialisationV1`, and `CandidateSyntheticIngressIndexEntryV1`; their run/runtime/controller/process/index, subject, delegation, account/candidate/revision, fingerprint, route-budget, and expiry projections must byte-match this authentication. Candidate scope rejects a null digest, and every primary or non-candidate loader rejects a non-null digest. `caller_valid_until` is nullable only when an ordinary live provider index has no finite endpoint and tenancy is nullable only for Claude; candidate synthetic authority is always finite. Every duplicated projection equals the tagged subject and caller-only desired/effective delegation result byte-for-byte. `issued_at <= valid_until` when finite; authority/index/key/subject/delegation/synthetic-index drift invalidates the authentication.

`K_caller_pre_body_authentication = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/caller-pre-body-authentication/v1"),L=32)` is supervisor-only. For `B=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerPreBodyAuthenticationCoreV1)`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_caller_pre_body_authentication, ASCII("cq/caller-pre-body-authentication-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))` and `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1={schema_version:1,core:CallerPreBodyAuthenticationCoreV1,mac}` is closed. For `P=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1)`, `caller_pre_body_authentication_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/caller-pre-body-authentication/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`. This object contains no provider-selection or route fact and therefore can be minted before a semantic-partition body is read.

One routed authenticated ingress is the exact closed `CallerIngressCapabilityCoreV1={schema_version:1,pre_body_authentication:CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1,caller_pre_body_authentication_digest,selected_provider:"claude"|"codex",route_id,transport:"http"|"websocket",candidate_synthetic_route_budget_purpose:null|CandidateSyntheticRouteBudgetPurposeV1,candidate_synthetic_route_budget_consumption:CandidateSyntheticRouteBudgetConsumptionV1|null,candidate_synthetic_route_budget_consumption_digest:null|string,candidate_synthetic_route_budget_head_digest:null|string,capability_issue_nonce:null|string,issued_at,valid_until}`. The nested authentication and digest recompute exactly; `issued_at` is no earlier than its authentication issue time, and `valid_until` equals the authentication endpoint or an earlier non-null route-admission endpoint. Direct catalogue rows construct this core only after exact route and transport selection. Anthropic-compatible semantic partitions construct it only after validating `ProviderBranchClassificationCoreV1`; selected provider, route, and transport equal the classification and selected catalogue row. Local-owner provider selection is explicit at this boundary and is never inferred from credential bytes. Provider-subject selection equals the tag and credential domain in the nested authentication. Primary/non-candidate ingress requires the purpose, consumption, consumption digest, head digest, and issue nonce all null. Candidate synthetic ingress requires the complete non-null budget tuple, purpose exactly `base_ingress`, and an issue nonce byte-equal to its nested consumption; a WebSocket-application-send successor can never substitute for ingress capability authority.

The four synthetic-budget fields are paired non-null exactly when the nested synthetic-authority digest is non-null and otherwise all four are literal null. A synthetic capability is Codex-only; its route and transport equal one allowed row, its complete consumption and digest reopen from `CandidateSyntheticRouteBudgetStoreV1`, its head digest equals the successor selected by the completed head CAS, and its fresh issue nonce equals the consumption core. The consumption's pre-body digest, request nonce, connection identity, source tag, authority/index member, route, transport, count transition, and validity byte-match this capability and authentication. Capability construction occurs only after the durable head CAS and never performs another budget mutation. Missing complete consumption, exhausted row, wrong transport, stale head transition, duplicate issue nonce, digest-only history, or a second capability for one consumption rejects before ordinary owner creation, worker route, broker acquisition, inventory, continuity, or provider work. A spent unit remains spent if later owner creation or issue fails. The capability remains synthetic caller provenance, never provider egress credential authority. No pre-body object may be treated as a routed capability.

`K_caller_ingress_capability = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/caller-ingress-capability/v1"),L=32)` is supervisor-only. For `C=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerIngressCapabilityCoreV1)`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_caller_ingress_capability, ASCII("cq/caller-ingress-capability-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))` and `CallerIngressCapabilityV1={schema_version:1,core:CallerIngressCapabilityCoreV1,mac}` is closed. For `I=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerIngressCapabilityV1)`, `caller_ingress_capability_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/caller-ingress-capability/v1\0") || uint32be(len(I)) || I))`. Before owner creation the complete routed capability is runtime-only. The atomic active-non-V4/V4 owner-creation or prewarm-planning CAS persists one byte-identical complete `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1` and `CallerIngressCapabilityV1` inside its `CallerRequestAuthorityV1`; every later permit, retry, refresh, adoption, restart, and contraction reopens that nested pair and recomputes both MACs and digests. A digest or projection without both complete objects is never durable caller authority. No other object called an authentication or capability digest is legal.

For candidate synthetic provenance, that required complete nested capability also carries the complete signed `CandidateSyntheticRouteBudgetConsumptionV1`, its digest, selected historical head digest, transport, and issue nonce. Active-non-V4, V4 base/final/envelope/journal, prewarm plan/dial/adoption, every dispatch permit/consumption, retry/restart/contraction, broker proposal/routing/dispatch tuple/capability/issued/provider-consumption/terminal record, RCV envelope, recovery, migration, accounting, and final release either embed that complete caller authority or an explicitly declared byte-identical duplicate of those five budget projections. A missing complete consumption, digest-only reconstruction, current-head substitution for the historical selected head, route/transport drift, or one consumption referenced by two capability/owner/issued tuples rejects before further phase or provider work.

Document load verifies the complete routing-document MAC, strictly decodes each persisted Codex delegation record, validates every locally checkable stored digest/field relation, and enforces record and subject uniqueness without consulting the live caller index. Because the raw subject union is deliberately not persisted, load treats its MAC-protected `caller_subject_hmac` as an opaque exact Codex handle and does not reconstruct or recompute it. Absence, expiry, revision drift, or fingerprint-key drift of one subject never invalidates the complete otherwise-valid routing document. Grant, ingress lookup, provider-branch admission/consumption, and immediately-before-dispatch activation reconstruct the exact tagged union from the current authenticated provider index, recompute its provider-domain HMAC, and require constant-time equality; Codex delegation additionally requires equality with the stored `caller_subject_hmac`. A persisted record whose subject cannot be reconstructed is inert/inhibited for that subject only and remains visible to explicit delegation inspection; unrelated delegations, bindings, and callers remain usable. No provider caller subject has a dispatch-time refresh exception: exact provider rejection invalidates it for the complete current request even when its validity endpoint is null. Fingerprint-key rotation, validity-start drift, candidate/revision drift, Codex account-ID presence drift, or Codex tenancy-scope drift changes the union and invalidates only the matching delegation or live provider capability.

Request bearer must constant-time match one entry and satisfy `valid_from <= now < valid_until` when finite. Missing index is `503 normal_caller_auth_unavailable`; mismatch/expired is `401 normal_caller_auth_required`; ambiguous raw subject or delegation is `403 normal_caller_auth_scope_violation`. Raw bearer/index/subject validation precedes body read, inventory, planning, or continuity lookup. The supervisor then constructs and MACs exactly one route-independent `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1`; every later pre-route boundary verifies its complete core/MAC/digest. After a direct route is known or semantic classification completes, the supervisor constructs exactly one routed `CallerIngressCapabilityV1`; every downstream boundary verifies both complete objects and the exact closed delegation-authority projection instead of comparing an implementation-private capability shape. Without active operator delegation, caller-authorised set is exactly matched caller account. Delegation is composite authority binding exact caller credential subject to exact frozen pool/account-set and tenancy-scope digests, expiry no later than credential expiry, and revocation generation; it can only narrow other authority and never adds retry slots.

For an Anthropic-compatible semantic partition, the pre-body lookup must yield exactly one local-owner or provider-subject `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1`; zero or multiple domain matches fail before body read and no provider inventory or credential is consulted. After `ProviderBranchClassificationCoreV1`, `CallerAdmissionGate` narrows that authentication to exactly the selected provider, mints the routed `CallerIngressCapabilityV1`, and only then issues `ProviderBranchAdmissionV1`. A Codex-selected branch therefore requires the Codex-tagged subject and applies its exact caller-account singleton or active delegation before any Codex inventory or stored credential is visible; a Claude-tagged subject produces zero Codex attempts. A Claude-selected branch symmetrically requires local-owner authority or the Claude-tagged subject and cannot consume a Codex credential. Selected provider, route/classifier/body digests, ingress credential domain, exact provider-subject HMAC/delegation or local-owner kind, origin-binding digest, routed capability, and the exact classified `ProviderBranchAuthorityV1` remain bound through plan, `OpenHTTP`, every dispatch permit/attempt/retry, receipt, marker, and differential fixture. Every route outside those semantic partitions carries the exact route-matching `not_applicable` branch through the same surfaces.

Normal cross-account dispatch with `OpenAI-Organization`, `OpenAI-Project`, `x-openai-fedramp`, or residency selector is rejected unless a registered credential adapter supplies authoritative exact presence/value for both caller subject and selected outbound candidate, and delegation snapshot explicitly binds those values. V1 baseline inventory supplies none, so any such selector plus cross-account delegation fails before planning; same-account byte-preserving dispatch remains subject to indexed caller match. No caller-controlled tenancy field may steer another stored credential.

Every HTTP attempt, WebSocket upgrade/first send, retry, retained dispatch, prewarm dial/probe-send/adoption, and prewarm first send obtains one single-use `CallerDispatchAuthorityV1`. It is the exact closed canonical union `{schema_version:1,kind:"ordinary_permit",ordinary_permit_core:CallerDispatchPermitCoreV1,ordinary_permit_digest,local_owner_refresh_grant_digest:null,prewarm_adoption_authority_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_owner_state_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_consumption_digest:null,transition_id:null,receipt_digest:null,new_outbound_revision_hmac:null}`, `{schema_version:1,kind:"local_owner_refresh_grant",ordinary_permit_core:null,ordinary_permit_digest:null,local_owner_refresh_grant_digest,prewarm_adoption_authority_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_owner_state_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_consumption_digest:null,transition_id,receipt_digest,new_outbound_revision_hmac}`, `{schema_version:1,kind:"prewarm_adoption_authority",ordinary_permit_core:null,ordinary_permit_digest:null,local_owner_refresh_grant_digest:null,prewarm_adoption_authority_digest,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_owner_state_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_consumption_digest:null,transition_id:null,receipt_digest:null,new_outbound_revision_hmac:null}`, or `{schema_version:1,kind:"real_client_validation_grant",ordinary_permit_core:null,ordinary_permit_digest:null,local_owner_refresh_grant_digest:null,prewarm_adoption_authority_digest:null,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_digest,real_client_validation_dispatch_grant_owner_state_digest,real_client_validation_dispatch_consumption_digest,transition_id:null,receipt_digest:null,new_outbound_revision_hmac:null}`; every listed object/digest/ID in the selected branch is non-null and every other branch field is exactly null. Ordinary authority embeds one complete live `CallerDispatchPermitCoreV1`; its recomputed digest binds the exact owner plus the byte-identical closed caller-request authority, complete desired/effective resolver core and digest, request/attempt or reservation generations, exact account/candidate/revision, exact provider-branch/origin authority, final route/body/slot digests, evidence/member scope and expiry, and connection. A digest-only ordinary branch is invalid. Local-owner-refresh authority is legal only inside the exact universal refresh CAS below, requires independently current local-owner ingress from pre-body admission through final CAS, and substitutes for an ordinary permit; no Claude or Codex provider subject can create or consume it. Prewarm-adoption authority is legal only inside the adoption CAS below and binds the independently current reservation authority and independently constructed real V4 request authority; it is never an ordinary permit copied from either side, although its CAS separately consumes the complete reservation permit embedded in that authority. Real-client-validation authority is legal only for the exact final-target HTTP proof and only inside its journal/operation-store CAS; its consumed owner-state digest and complete consumption prove the ordinary resolver independently selected the production caller's own account, and it grants no resolver, membership, delegation, retry, refresh, prewarm, or WebSocket authority. For `A=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerDispatchAuthorityV1)`, `caller_dispatch_authority_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/caller-dispatch-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`. `CallerAdmissionGate` holds the selected bounded authority lease through journal `DispatchAdmitted` CAS or the matching volatile prewarm phase CAS. Index publication, delegation revocation, rescue activation, and authority close take the exclusive side, so none interleave between final validation and CAS. Gates/authority release before upstream I/O. Index change invalidates every ordinary capability not yet committed; worker death leaves one durable committed attempt or abandons the uncommitted authority. Credential refresh may update a same-account frozen outbound slot but never rewrites caller identity or revives delegation.

When and only when a Codex-selected V4 request entered with an independently current local-owner capability, `refresh_begin` may persist one immutable grant. Its closed core is `LocalOwnerRefreshGrantCoreV1={schema_version:1,transition_id,caller_pre_body_authentication_digest,caller_ingress_capability_digest,local_token_index_epoch,request_nonce,connection_identity_digest,request_generation,attempt_generation,provider_branch_authority:ProviderBranchAuthorityV1,normal_credential_origin_binding_digest,final_route_choice_digest,encoded_request_digest,refresh_slot_digest,account_key_hmac,candidate_id_hmac,old_outbound_revision_hmac,issued_at,valid_until}`. Both caller digests must equal the owning `CallerRequestAuthorityV1` projections and recompute from one `CallerIngressCapabilityV1` whose `core.pre_body_authentication.core.kind` is exactly `local_owner` and whose nested credential domain is exactly `local_token_v1`; `local_token_index_epoch`, request nonce, and connection-identity digest must byte-match that same caller authority. `valid_until` is non-null, at most five seconds after `issued_at`, and no credential revision supplied by the owner transaction is part of the immutable core. Let `G=CanonicalJSONV1(LocalOwnerRefreshGrantCoreV1)` and `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/local-owner-refresh-grant-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(G)) || G))`; the complete closed object is `LocalOwnerRefreshGrantV1={schema_version:1,core:LocalOwnerRefreshGrantCoreV1,mac}`. Let `L=CanonicalJSONV1(LocalOwnerRefreshGrantV1)`; `local_owner_refresh_grant_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/local-owner-refresh-grant/v1\0") || uint32be(len(L)) || L))`. Both the inner MAC and outer digest must verify before any use. The credential-owner transaction never mutates V4; its matching committed receipt is external input after complete gates are reacquired. Immediately before dispatch, one V4 CAS validates the exact grant and receipt, reconstructs the same still-current local-owner authentication and routed capability, validates current inventory/prepared revision and every bound request/route/body/origin/connection fact, constructs the exact `local_owner_refresh_grant` dispatch-authority branch, and consumes grant plus receipt while recording `DispatchAdmitted`. A provider-bearer request never creates a grant. Exact rejection of its ingress subject records `provider_subject_rejected` and atomically destroys that subject capability plus every uncommitted request authority. If the refreshable rejected outbound account/candidate/revision differs from the ingress subject, `refresh_begin` instead records `provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh` before owner work and destroys every remaining dispatch authority for this request while leaving the still-current ingress subject usable only by fresh ingress. Either branch may persist the credential-owner refresh result and publish the new index for future ingress, but must terminalise through the no-dispatch CAS with the retained `401` and zero refreshed replay. Every Claude-selected `401` likewise permits owner refresh/index publication only for future ingress, creates no V4 grant, retains and relays the `401`, and performs zero same-request replay regardless of caller kind, transport, or finite/null expiry. Multiple or no selected authority branches reject with zero dispatches; no durable consumed-without-dispatch grant or separately prepared refreshed attempt is valid. Installed migration proof covers both provider-bearer terminal reasons, Claude terminal `401`, and independently local-owner Codex refresh on HTTP and WebSocket without local-token fallback or subject conversion.

`LocalOwnerRefreshGrantV1` is purpose-bound by the complete final route already selected by its owning V4 envelope: the sole canonical projection is `LocalOwnerRefreshDispatchPurposeV1={schema_version:1,purpose:"http_retry"|"ws_upgrade",final_route_choice_digest}`, where HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 maps only to `http_retry` and `websocket_http1_upgrade` maps only to `ws_upgrade`. For `P=CanonicalJSONV1(LocalOwnerRefreshDispatchPurposeV1)`, `local_owner_refresh_dispatch_purpose_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/local-owner-refresh-dispatch-purpose/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`. `refresh_begin` persists the complete projection/digest alongside the immutable grant and the V4 journal; grant validation recomputes it from the complete stored route rather than accepting a caller-supplied purpose. A route/purpose/digest substitution invalidates the grant. The existing `local_owner_refresh_grant_digest` remains the digest of the grant itself; dispatch authority requires both byte-matching objects.

### Caller authentication contract

Rescue uses opaque-bearer shape above. It forwards optional account ID and exact FedRAMP field when present. It cannot prove bearer issuer without credential authority; generation-scoped `--acknowledge-caller-bearer-forwarding=chatgpt.com` is therefore mandatory and binds fixed origin plus protocol/header-contract digests.

Shape-valid rescue bearer is `unverified_rescue_bearer`, not authenticated identity. It never bypasses the global pre-body rescue-admission bucket below, and its HMAC fingerprint is only an ephemeral fairness key. The sole higher-priority class is `owner_permitted_rescue`: owner Unix control issues one single-use, five-second owner-control-MAC `RescueOwnerAdmissionPermitV1={schema_version:1,proxy_instance_id,listener_generation,mode_generation,request_nonce,connection_identity,issued_at,valid_until}` for one already shape-valid request; permit contains no bearer, is non-transferable, and is consumed before body/upstream work. Possession or shape of an opaque bearer cannot create this permit.

- Rescue never reads `auth.json`, CQ keyrings, browser state, or any credential file.
- Rescue never derives, injects, refreshes, selects, switches, logs, or writes credentials.
- Known non-Bearer/AgentAssertion schemes, arbitrary configured identity headers, cookies, `Proxy-Authorization`, duplicated identity, and fields outside contract reject before dispatch. PAT/API-key provenance is not wire-detectable and is not claimed.
- Authority stores padded deny-set fingerprints for every current/transition/rollback CQ local token. Rescue performs constant-work comparison and rejects any match as `401 rescue_local_token_refused`. Missing classification needs acknowledgement bound to exact reference-set digest; set change expires it. Status exposes acknowledgement only.
- Missing or unsupported caller authentication returns local `401 rescue_caller_auth_required` with zero upstream attempts. Expiry remains upstream authority; upstream `401` and `403` responses relay unchanged because rescue neither parses nor refreshes opaque bearer material.
- Common Host/Origin gate prevents browser or generic local forward proxy from turning CQ into credential-bearing cross-origin relay.
- Health reports `auth_source=caller`, `auth_contract=opaque_bearer_v1`, and availability `per_request`; it never reports whether any credential exists on disk.

This contract deliberately prefers recoverability without CQ credential dependencies over guaranteed success for clients that omit upstream authentication. Unsupported callers fail explicitly and can be diagnosed without CQ silently choosing an account.

### External protocol authority

V1 is pinned to installed `codex-cli 0.147.0`, official tag `rust-v0.147.0`, commit `be6e8eac029b183056b7e4402879f15d2c85f61b`, `tokio-tungstenite` revision `0e5b2d73aa18dd9f0a50ee9ff199d5aef7594186`, and `tungstenite-rs` revision `4fffad30fe373adbdcffab9545e9e9bf4f2fc19f`. Official client source is observational authority for private ChatGPT backend behaviour, not a public stability guarantee. Build records Codex version, commit, route corpus digest, header-contract digest, and WebSocket semantics digest. A different installed Codex version does not silently widen relay behaviour: `doctor` reports protocol drift, rescue continues only for requests matching pinned V1, and support for changed routes, headers, authentication, or framing requires a reviewed semantics revision and new corpus.

### Route allowlist

V1 serves only core Codex recovery routes:

Upstream base URI is exactly `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` with TLS SNI/HTTP authority `chatgpt.com`; route suffix below is appended once to that parsed base. Caller/config cannot supply scheme, host, port, base path, DNS target, or alternate origin. Downstream `/backend-api/codex/*` therefore remains unsupported and is not double-prefixed upstream.

| Downstream | Method | Raw query | Upstream suffix | Body |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/models` | GET | exact `client_version=0.147.0` | `/models` | absent |
| `/responses` | POST | empty | `/responses` | JSON or zstd JSON |
| `/v1/responses` | POST | empty | `/responses` | JSON or zstd JSON |
| `/responses/compact` | POST | empty | `/responses/compact` | JSON only |
| `/v1/responses/compact` | POST | empty | `/responses/compact` | JSON only |
| `/responses` | WebSocket GET | empty | `/responses` | upgrade only |

Local health, identity, and owner-authenticated Unix control remain available. Every other route fails locally. Named exclusions include `GET /v1/models`, downstream `/backend-api/codex/*`, wrong methods on compact routes, WebSocket `/v1/responses`, `POST /memories/trace_summarize`, `/alpha/search` and aliases, image generation/edit aliases, `/live`, realtime/calls/sideband variants, `/app-server`, Claude, arbitrary fallback routes, CONNECT, and absolute-form requests. Unsupported paths return `404 rescue_route_unsupported`; wrong methods return 405 with exact `Allow`; `OPTIONS` has no CORS exception. `/models` requires exact raw query `client_version=0.147.0`; duplicate, reordered, encoded, additional, or empty forms fail `400 rescue_query_unsupported`. `originator` is header, not query. Every response/compact/WS route requires empty query. Unlike normal CQ, rescue never serves local catalogue.

### HTTP relay contract

- Supervisor V1 HTTP/1 admission preserves raw request-line, header-field cardinality, and `Content-Length` spelling before normalised Go request construction. It never treats `http.Request.Header` alone as evidence for framing or duplicate authority. HTTP V1 accepts exact path/query row above and only HTTP/1.1. Header names compare case-insensitively; “one” means one raw parsed field-value, never comma-joined duplicates. Host/framing validate separately and are not copied.

| Common request field | Cardinality/value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | one opaque bearer contract |
| `User-Agent` | one pinned generated Codex value with exact version; independent of thread `originator` |
| `originator` | one pinned value for which Rust `HeaderValue::from_str()` succeeds, including empty |
| `version` | one exact `0.147.0` |
| `ChatGPT-Account-Id` | zero/one non-empty opaque value |
| `x-openai-fedramp` | zero/one exact `true` |
| `x-openai-internal-codex-residency` | zero/one exact `us` |
| `OpenAI-Organization` | zero/one valid value whose ASCII trim is non-empty |
| `OpenAI-Project` | zero/one valid value whose ASCII trim is non-empty |

| Route | Required exactly once | Optional at most once |
|---|---|---|
| `/models` | common only | `traceparent`; `tracestate` only with `traceparent` |
| response POST | `Content-Type: application/json`; `Accept: text/event-stream`; `session-id`; `thread-id`; `x-client-request-id`; `x-codex-window-id` | `Content-Encoding: zstd`; `x-codex-turn-metadata`; `x-codex-turn-state`; `x-codex-parent-thread-id`; `x-openai-subagent`; exact-true `x-openai-memgen-request`; exact-true `x-openai-internal-codex-responses-lite`; `x-codex-beta-features`; `x-oai-attestation`; `x-codex-inference-call-id`; `traceparent`; `tracestate` |
| compact POST | `Content-Type: application/json`; `session-id`; `thread-id`; `x-codex-window-id`; `x-codex-installation-id` | `x-codex-turn-metadata`; `x-codex-turn-state`; `x-codex-parent-thread-id`; `x-openai-subagent`; exact-true memgen/responses-lite; `x-codex-beta-features`; `x-oai-attestation`; `traceparent`; `tracestate` |

User-Agent is 1–16384 visible ASCII and independently matches pinned generated shape `<process-originator>/0.147.0 (<os-type> <os-version>; <arch>) <terminal-agent>[ (<sanitised-suffix>)]`; process-originator may be empty, in which case the valid generated value begins `/0.147.0 `, and need not equal thread `originator`. Installed examples include differing and empty process/thread origins. Opaque ID/attestation and turn-metadata fields are non-empty valid values; turn-state may be empty when `HeaderValue::to_str()` succeeds. Inference-call ID is lower-case UUIDv4. `x-codex-beta-features` is absent for empty set; otherwise exact value is one of `network_proxy`, `prevent_idle_sleep`, `remote_compaction_v2`, `network_proxy,prevent_idle_sleep`, `network_proxy,remote_compaction_v2`, `prevent_idle_sleep,remote_compaction_v2`, or `network_proxy,prevent_idle_sleep,remote_compaction_v2`. Tokens follow pinned order with comma/no OWS; empty/unknown/duplicate/reordered/trailing-comma forms reject. Trace fields follow W3C; `tracestate` requires `traceparent`. Organisation/project bytes are provider-tenancy selectors: normal mode requires indexed candidate match; rescue forwards caller values under fixed-origin acknowledgement. Values bind request and probe receipts. Compact forbids `Accept`, encoding, client-request and inference-call IDs. Models forbids `Accept` and content fields but permits tracing. Every route forbids `Accept-Encoding`. Unlisted semantic field rejects, not silently strips.

- Ordinary HTTP containing `Connection`, `Upgrade`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Trailer`, or parsed `Transfer-Encoding` is unsupported. No request/response trailers are admitted in V1.
- `/models` has no Content-Length/body. POST requires one canonical decimal Content-Length matching positive `Request.ContentLength`, no transfer encoding/trailer, and exact bytes. Rescue assigns upstream request `ContentLength` field; it never manually copies length header.
- Response requests allow absent encoding or exact `zstd`; compact requires absent encoding. Body streams exact bytes once; no JSON/zstd parsing, transformation, replay copy, `GetBody`, Headroom, diagnostics, or account selection.
- Each request creates fresh direct HTTP/1.1 transport: environment proxy off, compression off, fixed TLS authority/SNI/certificate verification, early data off, HTTP/2/ALPN alternatives off, keepalive off, request `Close=true`, redirects/idempotency retry off, single atomic `RoundTrip`/accepted-connection latch. No pooled/coalesced connection. Once any request byte writes, every error is terminal/indeterminate; no reconstruction, redial, or bodyless GET resend.
- Response header allowlist is separately versioned below. Unlisted incidental fields drop; malformed/duplicated allowlisted or forbidden framing/redirect fields fail locally before status when possible.
- Preserve upstream non-redirect status, allowlisted headers, and response bytes; trailers are unsupported. Flush every upstream read for SSE timing/backpressure. Partial body preserves written bytes then closes; never synthesize second status/retry.
- Relay `304` and non-navigation `3xx` without `Location`. Any response carrying redirect `Location` becomes local `502 rescue_redirect_refused`; never follow or expose an origin escape. Perform no CQ-layer retry for any method or outcome.
- Downstream cancellation cancels sole upstream attempt. Unknown upstream outcome remains indeterminate; rescue never replays or switches credentials.

### Exact response-header contract

Framing is transport-derived; raw hop-by-hop, transfer-encoding, trailer, and length fields are never copied. Each semantic allowlisted field is absent or exactly once. Duplicate/bad allowlisted value, declared trailer, forbidden redirect, or header section over 64 KiB yields `502 rescue_upstream_header_invalid` before downstream status. `Set-Cookie`, `WWW-Authenticate`, and unlisted end-to-end fields drop. `Location` instead yields `502 rescue_redirect_refused`.

Common HTTP and WS non-101 allowlist:

| Field | Exact value schema |
|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | valid RFC 9110 media type |
| `Content-Encoding` | one `identity`, `gzip`, or `zstd`; body remains opaque |
| `x-request-id`, `x-oai-request-id`, `cf-ray`, `x-openai-authorization-error` | any single value whose Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()` succeeds, including empty |
| `x-error-json` | standard base64 decoding to JSON object with string `error.code` |
| `x-codex-active-limit` | any single `to_str()` value; interpretation trims, defaults empty to `codex`, lowercases ASCII, changes `_` to `-` |
| `x-codex-promo-message` | any single value whose pinned Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()` succeeds; relay exact bytes, including empty; interpretation applies `str::trim()`, and empty-after-trim means absent |
| `x-codex-credits-balance` | any single value whose pinned Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()` succeeds; relay exact bytes, including empty; only after both credit booleans parse, interpretation applies `str::trim()`, and empty-after-trim means `balance=None` |
| `x-codex-rate-limit-reached-type` | any single value whose pinned Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()` succeeds; relay exact bytes; interpretation applies `str::trim()` and requires exactly one of `rate_limit_reached`, `workspace_owner_credits_depleted`, `workspace_member_credits_depleted`, `workspace_owner_usage_limit_reached`, or `workspace_member_usage_limit_reached`; empty-after-trim and every other trimmed value reject |
| `x-codex-credits-has-credits`, `x-codex-credits-unlimited` | case-insensitive boolean or exact 1/0 |

For lower-case limit ID `[a-z0-9-]+`, only dynamic names `x-<limit>-{primary,secondary}-{used-percent,window-minutes,reset-at}` and `x-<limit>-limit-name` are admitted. Percent uses finite Rust `f64::from_str`; window/reset use Rust `i64::from_str`, including accepted leading `+`/zeroes. Every limit-name value must pass pinned Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()`; interpretation applies `str::trim()` and maps empty-after-trim to absent, while relay preserves exact bytes including empty. Promo and credits-balance use same `to_str()`/trim/empty-as-absent interpretation defined above. No other wildcard.

Route additions follow pinned consumer semantics without altering relayed bytes. Models permits `ETag` only when one value passes pinned Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()`; relay and client storage preserve exact string, including empty, with no trimming. Response POST permits `OpenAI-Model`, `X-Codex-Turn-State`, `X-Models-Etag`, and `X-Codex-Safety-Buffering-Faster-Model` whenever one value passes `to_str()`, including empty. `X-Reasoning-Included` and `X-Codex-Safety-Buffering-Enabled` are presence-only: any syntactically valid single value including empty/`false` has pinned presence semantics. Compact permits empty-capable `X-Codex-Turn-State`; returned empty state may be sent unchanged next request. `X-Codex-Model` is unsupported. Successful models/compact use JSON; response POST uses SSE; error may use any media type.

Known response length sets downstream length field and streamed count must agree; unknown length uses local HTTP/1 framing. Declared trailer rejects before status. Late/undeclared trailer or length failure after status is partial upstream failure: preserve bytes, close, no retry. Body stays opaque; automatic decompression is disabled.

### WebSocket relay contract

- Only HTTP/1.1 `GET /responses`, empty query/body, exact Host, no Origin/`Sec-Fetch-*`. Require exactly one `Connection: Upgrade`, `Upgrade: websocket`, `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13`, and key decoding to 16 bytes. Subprotocol must be absent.
- Pinned client offers exactly `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate; client_max_window_bits`. Admit this one offer but decline it: omit extension and subprotocol upstream/downstream. Other/duplicate offer fails. Upstream negotiated extension/subprotocol is local 502; RSV1 on established leg closes 1002.
- Required semantic fields are common auth/User-Agent/originator/version; exact `OpenAI-Beta: responses_websockets=2026-02-06`; session/thread/client-request/window IDs. Optional zero/one: common account/FedRAMP/residency/organisation/project, turn metadata, parent thread, subagent, exact-true memgen, beta features, attestation, exact-true `x-responsesapi-include-timing-metrics`. Organisation/project use common trim-non-empty grammar and tenancy binding and relay unchanged in rescue. Turn-state, installation ID, responses-lite, inference-call, trace fields are forbidden in handshake. Every unlisted semantic field fails before dial.
- Treat legs as independent RFC 6455 handshakes. Retain exact admitted downstream `Sec-WebSocket-Key` field-value octets as `K_d`. Generate `K_u` as canonical padded RFC 4648 base64 of 16 CSPRNG bytes, regenerating when encoded `K_u == K_d`; never forward `K_d`. Send exactly one upstream HTTP/1.1 request with generated transport fields and fixed semantic set.
- Complete/validate upstream before downstream 101. Require HTTP/1.1 101; exactly one whole-value ASCII-case-insensitive `Upgrade: websocket`; exactly one whole-value `Connection: Upgrade`; exactly one `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` equal byte-for-byte to `BASE64(SHA-1(K_u || "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11"))`, where `K_u` means encoded field-value bytes. Any missing/duplicate/malformed/mismatch fails 502 before downstream upgrade. Construct downstream accept independently using exact encoded `K_d` bytes and same literal GUID; never copy upstream accept. Optional 101 semantics are zero/one presence-only `X-Reasoning-Included` with any valid value including empty/false, and zero/one `X-Models-Etag`, `OpenAI-Model`, `X-Codex-Turn-State` passing Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()`, including empty. Relay admitted values unchanged. Any `Set-Cookie`, `Location`, `WWW-Authenticate`, `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions`, or `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` field fails before downstream upgrade. Every other unlisted 101 field is incidental and drops; it is neither relayed nor interpreted.
- For non-101, buffer through 1,048,577-byte counter before downstream status. Complete ≤1,048,576 bytes relays status, ordinary response-POST allowlist, exact body, generated length. Byte +1 returns `502 rescue_ws_handshake_body_too_large`; incomplete declared body returns `502 rescue_ws_handshake_body_incomplete`; no upstream status/body leak or retry.
- Frame-aware V1 codec enforces 16,777,216-byte data-frame payload cap and cumulative 67,108,864-byte uncompressed payload per reassembled message. Upstream frame over cap closes upstream/fails downstream; outbound messages are fragmented into frames no larger than cap so pinned tungstenite client can receive them. CQ imposes same cap on downstream-client frames as additional symmetric security policy. Frame/message limit−1 and exact relay; first byte above closes 1009 with no partial application message. Control payload ≤125 bytes. Implementation must use frame-aware codec with bounded streaming accumulation; message-only Gorilla `ReadMessage` is insufficient.
- Relay text/binary type, complete message boundary, payload, and order; validate text UTF-8. Fragmentation/masking are hop-local. Protocol/UTF-8/control violation closes 1002. Ping/pong stay hop-local with same payload. Propagate valid close code and ≤123-byte UTF-8 reason; invalid close becomes 1002.
- Do not parse application messages/events/model/account. Never reconnect/replay. Join pumps, serialize writes, fence late writes, close both legs deterministically.

### V1 resource budgets

Supervisor applies hard maxima before worker/upstream dispatch. Configuration may lower them; widening needs reviewed transport-semantics revision.

| Resource | Maximum |
|---|---:|
| downstream TCP connections | 128 |
| admitted HTTP / rescue HTTP | 32 / 8 total: 2 owner-permit reserved, at most 6 unverified |
| WebSockets / rescue WebSockets | 8 / 4 total: 1 owner-permit reserved, at most 3 unverified |
| upstream / rescue upstream connections | 32 / 8 total: 2 owner-permit reserved, at most 6 unverified |
| request target / total headers / header count | 8 KiB / 64 KiB / 64 |
| header name / ordinary value / bearer / account ID | 128 B / 16 KiB / 16 KiB / 512 B |
| HTTP encoded request body | 64 MiB (`/models`: zero) |
| normal memory body / aggregate spool / aggregate decoded memory | 1 MiB / 512 MiB / 128 MiB |
| response headers / buffered error or non-101 body | 64 KiB / 1 MiB |
| WebSocket data-frame payload | 16 MiB |
| uncompressed reassembled WS message / aggregate reassembly | 64 MiB / 128 MiB |
| WS control payload | 125 B |
| payload diagnostic source / encoded event / queue | 256 KiB / 2 MiB / 8 events and 16 MiB |
| payload diagnostic files / aggregate / retention | 5 × 10 MiB / 50 MiB / 24 h |

Known length reserves complete budget before read. Normal body above 1 MiB spills to unlinked owner-only instance temporary; normal chunked input reserves incrementally. Rescue requires canonical known positive Content-Length on POST, rejects transfer encoding/unknown length and length above 64 MiB before upstream, and streams sole admitted body through counting reader with no replay spool. Oversize returns 413; aggregate exhaustion returns 503 plus `Retry-After: 1`; unauthenticated body is not drained. Unsupported `Expect`, conflicting length, or ambiguous framing rejects before upstream.

Owner Unix control has independent descriptors, goroutine budget, and queue; TCP saturation cannot consume its reserved management capacity. Of 128 TCP application slots, 112 are ordinary and 16 are fast-auth reserve: reserved slot must finish bounded headers and valid normal/rescue bearer admission within 250 ms or closes, and a newly validated normal bearer or valid owner rescue permit may evict the oldest non-progressing unauthenticated header slot. Every `unverified_rescue_bearer` connection consumes a non-bypassable global pre-body token bucket of 16 attempts/second with burst 32; excess closes before body or upstream work. Unverified rescue traffic is then confined to six HTTP, six upstream, and three WebSocket slots and receives a per-fingerprint bucket of 2 new requests/second with burst 4, at most two concurrent HTTP and one WebSocket, 15-second total HTTP lifetime, and five-minute WebSocket lifetime. The remaining two rescue HTTP/upstream slots and one WebSocket slot are reserved exclusively for a fresh `RescueOwnerAdmissionPermitV1`; unverified traffic cannot consume, borrow, or evict them. Owner-permitted traffic consumes an independent owner bucket of 4 attempts/second with burst 8 and the total mode caps, so exhaustion of the unverified bucket cannot starve the reserved capacity and the permit does not disable DoS controls. Failed normal authentication separately uses global token bucket 64 attempts/second with burst 128 plus fixed-cost constant-time fingerprint work; excess closes before body. After normal authentication, keyed bearer fingerprint receives at most 8 concurrent HTTP requests and 2 WebSockets. Rescue HMAC fairness keys are never displayed/persisted and rotating opaque strings cannot exceed the global unverified partition. No UID claim is made for TCP. Another local UID can still exhaust kernel listen backlog or CPU with sustained loopback traffic; V1 accepts that residual availability threat, while owner control and its reserved rescue permits remain recoverable over Unix socket.

Deadlines: downstream headers 5s; request body 30s without progress and 5m total; response write 30s without progress; keepalive 60s; upstream connect 5s, TLS 10s, response headers 30s; normal SSE/stream 5m without progress and no total limit; rescue owner-permitted HTTP/SSE 5m without progress and no total limit; unverified rescue HTTP/SSE 15s total; WS handshake 15s; normal and owner-permitted rescue WS 30m without data/control progress; unverified rescue WS five minutes total and 30s without progress. Limit/progress clocks are injected in tests. Capacity logs expose limit kind/count/status/latency only.

### Entry state machine

`cq proxy rescue enter`:

1. Construct instance context; acquire authority lock; validate key, anchor, manifest, artifact floor, and unfinished journal. Resolve exact supervisor/manager/socket/listener/worker. If `--listener` is present, compare its canonical numeric loopback tuple with the sealed listener and return `instance_mismatch`/3 plus exact `authority migrate` remediation before intent on disagreement; the flag never changes desired authority. Foreign, ambiguous, incompatible, or indeterminate authority refuses before write.
2. Rescue requires existing initialised primary authority with active `rescue_relay_v1`, verified listener definition, authority key, floor, artifact manifest, and local-token deny set. Never-initialised rescue is unsupported and returns exact `authority initialise prepare` remediation. Malformed normal config is never parsed to reconstruct these prerequisites.
3. Evaluate complete proposed authority. Any desired, pending, or effective binding—or unreadable initialised routing—requires `--suspend-session-policy`. Proposed generation records fixed-origin bearer acknowledgement and suspension. Binding addition refuses while desired/effective rescue, draining, or suspension exists.
4. Idempotent matching state returns without write. Otherwise commit one composite rescue intent plus `intent` journal phase before runtime action.
5. If the managed supervisor is stopped, commit manager-attempt phase/counter before starting the exact manifest-bound socket LaunchAgent. Never start a guessed binary.
6. Supervisor publishes `rescue_draining`, closes new normal ingress and single-use dispatch permits. New requests use rescue. Prepared and connected-unsent normal work fails `mode_changed`; it never becomes rescue. Dispatch-admitted work alone drains under captured worker.
7. Worker stops autonomous tasks and idle/undispatched WS. Dispatch-admitted operation may finish until true pinned terminal boundary. `response.completed` with `end_turn=false` is continuation-pending, not whole-turn release. At recorded 30-second deadline supervisor terminates exact worker; unfinished dispatches become indeterminate and downstream closes (`1012` for WS).
8. After worker absence, autonomous-work join, and dispatch-admitted count zero, commit terminal rescue authority generation. Supervisor acknowledges that exact terminal generation and only then marks full rescue effective. Lost acknowledgement reconciles journal/runtime; no side effect repeats.
9. Return 0 after exact target-generation rescue acknowledgement, 1 when durable intent pending, or typed conflict/down/indeterminate. Strict status stays 1 in rescue.

No provider failure, classifier result, quota signal, health degradation, or worker crash changes desired mode. Normal worker failure remains normal plus local 503. Worker/supervisor transition retains launchd socket; accepted connections may fail during supervisor replacement, but public bind authority never releases.

### Exit state machine

`cq proxy rescue exit`:

1. Construct context, acquire authority lock, validate anchor/artifacts/config/routing/semantics/manager/socket, and resume unfinished journal. Matching normal is idempotent.
2. Commit normal intent plus a fresh worker-attempt token before spawning the selected digest on the owner-only Unix endpoint through the sealed LaunchAgent supervisor.
3. Worker loads normal-only dependencies and reports attempt token, artifact/config/routing/semantics digests, process identity, current caller-credential fingerprint index, and readiness. Supervisor rejects stale/partial result; rescue remains effective.
4. After readiness, supervisor commits `rescue_exit_draining` before changing ingress gates. New rescue and normal requests, including next keepalive request, fail before body with `503 mode_changed`. Already admitted rescue HTTP may complete sole one-shot attempt within 30-second drain; it gains no retry/new upstream connection. Every rescue WS stops data forwarding, sends downstream 1012, closes upstream, joins pumps, and carries no later application message. Generation-bound counts track active rescue HTTP, WS, and connected-unsent relay.
5. Normal worker preparation may continue, but normal ingress stays closed. At deadline supervisor cancels HTTP and force-closes/reaps relay pumps. Only after all rescue counts are zero and worker still acknowledges exact boot/authority generation may it commit terminal normal, clear forwarding acknowledgement/policy suspension, and publish normal. Failure to prove zero remains `rescue_exit_draining`; supervisor crash treats lost sockets closed but must prove current counts zero.
6. If the selected worker terminally fails before normal publication, supervisor commits `restoring`, stops/reaps that exact attempt, and restores the saved rescue intent/suspension once. It does not spawn a floor, alternate, or second worker, and `rollback_attempts` remains zero for `rescue_exit`.
7. After exact restored-generation acknowledgement and prior rescue topology proof, commit terminal `prior_restored` and return non-zero with remediation to run an explicit matched `service artifact switch --role runtime-bundle` while rescue, wait for its terminal proof, then start a new rescue-exit operation. Rescue exit never changes manager, selected artifact pair, listener, or policy intent and never admits a mixed supervisor/worker pair.
8. Timeout with a live nonterminal selected-worker boot is pending, not restoration authority. Lost acknowledgement uses journal/runtime. No loop or repeated spawn/restoration counter.

Every commit, spawn, readiness result, publication, and restoration is recoverable from durable journal. Status exposes operation/phase/deadline/counters, desired/effective generations, worker attempt, and dispatch-drain counts.

## Routing-policy document

Canonical schema:


Schema version 1 rejects the complete routing document when any object contains an unknown field; V1 defines no extension bag. Unknown schema or required feature is never applied. Canonical writes sort pool names, account keys, bindings, predicates, and evidence deterministically. Runtime accepts routing object only from committed composite authority generation and never falls back to generation zero after initialisation. The canonical example above has one checked-in path-addressed placeholder manifest and materialised golden fixture. The manifest replaces every `opaque-*` placeholder in object keys and values with one deterministic well-formed test value, including exactly 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters for `opaque-delegation-id` and exactly 64 for `opaque-session-binding-hmac`; it rejects an unlisted placeholder or a replacement at the wrong path. Every keyed digest is recomputed under the fixed fixture keys, and the inverse placeholder projection of the materialised fixture must equal the literal example byte-for-byte outside substituted scalar/key tokens. The materialised fixture must pass the same closed production loader, canonicaliser, cyber-binding validator, and digest recomputation used for committed policy; the literal unmaterialised example must fail production validation, and documentation/manifest/fixture drift fails CU-7.

New routing keyed digests use lower-case hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 output and explicit length framing; bare `HMAC`, `HKDF`, `length`, or `session-key` shorthand is invalid. `K_session = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/session-hmac/v1"),L=32)`. `K_pool_definition = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=authority.key,salt=empty,info=ASCII("cq/pool-definition-hmac/v1"),L=32)`. `K_lease` is the exact existing 32-byte continuity-journal HMAC key for this instance, loaded through the retained secure `codex-turn-leases.key` authority; it is never `authority.key`, `K_session`, or `K_pool_definition`. Provider-branch admission and provider-caller subjects use only their exact separately domain-separated `authority.key`-derived keys defined above; they are never recomputed under a continuity or pool key. Every new formula below names one of `K_session|K_pool_definition|K_lease`, exact ASCII domain bytes, `uint32be` byte length, canonical bytes, and encoding. Key rotation follows its owning authority transaction and never silently reinterprets an existing digest.

The sole framing compatibility exception is the already-installed lease identity primitive. For exact validated bytes `V` and domain `D` in the closed set `session|thread|namespace|turn|account|candidate|requested-model|correlation|turn-state`, `LegacyLeaseIdentityBytesV1(D,V) = HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII(D) || 0x00 || V)`. V2/V3 rendered those exact 32 bytes as canonical unpadded RFC 4648 base64url; V4 renders the same bytes as 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters and never re-HMACs a legacy digest string. New V4 `account_key_hmac` and `candidate_id_hmac` use the `account` and `candidate` domains respectively and the same byte primitive, so live inventory and migrated continuity compare identical decoded digest bytes. New credential revisions have no legacy encoding: for exact revision bytes `V`, `credential_revision_hmac = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/lease-credential-revision/v1\0") || uint32be(len(V)) || V))`. These three names in V4/prewarm are continuity-journal identities; caller-index subject HMACs retain their separately named owner/key formulas.

Lane identity is the one composite legacy codec and is not a `hash_version:1` field. For exact 32-byte component identities `S=LegacyLeaseIdentityBytesV1("session",session)`, `T=LegacyLeaseIdentityBytesV1("thread",thread)`, and `N=LegacyLeaseIdentityBytesV1("namespace",namespace)`, let `s=Base64RawURLEncode(S)`, `t=Base64RawURLEncode(T)`, and `n=Base64RawURLEncode(N)`. `LegacyLaneIdentityBytesV1(S,T,N) = SHA256(ASCII(s) || 0x00 || ASCII(t) || 0x00 || ASCII(n))`. V2/V3 persist `Base64RawURLEncode(LegacyLaneIdentityBytesV1(S,T,N))`; V4 persists `hex(LegacyLaneIdentityBytesV1(S,T,N))`. Live V4 construction and migration therefore validate the three component identities first, reproduce the baseline text-framed lane bytes exactly, and only change their outer rendering. A lane digest that decodes to 32 bytes but does not equal this recomputation rejects the complete journal.

The remaining request-bound digests have these exact closed cores. `PolicyAuthorityCoreV1={schema_version:1,authority_generation,routing_generation,delegation_revocation_generation,routing_document}` contains the complete canonical routing document and no desired/effective role tag; `desired_policy_digest` and `effective_policy_digest` are respectively `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/routing-policy-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))` over `P=CanonicalJSONV1(PolicyAuthorityCoreV1)` from the desired or applied snapshot, so byte-identical snapshots have byte-identical digests. `EncodedRequestCoreV1={schema_version:1,content_type,content_encoding,wire_payload_sha256,wire_payload_length,ordered_semantic_headers}` hashes the exact final transmitted payload bytes and the duplicate-checked ordered semantic-header projection; only `content_type` and `content_encoding` may be null. For `E=CanonicalJSONV1(EncodedRequestCoreV1)`, `encoded_request_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/encoded-request/v1\0") || uint32be(len(E)) || E))`. `FinalRouteChoiceCoreV1={schema_version:1,route_id,provider,transport_kind:"http"|"websocket",method,upstream_origin_binding_digest,raw_path,raw_query,requested_model,outbound_model,transformation_digest,encoded_request_digest,normal_credential_origin_binding_digest,terminal_401_semantics:"codex_pinned_direct"|"generic_terminal_only",downstream_rejection_profile_map:DownstreamRejectionProfileMapV1}` has no nullable field. Its terminal tag and complete downstream map must byte-match the selected provider/transport members of the exact catalogue row above; a route/provider/target/transport/tag/profile-map mismatch rejects before permit issue. The tag is an authenticated status-401 selector only and is never an input to direct-candidate status-403 or exact-hard-quota status-429 classification. The map is immutable request authority used by capture, classifier-specific transition, exhaustion, live relay, restart, and recovery; none may infer a profile from the current handler, binary, or route ID alone. Canonical `F=CanonicalJSONV1(FinalRouteChoiceCoreV1)` is at most 32,768 bytes; an RCV held/grant/consumption projection requires `len(F) <= 4,096`, requires each complete enclosing object to remain at most 65,536 bytes, and charges every duplicate to the unchanged 3-MiB store cap. `final_route_choice_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/final-route-choice/v1\0") || uint32be(len(F)) || F))`.

Connection compatibility is distinct from acquired-socket identity. `ConnectionCompatibilityCoreV1={schema_version:1,downstream_connection_identity_digest,required_upstream_protocol:"http1"|"http2"|"websocket_http1_upgrade",ws_subprotocol,ws_extension_digest}` requires both WS fields non-null exactly for WebSocket and null otherwise; every other field is non-null. For `H=CanonicalJSONV1(ConnectionCompatibilityCoreV1)`, `connection_compatibility_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/connection-compatibility/v1\0") || uint32be(len(H)) || H))`. `ConnectionConstraintsCoreV1={schema_version:1,connection_compatibility_core:ConnectionCompatibilityCoreV1,connection_compatibility_digest,upstream_connection_identity_digest,connection_generation}` embeds the exact recomputed compatibility core/digest; `upstream_connection_identity_digest` and `connection_generation` are both null exactly before a socket is acquired and both non-null after acquisition. For `C=CanonicalJSONV1(ConnectionConstraintsCoreV1)`, `connection_constraints_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/connection-constraints/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`. Every immutable V4 request, active-non-V4 request authority, and prewarm plan input embeds the complete byte-identical pre-acquisition `ConnectionConstraintsCoreV1` plus its duplicated compatibility/constraint digests, with both socket fields null; a digest or projection without that complete core is never durable authority. Loader, permit issue/consume, retry, restart, prewarm dial/adoption, and real-client validation reopen the stored core and recompute both digests before using it. The acquired form is a transport-local observation and never request-, slot-, retry-, or adoption-plan authority; the immutable `AttemptLineageCoreV1` plus its phase event is the sole durable per-attempt acquired-socket authority. For `N=CanonicalJSONV1(NormalCredentialOriginBindingV1)`, `normal_credential_origin_binding_digest = hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/normal-credential-origin-binding/v1\0") || uint32be(len(N)) || N))`, exactly the unkeyed domain-separated construction required by that binding's security contract.

All routing evaluation instants use closed `CanonicalUTCInstantV1`: parse with Go `time.RFC3339Nano`, require UTC offset `Z`, year `0001..9999`, no leap second, at most nine fractional digits, and byte-equality to `parsed.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)`. `ResolverResultCoreV1.evaluated_at` is always one non-null `CanonicalUTCInstantV1` captured once from the one injected wall-clock read for the complete desired/effective resolution and copied byte-for-byte into every contraction evaluation; membership and caller validity endpoints are reopened from their authenticated owner objects and compared as canonical UTC instants against only that captured value, never against another clock read. Null, numeric, offset-equivalent, noncanonical fractional, unparsable, independently recaptured, or incomparable values make the complete contraction evaluation unavailable before cursor selection, permit issue, or upstream I/O.

`AuthorityComponentCoreV1={schema_version:1,first_excluding_component,owner_authority_generation,owner_routing_generation,evaluation_authority_generation,evaluation_routing_generation,component_projection}` is a closed tagged union whose projection is exactly one of `{kind:"global",global_set_digest}`, `{kind:"caller",caller_set_digest}`, `{kind:"binding",binding_digest}`, `{kind:"pool",pool_digest}`, `{kind:"route",final_route_choice_digest}`, `{kind:"capability",evidence_scope_digest,membership_valid_until}`, `{kind:"candidate",account_key_hmac,candidate_id_hmac}`, `{kind:"revision",credential_revision_hmac}`, `{kind:"delegation",caller_delegation_authority_digest}`, or `{kind:"validity",evaluated_at,membership_valid_until,caller_valid_until}`; the tag must equal `first_excluding_component`. Every digest and all four generations are non-null. The owner pair byte-equals the immutable owning active-non-V4, V4, or prewarm request/plan generations. The evaluation pair byte-equals the current composite-authority and routing generations held by the one retry/contraction snapshot and may advance beyond, but never precede, the owner pair; it is never copied from the frozen owner. When embedded in `AuthorityContractionExclusionV1`, both pairs additionally equal the corresponding enclosing pairs. `ResolverResultCoreV1` supplies desired/effective policy generations only and is never treated as containing either owner or evaluation pair. A validity component exists only for a valid expired result: `evaluated_at` byte-equals the enclosing resolver instant and is the one non-null injected `CanonicalUTCInstantV1`; each present endpoint is canonical, at least one endpoint is non-null, and `min(non-null membership_valid_until,caller_valid_until) <= evaluated_at`. Equality is expired. Canonical both-null endpoints and canonical all-future endpoints are valid non-exclusion outcomes and emit no `AuthorityComponentCoreV1` or exclusion row. A null/noncanonical/independently recaptured evaluation instant, a noncanonical/incomparable endpoint, or any second-clock substitution makes the whole contraction evaluation unavailable; it is never interpreted as a surviving group. The delegation projection names the complete desired/effective/intersection union and therefore cannot be replaced by one record or one revocation generation. Canonical `X=CanonicalJSONV1(AuthorityComponentCoreV1)` is at most 32,768 bytes; for valid `X`, `component_authority_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/authority-component/v1\0") || uint32be(len(X)) || X))`.

Caller authority retained by one request is one closed `CallerRequestAuthorityV1={schema_version:1,kind:"local_owner"|"provider_subject",selected_provider:"claude"|"codex",caller_pre_body_authentication:CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1,caller_pre_body_authentication_digest,caller_ingress_capability:CallerIngressCapabilityV1,caller_ingress_capability_digest,local_token_index_epoch,provider_caller_subject_hmac,caller_fingerprint_key_id,caller_index_epoch,caller_account_key_hmac,caller_candidate_id_hmac,caller_credential_revision_hmac,caller_delegation_authority:CallerDelegationAuthorityV1|null,caller_delegation_authority_digest,candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest:null|string,authority_generation,routing_generation,caller_set_digest,request_nonce,connection_identity_digest,issued_at,valid_until}`. Both complete nested objects and caller digests are non-null; their closed schemas, MACs, and digests recompute exactly, the routed capability embeds the byte-identical authentication, and every duplicated outer projection byte-matches those cores. Local-owner authority requires non-null `local_token_index_epoch` and null provider-subject/account/candidate/revision/delegation/synthetic fields. An ordinary provider-subject authority requires the inverse for provider and delegation fields while the synthetic digest remains null. A candidate synthetic provider-subject authority additionally requires a non-null synthetic digest equal to the nested authentication and reopened complete run authority/index/materialisation; candidate scope requires it and primary scope forbids it. Its selected-provider tag, subject HMAC, resolved account-set digest, and tenancy/validity projections must equal the exact ingress capability and resolver result. For a classified route, every caller kind, authentication, capability, tagged-subject/key/index, delegation union, synthetic provenance, request nonce, connection, authority generation, and validity fact represented by admission/consumption must match byte-for-byte; a `not_applicable` route still retains this complete caller object. `valid_until` may be null only when an ordinary owning current index has no finite endpoint; candidate synthetic authority is always finite. For `U=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerRequestAuthorityV1)`, `caller_request_authority_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/caller-request-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(U)) || U))`. The complete object/digest and both nested complete objects are immutable from ingress through terminal request state; index/key/revision/delegation/synthetic-authority drift can inhibit an uncommitted dispatch but can never replace the stored caller with another subject for the same account. A native loader never reconstructs either nested object or synthetic provenance from current index, route/body text, outer projections, or digest text.

Every ordinary dispatch authority names one purpose-bound `CallerDispatchPermitCoreV1={schema_version:1,purpose:"http_dispatch"|"http_retry"|"retained_dispatch"|"ws_upgrade"|"ws_first_send"|"prewarm_dial"|"prewarm_probe_send"|"prewarm_adoption"|"prewarm_first_send"|"websocket_application_send",websocket_application_send_ordinal:null|integer,permit_id,single_use_nonce,owner_kind:"active_non_v4_request"|"journal_v4_request"|"prewarm_reservation",owner_authority_digest,owner_state_digest,caller_request_authority:CallerRequestAuthorityV1,caller_request_authority_digest,resolver_result_core:ResolverResultCoreV1,resolver_result_digest,provider_branch_authority:ProviderBranchAuthorityV1,authority_generation,routing_generation,request_generation,attempt_generation,reservation_generation,account_key_hmac,candidate_id_hmac,credential_revision_hmac,normal_credential_origin_binding_digest,final_route_choice_digest,encoded_request_digest,slot_authority_digest,evidence_scope_digest,member_digest,connection_identity_digest,validity_endpoints:[DispatchPermitEndpointV1...],issued_at,valid_until}`. Closed `DispatchPermitEndpointV1={schema_version:1,kind:"fixed_ttl"|"owner"|"caller"|"delegation"|"membership"|"capability_evidence"|"request_deadline",source_digest,valid_until}` has null `source_digest` exactly for `fixed_ttl`; every other row names the exact reopened object that owns the endpoint. `validity_endpoints` contains exactly one fixed row with `valid_until=issued_at+5s` and exactly one row for every non-null finite endpoint in the complete owner request/reservation authority, caller request authority, caller delegation authority, selected slot/member, selected capability evidence, and explicitly present request deadline. Null endpoints produce no row. Rows are duplicate-free and sorted by `(parsed_valid_until,kind,source_digest)`: `parsed_valid_until` is the UTC instant returned by the common canonical parser and is compared chronologically, while kind and then raw source-digest bytes break ties only when instants are equal. Rendered RFC3339Nano bytes are never the primary time comparator because their variable fractional width is not chronological byte order; the already-canonical original timestamp spelling remains the serialised field. `owner_authority_digest` is exactly the active non-V4 request-authority digest, V4 `base_plan_digest`, or prewarm planning-authority digest selected by `owner_kind`; the caller object/digest and resolver object/digest must be byte-identical to that complete owner. `owner_state_digest` is non-null exactly for active non-V4 and names its current MACed state; it is null for V4 and prewarm. `request_generation` and `attempt_generation` are null, and `reservation_generation` non-null, exactly for `prewarm_dial|prewarm_probe_send|prewarm_adoption`; the inverse holds for every other purpose. `websocket_application_send_ordinal` is positive only for `websocket_application_send`, null otherwise, and contiguous on the selected parent connection. Every remaining field is non-null. Active non-V4 account, slot, and attempt generation must equal the current state selected from its frozen plan. The embedded provider-branch union must match the exact selected catalogue route and owning authority; direct routes therefore carry `not_applicable` rather than omitting authority. `permit_id` and `single_use_nonce` are independent 128-bit OS-CSPRNG values. Permit issue uses one injected `issued_at`, refuses when any required endpoint/source cannot be reopened or the chronologically first row's instant is not greater than `issued_at`, and sets `valid_until` to that row's canonical timestamp exactly. No omitted/extra row, later extension, current-policy reconstruction, null-as-infinity serialisation, or alternate TTL is legal. For `D=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerDispatchPermitCoreV1)`, `ordinary_permit_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/caller-dispatch-permit/v1\0") || uint32be(len(D)) || D))`.

Every ordinary-permit consumption is itself closed authenticated authority. `CallerDispatchPermitConsumptionCoreV1={schema_version:1,consumption_context:"ordinary_authority"|"prewarm_adoption_reservation",caller_dispatch_permit_core:CallerDispatchPermitCoreV1,ordinary_permit_digest,caller_dispatch_authority:CallerDispatchAuthorityV1,caller_dispatch_authority_digest,attempt_digest,phase:"http_dispatch"|"http_retry"|"retained_dispatch"|"ws_upgrade"|"ws_first_send"|"prewarm_dial"|"prewarm_probe_send"|"prewarm_adoption"|"prewarm_first_send"|"websocket_application_send",websocket_application_send_ordinal:null|integer,event_sequence,pre_cas_attempt_revision,consumed_at}` is closed. The ordinary context requires the embedded authority's `ordinary_permit_core` to byte-match the permit and its digest; the adoption-reservation context instead requires the embedded authority's `prewarm_adoption_authority_digest` and its reopened complete adoption authority to contain that byte-identical reservation permit. `phase` equals permit purpose and the send ordinal is positive and equal on both objects exactly for `websocket_application_send`, otherwise null; owner, state, attempt or reservation generations, caller/resolver/branch/route/slot/connection fields, event sequence, and nullable pre-CAS revision equal the owning CAS inputs. For `C=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerDispatchPermitConsumptionCoreV1)`, `mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/caller-dispatch-permit-consumption-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(C)) || C))`; `CallerDispatchPermitConsumptionV1={schema_version:1,core:CallerDispatchPermitConsumptionCoreV1,mac}` is closed, and for canonical complete bytes `V`, `caller_dispatch_permit_consumption_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/caller-dispatch-permit-consumption/v1\0") || uint32be(len(V)) || V))`. `CallerAdmissionGate` recomputes the owner, current state when present, complete permit and authority, every endpoint row, ordering, and minimum, injects one `consumed_at` satisfying `issued_at <= consumed_at < valid_until`, and in the same phase CAS creates the complete consumption, consumes the permit ID/nonce once, and persists the complete object plus digest in the V4 or active-non-V4 owner. Volatile prewarm persists it in the reservation; adoption copies its reservation-permit consumption into the durable adoption record. The owner/recovery index rejects any second occurrence of a permit ID, nonce, or consumption digest. Owner, state, purpose, replay, caller/subject, resolver-snapshot, branch, route/union, endpoint, clock, object/digest, or generation/validity substitution yields zero upstream bytes. A digest-only consumption, a phase event without its complete owning consumption, or a consumption created before/after rather than atomically with the phase CAS is invalid.

Non-V4 work is not authorised by an unnamed in-memory capability or a mutable account list. `ActiveNonV4RetryPlanCoreV1={schema_version:1,original_group_cores:[GroupCoreV1...],original_slot_cores:[SlotCoreV1...]}` is closed; the arrays use the exact V4 cores below, are non-empty, duplicate-free, contiguous, and sorted in frozen group/slot order. Every active-non-V4 slot requires `revision_mode="exact"`; `eligible_managed_refresh` is invalid for every provider and route in this authority kind. For `P=CanonicalJSONV1(ActiveNonV4RetryPlanCoreV1)`, `active_non_v4_retry_plan_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-retry-plan/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`. For canonical group bytes `G`, `active_non_v4_account_group_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-account-group/v1\0") || uint32be(len(ASCII(active_non_v4_retry_plan_digest))) || ASCII(active_non_v4_retry_plan_digest) || uint32be(account_group_index) || uint32be(len(G)) || G))`; for canonical slot bytes `S`, `active_non_v4_slot_authority_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-slot-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(ASCII(active_non_v4_retry_plan_digest))) || ASCII(active_non_v4_retry_plan_digest) || uint32be(slot_index) || uint32be(len(S)) || S))`. Its closed immutable request authority is `ActiveNonV4RequestAuthorityCoreV1={schema_version:1,active_request_id,request_generation,initial_attempt_generation,caller_request_authority:CallerRequestAuthorityV1,caller_request_authority_digest,resolver_result_core:ResolverResultCoreV1,resolver_result_digest,provider_branch_authority:ProviderBranchAuthorityV1,authority_generation,routing_generation,request_nonce,connection_identity_digest,caller_set_digest,member_digest,normal_credential_origin_binding_digest,final_route_choice_core:FinalRouteChoiceCoreV1,final_route_choice_digest,encoded_request_digest,connection_constraints_core:ConnectionConstraintsCoreV1,connection_compatibility_digest,connection_constraints_digest,retry_plan_core:ActiveNonV4RetryPlanCoreV1,retry_plan_digest,issued_at,valid_until}` with no nullable field except validity endpoints under their owning rules. The embedded final-route core is complete, its digest recomputes from it, and no retry, terminal capture, relay, restart, or recovery may reconstruct it from route ID, handler, current catalogue, or digest text. The embedded constraint is the complete pre-acquisition form, both duplicated digests recompute from it, and every slot is compatible with that one frozen route, body, and connection constraint; each slot carries its own evidence scope and membership endpoint. For `N=CanonicalJSONV1(ActiveNonV4RequestAuthorityCoreV1)`, `active_non_v4_request_authority_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-request-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(N)) || N))`.

The mutable supervisor state is `ActiveNonV4RequestAuthorityStateCoreV1={schema_version:1,active_non_v4_request_authority_digest,record_generation,state:"active"|"terminal",current_group_cursor,current_slot_cursor,current_attempt_generation,attempt_revision,transition_count,transition_head_digest,terminal_reason:null|"completed"|"cancelled"|"worker_lost"|"authority_lost"|"provider_subject_rejected"|"provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh"|"active_non_v4_no_same_request_refresh"|"exhausted_direct_403"|"exhausted_hard_quota_429"|"capture_unavailable",terminal_rejection_digest,terminal_at}`.
