Cursors select exactly one frozen direct slot, generations/revisions are monotonic, and `transition_head_digest` is null exactly when `transition_count=0`. Active requires both terminal fields and `terminal_rejection_digest` null. Terminal requires `terminal_reason` and `terminal_at` non-null; `terminal_rejection_digest` is non-null exactly for the three auth-rejection reasons, the two exhausted-provider reasons, and `capture_unavailable`, and null for every other reason. It selects `ActiveNonV4TerminalRejectionCoreV1` only for terminal `401`, and selects `FinalProviderRejectionAuthorityV1` only for terminal `403|429`; the two schemas and digest domains are never interchangeable. For `S=CanonicalJSONV1(ActiveNonV4RequestAuthorityStateCoreV1)`, `state_mac=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-request-authority-state-mac/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S)) || S))`; `ActiveNonV4RequestAuthorityStateV1={schema_version:1,core:ActiveNonV4RequestAuthorityStateCoreV1,mac:state_mac}` is closed, and for its canonical bytes `T`, `active_non_v4_state_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-request-authority-state/v1\0") || uint32be(len(T)) || T))`.

Each bounded retry appends one closed `ActiveNonV4RetryTransitionCoreV1={schema_version:1,active_non_v4_request_authority_digest,transition_ordinal,previous_transition_digest,evaluation_authority_generation,evaluation_routing_generation,resolver_result_core:ResolverResultCoreV1,resolver_result_digest,transition_kind:"direct_candidate_auth"|"exact_hard_quota",transition_evidence,transition_evidence_digest,from_group_cursor,from_slot_cursor,to_group_cursor,to_slot_cursor,previous_attempt_generation,next_attempt_generation,failed_account_group_digest:null|string,skipped_slot_range:SkippedSlotRangeV1|null,skipped_slot_range_digest:null|string,authority_contraction_exclusions:[AuthorityContractionExclusionV1...],authority_contraction_exclusion_digests:[string...]}`. The evaluation pair and complete resolver byte-match the one current retry snapshot; every embedded exclusion carries the immutable owner's pair plus this evaluation pair and resolver instant. The evidence is the complete tag-matching `DirectCandidateAuthRejectionEvidenceV1` or `ExactHardQuotaRejectionEvidenceV1`; ordinal zero requires a null predecessor, later ordinals require the immediately preceding transition digest. Direct-auth requires the failed-group and skipped-range fields null and both contraction arrays empty. Exact hard quota requires `failed_account_group_digest` to equal the from-group's active-non-V4 domain digest; it carries the complete inclusive skipped range when unused slots remain or the defined empty sentinel otherwise; its two equal-length contraction arrays contain every and only intervening excluded original group in order, with each digest recomputed from its complete object and the transition's exact resolver snapshot. The to-cursor is the first surviving exact slot after those proofs. Canonical `R=CanonicalJSONV1(ActiveNonV4RetryTransitionCoreV1)` is at most 2,097,152 bytes and the complete predecessor-linked transition chain is at most 8,388,608 bytes; both are charged to the frozen-plan pre-dispatch reserve. For valid `R`, `active_non_v4_retry_transition_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-retry-transition/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R)) || R))`. A classified route atomically creates the complete authority, initial state, and attempt lineage with the admission-consumption row, requires `active_request_id=owner_id` and `owner_kind="active_non_v4_request"`, and embeds the exact classified union; a `not_applicable` route atomically creates the same objects before `OpenHTTP|OpenWebSocket`. The owner record retains the complete authority/plan, state, immutable attempts and phase events, and ordered transitions. The MACed state's transition head authenticates the complete evidence, failed-group, skipped-range, contraction, cursor, owner/evaluation generation, resolver, and progression history through this predecessor chain. One retry CAS consumes the evidence once, appends the transition and next lineage, advances state, and invalidates every permit bound to the prior state. Direct-auth may advance only one next exact slot in the same group; exact hard quota skips the failed group and selects only the first surviving exact slot of the next original group after the recorded exclusions. No active non-V4 refresh slot is legal for any provider. Terminal CAS destroys unused permits. Supervisor restart never replays active work: after owner/worker identity proof it terminalises an orphaned active record as `worker_lost`, preserves its complete progression history and any classified consumption row until checkpoint, and opens zero upstream bytes. Missing, duplicate, substituted, oversized, unreserved, un-MACed, cursor-regressed, or evidence/progression/history-gapped active authority fails closed before any new upstream byte.

Every observed active-non-V4 `401` is terminalised only through closed `ActiveNonV4TerminalRejectionCoreV1={schema_version:1,active_non_v4_request_authority_digest,previous_active_non_v4_state_digest,terminal_reason:"provider_subject_rejected"|"provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh"|"active_non_v4_no_same_request_refresh"|"capture_unavailable",caller_kind:"local_owner"|"provider_subject",selected_provider:"claude"|"codex",attempt_digest,attempt_phase_authority_event_digest,slot_authority_digest,account_key_hmac,candidate_id_hmac,credential_revision_hmac,terminal_401_evidence:ActiveNonV4Terminal401EvidenceV1,terminal_401_evidence_digest,ingress_subject_exact_match,relay_disposition:"relay_retained_401"|"relay_live_baseline"|"continuity_unavailable",future_only_refresh_receipt_digest:null,final_request_generation,final_attempt_generation,final_record_generation,historical_attempts,further_attempts:0,terminal_at}`. The complete route-tagged evidence is non-null and byte-matches either the current attempt's qualifying complete captured HTTP or normal-WebSocket-handshake `401`, or its closed `capture_unavailable` observation after the transport resolved status `401` but exact bounded classifier capture could not be represented. A retained branch's embedded retained-response digest is the only durable response selector. The unavailable branch contains no durable response selector or response bytes; its optional authenticated `LiveDownstreamRelayDispositionV1` authorises only the exact still-live response/downstream pair and is never classifier, retry, refresh, restart, or replay authority. `ingress_subject_exact_match` is true when a provider subject equals outbound account/candidate/revision and independently causes destruction of only that exact live ingress subject even on `capture_unavailable`. For a retained branch, reason is `provider_subject_rejected` exactly for that equality, `provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh` exactly for a different provider subject, and `active_non_v4_no_same_request_refresh` for local owner and every Claude/local case not covered by the first two. For an unavailable branch reason is exactly `capture_unavailable`; relay disposition is `relay_live_baseline` iff its complete live disposition is non-null and the original downstream has committed no byte, otherwise `continuity_unavailable`. The exact-match Boolean still controls subject destruction without converting the terminal reason. `future_only_refresh_receipt_digest` is exactly null on every retained and unavailable branch. The active-non-V4 terminal CAS authorises no credential-owner refresh, index publication, acknowledgement, or later attempt; only a separate fresh ingress whose caller authority is independently current may begin any later owner-refresh protocol under its own request authority. Every other field is non-null. For `J=CanonicalJSONV1(ActiveNonV4TerminalRejectionCoreV1)`, `active_non_v4_terminal_rejection_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/active-non-v4-terminal-rejection/v1\0") || uint32be(len(J)) || J))`.

Before any active-non-V4 upstream byte, owner creation reserves the maximum route-specific retained-response after-image, a separate 32,768-canonical-byte `capture_unavailable` terminal after-image, the at-most-1,048,577-byte raw tee buffer, and the bounded-prefix plus transformed-output buffers when the final route requires them. One terminal CAS consumes the exact route-tagged evidence once, publishes the immutable terminal-rejection object/digest, advances the MACed state to the matching terminal reason/digest and final generations, invalidates every outstanding permit, appends no transition or attempt, and fixes `historical_attempts>0,further_attempts=0`. When bounded complete capture succeeds it durably captures and same-descriptor reopens the complete retained-response object in that CAS. When header/body/relay/object limits, framing validation, transformer disagreement, or a bounded capture read prevents complete classifier evidence after status `401` is known, the CAS must instead use the pre-reserved authenticated `capture_unavailable` evidence and terminal branch; it may not stay active, fall through, evict history, refresh, retry, or open another connection. If any required durable or transient reservation cannot be guaranteed, dispatch is refused before upstream I/O. The CAS destroys the exact live ingress subject whenever `ingress_subject_exact_match=true`; no other subject is destroyed or converted. The same still-live supervisor may relay a retained `401` or execute the unavailable object's exact route-mandated `LiveDownstreamRelayDispositionV1` once only while the original upstream response/downstream identities remain live and no response byte was attempted. Limit exhaustion, partial read, or oversized headers therefore disable classification but do not replace baseline `writeError` or raw streaming with continuity unavailable on the live path. Process/supervisor restart, response/downstream loss, null live disposition, or ambiguity after a response-write attempt always yields continuity unavailable and never replays response bytes. Recovery reopens the terminal object/state and retained or unavailable evidence only for verification; it never treats the live disposition as reopenable and never resumes owner refresh, index publication, acknowledgement, or dispatch. Missing/substituted evidence, reason/tag/equality/disposition disagreement, a transition append, or any classifier/permit/refresh replay dispatches zero bytes.

The complete terminal `401` object, including its complete `ActiveNonV4Terminal401EvidenceV1` and exactly one retained or unavailable response, or the mutually exclusive complete terminal `403|429` `FinalProviderRejectionAuthorityV1`, is embedded in the existing MACed active-owner record and covered by its bounded journal publication; `terminal_rejection_digest` is its content-addressed selector inside that record, not a sidecar or separately scanned file. The 16-MiB journal byte cap and one-terminal-capture-per-active-owner cardinality reserve the 1,851,392-byte response-object maximum, the independent 32,768-byte unavailable after-image, the complete terminal after-image, and publication temporary before owner creation. Transient reservation additionally covers the 1,048,577-byte raw tee maximum or, for a Codex-selected Anthropic-compatible route, the 1,048,576-byte bounded read result plus 6,291,531-byte maximum `writeError` output. Those buffers are not journal capacity and are zeroised under the retained-response rule below. Full classifier-capture overflow selects the unavailable branch from pre-reserved capacity while retaining only its small authenticated live disposition; no terminal CAS evicts progression history or exceeds either cap.

## Pool semantics

### Names and membership

- Pool names use lower-case kebab case, 1–63 characters.
- Explicit pools require at least one unique non-empty opaque account key.
- `pool set` is full replacement, not additive mutation.
- CLI resolves each account reference through existing exact-key, email, and alias resolution. Ambiguous or missing references reject the complete mutation.
- Persisted pool membership contains only opaque account keys.
- One `AccountKey` denotes one exact logical user/workspace authority, including exact ChatGPT account identity. Evidence for another workspace, even with same email or user ID, never transfers.
- Pool membership never expands global allowlist authority.
- Empty global allowlist retains existing meaning: every discovered globally authorised account.
- Empty named pool is invalid; it never means every account.
- Pool deletion fails while any session binding references it.
- Pool replacement/deletion fails while active caller delegation references it; revoke then re-grant against new exact set. Replacement also fails while any bound cyber-scoped pool would change its approved definition digest; explicitly unbind and rebind affected sessions with fresh authorised-use confirmation.
- No implicit or fallback pool exists in schema version 1.

`PoolDefinitionV1` is the exact closed canonical union `{kind:"explicit",account_keys:[...]}` or `{kind:"capability",requires:[...]}` with no pool name, evidence, or derived membership. Explicit account keys sort by exact UTF-8 bytes. Capability predicates sort by the exact UTF-8 tuple `(capability,product_surface,access_path,auth_mode,requested_model,effective_model)` and retain every field including explicit `*`. Let `P = CanonicalJSONV1(PoolDefinitionV1)`. `pool_definition_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_pool_definition, ASCII("cq/pool-definition/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`. Delegation `source_pool_definition_digest` and cyber `approved_pool_definition_digest` use this one function; no separately ordered or unkeyed definition digest is valid.

`PolicyAccountSetV1={schema_version:1,account_keys:[...]}` is a non-empty exact-UTF-8-byte-sorted duplicate-free list. For `A=CanonicalJSONV1(PolicyAccountSetV1)`, `allowed_set_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_pool_definition, ASCII("cq/policy-allowed-account-set/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`; the delegation's stored list and digest must recompute exactly. `TenancyScopeV1={schema_version:1,openai_organization,openai_project,fedramp,residency}` permits null only for an absent selector and otherwise retains exact validated value bytes. For `T=CanonicalJSONV1(TenancyScopeV1)`, `tenancy_scope_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_pool_definition, ASCII("cq/policy-tenancy-scope/v1\0") || uint32be(len(T)) || T))`; caller and allowed tenancy-scope fields use this one function over their respective exact scopes.

### Caller delegations

Default caller authority is exact account matched by downstream bearer. Cross-account CQ routing requires explicit delegation. `delegation grant` resolves caller account to exactly one current finite-lifetime credential candidate/revision; multiple candidates require explicit `--caller-candidate` opaque candidate ID, while missing, expired, or unknown-expiry candidates reject. It resolves one **explicit** pool through current global authority, snapshots sorted opaque member keys, and commits OS-CSPRNG 128-bit lower-case hexadecimal delegation ID, exact caller account/candidate/revision/subject HMACs, caller fingerprint-key ID, credential `valid_from` and `valid_until`, caller tenancy-scope digest, pool-definition digest, allowed-set and allowed-tenancy-scope digests, grant time, and mandatory future expiry no later than caller credential expiry. Capability-derived pools are not delegation sources in V1 because membership can expand without grant mutation. Confirmation names caller, candidate hint, pool, member count, and effective expiry before commit.

A complete routing document contains at most one delegation record for each `caller_subject_hmac`, regardless of expiry. Duplicate subjects reject complete document without consulting clock. Grant refuses whenever record exists unless `--replace-existing`; replacement removes prior record, increments revocation generation, and creates fresh delegation ID in one composite CAS. Expired records remain inert until explicit revoke or replacement and storage-only GC never removes them. Requests carry no delegation selector because authenticated bearer resolves exactly one subject and therefore zero or one record; implementations never union or choose by breadth, expiry, insertion order, or map order.

Delegation provenance is canonical rather than a singular optional record digest. `CallerDelegationRecordCoreV1={schema_version:1,delegation_id,caller_account_key,caller_candidate_id_hmac,caller_credential_revision_hmac,caller_subject_hmac,caller_fingerprint_key_id,caller_credential_valid_from,caller_credential_valid_until,caller_tenancy_scope_digest,source_pool,source_pool_definition_digest,allowed_account_keys,allowed_set_digest,allowed_tenancy_scope_digest,granted_at,expires_at}` is the exact map key plus closed persisted record; only `caller_tenancy_scope_digest` may be null and its lists obey the canonical ordering above. For `D=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerDelegationRecordCoreV1)`, `caller_delegation_record_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/caller-delegation-record/v1\0") || uint32be(len(D)) || D))`.

Every active provider-subject resolver result carries one closed `CallerDelegationAuthorityV1={schema_version:1,kind:"singleton_no_record"|"singleton_expired_record"|"effective_record"|"pending_grant_intersection"|"pending_replacement_intersection"|"pending_revoke_intersection",provider:"claude"|"codex",provider_caller_subject_hmac,desired_record_digest,effective_record_digest,desired_revocation_generation,effective_revocation_generation,resolved_account_set_digest,resolved_tenancy_scope_digest,evaluated_at,valid_until}`. `resolved_account_set_digest` and `evaluated_at` are always non-null; `resolved_tenancy_scope_digest` is null only when neither caller nor selected authority has a tenancy selector, and `valid_until` is null only for `singleton_no_record` whose live caller has no finite endpoint. `singleton_no_record` requires all record/generation fields null and is the only Claude-legal kind. `singleton_expired_record` and `effective_record` require byte-identical non-null desired/effective record digests and equal non-null revocation generations; the former resolves the caller singleton at the common expired-record evaluation row, while the latter resolves the active record. `pending_grant_intersection` requires only desired record/generation non-null; `pending_replacement_intersection` requires all four non-null and different record digests; `pending_revoke_intersection` requires only effective record/generation non-null. Each intersection's resolved account-set, tenancy, and earliest validity endpoint are the exact resolver-table result, never either wider input. For `A=CanonicalJSONV1(CallerDelegationAuthorityV1)`, `caller_delegation_authority_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/caller-delegation-authority/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`. The union and digest are byte-identical in ingress capability, resolver result, provider admission, caller-request authority, active non-V4/V4/prewarm authority, every permit, retry, contraction, and restart; a digest-only or singular desired/effective projection is invalid.

Active delegation replaces default singleton caller set with frozen delegated set; it does not union or widen global/session/route authority. Caller must remain discovered and fingerprint-index authenticated as exact same account/candidate/revision subject; current time must satisfy caller validity and precede both delegation and credential expiry; exact source pool definition/tenancy scope must remain unchanged; top-level revocation generation must match capability. Credential refresh, replacement, removal, re-addition, or index-key rotation invalidates grant and requires explicit re-grant. Grant cannot name empty pool or out-of-global member. Expired delegation is inactive and reported; it never falls back to cross-account routing. `revoke` removes exact record and increments `delegation_revocation_generation` in same composite generation, invalidating every unadmitted capability/permit. Delegation ID and opaque keys appear only in explicit delegation commands; health/status/info/doctor expose active/expired counts and earliest expiry.

This explicit authority preserves CQ multi-account routing without allowing any arbitrary loopback bearer to spend another stored account. Operator may create broad explicit pool deliberately, but no migration, global allowlist, account tier, or session binding creates delegation implicitly.

Delegation publication requires already-active monotonic feature `caller_delegation_v1`; release import or prior explicit `feature activate` must establish it through floor-before-authority transaction. Activation cannot commit until every CU-7 delegation marker child is current. First grant attempted before activation returns `feature_inactive`/3 without mutation. Revoking or expiring last delegation never lowers feature floor. Binary lacking `caller_delegation_v1` refuses authority document rather than ignoring delegation state.

### Capability pools

A capability pool contains one or more exact all-of `requires` predicates. Predicate scope is `(capability, product_surface, access_path, auth_mode, requested_model, effective_model)`. No field implies another; wildcard applies only when evidence and predicate both contain explicit `*`. `cyber.governance.trusted_access`, `cyber.daybreak.blue`, `cyber.daybreak.red`, and `model.invoke` are separate names; Blue, Red, legacy cyber models, generic invocation, and safety-classifier treatment never imply each other.

Evidence uniqueness key is `(AccountKey, predicate scope, source)`. Duplicate keys reject complete document. Source `manual` is reserved for operator writes; adapter source names are registered and cannot be supplied by manual CLI. Fusion truth table across fresh exact sources is: both eligible and ineligible => conflict; ineligible only => ineligible; eligible only => eligible; otherwise => unknown. Conflict remains excluded and appears as aggregate diagnostic. Exact `expires_at` is exclusive: evidence is fresh only when `observed_at <= now < expires_at`; future observations, invalid intervals, unknown enums, and wrong scopes are invalid rather than silently ignored.

A pool is **cyber-scoped** when any `requires` predicate capability begins literal `cyber.`, including mixed all-of pools. Explicit pools are not cyber-scoped merely because operator intends cyber use. Cyber-only, mixed, non-cyber, and replacement-to/from-cyber validation use this exact definition.

Base membership evaluates each account/predicate from fresh exact evidence at one injected clock instant. Final route qualification occurs only after candidate-specific `RouteChoice` determines actual surface, path, auth, requested model, locally resolved outbound model, transformation, and encoded bytes. Evidence `effective_model` means model previously observed from authoritative provider response; it can authorise only a route whose locally resolved outbound model matches that value or whose manual predicate/evidence both use explicit `*`. If current response later reports a different effective model, request is already provider-admitted: CQ records only source-owned observation, never retries or claims pre-send prevention. Every pre-send known field must match predicate/evidence; later local scope-changing transformation invalidates plan.

Capability scope uses only exact closed cores. `CapabilityFinalScopeCoreV1={schema_version:1,route_id,provider:"claude"|"codex",transport_kind:"http"|"websocket",product_surface,access_path,auth_mode,requested_model,effective_model,outbound_model,transformation_digest,encoded_request_digest,normal_credential_origin_binding_digest}` and `CapabilityPredicateCoreV1={schema_version:1,capability,product_surface,access_path,auth_mode,requested_model,effective_model}` have no nullable fields and retain explicit `*` literally. `CapabilityFinalScopeCoreV1.effective_model` must be byte-identical to `outbound_model`; every predicate and evidence comparison uses that final outbound value, never a pre-transformation alias. `CapabilityEvidenceUseCoreV1={schema_version:1,account_key_hmac,capability,product_surface,access_path,auth_mode,requested_model,effective_model,state:"eligible",source,observed_at,expires_at}` permits only `expires_at` to be null. `CapabilityRouteScopeCoreV1={schema_version:1,final_scope:CapabilityFinalScopeCoreV1,predicates:[CapabilityPredicateCoreV1...],evidence_used:[CapabilityEvidenceUseCoreV1...]}` requires non-empty duplicate-free predicates sorted by exact UTF-8 tuple `(capability,product_surface,access_path,auth_mode,requested_model,effective_model)` and duplicate-free evidence sorted by `(account_key_hmac,capability,product_surface,access_path,auth_mode,requested_model,effective_model,source,observed_at,expires_at_is_null,expires_at_or_empty)`, where `expires_at_is_null=false` sorts before `true`, `expires_at_or_empty` is the canonical timestamp when finite and the empty string when null, and neither sentinel appears in the stored evidence object. It contains exactly every eligible source fact used to satisfy each predicate for this account and final route, and no unknown/ineligible/conflicting/unused fact.

For `S=CanonicalJSONV1(CapabilityRouteScopeCoreV1)`, `evidence_scope_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/capability-route-scope/v1\0") || uint32be(len(S)) || S))`. An explicit-pool slot instead uses exactly `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/capability-route-scope-explicit/v1\0") || uint32be(0)))` and a global slot uses exactly `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/capability-route-scope-global/v1\0") || uint32be(0)))`; the three domains are disjoint and cross-kind substitution rejects. The slot freezes that digest, member digest, and earliest finite `membership_valid_until`. Runtime re-evaluates the complete core at prepare, retry, adoption, and first send. Expiry/change abandons unadmitted work within frozen-envelope rules.

V4 restriction digests use three closed cores. `PoolRestrictionV1={schema_version:1,pool_name,pool_definition_digest}`; `BindingRestrictionV1={schema_version:1,session_binding_hmac,pool_digest,approval_scope_ref_digest,approved_pool_definition_digest,authorised_use_ack}` with the exact cyber/non-cyber nullability above; and `LeaseAccountSetV1={schema_version:1,purpose:"member"|"caller"|"original",account_key_hmacs:[...]}` with a non-empty sorted duplicate-free lower-hex list. For canonical bytes `P`, `B`, and `A`, respectively: `pool_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/lease-pool-restriction/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P))`; `binding_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/lease-binding-restriction/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))`; and `lease_account_set_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/lease-account-set/v1\0") || uint32be(len(A)) || A))`. `member_digest`, provider-subject `caller_set_digest`, and `original_set_digest` are the last function with their matching literal purpose. Local-owner caller authority instead uses the closed identity sentinel `local_owner_global_caller_set_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/lease-caller-set-local-owner-global/v1\0") || uint32be(0)))`; it denotes no caller-account restriction and is intersected with global, binding, pool, continuity, route, capability, candidate, revision, and validity authority after inventory discovery. It is never a `LeaseAccountSetV1`, member, pool, or unrestricted-session digest and cannot be used by a provider subject. An unbound session uses the non-empty sentinel `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/lease-binding-unbound/v1\0") || uint32be(0)))`; global/no-named-pool uses the distinct non-empty sentinel `hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/lease-pool-global/v1\0") || uint32be(0)))`. No sentinel is a valid bound restriction or named pool digest, and all three sentinel domains are mutually non-substitutable.

Conflict is account-and-predicate local: fresh eligible plus ineligible excludes that account but does not disable safe members. `capability_evidence_conflict` is terminal only when conflict alone excluded every otherwise route-qualified member; otherwise it is aggregate diagnostic. Missing/expired/unknown/ineligible/scope mismatch follows ordinary eligibility errors.

Capability pool definitions contain no cached member list. Runtime derives membership from one policy snapshot and discovered global inventory, then records only aggregate effective counts in health.

For every local-owner `CallerRequestAuthorityV1`, `caller_set_digest` is exactly `local_owner_global_caller_set_digest` and its byte-identical resolver result is exactly the active `local_owner_global` branch; no concrete caller account set or delegation object may appear. For every provider-subject authority, `caller_set_digest` instead equals the non-empty `LeaseAccountSetV1` digest in its singleton/delegated resolver branch and the local-owner sentinel is forbidden. Active non-V4/V4/prewarm owner creation, every permit, retry, refresh, contraction, adoption, restart, and real-client held/grant/consumption boundary rechecks this exact kind/sentinel relation before inventory intersection or upstream I/O.

## Session bindings

`session bind` computes:

```text
B = exact validated UTF-8 session_id bytes
session_binding_hmac = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_session,
  ASCII("cq/session-binding/v1\0") || uint32be(len(B)) || B))
```

`CanonicalSessionID` is one shared CLI/protocol validator: non-empty valid UTF-8, at most 4096 bytes, with no NUL or other C0/DEL control. It performs no trimming, case folding, Unicode normalisation, UUID parsing, or textual rewriting; visually equivalent but byte-distinct values remain distinct. Protocol and CLI hash exact validated bytes. Full 32-byte lower-case hexadecimal digest is authoritative lookup. Short digest hints are display-only. CQ state, health, ordinary logs, and routing diagnostics never persist raw session IDs. Direct `--session-id` can remain in shell history/process arguments; privacy-preferred stdin is exact EOF-framed bytes.

Legacy-import real-client proof has stricter session authority. Fresh `authority import-legacy prepare` requires `--real-client-session-id-stdin`; that option reads exactly one EOF-framed `CanonicalSessionID`, has no argv-valued alternative, and rejects empty, over-limit, invalid, trailing-control, or second-value input before ticket publication. After the new instance key exists, prepare computes the ordinary `session_binding_hmac` above, persists only that value as ticket field `real_client_session_binding_hmac`, zeroises the live input buffer, and never writes, logs, receipts, exports, or diagnoses the raw bytes. Recovery reopens the persisted HMAC and never asks a resumed operation to reconstruct raw session authority.

Installed-client emission is pinned rather than inferred from a later observed correlation. `InstalledClientSessionEmissionFixtureV1={schema_version:1,client_build,client_executable_digest,transport:"http",metadata_semantics:"strict_codex_turn_metadata_v1",session_field:"session_id",emission_cardinality:"exactly_one_before_first_dispatch"}` is a checked-in duplicate-free registry row for the exact installed build. For `F=CanonicalJSONV1(InstalledClientSessionEmissionFixtureV1)`, `real_client_session_emission_fixture_digest=hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/installed-client-session-emission-fixture/v1\0") || uint32be(len(F)) || F))`. Import prepare selects the row through its exact candidate preflight/production-profile build and executable, binds the digest into the ticket, and refuses an unsupported or ambiguous build before ticket publication. Before launching `validate-real-client`, primary authority commits the ticket-created binding under exactly `real_client_session_binding_hmac`, installs the matching temporary pool and delegation, obtains `RuntimePolicyAckV1` for that complete routing generation, and binds the same HMAC and fixture digest into the validation invocation. The held child request must contain exactly one fixture-defined raw session value whose recomputed HMAC equals the ticket and binding before resolver/grant/dispatch authority; missing, duplicate, differently encoded, late, or unequal emission rejects with zero upstream bytes. The observed session/turn values remain correlation only after this authoritative equality has passed.

Binding one session covers every root and subagent thread carrying that exact canonical `session_id`. It restricts candidate accounts; it does not pin the entire session to one account. Existing lane/turn continuity still chooses and retains exact account identity within pool boundaries.

`session show --session-id ID` or stdin form hashes input locally and looks up exact full digest. Explicit operator `session list` exposes pool name, bind time, exact full keyed digest usable by `--digest`, and optional short hint; it never exposes raw ID. Health, info, status, doctor, and logs still expose counts/hints only. `session unbind` requires explicit raw-ID/stdin flag or exact full `--digest`; form is never guessed and prefix deletion is forbidden.

Desired binding or caller delegation becomes effective only after supervisor and ready worker publish and same-descriptor reopen the canonical `RuntimePolicyAckV1` defined above. Stable `proxy_instance_id` owns persisted policy identity; per-process `runtime_instance_id` proves the current supervisor/worker applied it and expires at supervisor restart. `RequiredMarkerChildren(required_features)` is the exact exhaustive table above, and the sole marker-set algorithm is the unkeyed canonical `MarkerSetFingerprintInputV1` SHA-256 formula defined with `InstalledMarkerV1`. Its rows equal the required set exactly: an extra, missing, duplicate, reordered, HTTP-only, WebSocket-only, expired-at-use, mixed-build, wrong-scope/run/ID/digest, or failed child invalidates the set. Exact supervisor/worker/client build and executable facts are authenticated inside every resolved marker and must agree across the set; they are not appended through another fingerprint input or keyed variant. CU-5 owns the reusable acknowledgement/marker schema and verifier primitives. CU-6 may issue only acknowledgements supported by its implemented children and cannot issue session-pool/delegation acknowledgement; CU-7 supplies and issues against the complete enforcement children. Build-scoped installed marker set is not rerun for each policy mutation; a fresh `RuntimePolicyAckV1` binds current runtime instance, exact required features, and whole desired policy digest to the existing valid set.

One `DesiredEffectivePolicyResolverV1` compares complete valid desired snapshot `D`, exact runtime-acknowledged effective snapshot `E`, their whole-policy digests/generations, and the current caller/session projection. It returns separate closed results `binding=unbound|bound(effective-record)|inhibited` and `caller_set=local-owner-global|singleton|delegated-intersection|inhibited`. Its closed `ResolverResultCoreV1={schema_version:1,desired_generation,desired_policy_digest,effective_generation,effective_policy_digest,evaluated_at,binding:{kind:"unbound"|"bound"|"inhibited",source:null|"effective",binding_digest:null|string},caller_set:{kind:"local_owner_global"|"singleton"|"delegated_intersection"|"inhibited",account_set_digest:null|string,local_owner_scope_digest:null|string,caller_delegation_authority:CallerDelegationAuthorityV1|null,caller_delegation_authority_digest:null|string}}` permits `source:"effective"` and a non-null binding digest only for `bound` and requires both null otherwise. An active provider-subject result requires non-null exact account-set, null local-owner scope, and non-null delegation union/digest. An active local-owner result is exactly `kind:"local_owner_global"`, has null account-set and delegation fields, and has `local_owner_scope_digest` equal to `local_owner_global_caller_set_digest`; it is the caller-intersection identity and does not materialise inventory before discovery. Inhibited requires all four fields null. The provider union kind and record projections must be the exact row below and its resolved account-set digest must equal `caller_set.account_set_digest`; the local-owner branch never enters that table. For `X=CanonicalJSONV1(ResolverResultCoreV1)`, `resolver_result_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/desired-effective-resolver-result/v1\0") || uint32be(len(X)) || X))`. Every active non-V4 request authority, V4 `RequestAuthorityCoreV1`, prewarm `PrewarmPlanInputCoreV1`, `CallerDispatchPermitCoreV1`, and `AuthorityContractionExclusionV1` persists the complete byte-identical core and digest. Loader, retry, restart, and final admission recompute the digest, reopen the exact two snapshot generations/digests, and reject a digest-only, independently regenerated, role-swapped, or singular-record result. For a current local-owner authentication and two valid snapshots whose caller projection contains no provider delegation, every acknowledged or explicitly safe pending relation returns `local_owner_global`; a missing/invalid snapshot or stale runtime/marker acknowledgement returns inhibited. These tables are otherwise exhaustive:

The shared branch-object nullability matrix is exhaustive and applies byte-for-byte to construction, canonical encoding, MAC/digest recomputation, load, retry, restart, contraction, and final admission:

| Closed object and discriminator | Required non-null branch objects | Required null branch objects |
|---|---|---|
| `ProviderCallerSubjectV1.provider="claude"` | `claude_subject` | `codex_subject` |
| `ProviderCallerSubjectV1.provider="codex"` | `codex_subject` | `claude_subject` |
| `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationCoreV1.kind="local_owner"` | none of the provider/delegation/synthetic objects | `provider_caller_subject`, `caller_delegation_authority`, both corresponding HMAC/digest fields, and `candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest` |
| ordinary primary `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationCoreV1.kind="provider_subject"` | `provider_caller_subject`, `caller_delegation_authority`, and both corresponding HMAC/digest fields | `candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest` |
| candidate synthetic `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationCoreV1.kind="provider_subject"` | `provider_caller_subject`, `caller_delegation_authority`, both corresponding HMAC/digest fields, and `candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest` | none of those five fields |
| `CallerRequestAuthorityV1.kind="local_owner"` | none of the delegation/synthetic objects | `caller_delegation_authority`, `caller_delegation_authority_digest`, `candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest` |
| ordinary primary `CallerRequestAuthorityV1.kind="provider_subject"` | `caller_delegation_authority`, `caller_delegation_authority_digest` | `candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest` |
| candidate synthetic `CallerRequestAuthorityV1.kind="provider_subject"` | `caller_delegation_authority`, `caller_delegation_authority_digest`, `candidate_synthetic_ingress_authority_digest` | none |
| `ResolverResultCoreV1.caller_set.kind="singleton"|"delegated_intersection"` | `caller_delegation_authority`, `caller_delegation_authority_digest` | none |
| `ResolverResultCoreV1.caller_set.kind="local_owner_global"|"inhibited"` | none of the delegation objects | `caller_delegation_authority`, `caller_delegation_authority_digest` |

For each row, every object and its corresponding HMAC/digest are one inseparable null/non-null pair, and every non-null nested object must satisfy its own tag before any outer MAC or digest is accepted. The candidate synthetic digest additionally reopens one complete live authority/materialisation/index triple and is non-null only in candidate role; it is never accepted as a digest-only substitute. `ProviderBranchAdmissionCoreV1` follows the same local-owner, ordinary-provider, and candidate-synthetic three-row provenance matrix. A wrong tag, both provider subjects present, neither provider subject present, an object without its HMAC/digest, a HMAC/digest without its object, a synthetic digest in primary scope, a missing synthetic digest in candidate scope, or any row substitution makes the complete enclosing authority unavailable; no loader infers a missing branch from another field.

| Binding relation for exact session | Binding result before next acknowledgement |
|---|---|
| `D` and `E` both absent, with current acknowledgement for `D` | `unbound` |
| `D` and `E` contain byte-identical binding and referenced pool definition, with current acknowledgement | the exact `E` restriction with `source:"effective"` |
| pending add: absent in `E`, present in `D` | inhibited; unacknowledged coverage cannot enforce the new boundary |
| pending replace: different binding, pool, definition, or cyber-approval digest | inhibited |
| pending unbind: present in `E`, absent in `D` | retain exact `E` restriction until acknowledgement; never expose the broader desired unbound path |
| missing/invalid snapshot, stale effective runtime instance/marker set, or any other relation | inhibited |

| Delegation relation for exact current caller subject | Caller-authorised set before next acknowledgement |
|---|---|
| both absent | singleton caller account with `CallerDelegationAuthorityV1.kind="singleton_no_record"` |
| byte-identical active record, definition/set/scope/revocation generation and expiry in `D` and `E` | exact delegated set with `kind="effective_record"` and both equal record/revocation projections |
| byte-identical record expired at the one injected clock instant in both snapshots | singleton caller account with `kind="singleton_expired_record"` when current index still proves it; otherwise inhibit |
| pending grant: absent in `E`, present in `D` | `singleton caller ∩ D.allowed` with `kind="pending_grant_intersection"`; empty intersection inhibits |
| pending replacement for the same exact caller subject | `E.allowed ∩ D.allowed` with `kind="pending_replacement_intersection"`, the earlier expiry, and exact common tenancy/definition scope; empty intersection inhibits |
| pending revoke: active in `E`, absent in `D` | `E.allowed ∩ singleton caller` with `kind="pending_revoke_intersection"`; empty intersection inhibits |
| record expiry/validity differs between snapshots or cannot be evaluated at the same injected clock instant | inhibited |
| caller subject, candidate/revision, source-pool definition, tenancy scope, revocation generation, or record identity cannot be reconciled exactly | inhibited |
| any other relation | inhibited |

The resolver never unions snapshots, selects by newest generation alone, treats absence as every account, or carries a stale broader delegation. A whole-policy generation mismatch is usable only through an explicit pending row above; unrelated fields must be byte-identical in the caller/session projection and both complete snapshots must validate. Binding and caller results are then intersected with global, continuity, credential, and route authority. Startup applies policy before normal admission. Older/incompatible binaries refuse after feature-floor activation.

### Canonical request classification and metadata

One `StrictCodexTurnMetadataParser` owns HTTP, compact, retained/fallback, WebSocket-frame, and prewarm parsing. It performs bounded strict JSON decoding and rejects invalid UTF-8, isolated UTF-16 surrogate escapes, duplicate members on every authority path, multiple direct metadata-header values, wrong types, unknown request kinds/phases, unknown fields inside CQ-owned authority object, malformed nested JSON strings, and over-limit values. Unrelated outer fields follow pinned protocol schema.

Parser decodes every supplied nested, direct-header, flat, and handshake projection. Every supplied strong projection must exactly match across canonical authority fields. Weak handshake may omit fields, but every supplied field must equal authoritative frame. Contradiction is `session_metadata_invalid`; handshake never becomes strong by agreement. Decoder never replaces invalid bytes, normalises, trims, or chooses one projection.

| Request kind | Required exact metadata | Binding coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `turn` | session, thread, turn; no compaction phase | HTTP response and each WS `response.create` |
| `compaction` | session, thread, turn, `compaction_phase` exactly `standalone_turn|pre_turn|mid_turn` wire bytes | standalone/pre-turn/mid-turn compact operation; retained/fallback path states preserve original phase and never introduce phase values |
| `prewarm` | exact semantic `prewarm_v1` frame below | terminating WS plan/dial only; adoption/first send reclassify real turn |
| `memory` | exact pinned memory shape below | global, outside session bindings |
| missing/unknown/malformed/contradictory | none | fail before legacy routing when any desired, pending, or effective binding exists |

Memory exemption is semantic, never caller label alone: pinned request must be `response.create`, nested CQ metadata contains only `request_kind=memory`, no session/thread/turn/window/compaction authority, and no model, instructions, input, tools, previous response, encrypted state, response anchor, incremental input, or other continuity field. Header/flat/handshake-only, additive, or relabelled memory does not qualify. Changed shape requires semantics revision and fixtures. Retained/fallback preserves original classification.

`prewarm_v1` is semantic and cannot be selected by `request_kind` alone. Its sole producer and acceptance oracle is the checked-in `codex-startup-prewarm-builder-v1` structural fixture generated from pinned Codex 0.147.0. The fixture runs the pinned startup path `build_prompt(Vec::new(), current_tool_router, startup_turn_context, BaseInstructions{current_base_instructions})`, the pinned ordinary `build_responses_request` with the exact selected `ModelInfo`, effort, summary, service tier, provider, and startup metadata, then serialises `ResponsesWsRequest::ResponseCreate(ResponseCreateWsRequest{previous_response_id:None,generate:Some(false),..ResponseCreateWsRequest::from(&request)})`. Its complete duplicate-free outer field set is therefore the pinned ordinary WebSocket request set: `type`, `model`, optional-by-Serde `instructions`, absent `previous_response_id`, `input`, optional `tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `reasoning`, `store`, `stream`, optional `stream_options`, `include`, optional `service_tier`, optional `prompt_cache_key`, optional `text`, `generate:false`, and `client_metadata`. Values and omission are exact builder output after only declared runtime substitutions; in particular `input` is the complete builder-derived startup input and is not required to be empty, while ChatGPT `store=false`, `stream=true`, `tool_choice="auto"`, and the pinned include/model/reasoning/tool/Responses-Lite rules remain exact.

Startup metadata is the pinned `TurnMetadataState::to_responses_metadata(installation_id,window_id,Prewarm)` output, not a synthetic reduced map. `client_metadata` therefore retains the exact installation, session, thread, **window**, empty initial turn, and nested `x-codex-turn-metadata` projections; the nested object requires `request_kind:"prewarm"`, the same non-empty session/thread/window, and empty turn, and retains every pinned optional parent/subagent/source/sandbox/workspace/code-mode/timestamp/filtered-extra projection actually produced by the startup context. Direct handshake/header and flat compatibility projections must agree with that body authority but cannot create it. The fixture manifest pins the complete `ModelInfo`, structural-builder source digest, optional-field matrix, metadata projection, decoded ordinary `ResponsesApiRequest`, and expected wire JSON; production parser and CU-7 use the same fixture decoder. Missing, true, null, non-Boolean, or duplicated `generate`; present `previous_response_id`; a body that differs from the fixture-derived request; HTTP use; or relabelled ordinary request fails `session_metadata_invalid` before plan/dial. Unknown pinned-body fields require a semantics revision. Classifier derives prewarm only after validating the complete frame.

## Routing admission contract

Session policy is a hard eligibility boundary, not a preference.

An always-installed `SessionPolicyCoverageGate` runs before native enforcing handlers and every legacy/off/observe fallback. It validates committed composite authority and both complete routing snapshots first, then parses strong metadata and invokes `DesiredEffectivePolicyResolverV1` for the exact binding and caller subject. If policy authority is unavailable after initialisation, every canonical policy-aware route fails closed. If any desired, pending, or effective binding exists, weak or missing metadata on canonical route returns `session_metadata_required`. A strong session continues only with the resolver's exact `unbound` or `bound` result and non-inhibited caller set. Pending binding add/replace inhibits; pending unbind remains bound to the exact effective restriction; delegation grant/replace/revoke/expiry uses only the table's singleton or intersection. Every bound result additionally requires effective `enforce` semantics and current transport markers for the exact runtime/listener; off, observe, missing coverage, stale readiness, or any inhibited resolver result returns `session_pool_policy_inhibited` before legacy selection. Stale broader authority never reaches the global path.

For each native HTTP request, every compact phase, retained request/fallback, WebSocket `response.create`, retry/rotation decision, prewarm plan/dial, and prewarm adoption, caller admission has two boundaries. `CallerIngressAdmission` runs before body bytes/worker/inventory and validates header/selector grammar, complete current index, and one exact live caller subject; it emits only caller-auth unavailable/required. `CallerRouteScopeAdmission` runs after bounded strict metadata and keyed continuity lookup but before candidate inventory expansion, route ranking, credential-owner work, or upstream bytes; exact routed account outside caller/delegation scope emits `normal_caller_auth_scope_violation`. Tenant-selector compatibility with caller subject is ingress; compatibility with delegated destination is route-scope and is rechecked at every attempt.

1. Strictly classify request and metadata; acquire ingress authority and capture composite mode generation.
2. Capture one immutable valid routing policy and injected-clock instant.
3. Resolve exact caller subject and zero-or-one delegation capability already authenticated at ingress.
4. Resolve keyed binding and durable continuity without expanding candidate inventory; apply global/caller/pool/continuity intersection. Admitted/non-migratable turn restricts to exact account. Outside pool is continuity conflict; outside caller scope is caller route-scope violation; deauthorised/unavailable exact account is continuity unavailable. None migrates.
5. Only then load full globally authorised inventory and enumerate credentials/account-candidate-route combinations inside hard intersection. Resolve candidate-specific final surface, path, auth, requested/outbound model, transformation, selector and evidence scope.
6. For exact-account continuation, ignore capacity exclusion and select highest-priority fully qualified route for exact account.
7. For new turn, evaluate capacity for every fully qualified account-candidate-route combination before route priority. Remove known-zero-capacity combinations; if any remain, select highest-priority route represented and rank only compatible combinations by capacity/fairness/affinity. If none remain, one configured default inside every hard intersection may supply exactly one terminal attempt on its highest-priority qualified route despite zero capacity. Otherwise return exhausted. A zero-capacity higher-priority route never hides available lower-priority route.
8. Append configured default at most once only inside every hard intersection and compatible with route selected above.
9. Freeze selected route, transformation, outbound model, and encoded bytes once. Retain only account-candidate combinations exactly compatible with frozen route/body; no retry/phase/account receives different semantics.
10. Freeze original ordered slots and acyclic routing envelope. Within each new-turn account group, append every direct candidate slot in existing resolved-candidate order, then at most one `eligible_managed_refresh` slot naming the first managed CQ-authored candidate; no refresh slot may be inserted beside its direct candidate or ahead of another direct slot. Account groups retain the original new-turn account order. Only `ExactHardQuotaRejectionV1` may skip the unused remainder of one group and select the first still-authorised direct slot of the next originally frozen group. Continuation freezes the current same-account candidate revision followed by at most its one explicit same-account managed-refresh slot, never another account.
11. Acquire gates in total order: caller-index/dispatch-authority → mode → routing → sorted accounts → credential-owner lifetime guard → continuity lifecycle → optional prewarm → journal. Final dispatch/WS first send holds exactly one `CallerDispatchAuthorityV1` branch through journal CAS. Revalidation is pure snapshot comparison; no callback acquires earlier gate. Release reverse order before network/credential-owner I/O.
12. Before first dispatch-admitted slot, changed authority may rebuild complete envelope. Afterwards each retry intersects unused original slots with latest global, caller, binding, pool, route, capability, candidate, revision, delegation, and validity authority. Order stays fixed; expansion, unbind, new affinity/default/delegation/evidence adds nothing. Publication after CAS does not cancel current attempt.

Hard eligibility is:

```text
global allowlist
∩ local-owner-global identity, caller account, or exact active delegation
∩ resolved session pool, when bound
∩ exact discovered/routable credential authority
∩ final route-qualified model/capability scope
```

Capacity is new-turn ordering/admission policy, not membership. `session_pool_empty` means no authorised routable member before model/capacity evaluation. `session_pool_model_incompatible` means members exist but none supports request. `session_pool_exhausted` is zero-attempt only when compatible members are excluded by capacity and no in-pool terminal-default exception exists.

Canonical covered routes are HTTP `/responses`, `/v1/responses`, `/responses/compact`, `/v1/responses/compact`, all listed compact phases, retained execution/fallback, and WebSocket `/responses` `response.create`/prewarm. Only exact pinned memory shape is exempt. Realtime, app-server, and routes without canonical authority remain global and explicitly outside coverage. Status commands report route-by-route desired/effective coverage and inhibition.

Transport phase and provider admission are orthogonal. HTTP legal transitions are `prepared -> connected_unsent|dispatch_admitted|provider_failed|abandoned_before_dispatch`; unadmitted `connected_unsent -> dispatch_admitted|provider_failed|abandoned_before_dispatch`; admitted `connected_unsent -> dispatch_admitted|provider_failed|indeterminate`; `dispatch_admitted -> streaming|provider_completed|provider_failed|indeterminate`; `streaming -> provider_completed|provider_failed|indeterminate`. Prepared failure is legal only definite zero-byte/pre-send rejection. Connected-unsent indeterminate requires admission or ambiguous admission persistence. `provider_admitted` may change false→true from connected-unsent onward and never clears.

Fresh identified-turn WS obtains `ws_upgrade` permit and commits `prepared -> upgrade_dispatched` immediately before first upstream upgrade byte. `upgrade_dispatched` means provider may have observed authenticated upgrade; it is not `response.create` dispatch admission. It becomes `connected_unsent` only after complete valid 101; definite zero-byte or complete non-admitting rejection becomes `provider_failed`; timeout, EOF, cancellation, malformed/incomplete response, process loss, or other ambiguity becomes exact-attempt-account non-migratable `indeterminate/orphaned`. Valid 101 with authoritative Turn-State atomically marks provider admission; without it remains unadmitted. Reused validated socket enters connected-unsent after exact connection/account/candidate/revision/route/selector revalidation. First frame still needs independent `ws_first_send` permit and dispatch CAS. No ambiguous upgrade replans/migrates.

`BeginRequest` on admitted record stores `request_base_state=continuation_pending|bound_quiescent`; a later unadmitted attempt may hold `bound_active` without claiming current admission. Closed matrix:

| Phase | Admitted | Ever | Lease/result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| prepared/connected-unsent | false | false | `provisional`; abandon→`failed_unadmitted` |
| prepared/connected-unsent | false | true | `bound_active`; abandon restores `request_base_state` |
| upgrade-dispatched | false | false | `provisional`; ambiguity/restart→pre-admission `orphaned`, attempted account retained |
| upgrade-dispatched | false | true | `bound_active`; ambiguity/restart→`orphaned`, prior tuple retained |
| upgrade-dispatched | true | true | valid only while atomically becoming connected-unsent; failure/restart→`orphaned` |
| connected-unsent | true | true | `bound_active`; restart/authority loss→`indeterminate/orphaned` |
| dispatch-admitted | false | false | `provisional`; restart→pre-admission `orphaned` |
| dispatch-admitted | false | true | `bound_active`; restart→`orphaned` preserving prior tuple |
| dispatch-admitted/streaming | true | true | `bound_active`; restart→`orphaned` |
| provider-failed | false | false | next retry prepared/provisional, else `failed_unadmitted` |
| provider-failed | false | true | next same-account retry prepared/bound-active, else `bound_quiescent` |
| provider-failed | true | true | `bound_quiescent`; no retry |
| provider-completed | true | true | `continuation_pending` when exact end-turn false, else `bound_quiescent` |
| indeterminate | false | false | `orphaned`, attempted account retained, tuple absent, non-migratable |
| indeterminate | false/true | true | `orphaned`, exact account/prior tuple retained, non-migratable |
| abandoned-before-dispatch | false | false | `failed_unadmitted` |
| abandoned-before-dispatch | false | true | restore `request_base_state` |

Every omitted combination is invalid: prepared-admitted, streaming-unadmitted, completed-unadmitted, abandoned-admitted, admission tuple with Ever=false, or admitted with Ever=false. Orphan always retains exact attempted account and never retries/refreshes/prewarms/migrates; pre-admission orphan validly lacks tuple and later exact-turn request returns continuity-unavailable. Dispatch admission is durable last-pre-send boundary. Rescue drains every admitted or dispatch-admitted operation; unadmitted prepared/connected work records `mode_changed`; admitted connected-unsent closes without send and becomes orphaned.

## Continuity and live policy changes

- Provider-admitted and indeterminate turns never migrate accounts.
- Dispatch-admitted but definitely provider-rejected attempts may use only unused original slots intersected with latest restrictive authority; expansion never adds slot.
- Policy expansion affects only request with no dispatch-admitted slot or new real turn. Contraction may remove unused slots but cannot cancel current dispatch.
- Exact account removed from base pool returns `session_pool_continuity_conflict`; still in base pool but currently deauthorised/unavailable/incompatible returns `session_pool_continuity_unavailable`. Neither falls back to another account.
- New real turns use latest policy and may discard predecessor soft affinity outside pool.
- Classifier, safety, cyber ineligibility, generic 4xx/5xx, ambiguous transport failure, or post-admission failure never rotates accounts. `ExactHardQuotaRejectionV1` on portable provider-unadmitted new-turn or prewarm work is the sole cross-account exception and may use only the next surviving originally frozen account group.
- Credential revocation blocks new unadmitted operation. Already dispatch-admitted work may finish because abort cannot prove non-dispatch.
- Policy store is never consulted while continuity, lane, credential, or prewarm locks are held.

### Lease journal v4 routing authority

Where a request, plan, permit, contraction, or validation clause requires `caller_set_digest` to equal the resolver caller-set projection, the selected projection is branch-specific: `ResolverResultCoreV1.caller_set.local_owner_scope_digest` for `local_owner_global`, and `.account_set_digest` for `singleton|delegated_intersection`. Inhibited has neither and cannot create an owner. No consumer compares the local-owner sentinel to null or materialises a concrete local-owner set from inventory.

Every durable or volatile outbound attempt has one immutable pre-evidence lineage. `AttemptLineageCoreV1={schema_version:1,authority_kind:"journal_v4"|"active_non_v4"|"prewarm_reservation",request_generation,attempt_generation,reservation_generation,volatile_attempt_ordinal,final_plan_digest,account_group_index,account_group_digest,slot_index,slot_authority_digest,actual_credential_revision_hmac,transport_family:"http1"|"http2"|"websocket"|"prewarm_websocket",connection_identity_digest,connection_generation}`. Routing transition, terminal-proof, and prewarm-history capacity uses one canonical table and is admitted before dispatch, never discovered after a provider response. These substitutions are capacity-only raw-value measurements; canonical `null` is exactly four bytes and none of the substituted forms is authority or persistable state. The publication temporary is the byte-identical proposed journal after-image, so `t=j`. Define `a_fit=min(K,K-s_c,K-s_p-s_c,floor((K-s_j-s_p-2*s_c)/2))`; checked subtraction or division failure, including any negative term, refuses. Adoption is capacity-eligible exactly when both complete dial and contraction histories satisfy their independent 8,388,608-byte bounds, every other object satisfies its listed bound, and `a<=a_fit`, equivalently `a<=K && c<=K && p<=K && j<=K && t<=K`. Measuring the complete consumption and proof counts the authority and both histories twice: once inside the top-level consumption and once inside the consumption nested by the top-level proof. It neither pads a legal object to a bound nor sums abstract maxima as if they were constructible bytes. From immutable original group/slot arrays, the counting serialiser constructs the maximum legal monotonic path and complete terminal after-image: every original slot is charged once at its owning transition/disposition maximum, every possibly intervening excluded group once at the complete 65,536-byte exclusion maximum, and every complete evidence, skipped range, contraction component/object/digest, predecessor, attempt, lineage, phase event, permit consumption, state projection, tagged transition union/selector duplicate, terminal evaluation, proof, response family, head/count, journal after-image, and publication temporary at its literal nesting depth. Before prewarm reservation creation and before each next dial or probe permit, the same serialiser applies the equation with conservative maximum legal non-history shells and the maximum legal histories reachable from the frozen plan plus current proposal; inability to satisfy it refuses before network I/O. Immediately before adoption authority/permit consumption and its journal CAS, it measures the fully constructed actual canonical `a,s_c,c,s_p,p,s_j,j,t` and reapplies the same equation. The adopted real V4 plan independently reserves its complete later V4 maximum before `prewarm_first_send`. A per-object exact bound succeeds only when the joint equation and every other limit also hold; the first per-object, history, envelope, full-journal, or publication-temporary byte over its bound refuses `resource_capacity_exhausted` before permit issue, dial, adoption, or send. Loader/recovery recomputes the same equation and canonical table from the same complete frozen bytes and reopens every complete object/digest/head/count; no separate capacity-reserve proof is persisted, inferred, or required. Digest-only history, mismatch, oversize, an uncharged literal duplicate, or a first post-I/O capacity failure is unavailable authority. No retry or terminal CAS may prune history.

All identities/revisions use the exact codecs above; raw identifiers never persist. Each attempt carries immutable lineage, ordered immutable phase events, monotonic provider admission/evidence, mutable `attempt_revision`, actual credential revision, connection generation, optional refresh receipt, closed `retry_authority=none|direct_candidate_auth|exact_hard_quota|managed_refresh`, monotonic `account_group_cursor`, monotonic `slot_cursor`, and state. Record carries monotonic first-admission tuple and immutable original group/slot digests. A same-account retry must advance exactly one unused direct slot within the current group. A cross-account attempt must carry exact hard-quota evidence below, mark the failed group, record the exact skipped range or empty sentinel, and advance both cursors to the first direct slot of the next surviving original group; every intervening group carries the exact contraction object/digest, including its complete component authority/digest, from the same clock/snapshot. Loader and every CAS reject a lineage rewrite, phase-event reorder/replay, revision mismatch, cursor regression, revisited/skipped eligible group, unproved skipped slot, refresh-slot landing, or cross-account transition with missing/mismatched attempt/evidence/range/contraction/component authority. Legal transitions and lease combinations are exactly the closed matrix above; loader fully decodes every enum/flag/object before validation and never defaults/classifies by phase alone.

V1-v3 migration is startup-only with proxy stopped/drained, socket lineage extinct, and every routing/attempt/prewarm/dispatch-permit/credential-owner operation reference zero. Loader order is exact: retain source directory/key/journal identities and raw bytes; strictly decode source schema and verify MAC/uniqueness/enums/generations/references/invariants without restart normalisation; write/sync exact archive `continuity/migrations/<version>-<keyed-source-digest>.archive` and directory; construct off-path the **final restart-normalised V4 after-image**; validate it; revalidate source/archive identities/bytes/MACs/generations and absence of desired/effective binding; install that final image through one atomic migration CAS; sync directory; reread/validate installed bytes. No semantic normaliser runs after installation. Thus no raw routable V4 intermediate exists and each changed generation increments at most once.

Version mapping is closed. Empty V1 becomes empty V4. Non-empty V1 becomes V4 `legacy_quarantine` containing source version/digest, authoritative/shadow epochs, retention deadline, and no routable records; activation remains inhibited until existing quarantine protocol proves `NoLegacyAuthority`, because V1 lacks lanes/requests/attempts/admission/revision evidence. V2 copies only valid V2 facts and V3 copies valid V3 facts. Their generations, timestamps, predecessor facts, refs, and complete record-level admission tuples copy exactly. Every retained V2/V3 scalar identity field produced by the source `hash_version:1` codec—session/thread/namespace/turn references, account/candidate, requested-model, correlation, turn-state, predecessor, and admitted-affinity references—is first required to be the canonical 43-character unpadded base64url spelling of exactly 32 decoded bytes, then mapped to V4 as `hex(Base64RawURLDecode(source_value))`. Lane is excluded from that scalar list: migration first decodes its session/thread/namespace components, recomputes `LegacyLaneIdentityBytesV1`, requires the source lane's canonical base64url bytes to equal that result, and writes the lower-hex result to the V4 lane definition and every lane reference. Empty optional identity stays absent. The mapping is applied consistently to definitions and every reference and never hashes encoded digest text; malformed/noncanonical input, a lane/component mismatch, a post-map duplicate, or any reference disagreement refuses the complete migration. Thus live and migrated V4 lane resolution use identical baseline bytes while all persisted V4 identities are lower hex. Missing V4 credential, route/evidence, complete nested `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1`, complete nested routed `CallerIngressCapabilityV1`, the exact branch-selected `CallerDelegationAuthorityV1|null` plus paired `caller_delegation_authority_digest:null|string`, caller-request authority, complete desired/effective resolver result, provider-branch classification/admission/consumption, supervisor owner row, active non-V4 authority, complete pre-acquisition connection constraint, complete `FinalRouteChoiceCoreV1` plus its recomputed digest, complete journal-V4 routing envelope, real-client validation issued/terminal grant-owner state, grant, or consumption, prewarm adoption authority/consumption, receipt, phase-event, provider-subject, per-attempt admission, catalogue-selected `terminal_401_semantics`, `RetainedProviderRejectionCoreV1`, complete `RetainedDownstreamRelayV1` plus any required transformer input/output cores and digests, `ActiveNonV4Terminal401EvidenceV1`, `FinalV4Terminal401AuthorityV1`, V4 terminal-401 exhaustion proof and WS one-use relay facts, dispatch-permit endpoint, or permit-consumption-time facts are never fabricated: old attempts enter bounded non-authoritative `legacy_attempt_history` with source-specific unavailable sentinel and can never dispatch/retry/admit/classify/relay, while non-V4 work has no legacy migration lane at all. A post-migration fresh request obtains new exact pre-body authentication, routed ingress capability, the branch-correct delegation object/digest pair, caller authority, resolver result, provider-branch admission/consumption when applicable, tagged provider subject, catalogue-derived terminal-401 tag, canonical permit endpoint minimum, and durable permit-consumption phase event through ordinary ingress; restart of an existing native V4 request instead requires its `CallerRequestAuthorityV1` to embed the already stored complete authentication and capability plus its complete caller/resolver/delegation/branch/consumption authority and exact supervisor owner row, and never reconstructs any of them from projections, digest text, route/body text, current index, current policy, or a legacy response. A pre-amendment V4 record that lacks any newly required closed field is not upgraded in place: it is retained only as unavailable history and its request returns continuity unavailable with zero replay or retry.

The migration boundary also treats complete `CallerDispatchPermitCoreV1`, `CallerDispatchAuthorityV1`, `CallerDispatchPermitConsumptionV1`, and their event linkage as one indivisible native-V4 fact; it never derives a permit object or consumption MAC from a legacy digest/timestamp. It never fabricates `RawUpstreamResponseHeadersV1`, `RawUpstreamResponseTrailersV1`, `DownstreamRelayResponseHeadersV1`, a classifier projection, `RetainedProviderRejectionCoreV1`, `RetainedDownstreamRelayV1`, either transformer core/digest, `RetainedProviderRejectionUnavailableV1`, `ConsumedRetryTransitionV1`, `TerminalEvaluationCoreV1`, `FinalProviderRejectionExhaustionProofV1`, or `FinalProviderRejectionAuthorityV1` from an old response/history row. A native pre-amendment V4 or active-non-V4 owner lacking any complete required object, route-profile status/header/trailer relation, RCV parent arm receipt where applicable, or terminal-response union is retained only as unavailable history and opens zero upstream/downstream replay bytes. Fresh post-migration work creates all objects through the owning issue/phase/arm/terminal CAS under current bounds.

The caller and prewarm tag/nullability matrices are also indivisible native-V4 facts. Migration and every native loader require the exact selected provider subject, pre-body/request/delegation/resolver branch, and surviving-slot mapping row, including literal null members, before accepting any enclosing MAC or digest. They never infer a missing subject, delegation object, lineage, socket, or generation from a tag, digest, current index, dial head, or another mapping. A pre-amendment object with a wrong tag, both or neither provider subjects, an object/digest half-pair, a partial current-connected tuple, or any non-null future-unconnected attempt/socket member is unavailable history; an adoption with such a row has zero reuse, dial, dispatch, or downstream replay authority and is never capacity-normalised by dropping the row.

The terminal-proof boundary is likewise indivisible. Migration never fabricates a complete `AuthorityComponentCoreV1` inside `AuthorityContractionExclusionV1`, complete tagged `ConsumedRetryTransitionV1` inside `ConsumedAttemptTransitionSelectorV1`, `TerminalEvaluationCoreV1`, `ManagedRefreshGateFailureProjectionV1`, `TerminalRetryDispositionEvidenceV1`, `FinalProviderRejectionLaterGroupDispositionV1`, either complete exhaustion proof plus its digest, or the caller/disposition/reason/future-only-receipt fields of `FinalV4Terminal401AuthorityV1` from a cursor, enum, digest list, current resolver result, current inventory, or refresh-store scan. A native pre-amendment terminal row with a null/digest-only transition, digest-only component or disposition, absent nested object, absent proof digest, absent terminal evaluation, provider-subject `401` without its complete caller and exact-match disposition, or receipt not selected by the same terminal predecessor becomes unavailable history with zero retry, refresh, subject-conversion, downstream replay, or permit authority. A pre-amendment active-non-V4 terminal row with a missing or non-null `future_only_refresh_receipt_digest` is likewise unavailable history with zero owner-refresh, acknowledgement, index-publication, retry, or replay authority; migration never clears or rewrites it into native authority. Pre-amendment prewarm adoption without every complete `PrewarmDialHistoryEntryV1`/digest and its referenced lineage, dial/probe event, and permit consumption, the complete dial-history arrays/head/count, or the complete contraction objects/digests/head/count transitively embedded in authority, consumption, and proof is unavailable adoption history and authorises no recovered socket or first send. Migration never fabricates, reorders, truncates, or reconstructs a dial-history entry or reference from a dial-attempt digest, volatile socket state, current plan, or current permit store. Fresh native owners construct these complete objects only in the transition, observation, refresh-resolution, adoption, or final-rejection CAS. Migration/recovery apply every new component bound and recompute the canonical capacity table plus the prewarm `a,s_c,c,s_p,p,s_j,j,t,a_fit` equation from the same complete frozen bytes before accepting the journal; they neither require nor fabricate a persisted reserve-proof object.

The migration boundary additionally treats a real-client `dispatch_prepared` selector, its complete preparation, proposed consumed owner state and consumption, complete `RealClientValidationDispatchTransactionProjectionV1` with V4-CAS-injected commit time, projection digest, transaction digest, `DispatchAdmitted` phase event, and RCV `dispatch_committed` projection as one indivisible native-V4 fact. It never fabricates any member or infers admission from an unselected RCV preparation/anchor alone.
