Likewise migration never fabricates `BaselineCodexErrorReadResultCoreV1`, `LiveDownstreamRelayDispositionV1`, widened error-status relay facts, or a transformed 403/429 response from old body/header history. A legacy or pre-amendment retained rejection can supply neither classifier nor downstream replay authority; only a fresh live response may construct the new complete retained or live-only branch.

R28 migration refinement is closed. No migrator fabricates `DownstreamRejectionProfileMapV1`, an embedded final-route profile map, `RetainedProviderWsTextRejectionCoreV1`, `LiveWsTextRelayDispositionV1`, `ProviderWsTextRejectionUnavailableV1`, or any of their MACs/digests from route labels, handler identity, response history, wire-frame fragments, or digest text. A legacy, active-non-V4, or pre-amendment V4 owner missing the complete authenticated profile map or the complete established-message retained/unavailable union is unavailable history with zero classifier, retry, refresh, dispatch, or downstream replay authority. Fresh work constructs the map from the current signed catalogue before final route selection and constructs established-message authority only from the exact live logical message and socket-bound attempt phase.

V2/V3 mapping priority is closed and non-overlapping, in this order:

1. Explicit stable `continuation_pending|bound_quiescent` with complete admission tuple and no live in-flight attempt preserves exact state/account/tuple.
2. Existing valid orphan preserves exact account, tuple or valid pre-admission absence, and non-migratable state. This includes the only valid legacy result of abandoning a prepared request whose record had `EverAdmitted=true`.
3. Valid source `LeaseReserving` with zero current attempt restart-normalises to failed-unadmitted, preserves validated record/lease generations and `last_request_generation`, increments only semantic after-image generations once, and clears exact matching lane. Any current attempt makes this row inapplicable.
4. Any prepared/connected/dispatched/streaming/indeterminate current request with `EverAdmitted` becomes orphaned on exact attempted account with prior tuple retained and non-migratable.
5. Completed/provider-failed current with `EverAdmitted` but without explicit source stable record also becomes orphaned. Legacy lacks authenticated request-base/end-turn proof and never fabricates bound-quiescent.
6. Prepared/connected-unsent current without `EverAdmitted` becomes failed-unadmitted only with authenticated proof that no request/application byte could have crossed its dispatch fence, and clears the exact matching lane.
7. Provider-failed current without `EverAdmitted` instead requires complete definite rejection evidence, no provider admission, no downstream commit, and no transport ambiguity. It becomes failed-unadmitted and clears the exact matching lane even though a send occurred; zero-send proof is neither required nor valid for this row.
8. Abandoned-before-dispatch current without `EverAdmitted` requires the valid legacy terminal combination: source lease `provisional`, prepared-origin attempt, zero routing/attempt/observer references, extinct socket lineage, and authenticated abandonment before its dispatch fence. It preserves bounded legacy attempt history, becomes failed-unadmitted, and clears the exact matching lane. Any abandoned-before-dispatch record with `EverAdmitted` that is not already a valid source orphan refuses migration.
9. Dispatched/streaming/indeterminate without `EverAdmitted` becomes pre-admission orphan, attempted account required, tuple absent, non-migratable.
10. Superseded/expired/failed-unadmitted history preserves bounded history and clears only stale matching pointer.

Every other or inconsistent combination refuses complete migration.

V4 adds `last_request_generation`, initialised to maximum validated current/admission/history request generation; clearing current never resets it and next begins +1. Envelope and `migration_generation` equal source+1. Record/lease/lane generation increments exactly once when respective semantic after-image changes; each changed attempt revision increments once; unchanged history preserves it. Overflow refuses entire migration.

Immediately before rename migration CAS revalidates directory/key/journal descriptor identities, exact source bytes/schema/generation/MAC/keyed digest, archive identity/path/exact bytes/digest, and absence of desired/effective binding. It writes synced final-image temp, atomically renames once, syncs directory, rereads exact installed bytes/identity. Recovery: source+no archive creates/verifies archive; source+exact archive rebuilds/retries same final image; exact final V4+archive after lost acknowledgement succeeds only when prior version/source/archive/migration generation match; every pre-normalised or other combination poisons/refuses. After feature floor, any request-path V1-v3 returns continuity-unavailable.

V1 `PinnedAuthRejectionV1` is conservative closed managed-refresh classifier. HTTP Responses/compact qualifies only after one complete upstream response with status exactly `401` over an admitted HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 transport, complete validated headers/body framing, no downstream status/body committed, no provider admission, and non-ambiguous transport. HTTP/1.1 completion requires its declared framing to terminate exactly. HTTP/2 completion requires the qualifying response stream to reach `END_STREAM`, whether on response headers, data, or admitted trailers. `RST_STREAM`, connection loss, or `GOAWAY` that leaves that stream's completion ambiguous is ineligible; `GOAWAY` observed only after the stream reached `END_STREAM` does not invalidate the already-complete response. Normal terminating WebSocket qualifies only from one complete upstream HTTP/1.1 non-`101` handshake with status exactly `401`; authenticated downstream ingress upgrade may already exist, but no upstream application message, provider admission, or downstream application event may have occurred. This is distinct from Rescue's upstream-first handshake contract and never uses a Rescue non-`101` as normal refresh authority. HTTP/WS `403`, including any `x-openai-authorization-error`; established WS error/event; SSE error after 2xx; 400/404/407/429/5xx; incomplete/oversized/malformed response; or any body/event code never qualifies in V1. The classifier emits the closed evidence below and does not parse provider error text. Future 403 refresh grammar needs protocol revision and installed corpus.

`PinnedWsErrorMessageV1` is the shared closed established-WebSocket decoder used only by `DirectCandidateAuthRejectionV1` and `ExactHardQuotaRejectionV1`. It evaluates one complete RFC 6455 text message produced by the pinned message codec, never an individual wire frame: negotiated extension processing completes, all continuation frames through `FIN` are reassembled, each data-frame payload is at most 16,777,216 bytes, cumulative uncompressed message payload is at most 67,108,864 bytes, and the result is valid UTF-8. Fragmentation and masking are hop-local. Interleaved ping/pong are processed normally but are not upstream application events. Close, connection loss, protocol/UTF-8/limit failure, or any other ambiguity before `FIN` is ineligible, and no classifier may act before `FIN`. Let `P` be the exact UTF-8 byte sequence of the resulting logical uncompressed message before JSON decoding; fragmentation and negotiated compression do not alter `P`.

The decoder accepts exactly one duplicate-aware JSON object followed only by JSON whitespace and requires top-level `type` exactly string `error`. Classifier eligibility requires exactly one of top-level `status` or `status_code`, encoded as a JSON unsigned integer in `0..=65535`; both aliases, any duplicate known member, or any case variant of authority members `type|status|status_code|error` rejects. Optional top-level `error` is null or one object; its known `code`, `message`, and `type` members are absent, null, or strings, duplicate known members reject, and a case variant of authority member `code|type` rejects. Optional `headers` is null or one object. Unknown non-authority members retain pinned ignore semantics. Before status classification, nested `error.code` exactly `websocket_connection_limit_reached` or `previous_response_not_found` has pinned retryable precedence and makes both CQ classifiers ineligible regardless of status or other members.

Separate `DirectCandidateAuthRejectionV1` uses the same complete, validated, provider-unadmitted, non-ambiguous HTTP/1.1-or-HTTP/2, normal-WS-handshake, or prewarm-handshake boundary, including the version-specific completion and ambiguity rules above, but accepts status exactly `401|403` only for a Codex-selected route. Status `401` additionally requires that route's terminal tag to be `codex_pinned_direct`; status `403` is route-neutral across every Codex credential-bearing catalogue row with such a boundary and never consults that tag. One first complete unrelayed `PinnedWsErrorMessageV1` may use the same classification only when its resolved status is exactly `401|403` and either (a) the volatile prewarm probe lineage has family `prewarm_websocket` and phase `prewarm_probe_send`, the reservation remains provider-unadmitted, and no other upstream application event occurred, or (b) adoption already created the real durable lineage with family `websocket` and phase `prewarm_first_send`, that real attempt remains provider-unadmitted, and no earlier real application event occurred. It authorises only advancement to the next already-frozen direct candidate slot for the same logical account within the owning reservation or V4 plan. It never creates a slot, skips direct order, invokes refresh, excludes or changes account, or treats classifier/safety/cyber/free-form message text as authority. Prewarm and adopted-real direct recovery are same-account only; their `401|403` never invokes refresh or changes account. Exhaustion relays the last safely retained provider rejection under the transport contract below. Thus complete `403` preserves bounded direct same-account recovery but is deliberately not managed-refresh authority.

Raw upstream capture, classifier projection, and route-specific downstream relay authority are three distinct objects. `RawUpstreamResponseHeadersV1={schema_version:1,headers:[{name_ascii_lower,values_base64url:[string...]}...]}` contains every field and every value of the selected transport's `http.Response.Header` after transport parsing but before any route writer, hop-by-hop sanitation, allowlist projection, `Header.Get`, status clamp, or Codex-to-Anthropic transformation. Names are valid lower-case ASCII, unique, and sorted; each value array may be empty and otherwise preserves exact per-name order, with every uninterpreted value encoded as canonical unpadded base64url. `RawUpstreamResponseTrailersV1={schema_version:1,trailers:[{name_ascii_lower,declared_before_body,values_base64url:[string...]}...]}` is populated only after an exact framing end, includes every declared or observed trailer name, permits an empty values array, preserves exact value order, and distinguishes a pre-body declaration from a trailer observed only at EOF. Each raw object is limited to 65,536 decoded name-plus-value bytes and 131,072 canonical bytes. For canonical bytes `N` and `T`, `raw_upstream_response_headers_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/raw-upstream-response-headers/v1\0") || uint32be(len(N)) || N))` and `raw_upstream_response_trailers_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/raw-upstream-response-trailers/v1\0") || uint32be(len(T)) || T))`. Neither object is downstream authority. `PinnedHTTPRejectionHeadersV1={schema_version:1,headers:[{name_ascii_lower,value_base64url}...]}` is derived deterministically only from the complete raw-header object and contains exactly the fields admitted by the **Common HTTP and WS non-101 allowlist** above after that contract's duplicate/case/value validation, sorted by lower-case ASCII name, with each exact uninterpreted classifier value encoded as canonical unpadded base64url; absent fields produce an empty list. Dynamic limit fields use their complete lower-case field names, and no unlisted field is present. For `H=CanonicalJSONV1(PinnedHTTPRejectionHeadersV1)`, `allowlisted_header_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease, ASCII("cq/pinned-http-rejection-headers/v1\0") || uint32be(len(H)) || H))`. The classifier projection is never relay authority and may not alter raw evidence or downstream representation. HTTP body/message digests below are lower-case hex SHA-256 over exact undecoded upstream body bytes or exact `PinnedWsErrorMessageV1` bytes `P` respectively. HTTP/1 completion is exactly `{kind:"http1_exact_framing_end",complete:true}`; HTTP/2 completion is exactly `{kind:"http2_end_stream",end_stream_observed:true,rst_stream_before_end:false,ambiguous_goaway_before_end:false}`.

Route-specific downstream HTTP representation starts with closed `DownstreamRelayResponseHeadersV1={schema_version:1,relay_profile:"native_codex_http_v1"|"claude_reverse_proxy_v1"|"codex_live_get_set_v1"|"codex_anthropic_write_error_v1"|"codex_live_sideband_local_502_v1",headers:[{name_ascii_lower,values_base64url:[string...]}...]}`. Names are unique and sorted and values preserve exact per-name order; the object contains the exact application-level header map handed to the downstream HTTP writer after the selected route's transformations and is limited to 131,072 canonical bytes. For canonical bytes `E`, `downstream_relay_response_headers_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/downstream-relay-response-headers/v1\0") || uint32be(len(E)) || E))`. The selected profile must equal the exact observation-variant entry in the immutable `FinalRouteChoiceCoreV1.downstream_rejection_profile_map`: native Codex HTTP preserves upstream status and adds every value from `http.Response.Header`; Claude reverse proxy preserves status and contains exactly the post-hop-by-hop `httputil.ReverseProxy` header map before `WriteHeader`; live-create preserves status and contains only non-empty `Content-Type` and `Location` results obtained by exact `Header.Get` then `Header.Set` semantics; and Codex-to-Anthropic error output has only singleton `content-type: application/json`. `codex_live_sideband_local_502_v1` is legal only for a Codex-selected `codex_live_sideband_path|codex_live_sideband_query` upstream-first `ws_handshake`: it closes the rejected upstream response and reproduces baseline `writeError(w,502,"api_error","codex live sideband upstream error")`, with downstream status exactly `502`, singleton `content-type: application/json`, the exact Go `encoding/json.Encoder.Encode` body `{"error":{"message":"codex live sideband upstream error","type":"api_error"},"type":"error"}\n`, SHA-256 `582149208b6ead37d08712dcb229d67fab039bf6ebf5f8bee0af5ffa227f4275` and length `93`, no trailer, and no upstream header or body in downstream output. Normal Responses WebSocket/prewarm post-upgrade failure has no downstream HTTP status, header object, body, or trailer and uses only its closed Text-plus-Close transformer.

The closed `RetainedDownstreamRelayV1` union uses the HTTP projection or one exact transformed output, where `ErrorStatusV1` is the exact upstream integer range `400..999`. Its route-profile branch is `{schema_version:1,kind:"route_profile_v1",relay_profile:"native_codex_http_v1"|"claude_reverse_proxy_v1"|"codex_live_get_set_v1"|"codex_live_sideband_local_502_v1",upstream_status:ErrorStatusV1,downstream_status:ErrorStatusV1,downstream_headers:DownstreamRelayResponseHeadersV1,downstream_headers_digest,downstream_trailer_disposition:"discarded_by_profile"|"no_trailers",body_sha256,body_length}`; every field is the exact selected baseline writer output and matches the authenticated final-route map. Claude reverse-proxy retention requires an empty raw-trailer object because a declared or observed trailer must instead use live-only baseline relay. The live-sideband profile requires downstream status `502`, its exact constant local body/header digests and length, and `no_trailers` irrespective of upstream status/headers/body. Its two transformed branches are `{schema_version:1,kind:"codex_anthropic_write_error_v1",transformer_input_core:CodexAnthropicWriteErrorInputCoreV1,transformer_input_digest,transformer_output_core:CodexAnthropicWriteErrorOutputCoreV1,transformer_output_digest}` and `{schema_version:1,kind:"codex_ws_postupgrade_handshake_error_v1",transformer_input_core:CodexWSPostUpgradeHandshakeErrorInputCoreV1,transformer_input_digest,transformer_output_core:CodexWSPostUpgradeHandshakeErrorOutputCoreV1,transformer_output_digest}`. The Anthropic branch is legal iff `selected_provider="codex"`, `variant="http_response"`, and `route_id` is exactly `anthropic_messages_model_dispatch|anthropic_count_tokens_model_dispatch|claude_fallback`. The post-upgrade branch is legal iff `selected_provider="codex"`, `variant="ws_handshake"`, `route_id="codex_responses_legacy"`, and the final-route map selects `codex_ws_postupgrade_handshake_error_v1`; it contains no downstream HTTP header/body/trailer projection. Every other provider/route/variant requires the exact route-profile branch selected by the final-route map. `BaselineCodexErrorReadResultCoreV1={schema_version:1,read_limit_bytes:1048576,returned_prefix_sha256,returned_prefix_length,read_outcome:"complete_before_limit"|"limit_exhausted"|"non_eof_error"}` is closed with disjoint precedence: any observed non-EOF read error selects `non_eof_error`, including when length is exactly `1048576`; otherwise length exactly `1048576` selects `limit_exhausted`; only observed EOF with length `<1048576` selects `complete_before_limit`. `CodexAnthropicWriteErrorInputCoreV1={schema_version:1,transformer_id:"codex_anthropic_write_error_v1",route_id,upstream_status:ErrorStatusV1,read_result:BaselineCodexErrorReadResultCoreV1,error_type:"api_error",message_prefix_utf8:"codex upstream: "}` binds exactly the bytes returned by `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body,1<<20))`; for `I=CanonicalJSONV1(input)`, `transformer_input_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/codex-anthropic-write-error-input/v1\0") || uint32be(len(I)) || I))`. Let `B` be that exact returned prefix in the still-live bounded buffer. Transformer V1 is byte-for-byte the baseline Go 1.22+ `writeError` operation for every `ErrorStatusV1`: ignore the read error, convert `B` to a Go string, concatenate the exact prefix, invoke one default `encoding/json.Encoder.Encode` over `map[string]any{"type":"error","error":map[string]string{"type":"api_error","message":message}}`, retain default HTML and invalid-UTF-8 escaping, and append exactly the encoder's one LF. `CodexAnthropicWriteErrorOutputCoreV1={schema_version:1,transformer_id:"codex_anthropic_write_error_v1",output_status:ErrorStatusV1,output_headers:DownstreamRelayResponseHeadersV1,output_headers_digest,output_content_type:"application/json",output_body_sha256,output_body_length,output_trailing_lf:true}` requires `output_status=input.upstream_status`, the exact `codex_anthropic_write_error_v1` singleton header projection, and its recomputed downstream-header digest; its body fields are the SHA-256/length of the complete encoded output. `output_body_length <= 6,291,531`, where the bound is six escaped bytes per at most 1,048,576 returned bytes plus the exact 75 fixed bytes. For `O=CanonicalJSONV1(output)`, `transformer_output_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/codex-anthropic-write-error-output/v1\0") || uint32be(len(O)) || O))`. For `D=CanonicalJSONV1(RetainedDownstreamRelayV1)`, `downstream_relay_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/retained-downstream-relay/v1\0") || uint32be(len(D)) || D))`; the complete union is at most 147,456 canonical bytes. A complete transformed response additionally proves its transformer input equals the exact source-read projection of its complete raw body; classifier completeness remains an independent transport/body fact and is never inferred from either transformer read result.

When complete classifier capture or an exact durable route representation is unavailable but the original response and downstream are still live, closed `LiveDownstreamRelayDispositionV1` is exactly one of `{schema_version:1,kind:"route_profile_live_v1",route_id,relay_profile:"native_codex_http_v1"|"claude_reverse_proxy_v1"|"codex_live_get_set_v1"|"codex_live_sideband_local_502_v1",upstream_status:ErrorStatusV1,downstream_status:ErrorStatusV1,attempt_digest,connection_identity_digest,response_sequence,upstream_response_identity_digest,buffered_prefix_sha256,buffered_prefix_length,relay_contract:"exact_route_writer_live_v1"}`, `{schema_version:1,kind:"codex_anthropic_write_error_live_v1",route_id,status:ErrorStatusV1,attempt_digest,connection_identity_digest,response_sequence,upstream_response_identity_digest,transformer_input_core:CodexAnthropicWriteErrorInputCoreV1,transformer_input_digest,transformer_output_core:CodexAnthropicWriteErrorOutputCoreV1,transformer_output_digest}`, or `{schema_version:1,kind:"codex_ws_postupgrade_handshake_error_live_v1",route_id:"codex_responses_legacy",status:ErrorStatusV1,attempt_digest,connection_identity_digest,response_sequence,upstream_response_identity_digest,transformer_input_core:CodexWSPostUpgradeHandshakeErrorInputCoreV1,transformer_input_digest,transformer_output_core:CodexWSPostUpgradeHandshakeErrorOutputCoreV1,transformer_output_digest}`. The Anthropic transformed branch is mandatory exactly for its three Codex-selected HTTP routes; the post-upgrade transformed branch is mandatory for the normal Responses WebSocket/prewarm handshake; the route-profile branch and its status mapping are mandatory for every other HTTP or upstream-first handshake and must equal the final-route map. For canonical bytes `L`, `live_downstream_relay_disposition_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/live-downstream-relay-disposition/v1\0") || uint32be(len(L)) || L))`. The identity fields bind the exact current worker, attempt, connection, and one response sequence; the object contains no durable header/body/trailer bytes and cannot be reopened after connection loss. Route-profile live relay invokes exactly the selected baseline writer once against the same response, including its native all-header copy, reverse-proxy sanitation and trailer suffix, live-create `Get`/`Set` projection, or live-sideband deterministic local-502 `writeError`; the live-sideband branch first closes the rejected upstream response and writes no upstream status/header/body byte. A streaming writer writes the already buffered prefix once then consumes only the unread tail. A previously observed read error writes only the bytes the pinned baseline writer would have written. Either transformed live relay writes only the one materialised output whose cores/digests were computed from the exact bounded source projection, including on limit exhaustion or non-EOF read error; post-upgrade output is its exact Text then Close pair and never a downstream HTTP response. No branch sends a classifier projection or permits another downstream connection. A crash/restart or ambiguous/partial write never rematerialises or replays any durable or live branch.

Live transformed status is an equality, not a second classification. For `codex_anthropic_write_error_live_v1`, outer `status == transformer_input_core.upstream_status == transformer_output_core.output_status` and equals the enclosing unavailable-core status. For `codex_ws_postupgrade_handshake_error_live_v1`, `response_present=true`, outer `status == transformer_input_core.upstream_status` and equals the enclosing unavailable-core status; `transformer_output_core.canonical_status` is exactly the pinned clamp derived from that same input status. Any outer/input/output/enclosing status substitution rejects before relay.

Durable terminal relay uses one bounded closed response object rather than a process-memory `*http.Response`. `RetainedProviderRejectionCoreV1` has common fields `{schema_version:1,route_id,terminal_401_semantics:"codex_pinned_direct"|"generic_terminal_only",selected_provider:"claude"|"codex",variant:"http_response"|"ws_handshake",attempt_digest,attempt_phase_authority_event_digest,slot_authority_digest,status:ErrorStatusV1,raw_upstream_headers:RawUpstreamResponseHeadersV1,raw_upstream_response_headers_digest,raw_upstream_trailers:RawUpstreamResponseTrailersV1,raw_upstream_response_trailers_digest,allowlisted_header_digest,body_base64url,raw_body_sha256,raw_body_length,downstream_relay:RetainedDownstreamRelayV1,downstream_relay_digest,automatic_decompression:false,provider_admitted:false,downstream_committed:false,prior_upstream_application_event_count:0}`. `http_response` adds exactly `{transport_version:"http/1.1"|"http/2",completion}` with the matching completion union above; `ws_handshake` adds exactly `{transport_version:"http/1.1",completion:{kind:"http1_exact_framing_end",complete:true}}`. `route_id`, selected provider, terminal tag, attempt, phase, slot, status, and transport byte-match the reopened final route choice, active owner, immutable attempt, and complete response boundary; the terminal tag is classification authority only when status is `401`. Each complete retained HTTP/handshake object or retained established-WebSocket message object is at most 1,851,392 canonical bytes; the former includes its at-most-147,456-byte downstream union plus independently complete raw header and trailer objects, while the latter includes at most 1,048,576 exact message bytes. Exactly one retained or unavailable object from the matching HTTP/handshake or WebSocket-message family is embedded in the owner-only `0600` active-owner journal; none is a sidecar, payload capture, status/health/info/doctor/log field, receipt export, or diagnostic body. The 16-MiB journal limit reserves one maximum retained object, one independent at-most-32,768-byte matching unavailable object, complete terminal after-image, and publication temporary before active-owner creation. A transformed route additionally pre-reserves at most 1,048,576 returned-prefix bytes and 6,291,531 transformed-output bytes before dispatch; no transformed body or prefix is persisted or included in the journal cap. A route-profile branch pre-reserves an at-most-1,048,577-byte tee buffer: a complete body through 1,048,576 bytes may become retained evidence; the first byte beyond that bound selects unavailable and remains part of the one live baseline stream followed by the unread tail. A non-EOF read error likewise selects unavailable but preserves the exact returned prefix for the one route-mandated live write. Established-WS parsing already owns the bounded `PinnedWsErrorMessageV1` buffer; it copies at most 1,048,576 bytes into durable capture, and a larger complete qualifying message uses only the small unavailable object plus current-buffer live disposition. Oversized raw headers or trailers never become downstream authority: a transformed route may still write its singleton output, while another route may use only its exact still-live route writer. Raw, transformed, and WS-message in-memory copies are zeroised after durable capture, successful live relay, or failure. Reference-aware GC removes the terminal owner only after response/message delivery or continuity-unavailable closure, owner acknowledgement/checkpoint, and every continuity/history reference clear, with directory sync; privacy retention never outlives those existing references merely to preserve a classifier sample. Restart, response/socket-identity loss, or any prior/ambiguous downstream byte makes a live disposition unusable and returns continuity unavailable without replay.

Complete terminal-retry disposition evidence, V4 terminal-`401` exhaustion proof, and final-provider exhaustion proof are embedded in that same authenticated owner after-image, never stored or scanned as sidecars. The sole capacity table above is controlling; this paragraph defines no shadow limit. Before owner creation and the first upstream application byte, its counting serialiser includes the exact frozen plan, maximum legal contraction and consumed-transition histories, complete caller/selector/contraction/failure objects, one maximum complete exhaustion proof, one maximum retained or unavailable response family, terminal after-image, and publication temporary at their literal nesting depths under the unchanged 16-MiB journal and 16-MiB temporary ceilings. A plan whose worst-case original-order transition, disposition, proof, response, after-image, or temporary cannot fit refuses `resource_capacity_exhausted` before permit issue. Exact and first-byte-over vectors are generated from that same table for every listed object, history, proof, and aggregate; no older local proof, selector, disposition, or later-group constant is accepted by implementation, verifier, or fixture.

Final downstream error representation is authenticated-route-profile exact and classifier-neutral. For every complete or live-only HTTP error with `ErrorStatusV1`, including exhausted direct `403`, exact hard-quota `429`, and non-classifier errors, Codex selection on `anthropic_messages_model_dispatch|anthropic_count_tokens_model_dispatch|claude_fallback` must use `codex_anthropic_write_error_v1` from the baseline bounded read result and emit that same upstream status; it may never relay raw Codex error bytes. Every other HTTP/handshake branch uses the exact native-Codex, Claude-reverse-proxy, live-create, WS-preupgrade, or live-sideband-local-502 profile selected by the immutable final-route map: native, Claude, and live-create preserve status; normal WS copies only its five pinned headers and clamps upstream `600|999` and every other status outside `400..599` to `502`; live-sideband closes the rejected upstream handshake and emits only its constant local `502` JSON/LF representation. An exhausted established-WebSocket classifier message instead uses only `codex_ws_text_message_v1` and writes the exact original logical text message once on its original still-live downstream WebSocket. The raw classifier object, if any, is unchanged by this choice. Exhaustion may relay only the last branch-correct retained representation or one still-live exact route/message writer; if neither is safe it returns continuity unavailable, never substitutes a different status/header/body/trailer/message profile or opens a new downstream/upstream connection.

Evidence may name a phase only through this exhaustive observation matrix; status and classifier-specific grammar still apply:

| Observation origin | Evidence variant | Required immutable `transport_family` | Required phase event | Eligible classifiers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| complete ordinary HTTP response | `http_response` | `http1|http2` matching completion | exact selected purpose among `http_dispatch|http_retry|retained_dispatch` | pinned auth, direct candidate auth, hard quota |
| complete normal WebSocket non-`101` handshake | `ws_handshake` | `websocket` | `ws_upgrade` | pinned auth, direct candidate auth, hard quota |
| complete prewarm WebSocket non-`101` handshake | `ws_handshake` | `prewarm_websocket` | `prewarm_dial` | direct candidate auth, hard quota; pinned auth is ineligible |
| first complete unrelayed normal-WebSocket application error message | `ws_text_message` | `websocket` | `ws_first_send` | hard quota only |
| first complete unrelayed prewarm error message after the exact probe frame and before adoption | `ws_text_message` | `prewarm_websocket` | `prewarm_probe_send` | direct candidate auth, hard quota |
| first complete unrelayed response to the adopted real frame | `ws_text_message` | `websocket` | `prewarm_first_send` | direct candidate auth, hard quota |

No other origin/variant/family/phase/classifier combination is evidence authority. In particular, `prewarm_adoption` authorises the adoption CAS but cannot itself produce a rejection observation.

Only one classifier-specific direct-auth transition may consume an evidence object. For status `401`, its constructor first requires the reopened final route choice to carry `terminal_401_semantics="codex_pinned_direct"`; generic-terminal-only Claude or other Codex routes cannot construct pinned or direct evidence from that `401`. Before any direct, retry, or same-request refresh advancement, every retained or capture-unavailable V4 `401` reopens the complete `CallerRequestAuthorityV1`. If `kind="provider_subject"`, the observation CAS byte-compares outbound account/candidate/revision with the ingress subject, fixes exactly `provider_subject_rejected` for equality or `provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh` otherwise, destroys every uncommitted request permit and dispatch authority, and makes all remaining direct, refresh, and account slots unusable for this request. Equality also destroys the exact live subject capability; inequality preserves that still-current subject only for a fresh ingress and never converts it. A qualifying pinned managed-owner refresh may then run solely to publish a future-ingress credential receipt before terminal selection; absent such authority, rejected/absent owner work, every `ws_text_message`, or unavailable capture selects the terminal authority immediately with a null future-only receipt. Neither provider-subject branch may append an attempt, even when a later direct slot exists or caller expiry is null. Only an independently current `local_owner` may continue after a complete classifier-eligible `401`: durable V4 atomically persists the complete direct evidence/digest and any qualifying pinned evidence/digest on the current attempt, records it `provider_failed`, advances exactly one unused next direct slot in the same group when present, and sets `retry_authority=direct_candidate_auth`; without a next direct slot it either enters its complete managed-refresh gate or selects `FinalV4Terminal401AuthorityV1` with the closed exhaustion proof below. Every active non-V4 owner treats every complete `401` as terminal for the current request before any refresh or body replay, irrespective of provider or ingress authority kind: one terminal CAS persists the exact `ActiveNonV4Terminal401EvidenceV1` branch with null `future_only_refresh_receipt_digest`, starts no credential-owner refresh or index publication, and sends zero later attempts. Only a separate fresh ingress with independently current caller authority may acquire owner-refresh authority under its own request. A catalogue-tagged eligible Codex route uses the classifier branch; every Claude-selected or other route uses `generic_terminal`, constructs no classifier pair, and can never retry or refresh this `401`.

Terminal exhaustion never trusts a disposition enum or orphan digest. Closed `ConsumedRetryTransitionV1={schema_version:1,kind:"active_non_v4"|"journal_v4",active_non_v4_retry_transition_core:ActiveNonV4RetryTransitionCoreV1|null,active_non_v4_retry_transition_digest:null|string,v4_retry_transition_core:V4RetryTransitionCoreV1|null,v4_retry_transition_digest:null|string}` has exactly the tag-matching complete core/digest pair non-null; the digest recomputes under that core's native domain, and the other pair is null. The selected core's owner, authenticated predecessor, ordinal, attempt generation, classifier tag/evidence, skipped range, cursors, and next state must byte-match the consuming owner step. For canonical bytes `U`, `consumed_retry_transition_digest=hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_lease,ASCII("cq/consumed-retry-transition/v1\0") || uint32be(len(U)) || U))`. Closed `ConsumedAttemptTransitionSelectorV1={schema_version:1,owner_kind:"journal_v4_request"|"active_non_v4_request",owner_authority_digest,owner_predecessor_digest,disposition_slot_authority_digest,transition_attempt_slot_authority_digest,attempt_generation,attempt_revision,attempt_digest,attempt_phase_authority_event_digest,caller_dispatch_permit_consumption_digest:null|string,classifier_transition_kind:"direct_candidate_auth"|"exact_hard_quota",classifier_evidence_digest,skipped_slot_range:SkippedSlotRangeV1|null,skipped_slot_range_digest:null|string,retry_transition:ConsumedRetryTransitionV1,retry_transition_digest}` names one complete attempt/phase/consumption and its complete classifier transition in the exact authenticated predecessor. `owner_kind="active_non_v4_request"` requires `retry_transition.kind="active_non_v4"`; `journal_v4_request` requires `journal_v4`; no null or digest-only transition branch exists. Independently, a complete qualifying status `403` from any Codex-selected credential-bearing catalogue route with an eligible observation boundary may drive one direct-candidate transition; `terminal_401_semantics` is ignored. Exactly one owner CAS may select that authority. Active non-V4 increments its record generation, embeds the complete object/digest, selects it as `terminal_rejection_digest`, and moves to `exhausted_direct_403|exhausted_hard_quota_429|capture_unavailable` with no next lineage or permit. V4 increments its journal generation, embeds the complete object/digest in the current attempt's terminal after-image, records `provider_failed`, destroys all unused request permits, and appends no next attempt. The journal MAC or active-state MAC covers the complete authority and predecessor; the pre-existing dispatch `AttemptPhaseAuthorityEventV1` remains immutable and is referenced by the authority rather than rewritten. On this classification only, one classifier-specific V4 CAS persists the complete evidence and digest on the current attempt, records it `provider_failed`, marks the complete current account group hard-limited for this request, skips every unused direct and refresh slot in that group, records any later contracted groups and their exclusion digest, advances the monotonic group cursor, and re-intersects authority. Active non-V4 performs the same bounded split only through one CAS over its immutable frozen plan and current MACed state: a surviving group appends `ActiveNonV4RetryTransitionCoreV1`, advances monotonically, increments attempt generation/revision, and makes only a fresh state-bound permit eligible; exhaustion selects the final-provider authority and terminal state without creating a transition successor or refresh slot. If exact bounded capture is unavailable at resolved status `429`, neither owner constructs hard-quota evidence: it selects `capture_unavailable_429` with only the variant-matching authenticated unavailable object and at most its same-process exact profile/message relay, and creates zero retry authority. A generic slot-only `RejectAndPrepare` mutation is not cross-account authority. No durable transition revisits or adds a group or applies to continuation, prior-response/encrypted-state affinity, provider-admitted, or indeterminate work. Prewarm performs the equivalent single volatile reservation transition only after closing the exact failed socket lineage; with complete evidence and a surviving later group it persists that evidence, failed-group mark, contraction exclusions, and cursor, then may append one next `PrewarmDialAttemptCoreV1` whose predecessor is the prior sequence head and whose transition evidence is that exact digest. Exhausted or capture-unavailable prewarm work remains volatile and either relays its current route-specific response/message once or reports continuity unavailable; it creates no V4 record and never refreshes. HTTP, compact, retained, normal WS, and prewarm share this classifier and ordered transition; no transport-specific auth/quota shortcut may rotate accounts.

Codex V4 `eligible_managed_refresh` is conditional same-account credential-owner authority, not continuing provider-caller authority; Claude never enters this mechanism. For independently current local-owner ingress, same-request refresh activates only after every frozen direct slot for that account was consumed in exact order through `DirectCandidateAuthRejectionV1`, the refresh slot is the next unused original slot, and the exact retained direct attempt for the refresh slot's same outbound account/candidate carries one complete valid `PinnedAuthRejectionEvidenceV1` plus its recomputed digest, is definitely provider-unadmitted/non-indeterminate, committed no downstream response, and remains bound to this plan. Provider-subject ingress never enters that advancement order: its first complete retained `401` fixes the exact or different-outbound terminal disposition and closes all request permits before any later direct slot. Only when that same rejection independently satisfies the pinned managed-owner predicate for a frozen refresh slot of the rejected outbound account/candidate/revision may the already-terminal request enter `refresh_begin` solely to publish an owner receipt for future ingress; later direct slots are neither consumed nor candidates, and no grant or refreshed attempt is prepared. The qualifying local-owner `401` need not be temporally adjacent when later direct candidates were tried; its attempt, slot, candidate, revision, complete pinned/direct evidence, and refresh slot remain explicit inputs. Capacity, 429, every 403, safety/classifier/cyber outcome, generic 4xx/5xx, route/policy/caller/selector loss, ambiguous transport, provider admission, post-admission error, evidence from a different outbound account/candidate, every generic terminal `401`, every `ws_text_message`, unavailable capture, or prewarm never supplies refresh authority. Under complete gate order, `refresh_begin` CAS recomputes and persists both complete evidence objects/digests plus transition ID; creates `LocalOwnerRefreshGrantV1` only for independently current local-owner ingress; or, for provider-subject ingress, reopens the already fixed terminal reason/disposition, creates no grant, and proves every request permit was destroyed before owner work. It also records request/attempt/slot generations; qualifying direct-attempt and refresh-slot digests; account/candidate/old-revision digests; routing/credential generations; owner ID/key/generation; receipt cursor and prior digest. Both provider-subject reasons are immutable before owner work and force `FinalV4Terminal401AuthorityV1` after committed, rejected, or absent-terminal owner resolution. Evidence already attached by the observation CAS must match byte-for-byte and is referenced, not reclassified; a bare status, enum, or digest is insufficient. Gates including owner-lifetime release before `RefreshWithReceipt(transition_id,ref,expected_revision,pinned_owner,expected_cursor)`.

Owner durably registers transition before work. Lookup is exactly `in_progress|committed|rejected|absent_terminal`. If absent, CQ may atomically `SealRefreshTransitionAbsent`; later refresh then fails. Credential replacement and committed receipt are one recoverable owner transaction: no revision visible without receipt and no receipt names invisible revision. Closed receipt fields are `(schema,owner identity/key/generation,sequence,previous digest,transition,account,candidate,old revision,new revision?,outcome,reason?,commit generation?,resolved_at,mac)`. Committed requires new revision/positive commit and no reason; rejected requires closed reason and no new revision/commit. Identical input returns byte-identical receipt; substitution/gap/replay/unknown refuses.

After reacquiring gates, exact revision mode forbids transition. Managed-refresh mode requires committed receipt old revision equals slot expectation; account/candidate/transition/direct-attempt/refresh-slot match; new revision equals the candidate exposed by current inventory. A committed refresh selected by `provider_subject_rejected|provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh` must use `TerminateCommittedManagedRefreshWithoutDispatchV1` with that exact stored reason: it publishes/revalidates the new index, destroys every remaining provider-subject authority for this request, appends zero attempt, fixes `historical_attempts>0,further_attempts=0`, and relays the retained `401`. `provider_subject_rejected` additionally destroys the rejected live subject capability; the different-outbound reason does not convert or extend the still-current ingress subject. Neither finite nor null caller expiry and neither HTTP nor WebSocket can choose another branch. Only independently local-owner ingress may instead use `CommitManagedRefreshAndDispatchV1`. That single V4 CAS validates and consumes the exact receipt without mutating owner store, validates current inventory, the immutable `LocalOwnerRefreshGrantV1`, the same still-current local-owner capability, the byte-identical provider-branch authority in the request/grant, and every routing/credential/connection gate, then selects only the `local_owner_refresh_grant` branch of `CallerDispatchAuthorityV1`. Any provider subject, ordinary permit, missing/expired/substituted grant, or local-owner drift makes zero dispatches. The successful CAS records `caller_dispatch_authority_digest`, appends the refreshed attempt directly in `DispatchAdmitted`, binds `retry_authority=managed_refresh`, and records receipt/journal digests for owner-store acknowledgement. There is no separately durable consumed grant or prepared refreshed attempt.

A valid committed receipt that cannot satisfy the successful CAS must not remain an indefinitely consumable transition. `TerminateCommittedManagedRefreshWithoutDispatchV1` is the only alternative V4 CAS. It first validates the exact committed receipt/MAC/owner/sequence/previous-digest, transition and complete retained evidence authority, and the same immutable account/candidate/old/new-revision facts as the successful CAS. It is authorised only by one closed terminal reason: `provider_subject_rejected|provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh|caller_scope_lost|caller_expired|fingerprint_key_rotated|policy_contracted|delegation_revoked|mode_changed|connection_lost|inventory_revision_mismatch|local_owner_grant_invalid|request_cancelled|request_terminal|dispatch_authority_deadline`. `provider_subject_rejected` is mandatory exactly when the complete retained `401` names the ingress provider subject. `provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh` is mandatory exactly when ingress authority is a provider subject but the refreshable rejected outbound account/candidate/revision is different; it is illegal for local-owner ingress. Both are established before owner work, survive index publication, are never transient, and prohibit every same-request refreshed attempt. Here `inventory_revision_mismatch` means current inventory moved away after a valid receipt, and `local_owner_grant_invalid` means the byte-identical stored grant lost a final lifecycle gate. Before the request deadline, transient index, owner-store, lock, or permit unavailability remains pending and is not terminal authority. In one CAS the transition becomes `committed_no_dispatch`, the refresh slot becomes unusable for this request, any local-owner grant or ordinary dispatch authority is destroyed, complete pinned/direct rejection evidence and digests plus receipt digest and terminal reason are retained, zero attempt is appended, and `historical_attempts>0,further_attempts=0` is fixed. It relays the retained provider rejection when still safe, otherwise emits continuity-unavailable. Receipt substitution, gap, replay, invalid MAC, owner mismatch, receipt-declared revision disagreement with the owner transaction, or grant substitution/MAC failure is refusal/poison evidence, not terminal-CAS authority.

Rejected/absent-terminal appends no attempt, consumes no refresh attempt, destroys any local-owner grant, terminates transition, and relays retained provider rejection with zero further attempts; if no longer safely relayable emit continuity-unavailable with only `historical_attempts>0,further_attempts=0`. In-progress stays pending; mismatch fails. After either `CommitManagedRefreshAndDispatchV1` or `TerminateCommittedManagedRefreshWithoutDispatchV1` journal consumption, CQ idempotently calls `AcknowledgeRefreshReceiptConsumed(transition_id,receipt_digest,journal_generation,journal_digest)`. Crash recovery revalidates the journal and repeats exactly the uncommitted CAS or acknowledgement; it can neither strand a committed receipt nor create an attempt after the terminal CAS. Owner GC requires acknowledgement plus next checkpoint; unacknowledged receipt/tombstone remains at least 30 days and store cap blocks new refresh. Refresh never widens slots, caller scope, or caller credential revision.

Provider-subject resolution is one total terminal protocol. With no qualifying future-only owner transition, the observation CAS directly selects `FinalV4Terminal401AuthorityV1` with the fixed caller disposition/reason and null receipt. A committed owner result selects that same authority through `TerminateCommittedManagedRefreshWithoutDispatchV1`, with `future_only_refresh_receipt_digest` equal to the exact committed receipt; rejected or absent-terminal owner resolution selects it with null receipt. The selected terminal object's predecessor must be the exact observation/refresh transition after-image and its complete retained response, or the transport-matching unavailable family when no classifier-complete capture exists. Every branch proves all request permits were destroyed before owner work, appends zero attempts, and retains the exact-match capability-destruction fact independently of receipt outcome. Crash before terminal selection resumes only the already fixed future-only owner transition; crash after selection reopens only the complete terminal authority and optional receipt and never restarts owner work, advances a slot, or dispatches.

For a local-owner managed refresh, the phrase “appends the refreshed attempt directly in `DispatchAdmitted`” above is legal only when `LocalOwnerRefreshDispatchPurposeV1.purpose="http_retry"`. Its HTTP CAS creates the fresh `http1|http2` lineage, consumes grant and receipt, and records the purpose-matching phase event plus `DispatchAdmitted` atomically. For `purpose="ws_upgrade"`, `CommitManagedRefreshAndDispatchV1` is instead the sole refresh-upgrade CAS: it consumes the same immutable grant/receipt and route-purpose object, allocates a fresh connection identity/generation and immutable durable `transport_family="websocket"` lineage for the refreshed slot, records the `local_owner_refresh_grant` dispatch-authority digest in exactly one `ws_upgrade` phase event, and commits `upgrade_dispatched` immediately before the first upstream upgrade byte. It does not record `DispatchAdmitted`, send a WebSocket application frame, or reuse the rejected socket. This is the sole exception to the ordinary-permit requirement for `AttemptPhaseAuthorityEventV1.ws_upgrade`; it requires the purpose-bound refresh branch, while every other upgrade remains ordinary-permit-only.

A complete valid `101` advances that same refreshed lineage to `connected_unsent`. Its first application byte requires a newly minted one-use ordinary `ws_first_send` permit, a distinct phase CAS/event, and all current caller/resolver/branch/route/slot/revision/socket gates; only that CAS records `DispatchAdmitted`. A complete non-`101` rejection becomes provider-failed without reusing the consumed refresh authority; timeout, EOF, cancellation, malformed/incomplete response, process loss, or any other upgrade ambiguity becomes non-migratable orphan/indeterminate. Crash before refresh-upgrade CAS consumes nothing and may retry only the same CAS; crash after it reopens exactly one upgrade-dispatched attempt and never reconsumes the grant/receipt or redials; crash after `101` but before first send recovers connected-unsent with no application byte; crash after first-send CAS recovers exactly one admitted write authority. Owner acknowledgement binds the refresh-upgrade journal CAS and cannot authorise first send. No provider subject, Claude request, second grant use, another socket, or alternate phase enters this sequence.

Neither the adoption proof nor another mapping authorises reuse of the adopted socket. Crash before the adoption CAS leaves only the volatile reservation with both adoption authorities unconsumed and no admission-owner residue; reservation recovery closes it and permits no adoption replay. Crash after the CAS reopens and validates the complete authority/consumptions, embedded volatile dial and contraction histories and heads/counts, both nonces, proof, the independently constructed durable lineage, and exactly one durable connected-unsent attempt without consulting vanished volatile reservation state; it recomputes each native-domain lineage/digest separately and then verifies only the closed bridge fields. Missing, substituted, duplicate, digest-only, head/count-gapped, oversized, cross-domain-copied, or equality-substituted dial history, contraction, lineage, phase event, permit consumption, or adoption consumption refuses and never creates or replays an attempt. Only V4 record may enter connected-unsent, dispatch-admitted, or provider-admitted.
