The CAS destroys those volatile raw values whether it commits or refuses.
- Any caller, delegation, selector, generation, binding, pool, member, route, evidence, candidate, revision, expiry, or connection mismatch closes socket; identified turn may plan normally but inherits no reservation authority/evidence.
- Prewarm never grants grandfathered authority.

The warmup receive ordering is classification-before-observer-before-relay. For exactly the first complete logical text message after `prewarm_probe_send`, CQ first runs `PinnedWsErrorMessageV1` and the closed direct-auth/hard-quota classifiers while the message remains unrelayed. If and only if one classifier produces complete evidence and the same reservation CAS can commit the corresponding next-slot/group transition, that CAS consumes the evidence once, closes the failed socket lineage, and marks that one message consumed/suppressed; it is not passed to the readiness observer or downstream relay and its evidence requires `message_relayed:false`. The two classifiers are mutually exclusive by status. If classification is ineligible, transition authority is absent, or no next authorised transition exists, CQ persists no `message_relayed:false` transition evidence for that message and proceeds through the pinned readiness observer followed by byte-identical ordered relay. Every later complete message, and every first message not consumed by such a committed transition, follows observer then relay unchanged. Thus “every complete logical warmup text message is relayed” above means every non-consumed message; no message may both authorise a retry transition and be relayed or observed, and ordinary mapped observer errors that are not classifier-consumed retain their existing relay-then-close contract.

### WebSocket

- Downstream 101 is ingress only. Every `response.create`, reused socket, and prewarm adoption supplies strong frame-local authority and runs complete planner.
- Upstream dial/reuse for identified turn enters durable connected-unsent; prewarm remains volatile. Valid admitting upgrade may set provider-admitted only after V4 record exists and pins exact account, but grants no send authority.
- Every first byte, admitted or not, obtains exactly one `CallerDispatchAuthorityV1` branch and reacquires complete gates, revalidating mode/routing/caller/delegation/binding/pool/capability/account/candidate/revision/connection/journal/slot.
- If authority changed before send: unadmitted work closes and may replan through unused original intersection; admitted work closes without send, becomes indeterminate/orphaned, preserves exact admission, and never replans. Mode loss is `mode_changed`; caller loss is scope violation; other loss uses exact continuity error.
- With unchanged authority, permit-protected journal CAS enters dispatch-admitted; gates release before byte. Ambiguous write becomes indeterminate. Publication after CAS does not cancel current attempt.
- Prewarm evidence remains provisional; adoption creates V4 record before admitting evidence/first send. Definite rejection retries only through frozen intersection.

## Routing errors

External errors reveal no account key, email, raw session ID, digest, pool membership, token, upstream body, or policy document.

Stable codes:

| HTTP | Code | Meaning |
|---:|---|---|
| 400 | `session_metadata_required` | Bound-policy coverage cannot be proved |
| 400 | `session_metadata_invalid` | Canonical metadata is malformed or contradictory |
| 403 | `normal_caller_auth_scope_violation` | Valid caller credential does not authorise selected account/delegation scope |
| 503 | `mode_changed` | Normal authority changed before request dispatch admission |
| 503 | `session_pool_missing` | Binding references unavailable pool |
| 503 | `session_pool_empty` | Pool resolves to zero authorised routable accounts |
| 503 | `session_pool_exhausted` | Eligible accounts lack required capacity |
| 503 | `session_pool_model_incompatible` | No eligible account supports requested model |
| 503 | `session_pool_policy_inhibited` | Required HTTP/WS enforce mode is unavailable |
| 503 | `session_pool_continuity_conflict` | Existing exact turn account is outside current pool |
| 503 | `session_pool_continuity_unavailable` | Exact turn account remains member but current authority, route, model, candidate, or credential cannot dispatch |
| 503 | `routing_policy_unavailable` | Required policy generation cannot be loaded or validated |
| 503 | `routing_policy_incompatible` | Runtime lacks required policy feature or semantics revision |
| 503 | `capability_evidence_conflict` | Bound derived pool has conflicting current evidence |

Before HTTP dispatch/WS upgrade, errors use table status plus one safe JSON object. After downstream WebSocket upgrade, broker sends at most one text event `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"cq_routing_error","code":"<stable-code>","message":"request not dispatched"}}`, then closes 1013 with code reason; if unsafe, closes directly. `mode_changed` records unadmitted attempt abandoned-before-dispatch; admitted connected-unsent becomes indeterminate/orphaned. Work already committed drains. No error reveals identity. Caller authentication/scope precedes continuity, which precedes pool/capability/capacity/default. Pre-dispatch failure records zero request-dispatch attempts; connection dial remains separate metric.

After one dispatch-admitted attempt receives definite provider rejection, policy contraction may remove every unused frozen slot. CQ then relays retained provider rejection/status/body under existing safe provider-response contract, records diagnostic `retry_policy_contracted`, and performs zero further attempts; it does not replace known provider outcome with local routing error. If downstream protocol has already consumed that rejection internally and cannot safely relay it, CQ emits `session_pool_continuity_unavailable` annotated only with `historical_attempts>0,further_attempts=0`. Metrics and journal always distinguish total historical attempt count from further attempts.

Exact continuity conflict/unavailable precedes pool-wide capability, empty, model, capacity, and default errors. For new turn, `capability_evidence_conflict` wins over empty only when conflict is sole reason no otherwise route-qualified account remains. If safe member exists, routing proceeds and conflict is diagnostic.

## Capability evidence

### Evidence model

Each record contains:

- evidence schema version and exact opaque account/workspace key;
- registered capability name;
- exact product surface, access path, authentication mode, requested model, and observed effective model;
- state `eligible`, `ineligible`, or `unknown`;
- registered source identifier;
- `observed_at`;
- optional `expires_at`;
- policy generation and record digest through enclosing signed document.

Absence or expiry means `unknown`. Manual evidence may be non-expiring and remains user-owned until cleared. Automated or probe-derived evidence must expire.

Account tier is display metadata only. Model-list visibility is catalogue metadata, never eligibility. Refusal, classifier fallback, `cyber_policy`, quota, safety, generic failure, model-list absence, or `openai_verification_recommendation=trusted_access_for_cyber` never writes entitlement evidence. Successful direct operation may establish only exact `model.invoke` for observed effective model/surface/path/auth at that time; it never establishes cyber governance.

Capability evidence is routing metadata, not authorisation for actor, workflow, target, tool, or activity. It never establishes consent, ownership, legal authority, defensive purpose, internal approval, or Trusted Access compliance; CQ does not inspect prompts/targets/downstream users to decide these. Every `cyber.*` capability is manual-only in V1. Binding cyber-scoped pool requires one of `--approval-scope-ref` or privacy-preferred `--approval-scope-ref-stdin` plus `--confirm-authorised-use`; non-cyber pool rejects pair. Reference bytes `R` are non-empty valid UTF-8 ≤4096 with no controls. `approval_scope_ref_digest = hex(HMAC-SHA256(K_session, ASCII("cq/cyber-approval-scope/v1\0") || uint32be(len(R)) || R))`. CQ stores only that digest, acknowledgement, and `approved_pool_definition_digest` computed by the exact `PoolDefinitionV1` function above over the complete canonical capability definition, including every predicate and scope field. Cyber-scoped bindings require all three fields non-null/true; non-cyber bindings require both approval digests null and acknowledgement false. Evidence records and derived membership are outside the definition digest and may change under ordinary expiry/fusion rules. Any pool replacement that changes this digest while a desired or effective binding references the cyber-scoped pool—including cyber-to-different-cyber capability, model, surface, path, authentication, mixed-predicate, or wildcard changes—rejects until every affected session is explicitly unbound and rebound with fresh reference and confirmation. Runtime digest mismatch inhibits before planning. This supports correlation, not approval validation. Operator must ensure approved internal user/workflow/target and no customer/downstream/third-party extension.

### Discovery policy

Current official material describes trusted cyber access and general model listing, but no supported public per-ChatGPT-account entitlement endpoint is established by this blueprint:

- <https://openai.com/index/trusted-access-for-cyber/>
- <https://openai.com/index/expanding-daybreak-as-the-cyber-defense-window-narrows/>
- <https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001258-openai-daybreak-trusted-access-for-cyber-overview>
- <https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001259-trusted-access-for-cyber-common-issues-and-troubleshooting>
- <https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/models>

Therefore:

- Manual evidence and explicit pools are first supported authority.
- CQ does not automate `chatgpt.com/cyber` using stored browser cookies or scrape private page state.
- The visible `chatgpt.com/cyber` state is therefore not V1 machine authority. A future supported authenticated endpoint or documented export can become expiring source adapter only after contract review.
- Future supported official entitlement endpoints implement a new evidence adapter with source and expiry, without changing pool semantics.
- V1 probe supports only `model.invoke` through one normal HTTP Responses attempt to one resolved account/workspace. Command admission requires active `capability_evidence_v1`, whose dependency closure includes active `normal_codex_v1`; an inactive or inhibited normal-Codex dependency returns `feature_inactive` before inventory, credential resolution, request construction, network, probe receipt, or evidence mutation. Every other/cyber capability returns stable `probe_unsupported` with zero network/credential/browser/evidence writes. Adapter derives product surface/access path from fixed final route and auth mode from resolved candidate; CLI cannot label them. Unsupported candidate/scope fails pre-network. Receipt binds account/candidate/revision HMACs, canonical derived scope, requested/observed model, method/path/query/transport, request semantics/body/header digests, terminal outcome, and zero fallback.
- `codex-model-invoke-probe-v1` uses a checked-in Codex 0.147.0 structural-builder fixture. Supported models are exactly versioned fixture-set keys. Each entry contains complete serialised pinned `ModelInfo`, source digest, and expected decoded `ResponsesApiRequest`; missing model, fallback model metadata, or fixture/digest mismatch returns `probe_unsupported` before credential or network work.
- Common builder inputs are exact: default OpenAI/ChatGPT Responses provider; non-Azure; namespace tools enabled; empty base instructions; exactly one user `message` containing one `input_text` equal to `Return exactly PONG.`; no other input; no tools; `parallel_tool_calls=false`; no output schema; `output_schema_strict=true`; effort absent; reasoning summary `none`; service tier and model verbosity absent; concurrent reasoning-summary delivery disabled; prompt-cache override absent; `store=false`, `stream=true`, `tool_choice="auto"`, and `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. Model fixture supplies every request-affecting model field, including slug, default reasoning effort, reasoning-summary support, Responses Lite use, verbosity support/default, and service-tier set.
- Each operation creates distinct lower-case UUIDv4 placeholders `I`, `S`, `T`, and `W` for installation, session, thread, and window. `CodexResponsesMetadata::new(I,S,T,W)` has every optional identity, request-kind, parent, subagent, source, sandbox, workspace, code-mode, timestamp, and extra field absent/empty. Builder emits `prompt_cache_key=S`; `client_metadata` contains exactly pinned four entries from `I,S,T,W`. Session source is CLI; originator is exact `codex_cli_rs`; beta features, turn state, attestation, inference trace, memgen, parent, and subagent are absent; Responses Lite header follows model fixture. Candidate authentication/account/FedRAMP/residency/organisation/project remain resolved-candidate substitutions governed by normal request contract.
- Golden compares parsed JSON recursively: object order ignored; array order, member presence/absence, strings, numbers, booleans, and null exact. It separately compares lower-case request-header multiset by cardinality/exact value after declared runtime substitutions, plus method/path/query, HTTP version, content encoding, and Content-Length semantics. JSON object order, header wire order, and framing bytes are not Codex-owned identity. Receipt binds model-fixture digest, runtime-substitution HMACs, canonical structural-body digest, exact transmitted-body byte digest after optional zstd, safe canonical header/framing digest, and exact transmitted byte count. Byte digest covers immutable bytes supplied to sole transport attempt, not reconstructed body. Credential/tenancy values use existing keyed fingerprints; no bearer, account ID, organisation, project, prompt, or body persists.
- Probe SSE framing is fixed as `codex-responses-probe-sse-framing-v1`, a fail-closed port of the framing consumed by Codex 0.147.0 through pinned `eventsource-stream 0.2.3`. Decode UTF-8 incrementally across arbitrary transport chunks. A leading U+FEFF BOM is unsupported and makes outcome unknown rather than reproducing the pinned crate's unsafe byte-index path. Lines end with CRLF, bare CR, or bare LF. Empty line terminates a record. A leading colon is a comment. Every other non-empty line splits at its first colon; an absent colon means empty value, and at most one immediately following U+0020 is removed. Field names are case-sensitive. Exact lower-case `data` appends its value and one LF to the record data buffer; comments and `event`, `id`, `retry`, and unknown fields do not affect the oracle and never reconnect. At record termination, no-`data` records are discarded; otherwise remove one final appended LF and dispatch the result even when it is empty. EOF never dispatches an unterminated record. `[DONE]` has no sentinel meaning and therefore fails JSON decoding. Invalid UTF-8, framing failure, transport failure, or EOF before a successful terminal event makes outcome unknown/no write.
- Probe framing has independent hard caps: at most 16,777,216 response-body octets may enter the SSE decoder; one line excluding its terminator is at most 1,048,576 octets; one dispatched data buffer after LF joining is at most 1,048,576 UTF-8 octets; and at most 4,096 records containing at least one `data` field may dispatch before terminal completion. Each `response.output_text.delta` string and the cumulative concatenation are at most four UTF-8 octets. The concatenation is checked incrementally as a byte prefix of exact ASCII `PONG`; a non-prefix or cap breach terminates unknown/no write and cancels the sole attempt. Counts include empty, malformed, and ignored dispatched records and are enforced before allocation growth. These caps are independent of the 30-second capability-probe deadline.
- Probe response decoding is fixed as `codex-responses-probe-decoder-v1`, derived from Codex 0.147.0 `ResponsesStreamEvent`, `ResponseItem`, and `ResponseCompleted`. Each dispatched data buffer must decode as exactly one JSON object and then as pinned `ResponsesStreamEvent` with exactly one string `type`; malformed JSON, trailing data, duplicate oracle/model-relevant members before object materialisation, or a present pinned field of the wrong type makes outcome unknown. Unknown extra members retain pinned Serde tolerance. Model extraction below occurs before the event-kind transition. Event handling is closed:

| Exact event `type` | Probe transition |
|---|---|
| `response.created`, `response.in_progress`, `response.metadata`, `response.content_part.added`, `response.content_part.done`, `response.output_text.done` | Ignore after model extraction; never authoritative. |
| `response.output_item.added` | `item` must decode as pinned `ResponseItem`. Assistant `Message` and `Reasoning` are provisional only; every other item or role is unknown. |
| `response.output_text.delta` | Require string `delta`; append in wire order under the four-octet/prefix rule. Deltas have no item association in the pinned decoder. |
| `response.output_item.done` | Require `item` decoding as pinned `ResponseItem`. `Reasoning` is permitted and ignored. An assistant `Message` is authoritative. Every other item or role is unknown. |
| `response.reasoning_summary_part.added` | Require integer `summary_index`; ignore. |
| `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` | Require string `delta` and integer `summary_index`; ignore. |
| `response.reasoning_summary_text.done` | Require string `item_id`, string `text`, and integer `summary_index`; ignore. |
| `response.reasoning_text.delta` | Require string `delta` and integer `content_index`; ignore. |
| `response.failed`, `response.incomplete`, `response.custom_tool_call_input.delta`, `response.custom_tool_call_input.done`, `response.function_call_arguments.delta`, `response.function_call_arguments.done`, `response.refusal.delta`, `response.refusal.done` | Terminal unknown regardless of otherwise valid payload. |
| `response.completed` | Require `response` to decode as pinned `ResponseCompleted`, including string `id`, valid optional `usage`, and `end_turn` absent, null, or Boolean. Explicit `false` is terminal unknown. Absent, null, or `true` evaluates the complete oracle, then terminates without reading another record. |
| Every other string | Terminal unknown; a semantics revision and fixture are required to admit another kind. |

- Zero or more authoritative `ResponseItem::Reasoning` items may precede, interleave with, or follow message streaming and never contribute to the output oracle. At the first `response.completed`, success requires 2xx, exactly one authoritative `ResponseItem::Message` with `role:"assistant"`, exactly one `ContentItem::OutputText{text:"PONG"}`, and no other content item. Zero text deltas are allowed; when any occurred, their complete concatenation must equal authoritative text byte-for-byte. Absent or null `end_turn` follows pinned `None` fallback semantics and, like `true`, requires no follow-up; explicit `false` is unknown/no write. Any second authoritative message, agent message, refusal, tool/call, compaction, non-reasoning output item, or premature completion is unknown/no write.
- Model signals come only from initial HTTP `OpenAI-Model`, case-insensitive `OpenAI-Model` or `X-OpenAI-Model` in event `response.headers`, or either name in event top-level `headers`; `response.model` is ignored. Raw response-header cardinality is retained before normalisation: zero or one case-insensitive initial `OpenAI-Model` field-value is allowed, while identical, differing, or case-variant duplicate fields make outcome unknown. A sole initial value must pass pinned Rust `HeaderValue::to_str()`. For each event, inspect `response.headers` first. Exactly one declared case-insensitive model key there emits its value and suppresses top-level model inspection; no declared key falls through to top-level `headers`; an unextractable or duplicate declared key is unknown and never falls through. Apply the same zero/one rule to top-level `headers`, detecting repeated raw JSON members before map materialisation. JSON extraction accepts a string directly or an array whose first element recursively resolves to a string; later array elements are ignored. Empty arrays and first elements that are null, Boolean, number, object, or ultimately non-string produce no signal. Every emitted value across the HTTP head and decoded events must be identical, non-empty 1–512-byte UTF-8 without controls. Missing, differing, malformed, partial, or wrong output is unknown/no write. Eligible evidence expires exactly 24h.
- `--confirm-quota-use` names exact account/capability/requested model before execution. Output reports adapter-derived surface/path/auth/route/effective model. Only normalised evidence and safe receipt persist; never response body, cookie, token, prompt, or screenshot.
- Injected clock decides future/expiry boundaries. Exact expiry, future observations, invalid intervals, scope mismatch, duplicate source tuple, conflicting sources, and every all-of truth-table branch have deterministic validation/evaluation results.

## Privacy and logging

- Owner-authenticated status/detailed health expose aggregate pool, binding, evidence, conflict, and draining counts only. Public TCP health exposes no routing or instance facts.
- `info` may expose operator-relevant inspector/service/listener executable, selected manager plist, and standard-log paths after safe path acquisition; it fingerprints private state-root, config, credential, payload, and external-input paths. It may expose pool names/digest hints, never raw sessions or member identities.
- Explicit `pool show`, `session show`, and `capability show` may display operator-requested account references and opaque keys; output remains token-free.
- Routing diagnostics use safe codes plus HMAC digest hints. They never include raw session/thread/turn IDs.
- Control key, CQ local token, OAuth tokens, account IDs, browser data, prompts, tool inputs, and upstream error bodies never enter status or standard logs.
- Snapshot process arguments use a field allowlist (`proxy`, allowlisted subcommand tokens, manager label, port, and state-root digest). Unknown option names and values never appear; snapshot emits only `{unknown_argument_count,unknown_argument_fingerprint}` where fingerprint is domain-separated HMAC over length-prefixed raw unknown argv. Paths and log-derived text are length-bounded, control-character escaped, and rendered without terminal escape interpretation.
- Standard and payload logging are non-blocking side channels. One standard JSONL record, including LF, is at most 16,384 bytes; producer replaces larger serialisation with fixed safe overflow record. Service and routing each own 256-record/4-MiB bounded queue; full queue drops newest and increments safe counter. Payload owns eight-event/16-MiB queue and one 2-MiB active encoder buffer; it never retains another full request/response copy. Logging failure, slow disk, rotation, or retention never blocks/cancels/retries data plane. At most one identifier-free warning per source/generation enters service log; if service log itself fails, only counter/health fact changes.
- Every producer sanitises before enqueue; startup stderr follows same identifier ban. All directory/file/pointer opens are relative to retained instance log-directory descriptor with `O_NOFOLLOW`, current UID, `0700` directory, `0600` regular file, link count one, stable device/inode, local-filesystem, and no mount crossing. Service and routing each retain current+rotated+temporary+orphan generations within five files/50 MiB; combined standard cap is ten files/100 MiB. Exact generation/header/rotation chain is defined by `logs` inspection contract above. Service logs are selected from resolved effective manager/runtime metadata and must prove instance ownership; desired path alone is insufficient. Historical shared `~/Library/Logs/cq/proxy.log` is `legacy_sensitive`, never shown by ordinary `logs`, and reported—not deleted—by `doctor`.
- Legacy configured routing and payload diagnostics are no-copy by default. Their receipts contain only safe identity, size, and keyed fingerprint. A raw copy exists only under exact `LegacySensitiveDiagnosticsCapabilityV1`, kind-specific acknowledgement, verified pre-write backup exclusion, one-object/64-MiB per-kind and four-object/256-MiB store caps, and at-most-24-hour live-tree logical retention. Legacy routing hints are treated as sensitive correlators even when hashed. The store is never shown or followed through ordinary `logs`; V1 exposes metadata only. Independent `SensitiveRetentionControllerV1`, recovery, service start, and every import boundary purge and directory-sync expired finals, temporaries, and orphans before content or readiness without claiming secure erasure.
- Payload diagnostic capture is separate, disabled by default, and uses config-selection consent contract above; display separately requires `--confirm-sensitive`. Capture reads at most 262,144 source bytes/event and streaming-encodes at most 2 MiB including truncation marker; no second body or unbounded escaping/expansion exists. Payload directory retains current+rotated+temporary+orphan within five files/50 MiB. Each generation header records trusted wall time, boot-session ID, and `mach_continuous_time_v1` creation tick. Before first capture and every generation publication, the exact object is registered with `SensitiveRetentionControllerV1`; capture remains disabled unless its independent job, index, directory capability, backup exclusion, and exact-expiry schedule are attested. The controller runs independent of capture/service state. Capture enable, service/foreground start, recovery, rotation, and new event are already mutating boundaries and synchronously purge before content/readiness. Same-boot age uses continuous ticks; after reboot it uses valid wall time; invalid, future, regressed, or ambiguous metadata expires conservatively. Cleanup unlinks the recorded generation and syncs its directory before any new capture or mutating boundary completes.

After each successful purge and whenever the selected live-set or next expiry changes, the controller publishes owner-MACed `SensitivePurgeAttestationV1={schema_version:1,index_generation,directory_identity_digest,live_set_digest,boot_session_id,checked_tick_ns,checked_at,next_expiry_wall:null|string,next_expiry_tick_ns:null|integer,mac}` through its existing atomic/index-sync protocol. It is valid for a read snapshot only when directory identity, index generation, and recomputed live-set digest agree; its same-boot continuous tick or valid non-regressed cross-boot wall time proves the check is not from the future and current time is strictly before both applicable next-expiry values (or the selected live set is empty and both are null); and no invalid, future, regressed, ambiguous, expired, temporary, or orphan entry is present. Payload `logs` and `logs --follow` perform only retained-descriptor reads of that attestation/index/live set. They never wake the controller, request purge, unlink, sync, replace an index, or otherwise mutate state. Missing/stale/conflicting attestation or an object expiring during follow closes before the next payload record with `sensitive_retention_unavailable`; the operator may wait for the independent controller or use the separately explicit mutating recovery/start boundary. No sensitive byte is emitted before a valid initial attestation.

Twenty-four-hour limit is live-tree logical retention, not secure erasure: APFS snapshots/clones, backups, deleted blocks, and external copies may retain bytes. UI labels `sensitive logical retention`; stronger deletion is outside V1. ENOSPC/quota/encoding/rotation/retention failure disables capture for the generation, increments a safe counter, emits no sensitive byte, and never backpressures an already admitted data plane. Marker stores counts/reason/keyed digest only.
- Rescue logs include route family, status class, byte counts, latency, and safe error code only.

## Health and observability

Public TCP `GET /health` is unauthenticated and intentionally privacy-contracted to a constant shape: HTTP 200 body is exactly `{"schema_version":1,"status":"ok"}` when supervisor control plane can answer; HTTP 503 body is exactly `{"schema_version":1,"status":"degraded"}` during bounded internal overload. Both representations set exact `Content-Type: application/json` and decimal `Content-Length` equal to the selected canonical GET body. `HEAD /health` follows the GET matcher alias with identical status and application-owned headers but writes zero response-body bytes. No worker, discovery, credential, routing, registry, configuration, or private-state read is permitted on either method. No other JSON field is permitted. ## Security analysis

### Threat: local credential exfiltration

Normal and rescue authenticate before body/inventory/planner access. Normal maps caller bearer to one exact provider-tagged account/revision subject and, absent explicit Codex delegation, can use only that account; any multi-domain raw-bearer match fails before classification. Every route binds the route-matching classified/not-applicable provider-branch union, and each classified branch additionally binds the exact matching tagged provider subject/delegation or explicit current local-owner capability before credential resolution. Provider rejection of that exact provider subject terminates its request: CQ may persist an owner-managed refreshed credential/index, but relays the retained rejection and requires fresh ingress bearing the current revision. A delegated provider-bearer request whose rejected refreshable outbound differs from its ingress subject may likewise persist owner state only for future ingress and must consume its receipt through `provider_bearer_no_same_request_refresh` with zero replay. Every Claude-selected request retains a complete `401` with zero same-request replay; only independently current local-owner authority on Codex V4 may dispatch the refreshed revision in the same request. Rescue never opens credential storage; it forwards one caller opaque bearer to fixed TLS origin only after explicit risk acknowledgement and rejects constant-work deny fingerprints for every current/transition/rollback CQ local token. Fixed Host/Origin, exact routes/headers, socket activation, no redirects/environment proxy, and budgets prevent generic relay use. Another local UID may submit its own bearer but cannot use CQ-owned credentials or bootstrap their refresh authority. Socket activation closes worker/supervisor replacement capture windows; cold login and every explicit socket-definition release fail closed until every stateful or stateless sensitive request sender—including no-`Authorization` senders and the built-in stateless CQ adapter—proves `ClientBearerBarrierV1` enforcement and complete authoritative request-sender/authorisation-sender/domain/transport enumeration with zero application-byte foreign-bind evidence.

### Threat: automatic safety-policy bypass

Rescue requires explicit operator mutation. No runtime failure, classifier response, quota signal, or provider status can enter rescue automatically. Rescue exposes suspended routing policy.

### Threat: duplicate request dispatch

Normal retries use frozen slots and definite provider rejection only. Rescue uses fresh one-shot HTTP/1 transport with one request-header write latch and no application/transport retry. Mode/policy changes never replay dispatch-admitted unknown or provider-admitted work.

### Threat: pool escape

Policy checks full authority before dispatch-plan freeze, retry candidates, WebSocket reuse, and prewarm adoption. Empty, stale, incompatible, or exhausted pools fail locally with zero attempts except approved in-pool terminal-default attempt from existing routing semantics.

### Threat: continuity corruption

Durable route snapshots resolve against full global authority before pool compatibility is checked. Excluded exact bindings become policy conflicts, not missing-account recovery or migration.

### Threat: session identifier disclosure

Authoritative binding lookup uses a dedicated full keyed HMAC. Raw IDs never appear in output. Full digests appear only in explicit operator `session list|show` so exact `--digest` mutation is possible; health/status/info/doctor/logs expose counts or short hints. Short hints cannot mutate state.

### Threat: stale capability evidence

Derived pools require fresh positive evidence. Expired or absent evidence becomes unknown and excludes account. Manual non-expiring assertions remain explicit operator authority, never inferred truth.

### Threat: service confusion or hostile listener

Lifecycle mutation reconciles launchd socket definition, kernel listener, UID, supervisor/worker, plist, manager, launcher/artifacts, instance root, and authenticated identity. Ambiguity is conflict. Managed primary never releases public socket during rescue, worker restart, supervisor kickstart, or rollback. Explicit uninstall/listener migration requires quiescence, `ClientStopProofV1`, a fresh universal `ClientBearerBarrierReceiptV1`, and complete authoritative stateful/stateless request-sender/authorisation-sender/domain/transport enumeration and whole-request zero-byte evidence including `cq_config_read_per_call_v1`; operator confirmation alone never releases the socket.

### Threat: corrupt or partially written state

Immutable generation objects, single atomic signed anchor, sync ordering, bounded descriptor reads, owner/mode/link checks, and composite publication prevent partial/cross-store state. After initialisation, missing or invalid authority blocks data plane instead of broadening. High-water detects stale object while current key/anchor survive; whole-root rollback by root or same UID is outside guarantee and never described as prevented.

### Residual trust and resource assumptions

Same effective UID, root, kernel, launchd, filesystem integrity, system clock, DNS, and TLS roots are trusted. Same-UID code can read owner-only secrets, control jobs, or replace binaries; design does not isolate it. Another local UID may still exhaust TCP listen backlog/CPU despite application quotas, but cannot consume reserved Unix-control capacity. Socket activation preserves bind authority/new connection queue, not active application connections. Upstream necessarily receives one bearer/account/body/allowed metadata. Supervisor enforces exact V1 connection, header, body, spool, WS, concurrency, and progress budgets; limit rejection invokes no privileged worker path.

## Compatibility and migration

- Only provably fresh never-initialised instance means implicit normal/routing generation zero. Any key, anchor, object, manifest, feature-floor receipt, or residue makes missing authority invalid. Read-only inspection creates nothing.
- Existing `codex_routing_account_keys` remains global authority and is not migrated into named pools.
- Existing routing default remains valid globally and is used for bound sessions only when member of effective pool.
- Existing continuity journal remains authoritative through explicit v4 migration rules; routing envelope is embedded in same journal CAS, never sidecar.
- Existing config JSON unknown-field preservation remains intact.
- Existing flat CLI commands remain compatibility aliases.
- Existing `proxy start --migrate-legacy-managed` keeps its current credential-endpoint migration meaning; it is unrelated to instance/listener `authority migrate` and cannot waive that command's client-stop or ownership gates.
- Existing public `/health` intentionally contracts to minimal liveness for privacy; frozen bare `status` remains compatible because it accepts any decodable JSON object. Detailed legacy fields move additively into owner-authenticated Unix-control health. This is documented security hardening, not wire-schema preservation for third-party `/health` consumers.
- Previously parseable non-official `claude_upstream` or `codex_upstream` values intentionally become pre-intent `custom_upstream_unsupported`; official managed credentials are never silently retargeted. Compatibility restoration is to select the official origin/base, while future custom-origin support requires its separately provisioned compile-time adapter and credential domain.
- Rescue mode defaults off and cannot activate during upgrade.
- Legacy process-managed Homebrew service remains inspectable. Rescue/session-policy activation first performs journalled migration to CQ socket-activated LaunchAgent with stable launcher; migration preserves binary package provenance but changes lifecycle authority.
- Compatibility-mode socket supervisor import does not advance primary floor and remains capable of exact pre-floor legacy restoration. Only ticket-bound final release activation, explicit closed-enum `feature activate`, or fresh initialisation writes primary floor. Candidate resolves target before any compatibility operation, reads primary only for compatibility check, and advances candidate-local file only. Newly started pre-feature binary refuses structured floor instead of ignoring intent/binding; already-running scalar writers are killed/reaped by import barrier and deliberate same-UID relaunch remains trust-boundary residual.
- Retained rollback artifact manifest must support every activated `required_feature`, not coarse CU number. Artifact bytes, path, manager binding, architecture, build, schema/features, retention and verification are signed. Active/floor/transition dependencies prevent GC. Downgrade below floor refuses while authority active.
- N-1 migration tests cover desired rescue, active binding, continuation-pending turn, missing/corrupt state, and unknown schema. Allowed outcomes are preserved enforcement or startup refusal; silent normal/unpooled routing is forbidden.

## Construction units

R32 OAuth callback-query ownership is additive and exact. CU-1 owns the 1,695-byte raw-query parser, one-decode UTF-8/key/value grammar, duplicate/unknown rejection, semantic canonicalisation, and transient `OAuthAcceptedCallbackQueryV1` construction. CU-2 owns the nested encrypted-secret schema, 596-byte canonical-query and exact 1,477-byte secret bounds, purpose-separated callback-query commitment, and proof that the unchanged 4,096-byte plaintext envelope and structured-refresh unit/frame/byte ledgers remain sufficient. CU-3 carries the complete nested object only inside the existing one-use OAuth carrier, independently reparses and recomputes it in the worker before `exchange_consumed`, enforces nested/outer code-state equality, and zeroises every raw/canonical/duplicate buffer. CU-9 independently regenerates accepted order/escape variants, every rejection boundary, carrier/AAD/transcript substitutions, crash points, exact/`+1` caps, and durable plaintext-absence scans on target and accepted floor. No unit may persist the object, bind raw query spelling, accept a digest-only query projection, invent another control frame, or dispatch exchange before worker recomputation.

R24-R26 credential/reachability ownership is exact. CU-2 owns `CredentialOwnerCommitStoreV1`, its root-key custody, initialisation/bootstrap/composite-authority/`ProxyInstanceContext`/runtime/release fingerprint propagation, `worker.credential_owner_store`, purpose-key HKDF, commit/anchor/receipt MAC and digest formulas, path grammars, 55-file/4-MiB and per-object caps, publication/CAS/closed operator-or-normal parent-completion union, cross-store receipt binding, receipt-generation allocation, GC and key-loss recovery, `NativeKeychainUpsertServiceRowV1`, all four `CredentialSelectorProvenance*V1` object kinds and embedded bundle, `CredentialAccountSelectorCommitmentV1`, their canonical/MAC/digest/64-KiB/store/sync/reopen/retention rules, the nine-way `LegacyAtomicWriterReachabilityCatalogueV1.writer_kind`, transition grammars and file/move/promote/link/socket/mode/lock/native operation-policy pairs including distinct `exclusive_lock_create_or_open|exclusive_lock_create_new` shapes, `LegacyWriterCallChainV1`, row and catalogue digest framing, mutation-row binding, quiescence revalidation, and every named signed-writer/release-receipt binding. CU-3 constructs, publishes, CAS-selects, recovers, selects operator and normal parent completions, receipt-binds, and collects credential-owner chains; constructs and revalidates the platform environment observation, CQ same-descriptor manifest observation, complete ordered-row projection, first-matching-row/no-match proof, typed authenticated origin including `selected_account_inventory`, UUID/email/output/planned-row commitment; and implements each quota-cache invalidation, installed-validation, continuity/canary-stop, readiness, credential-endpoint, file/native deletion, and namespace-adapter edge with its signed warning/abort policy. It destroys every transient environment/account/UUID/email/service/value at the terminal boundary. CU-9 independently regenerates target and accepted-floor atomic-file, file-delete, file-move-no-replace, file-link-no-replace, socket-create, file-mode-change, create-or-open lock-acquire, create-new lock-acquire, native-upsert, and native-delete call graphs, fully qualified entrypoint symbols, typed binding edges, byte offsets, provenance bundles, selector commitments, namespace/nullability/operation pairs and failure policies; exercises every credential-owner store key-create/fingerprint propagation, publish/CAS/parent-completion/receipt-allocation/recovery/GC/key-loss/cap boundary; and requires byte-identical row/catalogue/bundle digests through all named release receipts. CU-2 and CU-3 cannot self-attest CU-9's regeneration, and no unit may infer an effect, planned UUID, email, output, selector origin, transition edge, deletion edge, or failure policy from a path name, keyring item, post-effect manifest, or unsigned call graph.

### Baseline and store gates

- R31-R34 coordinator crash gates stop before and after initial selector-temporary create, every partial `preparing` prefix, complete-byte write, file sync, no-replace install, operations-directory sync, and same-descriptor final reopen. ## Acceptance criteria

Blueprint is delivered only when all following statements are true:

1. `status`, `info`, and `doctor` distinguish desired config, service manager, listener owner, process, runtime, and data-plane evidence without mutation.
2. Homebrew and CQ launchd ownership are both visible; contradictory jobs/listeners produce conflict.
3. Socket-activated supervisor retains public listener and rescue starts from minimal signed authority even when normal config/worker subsystems fail.
4. Rescue forwards only fixed pinned Codex routes using caller-supplied compatible bearer authentication; it never opens credential storage, selects, injects, refreshes, retries, or writes an account.
5. Common normal/rescue auth runs before privileged work; public listener remains launchd-owned across worker/supervisor replacement; deterministic ingress/dispatch drain semantics are tested.
6. Primary/candidate state, coordinator, control, routing, continuity, logs, and caches are isolated and exact lifecycle ownership is proved before mutation.
7. Explicit pools persist opaque account keys and can only narrow global authority.
8. Session bindings persist domain-separated keyed digests and govern all canonical HTTP/compact/retained/WebSocket traffic only after exact runtime acknowledgement. Legacy-import real-client proof obtains its exact session only through bounded EOF-framed stdin before ticket publication, persists no raw session bytes, commits and acknowledges the ticket-keyed binding before child launch, and dispatches only when the pinned installed-client emission recomputes to that same HMAC.
9. Coverage gates, composite signed authority, journal v4, frozen retries, credential refresh receipts, WebSocket reuse, and prewarm cannot escape pool or migrate provider-admitted/indeterminate work. Every active non-V4/V4/prewarm owner and every RCV held/grant/consumption envelope persists and reopens one byte-identical complete `FinalRouteChoiceCoreV1` plus its recomputed digest without current-catalogue reconstruction. Every active non-V4/V4/prewarm owner and every owner-bound permit, contraction proof, retry, and restart carries its complete byte-identical nested `CallerPreBodyAuthenticationV1`, nested `CallerIngressCapabilityV1`, caller authority, the exact branch-selected `caller_delegation_authority:CallerDelegationAuthorityV1|null` plus paired `caller_delegation_authority_digest:null|string`, and desired/effective resolver core; provider-subject requires the complete non-null pair while local-owner and inhibited authority require both literal null, and no loader reconstructs caller or delegation authority from a digest or current policy/index. Every ordinary authority embeds the complete permit with exact canonical finite-endpoint rows ordered by parsed UTC instant, then kind and source-digest tie-breaks, and expiry copied from the chronologically earliest endpoint or five seconds after issue, whichever is earlier; its phase CAS persists one complete authenticated one-use consumption and event with `issued_at <= consumed_at < valid_until`, and recovery rejects digest-only or duplicate consumption. Every classified open also carries one durable historically valid admission-consumption owner receipt through active non-V4 or V4 authority and base/final plan. Active non-V4 work has exact single-purpose authority and never replays after restart. Every observed `401` reaches exactly one catalogue-derived retained or pre-reserved `capture_unavailable` terminal branch, including the closed ordinary V4 terminal authority when no direct or refresh successor is authorised: only eligible Codex Responses/compact/normal-WS routes may carry pinned/direct `401` evidence, every Claude-selected or other Codex route is generic terminal-only for `401`, raw upstream headers/body and their classifier projection remain distinct from route-specific downstream relay authority, and restart, unavailable capture, or ambiguous relay yields continuity unavailable with zero replay. The exact three Codex-selected Anthropic-compatible HTTP branches retain unchanged raw upstream classifier evidence but relay only the digest-bound baseline `writeError` representation; every other HTTP/upstream-first-handshake branch relays only its exact authenticated route-profile representation, a normal Responses WebSocket/prewarm final handshake failure relays only its authenticated post-upgrade JSON Text then 1011/status-text Close transformer, while an established-WebSocket terminal relays only its exact original logical message on the original live downstream socket. A future-only refresh-receipt digest is optional only on retained terminalisation and exactly null on `capture_unavailable`; it never authorises this request. The terminal-401 tag never gates a complete route/provider-bound Codex status-`403` direct-candidate or exact status-`429` hard-quota transition. Native prewarm carries `not_applicable` and creates no provider admission row; its acyclic plan consumes exact dial/probe permits, while adoption consumes one dual-bound reservation/real authority plus a complete reservation-permit consumption, persists and reopens every complete dial-history entry/digest and referenced lineage/dial/probe event/permit consumption plus both dial and contraction histories/heads/counts, persists exactly one current-connected mapping plus null-socket future mappings, and atomically creates exactly one durable connected-unsent `websocket` V4 attempt on the proven socket before a distinct first-real-send permit. Before reservation, each next dial/probe permit, adoption, and recovery, the same complete frozen bytes must satisfy the canonical per-object bounds and checked `a,s_c,c,s_p,p,s_j,j,t,a_fit` equation; each 8-MiB history value is only an independent upper bound, the full journal and byte-identical publication temporary each remain at most 16 MiB, and no persisted capacity-reserve proof exists. Any adopted retry requires a fresh per-attempt socket lineage. Every provider-bearer Codex refresh—whether the rejection names the exact ingress subject or a delegated different-outbound account/candidate/revision—terminalises with the matching immutable reason and zero same-request refreshed dispatch; every Claude-selected request terminalises its `401` with zero same-request replay; and an independently current local-owner Codex V4 request may dispatch a refreshed revision only through its own final authority gate.
   The optional future-only receipt rule above applies only to V4. Active non-V4 terminal `401` authority always stores a null receipt, authorises no owner refresh/index/acknowledgement, and sends zero later attempts; only a separate fresh independently current request may acquire later refresh authority. For V4 specifically, every provider-subject `401` selects exact-subject or different-outbound terminal disposition before any direct, refresh, or account advancement; all request permits are consumed or destroyed, zero attempt is appended, and an optional committed owner receipt is future-ingress authority only. Only independently current local-owner authority may use a post-`401` successor. Every terminal-`401`, direct-`403`, and hard-quota-`429` exhaustion row embeds one tag-matching complete consumed selector, complete contraction object/digest with its complete component authority/digest, or managed-refresh-gate-failure projection; every nested component and enclosing disposition/proof digest is recomputed from complete bytes under its fixed bound, and migration/recovery never accepts a disposition enum, digest-only component, or digest list as authority.
   Native prewarm accepts only the pinned full startup builder and metadata/window fixture; relays complete logical text messages unchanged; applies wrapped-error mapping before top-level event decoding; ignores observer-only top-level decode failures and `process_responses_event Ok(None)` results; becomes ready only after a completed response with a bound non-empty response ID; closes on a pinned mapped/processing, EOF, close, transport, or protocol error before completion; and adopts only the exact independently reconstructed follow-up bearing that `previous_response_id` and incremental input.
   For this criterion, “unavailable capture yields continuity unavailable” applies exactly when its live disposition is null, no longer identity-valid, restarted, or downstream-ambiguous. An identity-valid unavailable branch may perform only its one baseline live relay: bounded-prefix `writeError` on the exact three Codex-selected Anthropic-compatible HTTP routes for every `400..999` status, or raw status/header/body streaming everywhere else. It remains ineligible for classification, retry, refresh, restart, or replay. Real-client dispatch additionally requires one immutable RCV preparation and one matching journal-V4 transaction; only the V4 CAS admits dispatch, and RCV anchor lag is idempotent projection work. Pre-journal preparation always abandons with zero dispatch, while post-journal recovery never abandons or replays.
   Prewarm adoption preserves the final successful volatile dial lineage/digest and the independently constructed durable real lineage/digest as distinct complete authority. Only account, candidate, credential revision, socket identity, and connection generation bridge the domains; authority/transport tags, plan/group/slot digests, request/reservation generations, attempt generation/volatile ordinal, and attempt digest remain native and are neither copied nor equality-constrained. Recovery reopens both literal sides, charges both through the complete capacity equation, and dispatches nothing when either side or the bridge is incomplete.
10. Rescue cannot silently bypass desired, pending, or effective binding; operator must acknowledge explicit policy suspension in same composite generation.
11. Manual capability evidence can form exactly scoped derived pools; unknown, stale, conflicting, or differently scoped eligibility is excluded.
12. No supported entitlement endpoint is assumed without evidence; probes are explicit, scoped, source-owned, and time-bounded.
13. Health and JSON expose desired/effective modes, generations, route coverage, and suspension without sensitive identifiers.
14. Feature activation establishes compatibility and digest-pinned artifact floors so newly started older binaries refuse unsupported state; legacy import admits a live source only with disabled same-FD Headroom config plus exact-process serving-proof `headroom=false`, admits a stopped source only with disabled config plus complete source absence, revalidates the selected variant before action, kills/reaps known pre-schema writers, and runtime detects later floor replacement.
15. Candidate isolation is kernel-confined with signed run receipt, primary installed marker/policy acknowledgement proves all transports, and every construction unit has non-empty deterministic verification. Promotion and every public-listener release or migration additionally require a fresh signed `ClientBearerBarrierReceiptV1` covering every authoritatively enumerated stateful/stateless sensitive request sender, authorisation-sender/domain-or-null membership, and registered transport—including `cq_config_read_per_call_v1`—plus `ClientStopProofV1`; unsupported/unregistered senders/domains/transports, an omitted stateless sender, or missing hook support fail before action and no acknowledgement waives the gate. Every closed release member has a foreign-bind proof in which every sender writes zero application bytes across every registered transport, including unchanged-local-token paths.
16. Promotion accepts only signed release bundles under one pinned build authority: accepted CU-8 floor equals lineage root, target has signed strict-descendant ancestry, exact signed CU-0…CU-8 and CU-0…CU-9 report sets plus build/vet/race reports are bound and ≤64 KiB each, the complete source/toolchain/environment/role equality graph reopens, and floor boots only with the signed compatible launcher ABI.
17. Separate artifact payload and manifest stores pass exact nine-slot and 2,416,508,928-byte aggregate boundaries after deterministic orphan reconciliation; slot ten, byte +1, ambiguous residue, missing bundle member, or physical-reserve failure rejects before copy/selection/action.
18. Candidate and primary four-stage target→floor→failed-target/rollback-floor→target chains have closed scope-specific entry kinds, pairwise-distinct chained runtime IDs, exact `target,target/rollback,target` switch outcomes, content-addressed `RuntimeBootAckV1` and `BundleStageProofV1` bytes, distinct entry/effective generation bindings, and exact proof windows. Import release is not complete until persisted coordinator/CAS/evidence `G0` equality, immediate-successor release/terminal generations, exact three-object policy projection, legal still-live boot reuse or durable `restart` lineage, fresh post-release marker/policy acknowledgement, history checkpoint, manifest-directed ticket cleanup, and pinned completion receipt survive every crash boundary.
19. Candidate launcher, supervisor, worker, and installed-client processes receive no reusable provider bearer or provider-origin network authority. Every live-provider validation exchange traverses the trusted controller-owned broker under one exact signed capability; its durable consumption receipt precedes every provider byte, consumed or ambiguous authority never replays, exact journal/resource limits are enforced, and preflight, floor, confinement, export/import, or promotion rejects any missing, partial, foreign, breached, or unsealed broker evidence. Malicious-candidate gates prove that direct official-origin egress and off-plan requests to an otherwise allowed origin fail while legitimate HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket protocol bytes remain exact.

20. Every OAuth callback accepts only the closed bounded two-key grammar, carries one complete canonical semantic query object solely inside the existing authenticated encrypted carrier, and reaches exchange only after independent worker parsing and purpose-bound recomputation. Release rejects duplicate/unknown/order-or-escape substitution, nested/outer mismatch, digest-only authority, any raw/canonical query persistence, any cap overflow, or crash recovery that reconstructs or replays callback plaintext.

## Rejected alternatives

### Mode flag inside normal configuration

Rejected because malformed normal config or failed normal subsystem startup could prevent rescue from listening—the failure rescue must survive.

### Standalone same-port bypass process

Rejected because current listener owns port exclusively. Takeover requires stopping current owner and necessarily drops active connections.

### Automatic fail-open

Rejected because it could bypass user-selected account policy, use unintended identity, leak local authentication, or duplicate an ambiguously dispatched request.

### Process-owned front door with close-and-bind replacement

Rejected because another local UID could capture caller bearer during restart bind window. Managed primary instead uses launchd socket activation and stable supervisor/worker split.

### Pools embedded in `proxy.json`

Rejected because frequent session mutations would rewrite token-bearing static configuration, current reload semantics do not apply that state, and desired/effective generation would remain ambiguous.

### Tier-derived or refusal-derived capability

Rejected because tier and observed failures do not establish exact feature entitlement.

## Adversarial review record

Blueprint cannot advance to construction planning until one complete recursive review round reports no open issues across architecture, CLI/operations, routing/continuity, security/privacy, protocol fidelity, verification/release, and coverage/source consistency. Any finding restarts every lens against new artifact digest.

Not-clean history stays embedded because later edits invalidate reviewed digests. Historical rows below are non-normative defect/disposition snapshots; current normative clauses above decide the design whenever old wording differs. Terminal clean review is sibling `2026-08-13-proxy-resilience-and-routing-blueprint.review.json`, written only after seven separately dispatched lens reviews finish against same frozen bytes under trusted coordinator. Blueprint is never edited to record clean result; any later byte change invalidates attestation and restarts every lens.

Sibling file bytes are RFC 8785 JCS of closed object plus one LF:

```text
{
  schema_version: 1,
  kind: "cq_proxy_blueprint_recursive_review",
  blueprint_path: exact repository-relative path,
  blueprint_sha256: 64 lower-case hex,
  authority_baseline_commit: 40 lower-case hex,
  round: positive JCS-safe integer,
  records: seven records in fixed lens order declared below,
  aggregate_sha256: 64 lower-case hex
}
```

`BlueprintReviewFindingV1={schema_version:1,id,severity:"critical|high|medium|low",location,evidence,correction}` is the sole closed finding item. `id` is 1–64 ASCII bytes matching `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}`; `location` is a nonempty actionable source locator of at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes; `evidence` and `correction` are each nonempty and at most 8,192 UTF-8 bytes. Finding arrays contain at most 64 items, reject duplicate IDs, and sort by `(severity_rank,id_bytes)` with ranks `critical=0,high=1,medium=2,low=3` and raw ASCII byte order for the ID tie-break. Unknown members, enum values, empty required strings, invalid UTF-8, control NUL, over-bound values, wrong order, or duplicate IDs reject.

Each reviewer returns exactly closed `CQProxyBlueprintReviewResultV1={schema_version:1,kind:"cq_proxy_blueprint_review_result_v1",lens:"architecture|cli_operations|routing_continuity|security_privacy|protocol_fidelity|verification_release|coverage_source_consistency",blueprint_sha256,authority_baseline_commit,verdict:"clean|not_clean",findings:[BlueprintReviewFindingV1]}`. Blueprint digest is exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters, baseline commit exactly 40 lower-case hexadecimal characters, and complete JCS bytes are at most 2,097,152 bytes. `clean` is legal iff `findings=[]`; `not_clean` is legal iff findings contains 1–64 items. Review coordinator is procedural trust root: it dispatches seven separate lens tasks after freeze and withholds other results until each returns. `reviewer_task_id` is an opaque orchestration label observed and copied by the coordinator, but its encoded value is exactly 1–256 US-ASCII bytes matching `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{1,256}`; no JSON-escaping expansion, whitespace, control byte, non-ASCII byte, empty value, or 257th byte is legal. The seven labels are unique by exact byte equality. Uniqueness proves only distinct labels; it does not cryptographically prove server issuance, reviewer identity, context isolation, independence, or non-fabrication. Result/record/aggregate hashes prove byte linkage and structural consistency only. A valid `not_clean` result prevents sibling publication and restarts all seven lenses against the next frozen digest; only the seven clean results enter the terminal sibling. Sibling record has exactly `{lens,reviewer_task_id,reviewed_at,verdict,findings,review_result_sha256,record_sha256}`. Lens is each result's exact enum value, once in the fixed order above. `reviewed_at` is exactly 20 ASCII bytes in UTC-seconds form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`; terminal-record verdict is `clean`; findings is `[]`; and complete `JCS(record)`, including `record_sha256`, is at most 558 bytes. That bound is exact: the `coverage_source_consistency` record with a 256-byte legal label is 558 bytes. The top-level `blueprint_path` is the literal 75-byte repository-relative path above and `round` is in the JCS-lossless integer interval `1..9,007,199,254,740,991`; its accepted value is still encoded as `uint64be(round)` in the aggregate frame. Complete sibling JCS is at most 4,288 bytes and the required final LF makes the complete file at most 4,289 bytes; this bound is exact with seven distinct 256-byte labels and maximum legal `round`.

For retained complete result object `Q`, including its literal `kind` and every complete finding item, `review_result_sha256 = hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/proxy-blueprint-review-result/v1\0") || uint32be(len(JCS(Q))) || JCS(Q)))`. Record verdict/findings must equal its clean retained result exactly; reconstruction restores the invariant `schema_version`, literal `kind`, lens, top-level blueprint digest, and baseline before recomputing `Q`. For record object `R` without `record_sha256`, `record_sha256 = hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/proxy-blueprint-review-record/v1\0") || uint32be(len(JCS(R))) || JCS(R)))`. For UTF-8 repository-relative path bytes `P`, `aggregate_sha256 = hex(SHA256(ASCII("cq/proxy-blueprint-review/v1\0") || uint32be(len(P)) || P || hexdecode(blueprint_sha256)[32] || hexdecode(authority_baseline_commit)[20] || uint64be(round) || each hexdecode(record_sha256)[32] in fixed lens order))`. Digest/commit inputs are decoded bytes, never ASCII hex. Before any input-sized allocation, JSON parsing, canonicalisation, or hashing, the verifier reads each complete reviewer-result stream through a fixed-size buffer and a counter capped at 2,097,153 bytes and each sibling through the same bounded-stream primitive capped at 4,290 bytes; it accepts only EOF at at most 2,097,152 result bytes or exactly one terminal LF at at most 4,289 sibling-file bytes. It strips only that final LF after EOF, then enforces the 4,288-byte sibling-JCS cap and, while tokenising the bounded buffer, the 558-byte complete-record cap before materialising any record. Crossing a cap aborts immediately and supplies no input-sized allocation or bytes to the JSON/JCS or hash implementation. Parser rejects duplicate/unknown members, invalid Unicode, non-integer or zero/out-of-JCS-safe-range round, non-JCS spelling/order, BOM, missing/doubled/nonterminal LF, or other extra bytes.

Review coordinator validates retained result schema and current blueprint bytes before construction planning. CU-0 owns checked-in `scripts/verify-blueprint-review` plus JCS/golden vectors; verifier accepts both legal result branches before sibling construction, while any `not_clean` result returns the round for redispatch and writes no sibling. For a terminal sibling it reconstructs all seven clean result objects from attested fields, restores the literal kind and invariant members, reparses, recursively reserialises, byte-compares, and checks result/record/aggregate digests, fixed lens and finding order, all byte bounds, unique finding IDs, exact unique task labels, exact clean/empty findings, timestamps, and current blueprint/baseline. CU manifest pins the same authority baseline and review digest, so later construction commits do not redefine baseline. Every CU wrapper and release gate verifies current blueprint bytes still match attestation. Positive vectors include one canonical clean result, canonical `not_clean` results at each severity, 1/64-finding results, a maximum-cardinality result using every longest legal member value without invented padding, 1- and 256-byte legal task labels, the exact 558-byte longest-lens record, and the exact 4,289-byte sibling assembled with seven distinct legal 256-byte labels and maximum JCS-safe `round`. They independently recompute `review_result_sha256`, `record_sha256`, and `aggregate_sha256` from the complete domain-separated length-framed inputs and require identical results for every legal streaming chunk split, including one-byte chunks and boundaries inside a digest, timestamp, task label, and final LF. Negative vectors reject missing/wrong kind, lens or verdict enum drift, clean/nonempty or not-clean/empty relations, unknown/empty/oversized finding members, invalid ID grammar, duplicate IDs, wrong severity/ID order, finding 65, any actual result encoding of 2,097,153 bytes, a 559-byte record, a 4,290-byte sibling, zero or `9,007,199,254,740,992` round, key/order/whitespace/Unicode/integer-width/endian/ASCII-hex variants, empty/reused/257-byte/grammar-invalid task labels, digest/schema mismatch, stale digest/baseline, malformed timestamp, truncated input at every chunk boundary, missing/doubled/nonterminal LF, trailing byte, and later blueprint edit. Every over-cap vector asserts that the bounded reader reports refusal before input-sized allocation, JSON/JCS entry, or any SHA-256 call; exact-cap vectors assert the framed length is the accepted JCS length rather than the file length including LF. They do not claim to reject fabricated task IDs or missing external provenance. Stronger provenance requires future signed orchestration receipt and schema revision.
